CHAPTER 01

投资与投机：聪明的投资者可以期待的结果

Investment versus Speculation

你做的究竟是投资，还是把猜测包装成投资？

Chapter 1Investment versus Speculation: Results to Be Expected by the Intelligent Investor第1章 投资与投机：聪明的投资者可以期待的结果

精读增强副本：英文原文完整保留；每个正文块新增完整中文译文；“译者补充（非原文）”仅用于解释概念和数字，不属于格雷厄姆或茨威格原文。
本章导读格雷厄姆开篇就给出了贯穿全书的核心定义：投资，是经过透彻分析、能保证本金安全并带来适当回报的操作；不满足这三点的一律算投机。他抱怨华尔街把所有买卖股票的人都叫做“投资者”，并提醒读者：普通股天然带有投机成分，投资者的任务是把这一成分控制在很小的范围内；如果一定要投机，就单独拿一小笔钱、放在单独的账户里，赚了钱也不要往里加。随后他分别讨论两类投资者可以期待的结果。对防御型投资者，他坚持债券与股票各占 25%–75% 之间（最简单是各一半）的折中策略，并用 1964 到 1971 年的利率和股息数据说明：为什么此刻债券看起来比股票更可取，又为什么仍不应把钱全押在债券上；他顺带否定了追逐热门新股的做法，推荐基金、投资顾问和定期定额投资这三种辅助手段。对积极型投资者，他先泼冷水：市场交易、短期选股、长期选股这三条常走的路都很难跑赢平均水平，因为人会犯错，而且市场价格往往已经反映了大家都知道的信息。要想持续跑赢，策略必须既内在稳健、又不受华尔街欢迎——而这类机会（特殊情况套利、低于营运资本的廉价股等）会随着追逐者增多而逐渐消失。

This chapter will outline the viewpoints that will be set forth in the remainder of the book. In particular we wish to develop at the outset our concept of appropriate portfolio policy for the individual, nonprofessional investor.

完整译文本章将概述本书其余部分要展开的观点。尤其是，我们希望从一开始就说明：对于个人的、非专业投资者来说，什么样的投资组合策略才算合适。

outline概述，勾勒要点set forth阐述，提出at the outset一开始portfolio policy投资组合策略nonprofessional非专业的

Investment versus Speculation

投资与投机

What do we mean by “investor”? Throughout this book the term will be used in contradistinction to “speculator.” As far back as 1934, in our textbook Security Analysis,1 we attempted a precise formulation of the difference between the two, as follows: “An investment operation is one which, upon thorough analysis promises safety of principal and an adequate return. Operations not meeting these requirements are speculative.”

完整译文我们所说的“投资者”究竟是什么意思？在本书中，这个词始终是相对于“投机者”而言的。早在1934年出版的教科书《证券分析》中，我们就试图给两者作出精确定义：“投资操作，是指经过透彻分析后，能够保证本金安全并带来适当回报的操作；不符合这些条件的操作，都是投机。”

译者补充（非原文）这里的“保证本金安全”不是承诺股价永不下跌，而是说：在充分分析和合理价格的前提下，本金发生永久性损失的概率应足够低。例如，一家公司值约100元，你用60元买入，短期跌到50元是报价波动；如果公司基本面没有坏，不能自动等同于本金永久受损。

in contradistinction to与……相对、相区别formulation表述，明确的定义investment operation投资操作，投资行为upon thorough analysis经过透彻的分析之后safety of principal本金安全adequate return适当的回报speculative投机性的

An investment operation is one which, upon thorough analysis promises safety of principal and an adequate return. Operations not meeting these requirements are speculative.

投资操作，是指经过透彻分析后，能够保证本金安全并带来适当回报的操作；不满足这些要求的操作就是投机。

one which… 是定语从句，one 代指 operation；upon 在这里等于 after。这是全书最核心的定义，三个要素：透彻分析、本金安全、适当回报。

While we have clung tenaciously to this definition over the ensuing 38 years, it is worthwhile noting the radical changes that have occurred in the use of the term “investor” during this period. After the great market decline of 1929–1932 all common stocks were widely regarded as speculative by nature. (A leading authority stated flatly that only bonds could be bought for investment.2) Thus we had then to defend our definition against the charge that it gave too wide scope to the concept of investment.

完整译文在随后的38年里，我们一直坚定地坚持这一定义。不过，值得注意的是，在此期间“投资者”一词的用法发生了根本变化。1929—1932年股市大崩盘之后，所有普通股都普遍被视为天生具有投机性。（一位权威人士甚至断言，只有债券才可以作为投资购买。）所以当时，我们不得不为自己的定义辩护，因为有人指责它把“投资”的范围划得太宽。

Now our concern is of the opposite sort. We must prevent our readers from accepting the common jargon which applies the term “investor” to anybody and everybody in the stock market. In our last edition we cited the following headline of a front-page article of our leading financial journal in June 1962:

完整译文现在，我们担心的却正好相反。我们必须防止读者接受华尔街的通俗行话——这种说法把股市里任何一个人都叫作“投资者”。在上一版中，我们曾引用美国主要财经报纸1962年6月一篇头版文章的标题：

SMALL INVESTORS BEARISH, THEY ARE SELLING ODD-LOTS SHORT

In October 1970 the same journal had an editorial critical of what it called “reckless investors,” who this time were rushing in on the buying side.

完整译文到了1970年10月，同一家报纸又发表社论，批评所谓“鲁莽的投资者”；只不过这一次，他们是在买方一侧蜂拥入市。

editorial社论reckless鲁莽的rushing in蜂拥而入

These quotations well illustrate the confusion that has been dominant for many years in the use of the words investment and speculation. Think of our suggested definition of investment given above, and compare it with the sale of a few shares of stock by an inexperienced member of the public, who does not even own what he is selling, and has some largely emotional conviction that he will be able to buy them back at a much lower price. (It is not irrelevant to point out that when the 1962 article appeared the market had already experienced a decline of major size, and was now getting ready for an even greater upswing. It was about as poor a time as possible for selling short.) In a more general sense, the later-used phrase “reckless investors” could be regarded as a laughable contradiction in terms—something like “spendthrift misers”—were this misuse of language not so mischievous.

完整译文这些引文充分说明，多年来人们对“投资”与“投机”的用词一直十分混乱。请想想我们前面提出的投资定义，再拿它同这样一种行为比较：一个毫无经验的普通人卖出几股自己根本不拥有的股票，仅凭强烈的情绪化信念，认定以后能以低得多的价格买回来。（值得指出的是，1962年那篇文章发表时，市场已经经历了一轮大幅下跌，随后却正准备迎来更大的上涨。那几乎是最糟糕的卖空时点。）从更广泛的意义看，“鲁莽的投资者”本来可以算一种可笑的自相矛盾，好比“挥霍无度的守财奴”；只不过这种用词混乱造成的危害太大，实在笑不出来。

In a more general sense, the later-used phrase “reckless investors” could be regarded as a laughable contradiction in terms—something like “spendthrift misers”—were this misuse of language not so mischievous.

从更宽泛的意义上讲，后来出现的“鲁莽的投资者”这一说法本可以被看作一个可笑的自相矛盾——好比“挥霍的守财奴”——要不是这种语言误用危害如此之大的话。

句末 were this misuse of language not so mischievous 是虚拟语气的倒装，等于 if this misuse … were not so mischievous；主句用 could be regarded 与之呼应。

The newspaper employed the word “investor” in these instances because, in the easy language of Wall Street, everyone who buys or sells a security has become an investor, regardless of what he buys, or for what purpose, or at what price, or whether for cash or on margin. Compare this with the attitude of the public toward common stocks in 1948, when over 90% of those queried expressed themselves as opposed to the purchase of common stocks.3 About half gave as their reason “not safe, a gamble,” and about half, the reason “not familiar with.”* It is indeed ironical (though not surprising) that common-stock purchases of all kinds were quite generally regarded as highly speculative or risky at a time when they were selling on a most attractive basis, and due soon to begin their greatest advance in history; conversely the very fact they had advanced to what were undoubtedly dangerous levels as judged by past experience later transformed them into “investments,” and the entire stock-buying public into “investors.”

完整译文报纸在这些情形中使用“投资者”一词，是因为按照华尔街随意的说法，任何买卖证券的人都成了投资者——不管他买什么、为什么买、以什么价格买，也不管是用自有现金还是借保证金买。把这种态度同1948年公众对普通股的看法比较一下：当时超过90%的受访者反对购买普通股。约一半人的理由是“不安全、像赌博”，另一半则说“不了解”。颇具讽刺意味的是，在普通股价格极具吸引力、并且即将开启历史上最大涨势之际，几乎所有普通股买卖反而都被普遍视为高度投机或危险；反过来，后来股价已经涨到按历史经验判断无疑相当危险的水平，恰恰是这轮上涨把股票变成了所谓“投资”，也把所有买股票的人变成了“投资者”。

conversely the very fact they had advanced to what were undoubtedly dangerous levels as judged by past experience later transformed them into “investments,” and the entire stock-buying public into “investors.”

反过来，恰恰是股价已经涨到了以过往经验判断无疑很危险的水平这一事实，后来反而把它们变成了“投资”，把所有买股票的公众都变成了“投资者”。

The distinction between investment and speculation in common stocks has always been a useful one and its disappearance is a cause for concern. We have often said that Wall Street as an institution would be well advised to reinstate this distinction and to emphasize it in all its dealings with the public. Otherwise the stock exchanges may some day be blamed for heavy speculative losses, which those who suffered them had not been properly warned against. Ironically, once more, much of the recent financial embarrassment of some stock-exchange firms seems to have come from the inclusion of speculative common stocks in their own capital funds. We trust that the reader of this book will gain a reasonably clear idea of the risks that are inherent in common-stock commitments—risks which are inseparable from the opportunities of profit that they offer, and both of which must be allowed for in the investor’s calculations.

完整译文在普通股领域区分投资与投机，始终很有用；如今这种区分逐渐消失，令人担忧。我们常说，作为一个行业，华尔街最好恢复这条界线，并在同公众的一切业务往来中反复强调。否则，证券交易所有一天可能会因为巨额投机损失而受到指责，因为遭受损失的人从未得到充分警告。又一个讽刺是，近来一些证券公司的财务困境，似乎正是因为它们把投机性普通股也计入了自有资本。我们希望读者能清楚认识到，持有普通股本身就带有风险；这些风险同股票提供的获利机会不可分割，投资者在计算时必须把两者都考虑进去。

distinction区别a cause for concern令人担忧的事would be well advised to最好……，明智的做法是……reinstate恢复embarrassment财务困境（此处不是“尴尬”）capital funds自有资本inherent固有的commitments投入的资金，头寸（本书常用）allowed for被考虑在内

What we have just said indicates that there may no longer be such a thing as a simon-pure investment policy comprising representative common stocks—in the sense that one can always wait to buy them at a price that involves no risk of a market or “quotational” loss large enough to be disquieting. In most periods the investor must recognize the existence of a speculative factor in his common-stock holdings. It is his task to keep this component within minor limits, and to be prepared financially and psychologically for adverse results that may be of short or long duration.

完整译文上面的话意味着，也许已经不存在一种由代表性普通股组成、绝对纯粹的投资策略——也就是说，投资者未必总能等到一个完全不用担心市场价格大幅下跌的买入价。在大多数时期，投资者必须承认自己的普通股持仓中含有投机成分。他的任务，是把这一成分控制在较小范围内，同时在财务和心理上都做好准备，以承受可能持续很短、也可能持续很久的不利结果。

simon-pure纯粹的，货真价实的representative有代表性的quotational报价上的（市价下跌造成的账面损失）disquieting令人不安的holdings持仓adverse不利的duration持续时间

Two paragraphs should be added about stock speculation per se, as distinguished from the speculative component now inherent in most representative common stocks. Outright speculation is neither illegal, immoral, nor (for most people) fattening to the pocketbook. More than that, some speculation is necessary and unavoidable, for in many common-stock situations there are substantial possibilities of both profit and loss, and the risks therein must be assumed by someone.* There is intelligent speculation as there is intelligent investing. But there are many ways in which speculation may be unintelligent. Of these the foremost are: (1) speculating when you think you are investing; (2) speculating seriously instead of as a pastime, when you lack proper knowledge and skill for it; and (3) risking more money in speculation than you can afford to lose.

完整译文这里还应补充两段，专门谈普通股的纯粹投机，并把它同大多数代表性普通股中固有的投机成分区别开来。直接投机既不违法，也不违背道德，而且对大多数人来说也不会让钱包变鼓。更进一步说，某些投机是必要且不可避免的：很多普通股既有显著获利可能，也有显著亏损可能，其中的风险总得有人承担。投机也可以是聪明的，就像投资可以是聪明的一样；但投机变得愚蠢的方式很多，其中最主要的三种是：（1）明明在投机，却以为自己在投资；（2）缺乏必要知识和技巧，却不把投机当消遣，而是认真押上身家；（3）投入超过自己承受得起的亏损金额。

per se本身（拉丁语）inherent in内在于outright彻头彻尾的，纯粹的fattening to the pocketbook让钱包变鼓（幽默说法）assumed承担（风险）foremost最主要的pastime消遣

Outright speculation is neither illegal, immoral, nor (for most people) fattening to the pocketbook.

纯粹的投机既不违法，也不违背道德，但（对大多数人来说）也不会让钱包变鼓。

neither … nor … 连接三个并列成分，第三项 fattening to the pocketbook 是幽默的转折：前两项是替投机说话，第三项是泼冷水。

In our conservative view every nonprofessional who operates on margin † should recognize that he is ipso facto speculating, and it is his broker’s duty so to advise him. And everyone who buys a so-called “hot” common-stock issue, or makes a purchase in any way similar thereto, is either speculating or gambling. Speculation is always fascinating, and it can be a lot of fun while you are ahead of the game. If you want to try your luck at it, put aside a portion—the smaller the better—of your capital in a separate fund for this purpose. Never add more money to this account just because the market has gone up and profits are rolling in. (That’s the time to think of taking money out of your speculative fund.) Never mingle your speculative and investment operations in the same account, nor in any part of your thinking.

完整译文按我们的保守看法，任何使用保证金交易的非专业人士，都应承认自己事实上是在投机，经纪人也有责任明确告诉他这一点。任何购买所谓“热门股”或进行类似交易的人，不是在投机，就是在赌博。投机总是很迷人，顺风时甚至很有乐趣。如果你想试试运气，就从本金中单独拿出一小部分——越小越好——设立一个专门账户。绝不要仅仅因为市场上涨、利润滚滚而来，就往这个账户继续加钱；那反而是应该考虑从投机账户取钱的时候。无论在账户上还是在头脑里，都不要把投机操作同投资操作混在一起。

译者补充（非原文）假设你有100万元长期资金，真想体验热门题材，可以只划出2万元作为投机账户，并预先接受最坏情况是全部亏完。若它涨到4万元，不应因为“证明自己很准”再从长期账户加钱；更符合本段原则的做法，是把一部分盈利转回投资账户。

Results to Be Expected by the Defensive Investor

防御型投资者可以期待的结果

We have already defined the defensive investor as one interested chiefly in safety plus freedom from bother. In general what course should he follow and what return can he expect under “average normal conditions”—if such conditions really exist? To answer these questions we shall consider first what we wrote on the subject seven years ago, next what significant changes have occurred since then in the underlying factors governing the investor’s expectable return, and finally what he should do and what he should expect under present-day (early 1972) conditions.

完整译文我们已经把防御型投资者定义为：主要追求安全，并希望免去操心的人。一般来说，他应该采取什么做法？在所谓“平均的正常条件”下——假如这种条件真的存在——又能期待怎样的回报？为回答这些问题，我们先回顾七年前写过的观点，再考察此后决定预期回报的基础因素发生了哪些重大变化，最后讨论在当前（1972年初）的条件下，他应该怎么做、又可以期待什么。

chiefly主要地freedom from bother省心，不受麻烦course做法，路线underlying factors基本因素expectable可以预期的

1. What We Said Six Years Ago

1. 我们六年前说过什么

We recommended that the investor divide his holdings between high-grade bonds and leading common stocks; that the proportion held in bonds be never less than 25% or more than 75%, with the converse being necessarily true for the common-stock component; that his simplest choice would be to maintain a 50–50 proportion between the two, with adjustments to restore the equality when market developments had disturbed it by as much as, say, 5%. As an alternative policy he might choose to reduce his common-stock component to 25% “if he felt the market was dangerously high,” and conversely to advance it toward the maximum of 75% “if he felt that a decline in stock prices was making them increasingly attractive.”

完整译文我们建议投资者把资金分配在高等级债券和主要普通股之间：债券占比不得低于25%，也不得高于75%；普通股占比自然也遵循同样的上下限。最简单的选择，是始终各占50%；当市场变化使两者比例偏离约5个百分点时，再调仓恢复均衡。另一种策略是：如果他认为市场高得危险，可以把股票比例降到25%；反过来，如果他认为股价下跌使股票越来越有吸引力，就可以把股票比例提高到最高75%。

译者补充（非原文）例如最初股票、债券各50万元。股票上涨后变成60万元，债券仍为50万元，股票占比升到约54.5%，接近偏离5个百分点；再平衡就是卖出约5万元股票、买入约5万元债券，使两边重新各55万元。这套规则的作用是迫使你相对低买高卖，而不是预测顶部和底部。

high-grade高等级的leading一流的，龙头的proportion比例converse相反的情况restore恢复disturbed打乱

In 1965 the investor could obtain about 4½% on high-grade taxable bonds and 3¼% on good tax-free bonds. The dividend return on leading common stocks (with the DJIA at 892) was only about 3.2%. This fact, and others, suggested caution. We implied that “at normal levels of the market” the investor should be able to obtain an initial dividend return of between 3½% and 4½% on his stock purchases, to which should be added a steady increase in underlying value (and in the “normal market price”) of a representative stock list of about the same amount, giving a return from dividends and appreciation combined of about 7½% per year. The half and half division between bonds and stocks would yield about 6% before income tax. We added that the stock component should carry a fair degree of protection against a loss of purchasing power caused by large-scale inflation.

完整译文1965年，投资者购买高等级应税债券大约能获得4.5%的收益，购买优质免税债券可获得3.25%；而主要普通股的股息收益率只有约3.2%（当时道琼斯工业平均指数为892点）。这一事实以及其他因素都提示人们要谨慎。我们当时认为，在“正常市场水平”上，投资者买入股票时应能获得3.5%至4.5%的初始股息收益率，再加上一组代表性股票的内在价值（以及“正常市场价格”）每年大致同等幅度的稳定增长，股息加升值的总回报约为每年7.5%。如果债券和股票各占一半，税前回报大约是6%。我们还补充说，股票部分应当能在相当程度上防止大规模通胀造成的购买力损失。

It should be pointed out that the above arithmetic indicated expectation of a much lower rate of advance in the stock market than had been realized between 1949 and 1964. That rate had averaged a good deal better than 10% for listed stocks as a whole, and it was quite generally regarded as a sort of guarantee that similarly satisfactory results could be counted on in the future. Few people were willing to consider seriously the possibility that the high rate of advance in the past means that stock prices are “now too high,” and hence that “the wonderful results since 1949 would imply not very good but bad results for the future.”4

完整译文需要指出的是，上述计算意味着我们对股市上涨速度的预期，远低于1949—1964年间的实际表现。那段时期，全部上市股票的平均上涨率远高于10%，人们普遍把它看成一种保证，认为未来也可以指望同样令人满意的结果。很少有人愿意认真考虑另一种可能：过去涨得太快，恰恰意味着股票“现在已经太贵”，因此“1949年以来的辉煌成绩，预示的不是未来会很好，而是未来可能很差”。

arithmetic算术，计算realized实现的a good deal better than远好于listed stocks上市股票counted on指望hence因此imply意味着

2. What Has Happened Since 1964

2. 1964 年以来发生了什么

The major change since 1964 has been the rise in interest rates on first-grade bonds to record high levels, although there has since been a considerable recovery from the lowest prices of 1970. The obtainable return on good corporate issues is now about 7½% and even more against 4½% in 1964. In the meantime the dividend return on DJIA-type stocks had a fair advance also during the market decline of 1969–70, but as we write (with “the Dow” at 900) it is less than 3.5% against 3.2% at the end of 1964. The change in going interest rates produced a maximum decline of about 38% in the market price of medium-term (say 20-year) bonds during this period.

完整译文1964年以来最大的变化，是一流债券的利率升到了创纪录高位，尽管其价格后来已从1970年的最低点明显回升。目前，优质公司债券的收益率约为7.5%甚至更高，而1964年只有4.5%。与此同时，受1969—1970年市场下跌影响，道琼斯成分股的股息收益率也有所上升；但在我们写作时（道指约900点），它仍低于3.5%，1964年底则为3.2%。这一时期市场利率的变化，曾使中长期（比如20年期）债券的市场价格最多下跌约38%。

first-grade一流的record high创纪录的高位considerable相当大的corporate issues公司债券medium-term中期的

There is a paradoxical aspect to these developments. In 1964 we discussed at length the possibility that the price of stocks might be too high and subject ultimately to a serious decline; but we did not consider specifically the possibility that the same might happen to the price of high-grade bonds. (Neither did anyone else that we know of.) We did warn (on p. 90) that “a long-term bond may vary widely in price in response to changes in interest rates.” In the light of what has since happened we think that this warning—with attendant examples—was insufficiently stressed. For the fact is that if the investor had a given sum in the DJIA at its closing price of 874 in 1964 he would have had a small profit thereon in late 1971; even at the lowest level (631) in 1970 his indicated loss would have been less than that shown on good long-term bonds. On the other hand, if he had confined his bond-type investments to U.S. savings bonds, short-term corporate issues, or savings accounts, he would have had no loss in market value of his principal during this period and he would have enjoyed a higher income return than was offered by good stocks. It turned out, therefore, that true “cash equivalents” proved to be better investments in 1964 than common stocks—in spite of the inflation experience that in theory should have favored stocks over cash. The decline in quoted principal value of good longer-term bonds was due to developments in the money market, an abstruse area which ordinarily does not have an important bearing on the investment policy of individuals.

完整译文这些变化带有悖论意味。1964年，我们曾详细讨论股票价格可能过高、最终可能严重下跌，却没有特别考虑高等级债券价格也会发生同样的事。（据我们所知，当时其他人也没有。）我们的确警告过：“长期债券的价格会随利率变化而大幅波动。”但结合后来的情况看，这条警告以及配套例子强调得远远不够。事实是：假如投资者在1964年按874点的收盘水平买入一笔道指股票，到1971年末还会略有盈利；即使在1970年631点的最低位，账面损失也小于优质长期债券的跌幅。另一方面，如果他的债券类投资只限于美国储蓄债券、短期公司债或储蓄账户，那么这段时期本金的市场价值不会受损，而且收入回报还高于优质股票。因此，1964年真正的“现金等价物”实际上比普通股更好——尽管理论上那段通胀经历本应更有利于股票而非现金。优质长期债券本金报价的下跌，来自货币市场的变化；这是一个深奥领域，通常并不会显著影响个人的投资政策。

译者补充（非原文）长期债券并不等于价格稳定。举例说，旧债券每年只付4%利息，而市场新债券已能付8%，买家不会愿意按原价买旧债；旧债价格必须下跌，才能让新买家的实际收益率接近市场水平。期限越长，通常对利率变化越敏感。

This is just another of an endless series of experiences over time that have demonstrated that the future of security prices is never predictable.* Almost always bonds have fluctuated much less than stock prices, and investors generally could buy good bonds of any maturity without having to worry about changes in their market value. There were a few exceptions to this rule, and the period after 1964 proved to be one of them. We shall have more to say about change in bond prices in a later chapter.

完整译文这只是漫长历史中又一次说明：证券价格的未来永远无法预测。通常，债券的波动远小于股票，投资者购买任何期限的优质债券时，一般不必担心市场价值变化。不过，这条规律也有少数例外，1964年以后的时期就是其中之一。后面的章节还会继续讨论债券价格的变化。

endless series无穷无尽的一连串predictable可预测的fluctuated波动maturity到期期限

3. Expectations and Policy in Late 1971 and Early 1972

3. 1971 年末与 1972 年初的预期与策略

Toward the end of 1971 it was possible to obtain 8% taxable interest on good medium-term corporate bonds, and 5.7% tax-free on good state or municipal securities. In the shorter-term field the investor could realize about 6% on U.S. government issues due in five years. In the latter case the buyer need not be concerned about a possible loss in market value, since he is sure of full repayment, including the 6% interest return, at the end of a comparatively short holding period. The DJIA at its recurrent price level of 900 in 1971 yields only 3.5%.

完整译文到1971年末，优质中期公司债券可以提供8%的应税利息，优质州政府或市政债券可提供5.7%的免税收益。在较短期限上，投资者购买五年后到期的美国政府债券可获得约6%的收益。后一种情况下，买方无须担心市场价值可能下跌，因为在相对较短的持有期结束时，他确定能够收回全部本金并获得6%的利息回报。1971年，道琼斯工业平均指数反复徘徊在900点附近，股息收益率却只有3.5%。

municipal市政的realize获得（收益）due in five years五年后到期comparatively相对地recurrent反复出现的yields收益率为

Let us assume that now, as in the past, the basic policy decision to be made is how to divide the fund between high-grade bonds (or other so-called “cash equivalents”) and leading DJIA-type stocks. What course should the investor follow under present conditions, if we have no strong reason to predict either a significant upward or a significant downward movement for some time in the future? First let us point out that if there is no serious adverse change, the defensive investor should be able to count on the current 3.5% dividend return on his stocks and also on an average annual appreciation of about 4%. As we shall explain later this appreciation is based essentially on the reinvestment by the various companies of a corresponding amount annually out of undistributed profits. On a before-tax basis the combined return of his stocks would then average, say, 7.5%, somewhat less than his interest on high-grade bonds.* On an after-tax basis the average return on stocks would work out at some 5.3%.5 This would be about the same as is now obtainable on good tax-free medium-term bonds.

完整译文让我们假设，现在同过去一样，最基本的策略决定仍然是：资金应如何在高等级债券（或其他所谓“现金等价物”）和道琼斯代表性龙头股之间分配。如果我们没有充分理由预测市场在未来一段时间会显著上涨或下跌，那么投资者在当前条件下应该怎么做？先指出一点：只要没有严重的不利变化，防御型投资者应当能够获得股票当前3.5%的股息收益，并获得约4%的年均升值。正如后文将解释的，这部分升值主要来自各公司每年把相当数量的未分配利润留在企业中再投资。因此，股票的税前综合回报平均约为7.5%，略低于高等级债券的利息；税后股票平均回报约为5.3%。这大致相当于当时优质免税中期债券的收益。

count on指望reinvestment再投资undistributed profits未分配利润before-tax basis税前口径work out at算下来是

These expectations are much less favorable for stocks against bonds than they were in our 1964 analysis. (That conclusion follows inevitably from the basic fact that bond yields have gone up much more than stock yields since 1964.) We must never lose sight of the fact that the interest and principal payments on good bonds are much better protected and therefore more certain than the dividends and price appreciation on stocks. Consequently we are forced to the conclusion that now, toward the end of 1971, bond investment appears clearly preferable to stock investment. If we could be sure that this conclusion is right we would have to advise the defensive investor to put all his money in bonds and none in common stocks until the current yield relationship changes significantly in favor of stocks.

完整译文与1964年的分析相比，这些预期对股票明显更不利、对债券更有利。（结论直接来自一个基本事实：1964年以来，债券收益率上升的幅度远大于股票收益率。）我们绝不能忘记，优质债券的利息和本金偿付受到的保障远好于股票的股息与价格升值，因而也更确定。所以我们不得不得出结论：在1971年末，债券投资显然比股票投资更可取。如果我们能确定这个判断一定正确，就应该建议防御型投资者把全部资金放进债券，一分钱也不投普通股，直到收益率关系发生明显有利于股票的变化。

favorable有利的follows inevitably from必然由……推出lose sight of忽视preferable to比……更可取yield relationship收益率关系

But of course we cannot be certain that bonds will work out better than stocks from today’s levels. The reader will immediately think of the inflation factor as a potent reason on the other side. In the next chapter we shall argue that our considerable experience with inflation in the United States during this century would not support the choice of stocks against bonds at present differentials in yield. But there is always the possibility—though we consider it remote—of an accelerating inflation, which in one way or another would have to make stock equities preferable to bonds payable in a fixed amount of dollars.* There is the alternative possibility—which we also consider highly unlikely—that American business will become so profitable, without stepped-up inflation, as to justify a large increase in common-stock values in the next few years. Finally, there is the more familiar possibility that we shall witness another great speculative rise in the stock market without a real justification in the underlying values. Any of these reasons, and perhaps others we haven’t thought of, might cause the investor to regret a 100% concentration on bonds even at their more favorable yield levels.

完整译文然而，我们当然无法确定：从今天的价位出发，债券最终一定会比股票表现更好。读者马上会想到，通货膨胀是支持股票的一项有力理由。下一章我们会说明，本世纪美国相当丰富的通胀经验，并不支持在当前这种收益率差异下选择股票而放弃债券。但仍有一种可能——尽管我们认为概率很低——通胀持续加速，以某种方式使股票权益优于只能按固定美元金额偿付的债券。另一个可能——我们同样认为很不可能——是美国企业在通胀没有加速的情况下变得异常赚钱，从而为未来几年普通股价值大幅上升提供依据。最后，还有一种更熟悉的可能：股市再次出现一轮缺乏内在价值支撑的投机性大涨。以上任何一种原因，或我们没有想到的其他原因，都可能使投资者后悔自己即使在债券收益率更有利时仍把资金100%集中于债券。

译者补充（非原文）这里保留股票，不是因为作者断言股票一定上涨，而是承认预测存在盲区。100%押注债券看似依据充分，却会把组合暴露在通胀、企业利润意外增长或投机性行情等单一方向的机会成本中；折中配置是在为“自己可能判断错”付保险费。

Hence, after this foreshortened discussion of the major considerations, we once again enunciate the same basic compromise policy for defensive investors—namely that at all times they have a significant part of their funds in bond-type holdings and a significant part also in equities. It is still true that they may choose between maintaining a simple 50–50 division between the two components or a ratio, dependent on their judgment, varying between a minimum of 25% and a maximum of 75% of either. We shall give our more detailed view of these alternative policies in a later chapter.

完整译文因此，在简要权衡这些主要因素后，我们再次提出同一项适用于防御型投资者的基本折中策略：无论何时，都应把相当一部分资金放在债券类资产中，同时也把相当一部分放在股票中。他们仍可选择最简单的50∶50配置，也可以根据自己的判断，让任一类资产的比例在最低25%和最高75%之间变化。我们将在后面的章节更详细地讨论这些不同策略。

foreshortened缩短的，简略的enunciate阐明，宣布compromise折中namely即equities股票，股权

Since at present the overall return envisaged from common stocks is nearly the same as that from bonds, the presently expectable return (including growth of stock values) for the investor would change little regardless of how he divides his fund between the two components. As calculated above, the aggregate return from both parts should be about 7.8% before taxes or 5.5% on a tax-free (or estimated tax-paid) basis. A return of this order is appreciably higher than that realized by the typical conservative investor over most of the long-term past. It may not seem attractive in relation to the 14%, or so, return shown by common stocks during the 20 years of the predominantly bull market after 1949. But it should be remembered that between 1949 and 1969 the price of the DJIA had advanced more than fivefold while its earnings and dividends had about doubled. Hence the greater part of the impressive market record for that period was based on a change in investors’ and speculators’ attitudes rather than in underlying corporate values. To that extent it might well be called a “bootstrap operation.”

完整译文由于当时普通股的预计总回报同债券几乎相同，投资者无论怎样在两者间分配资金，目前可期待的回报（包括股票价值增长）都不会有多大变化。按上面的计算，两部分合计的税前回报约为7.8%，按免税口径（或估算缴税后口径）则约为5.5%。这个水平明显高于过去大部分长期时期中典型保守投资者的实际所得。与1949年后以牛市为主的20年里普通股约14%的回报相比，它可能并不诱人。但必须记住，1949—1969年间，道琼斯指数价格上涨了五倍多，成分股的盈利和股息却只增加约一倍。因此，那段时期漂亮的市场纪录，大部分来自投资者和投机者态度的改变，而不是企业内在价值的增长。就此而言，那可以称为一种“揪着自己的鞋带把自己提起来”的行情。

译者补充（非原文）所谓“揪鞋带行情”，可以理解为估值抬升：若企业利润从1元增到2元，但投资者愿付的市盈率从10倍升到25倍，股价就会从10元涨到50元。五倍股价中只有一部分来自利润翻倍，其余主要来自市场愿意出更高倍数；这种回报很难永久重复。

Hence the greater part of the impressive market record for that period was based on a change in investors’ and speculators’ attitudes rather than in underlying corporate values. To that extent it might well be called a “bootstrap operation.”

因此，那个时期令人瞩目的市场表现，大部分建立在投资者和投机者态度的改变上，而不是公司内在价值的变化上。就此而言，它完全可以被称作一场“自我拉抬”的行情。

rather than in underlying corporate values 前面省略了 a change；bootstrap 源自“拽着自己的靴带把自己提起来”，指没有外部支撑、靠自身推动的过程。

In discussing the common-stock portfolio of the defensive investor, we have spoken only of leading issues of the type included in the 30 components of the Dow Jones Industrial Average. We have done this for convenience, and not to imply that these 30 issues alone are suitable for purchase by him. Actually, there are many other companies of quality equal to or excelling the average of the Dow Jones list; these would include a host of public utilities (which have a separate Dow Jones average to represent them).* But the major point here is that the defensive investor’s overall results are not likely to be decisively different from one diversified or representative list than from another, or—more accurately—that neither he nor his advisers could predict with certainty whatever differences would ultimately develop. It is true that the art of skillful or shrewd investment is supposed to lie particularly in the selection of issues that will give better results than the general market. For reasons to be developed elsewhere we are skeptical of the ability of defensive investors generally to get better than average results—which in fact would mean to beat their own overall performance.* (Our skepticism extends to the management of large funds by experts.)

完整译文讨论防御型投资者的普通股组合时，我们只提到道琼斯工业平均指数30只成分股这一类龙头股票。这只是为了叙述方便，并不表示只有这30只股票适合买入。事实上，还有许多公司的质量达到甚至超过道指平均水平，其中包括大量公用事业公司（它们另有一个道琼斯公用事业指数作为代表）。这里的要点是：防御型投资者从一个分散且有代表性的股票组合换到另一个类似组合，总体结果不大可能出现决定性差异；更准确地说，无论投资者本人还是顾问，都无法事先确定最终会产生什么差异。人们确实常说，高明或精明投资的本领，尤其体现在选出能跑赢大盘的股票。但由于后文将说明的理由，我们怀疑一般防御型投资者能够取得高于平均的结果——实际上，那等于要求他们战胜由自己共同构成的整体市场表现。（这种怀疑也适用于专家管理的大型基金。）

Let us illustrate our point by an example that at first may seem to prove the opposite. Between December 1960 and December 1970 the DJIA advanced from 616 to 839, or 36%. But in the same period the much larger Standard & Poor’s weighted index of 500 stocks rose from 58.11 to 92.15, or 58%. Obviously the second group had proved a better “buy” than the first. But who would have been so rash as to predict in 1960 that what seemed like a miscellaneous assortment of all sorts of common stocks would definitely outper-forms the aristocratic “thirty tyrants” of the Dow? All this proves, we insist, that only rarely can one make dependable predictions about price changes, absolute or relative.

完整译文我们用一个乍看似乎能证明相反结论的例子来说明。1960年12月至1970年12月，道琼斯工业平均指数从616点升到839点，涨幅36%；同期，范围大得多的标准普尔500加权指数从58.11升到92.15，涨幅58%。显然，第二组股票后来证明是更好的“买入对象”。但在1960年，谁敢断言这组看上去五花八门、什么股票都有的组合，肯定会跑赢道指那30只贵族般的“专横巨头”？我们坚持认为，这个例子只说明：人们极少能对价格的绝对变化或相对变化作出可靠预测。

We shall repeat here without apology—for the warning cannot be given too often—that the investor cannot hope for better than average results by buying new offerings, or “hot” issues of any sort, meaning thereby those recommended for a quick profit.† The contrary is almost certain to be true in the long run. The defensive investor must confine himself to the shares of important companies with a long record of profitable operations and in strong financial condition. (Any security analyst worth his salt could make up such a list.) Aggressive investors may buy other types of common stocks, but they should be on a definitely attractive basis as established by intelligent analysis.

完整译文我们不厌其烦地再重复一次——这条警告说多少遍都不算多：投资者不能指望靠购买新发行证券或任何“热门股”（即被推荐用于迅速获利的股票）取得高于平均的成绩。长期来看，结果几乎必然相反。防御型投资者必须把范围限制在重要公司的股票上，这些公司应有长期盈利记录和稳健的财务状况。（任何称职的证券分析师都能列出这样的名单。）积极型投资者可以购买其他类型的普通股，但前提是经过理性分析，确认买入条件确实具有吸引力。

without apology毫不客气地new offerings新发行的股票thereby由此confine himself to只限于worth his salt称职的Aggressive进取型的（与 enterprising 同义）

To conclude this section, let us mention briefly three supplementary concepts or practices for the defensive investor. The first is the purchase of the shares of well-established investment funds as an alternative to creating his own common-stock portfolio. He might also utilize one of the “common trust funds,” or “commingled funds,” operated by trust companies and banks in many states; or, if his funds are substantial, use the services of a recognized investment-counsel firm. This will give him professional administration of his investment program along standard lines. The third is the device of “dollar-cost averaging,” which means simply that the practitioner invests in common stocks the same number of dollars each month or each quarter. In this way he buys more shares when the market is low than when it is high, and he is likely to end up with a satisfactory overall price for all his holdings. Strictly speaking, this method is an application of a broader approach known as “formula investing.” The latter was already alluded to in our suggestion that the investor may vary his holdings of common stocks between the 25% minimum and the 75% maximum, in inverse relationship to the action of the market. These ideas have merit for the defensive investor, and they will be discussed more amply in later chapters.*

完整译文结束这一节前，再简要介绍三种可供防御型投资者采用的补充理念或做法。第一，可以购买经营成熟的投资基金份额，代替自己组建普通股组合。第二，可以利用许多州由信托公司和银行经营的“共同信托基金”或“混合基金”；如果资金规模较大，也可以聘请公认的投资顾问公司，按标准方式对投资计划进行专业管理。第三，是“定期定额投资”：每月或每季度用相同金额买入普通股。这样，市场低时能买到更多股数，市场高时买到较少股数，全部持仓的平均买入价格很可能令人满意。严格说来，这种方法属于更广义的“公式化投资”。前面建议股票占比在25%至75%之间、并随市场涨跌反向调整，也已经涉及这种思路。这些理念对防御型投资者有价值，后面会更充分地讨论。

译者补充（非原文）定期定额降低的是择时依赖，不是消灭亏损。例如每月投入1000元，价格分别为10元、5元、8元时可买100、200、125份，共425份，平均成本约7.06元；它仍要求所买资产长期具有价值，若资产永久归零，分批买入只会持续增加损失。

Results to Be Expected by the Aggressive Investor

积极型投资者可以期待的结果

Our enterprising security buyer, of course, will desire and expect to attain better overall results than his defensive or passive companion. But first he must make sure that his results will not be worse. It is no difficult trick to bring a great deal of energy, study, and native ability into Wall Street and to end up with losses instead of profits. These virtues, if channeled in the wrong directions, become indistinguishable from handicaps. Thus it is most essential that the enterprising investor start with a clear conception as to which courses of action offer reasonable chances of success and which do not.

完整译文积极型证券买家自然希望并期待取得比防御型或被动型投资者更好的总体成绩。但首先，他必须确保自己的成绩不会更差。带着大量精力、研究投入和天赋进入华尔街，最后得到的却是亏损而非利润，一点也不稀奇。如果把这些优点用错方向，它们就和缺点没有区别。因此，积极型投资者最重要的起点，是清楚知道哪些行动路线具有合理的成功机会，哪些没有。

First let us consider several ways in which investors and speculators generally have endeavored to obtain better than average results. These include:

完整译文先看看投资者和投机者通常用来争取高于平均成绩的几种方法，其中包括：

endeavored努力

1. TRADING IN THE MARKET. This usually means buying stocks when the market has been advancing and selling them after it has turned downward. The stocks selected are likely to be among those which have been “behaving” better than the market average. A small number of professionals frequently engage in short selling. Here they will sell issues they do not own but borrow through the established mechanism of the stock exchanges. Their object is to benefit from a subsequent decline in the price of these issues, by buying them back at a price lower than they sold them for. (As our quotation from the Wall Street Journal on p. 19 indicates, even “small investors”—perish the term!—sometimes try their unskilled hand at short selling.)

完整译文1．市场交易。这通常是指在市场已经上涨后买入股票，等市场转跌后再卖出。被选中的股票，多半是近期表现优于市场平均水平的品种。少数专业人士经常进行卖空：他们通过证券交易所的既定机制借入自己并不拥有的股票，再将其卖出，目的是等股价下跌后以更低价格买回，从中获利。（正如本书第19页引用的《华尔街日报》所示，甚至所谓“小投资者”——真该废掉这个称呼！——有时也会不熟练地尝试卖空。）

2. SHORT-TERM SELECTIVITY. This means buying stocks of companies which are reporting or expected to report increased earnings, or for which some other favorable development is anticipated.

完整译文2．短期选股。这是指买入正在报告盈利增长、预计即将报告盈利增长，或预期会出现其他利好进展的公司股票。

SELECTIVITY选股anticipated预期的

3. LONG-TERM SELECTIVITY. Here the usual emphasis is on an excellent record of past growth, which is considered likely to continue in the future. In some cases also the “investor” may choose companies which have not yet shown impressive results, but are expected to establish a high earning power later. (Such companies belong frequently in some technological area—e.g., computers, drugs, electronics—and they often are developing new processes or products that are deemed to be especially promising.)

完整译文3．长期选股。这种方法通常看重公司过去优秀的增长记录，并认为增长会在未来延续。有时，“投资者”也会选择尚未拿出亮眼业绩、但预计以后能形成很强盈利能力的公司。（这类公司经常属于某个技术领域，例如计算机、医药或电子，并常常在开发被认为特别有前景的新工艺或新产品。）

We have already expressed a negative view about the investor’s overall chances of success in these areas of activity. The first we have ruled out, on both theoretical and realistic grounds, from the domain of investment. Stock trading is not an operation “which, on thorough analysis, offers safety of principal and a satisfactory return.” More will be said on stock trading in a later chapter.*

完整译文对于投资者在这些活动领域中取得总体成功的机会，我们已经表达了否定看法。第一种方法——市场交易——无论从理论还是现实角度，我们都把它排除在投资范畴之外。股票交易并不是一种“经过透彻分析，能够保证本金安全并带来适当回报”的操作。后面的章节还会进一步讨论股票交易。

ruled out排除domain领域

In his endeavor to select the most promising stocks either for the near term or the longer future, the investor faces obstacles of two kinds—the first stemming from human fallibility and the second from the nature of his competition. He may be wrong in his estimate of the future; or even if he is right, the current market price may already fully reflect what he is anticipating. In the area of near-term selectivity, the current year’s results of the company are generally common property on Wall Street; next year’s results, to the extent they are predictable, are already being carefully considered. Hence the investor who selects issues chiefly on the basis of this year’s superior results, or on what he is told he may expect for next year, is likely to find that others have done the same thing for the same reason.

完整译文投资者无论想挑选短期还是长期最有前途的股票，都会遇到两类障碍：一类源于人本身会犯错，另一类源于竞争的性质。他可能对未来判断错误；即使判断正确，当前市场价格也可能已经充分反映了他的预期。在短期选股中，公司本年度业绩通常已是华尔街的公开信息；下一年度业绩只要能够预测，也早就在被仔细评估。因此，主要依据今年的优异成绩或别人告诉他的明年预期来选股，投资者很可能会发现，其他人早已出于同一理由做了同样的事。

译者补充（非原文）“好消息”不等于“好投资”。若所有人都预计某公司明年利润增长30%，股价可能早已按这个预期上涨；真正决定回报的，是实际结果相对市场已经计入价格的预期究竟更好还是更差。

In choosing stocks for their long-term prospects, the investor’s handicaps are basically the same. The possibility of outright error in the prediction—which we illustrated by our airlines example on p. 6—is no doubt greater than when dealing with near-term earnings. Because the experts frequently go astray in such forecasts, it is theoretically possible for an investor to benefit greatly by making correct predictions when Wall Street as a whole is making incorrect ones. But that is only theoretical. How many enterprising investors could count on having the acumen or prophetic gift to beat the professional analysts at their favorite game of estimating long-term future earnings?

完整译文依据长期前景选股时，投资者面临的障碍基本相同。正如第6页航空公司案例所示，长期预测完全出错的可能性，无疑比预测短期盈利更大。由于专家也经常在这类预测中走偏，理论上，如果整个华尔街都判断错误，而某位投资者判断正确，他当然可能获得巨大利益。但这只存在于理论上。究竟有多少积极型投资者，能够确信自己具备足够的洞察力或预言天赋，在专业分析师最擅长的长期盈利预测游戏中击败他们？

We are thus led to the following logical if disconcerting conclusion: To enjoy a reasonable chance for continued better than average results, the investor must follow policies which are (1) inherently sound and promising, and (2) not popular on Wall Street.

完整译文于是，我们得到一个合乎逻辑却令人不安的结论：要获得持续跑赢平均水平的合理机会，投资者必须采用同时满足两个条件的策略：（1）策略本身稳健且有前景；（2）它在华尔街并不流行。

译者补充（非原文）这两个条件缺一不可：冷门但脆弱的公司不因无人关注就值得买；优秀但人人追捧、价格已经过高的公司也未必能带来超额回报。策略要同时回答“为什么它本身站得住脚”和“为什么这个优势还没被竞争者买没”。

disconcerting令人不安的inherently内在地sound稳健的，正确的

To enjoy a reasonable chance for continued better than average results, the investor must follow policies which are (1) inherently sound and promising, and (2) not popular on Wall Street.

要想有合理的机会持续取得高于平均的成绩，投资者必须遵循这样的策略：（1）本身稳健且有前景，（2）在华尔街并不流行。

本章的核心结论。continued better than average results 是一个名词短语，better than average 整体作定语修饰 results。

Are there any such policies available for the enterprising investor? In theory once again, the answer should be yes; and there are broad reasons to think that the answer should be affirmative in practice as well. Everyone knows that speculative stock movements are carried too far in both directions, frequently in the general market and at all times in at least some of the individual issues. Furthermore, a common stock may be undervalued because of lack of interest or unjustified popular prejudice. We can go further and assert that in an astonishingly large proportion of the trading in common stocks, those engaged therein don’t appear to know—in polite terms—one part of their anatomy from another. In this book we shall point out numerous examples of (past) discrepancies between price and value. Thus it seems that any intelligent person, with a good head for figures, should have a veritable picnic on Wall Street, battening off other people’s foolishness. So it seems, but somehow it doesn’t work out that simply. Buying a neglected and therefore undervalued issue for profit generally proves a protracted and patience-trying experience. And selling short a too popular and therefore overvalued issue is apt to be a test not only of one’s courage and stamina but also of the depth of one’s pocketbook.* The principle is sound, its successful application is not impossible, but it is distinctly not an easy art to master.

完整译文积极型投资者真能找到这样的策略吗？理论上，答案仍应是肯定的；而且有充分的一般性理由认为，实践中也可能如此。人人都知道，投机性股价运动经常在上涨和下跌两个方向上走过头：整个市场时常如此，个别股票则随时都可能如此。此外，一只普通股可能因为无人关注，或因为公众无正当理由的偏见而被低估。甚至可以说，在数量惊人的普通股交易中，参与者——客气地讲——常常根本不知道自己在做什么。本书将列举许多过去价格与价值脱节的例子。于是，看起来任何头脑清楚、善于算数的人，都应该能在华尔街大摆宴席，靠别人的愚蠢饱餐一顿。看似如此，实际却没有这么简单。买入一只因受冷落而低估的股票，通常要经历漫长而磨炼耐心的等待；卖空一只过度热门、因而高估的股票，则不仅考验勇气与耐力，也考验口袋有多深。原则本身是正确的，成功运用也并非不可能，但这绝不是一门容易掌握的艺术。

There is also a fairly wide group of “special situations,” which over many years could be counted on to bring a nice annual return of 20% or better, with a minimum of overall risk to those who knew their way around in this field. They include intersecurity arbitrages, payouts or workouts in liquidations, protected hedges of certain kinds. The most typical case is a projected merger or acquisition which offers a substantially higher value for certain shares than their price on the date of the announcement. The number of such deals increased greatly in recent years, and it should have been a highly profitable period for the cognoscenti. But with the multiplication of merger announcements came a multiplication of obstacles to mergers and of deals that didn’t go through; quite a few individual losses were thus realized in these once-reliable operations. Perhaps, too, the overall rate of profit was diminished by too much competition.†

完整译文此外，还有相当广泛的一类“特殊情况”。多年来，熟悉这一领域的人往往能凭此取得20%甚至更高的良好年回报，同时把总体风险降到很低。它们包括证券间套利、清算中的分配或重组，以及某些有保护的对冲。最典型的情形，是已经计划的合并或收购：收购条件赋予某些股票的价值，明显高于公告日股价。近年此类交易数量大增，照理说，行家应当迎来一个利润丰厚的时期。然而，并购公告变多的同时，并购障碍和最终未能完成的交易也同步增多；这些过去可靠的操作因此出现了不少单笔亏损。也许，竞争过于激烈还压低了总体利润率。

译者补充（非原文）例如某股现价90元，已宣布以100元现金收购，表面价差11.1%。这并非无风险利息：若交易需半年完成，期间资金被占用；若监管否决后股价跌回60元，一次失败就可能吞掉多次成功的小价差。参与者越多，90元也可能被抬到98元，剩余收益进一步缩小。

The lessened profitability of these special situations appears one manifestation of a kind of self-destructive process—akin to the law of diminishing returns—which has developed during the lifetime of this book. In 1949 we could present a study of stock-market fluctuations over the preceding 75 years, which supported a formula—based on earnings and current interest rates—for determining a level to buy the DJIA below its “central” or “intrinsic” value, and to sell out above such value. It was an application of the governing maxim of the Rothschilds: “Buy cheap and sell dear.”* And it had the advantage of running directly counter to the ingrained and pernicious maxim of Wall Street that stocks should be bought because they have gone up and sold because they have gone down. Alas, after 1949 this formula no longer worked. A second illustration is provided by the famous “Dow Theory” of stock-market movements, in a comparison of its indicated splendid results for 1897–1933 and its much more questionable performance since 1934.

完整译文这些特殊情况的盈利能力下降，似乎体现了一种自我毁灭过程，类似收益递减规律；这种过程是在本书出版后的岁月中逐渐形成的。1949年，我们曾研究此前75年的股市波动，并据此提出一套以盈利和当前利率为基础的公式：当道琼斯指数低于其“中心价值”或“内在价值”时买入，高于该价值时卖出。这是罗斯柴尔德家族“低买高卖”准则的具体应用。它还有一个优点：同华尔街根深蒂固而有害的习惯完全相反——股价涨了才买，跌了反而卖。遗憾的是，1949年后这套公式不再有效。第二个例子是著名的股市“道氏理论”：它在1897—1933年间显示出极佳效果，1934年后的表现却可疑得多。

manifestation表现self-destructive自我毁灭的akin to类似于law of diminishing returns收益递减规律preceding之前的intrinsic内在的governing maxim指导格言Rothschilds罗斯柴尔德家族Buy cheap and sell dear低买高卖running directly counter to与……背道而驰ingrained根深蒂固的pernicious有害的Alas唉Dow Theory道氏理论questionable可疑的

A third and final example of the golden opportunities not recently available: A good part of our own operations on Wall Street had been concentrated on the purchase of bargain issues easily identified as such by the fact that they were selling at less than their share in the net current assets (working capital) alone, not counting the plant account and other assets, and after deducting all liabilities ahead of the stock. It is clear that these issues were selling at a price well below the value of the enterprise as a private business. No proprietor or majority holder would think of selling what he owned at so ridiculously low a figure. Strangely enough, such anomalies were not hard to find. In 1957 a list was published showing nearly 200 issues of this type available in the market. In various ways practically all these bargain issues turned out to be profitable, and the average annual result proved much more remunerative than most other investments. But they too virtually disappeared from the stock market in the next decade, and with them a dependable area for shrewd and successful operation by the enterprising investor. However, at the low prices of 1970 there again appeared a considerable number of such “sub-working-capital” issues, and despite the strong recovery of the market, enough of them remained at the end of the year to make up a full-sized portfolio.

完整译文第三个也是最后一个近年已难再见的黄金机会，来自我们自己在华尔街的大量实践：集中买入“廉价证券”。识别方法很简单——它们的售价甚至低于每股应占的净流动资产（营运资本），还没有把厂房设备等其他资产算进去，而且已经扣除了在普通股之前受偿的全部负债。显然，这些证券的价格远低于把企业当作一家私人公司来出售时的价值。任何业主或控股股东都不会考虑用如此荒唐的低价卖掉自己的企业。奇怪的是，这类异常当时并不难找。1957年公布的一份名单中，市场上有近200只这样的证券。它们几乎都通过不同方式实现了盈利，平均年回报也远高于大多数其他投资。但随后十年，它们几乎也从股市消失了；积极型投资者一个可靠而成功的操作领域随之消失。不过，在1970年的低价环境下，大量“低于净营运资本”的股票再次出现；即使市场强劲反弹，到年底仍有足够多的标的可以组成一个完整规模的组合。

译者补充（非原文）简化例子：公司有现金、存货和应收款共1亿元，总负债4000万元，因此净流动资产为6000万元；若公司总市值只有4000万元，相当于用4000万元购买6000万元净流动资产，还免费得到厂房等长期资产。但这不代表必赚：存货可能滞销、应收款可能收不回，所以作者强调分散和进一步分析。

bargain issues廉价股net current assets净流动资产working capital营运资本plant account厂房设备账户（固定资产）liabilities负债ahead of the stock优先于股票（受偿）proprietor业主majority holder大股东anomalies反常现象remunerative有利可图的virtually几乎sub-working-capital低于营运资本的full-sized portfolio完整规模的投资组合

The enterprising investor under today’s conditions still has various possibilities of achieving better than average results. The huge list of marketable securities must include a fair number that can be identified as undervalued by logical and reasonably dependable standards. These should yield more satisfactory results on the average than will the DJIA or any similarly representative list. In our view the search for these would not be worth the investor’s effort unless he could hope to add, say, 5% before taxes to the average annual return from the stock portion of his portfolio. We shall try to develop one or more such approaches to stock selection for use by the active investor.

完整译文在今天的条件下，积极型投资者仍有多种可能取得高于平均的结果。庞大的可交易证券清单中，必然存在相当数量的标的，可以用合乎逻辑且较可靠的标准识别为低估。平均而言，它们应当能比道琼斯指数或其他类似代表性组合带来更令人满意的结果。我们认为，除非投资者有希望让股票部分的税前年均回报比市场平均多出约5个百分点，否则就不值得为寻找这些标的付出精力。后面的章节将尝试为积极型投资者提出一种或多种这样的选股方法。

译者补充（非原文）“多5%”是精力成本门槛，不是收益承诺。若市场平均预期8%，主动研究只可能做到8.5%，额外0.5个百分点或许不足以补偿时间、交易成本、税费和犯错风险；只有潜在优势足够大，主动选择才值得做。

marketable securities可交易证券a fair number相当数量dependable standards可靠的标准worth the investor's effort值得投资者花力气active investor主动型投资者

Notes · 注释（贾森·兹威格）

* The survey Graham cites was conducted for the Fed by the University of Michigan and was published in the Federal Reserve Bulletin, July, 1948. People were asked, “Suppose a man decides not to spend his money. He can either put it in a bank or in bonds or he can invest it. What do you think would be the wisest thing for him to do with the money nowadays—put it in the bank, buy savings bonds with it, invest it in real estate, or buy common stock with it?” Only 4% thought common stock would offer a “satisfactory” return; 26% considered it “not safe” or a “gamble.” From 1949 through 1958, the stock market earned one of its highest 10-year returns in history, averaging 18.7% annually. In a fascinating echo of that early Fed survey, a poll conducted by BusinessWeek at year-end 2002 found that only 24% of investors were willing to invest more in their mutual funds or stock portfolios, down from 47% just three years earlier.
中文格雷厄姆引用的这项调查由密歇根大学替美联储实施，并发表于1948年7月的《联邦储备公报》。受访者被问道：“假设一个人决定不把钱花掉。他可以把钱存进银行或购买债券，也可以拿去投资。你认为如今最明智的做法是什么——存入银行、购买储蓄债券、投资房地产，还是购买普通股？”只有4%的人认为普通股能提供“令人满意”的回报；26%的人认为普通股“不安全”或是在“赌博”。1949—1958年，股市取得历史上最高的十年期回报之一，年均18.7%。有趣的是，早期美联储调查后来出现了回声：2002年末《商业周刊》的一项调查发现，只有24%的投资者愿意增加对共同基金或股票组合的投资，而三年前这一比例为47%。
* Speculation is beneficial on two levels: First, without speculation, untested new companies (like Amazon.com or, in earlier times, the Edison Electric Light Co.) would never be able to raise the necessary capital for expansion. The alluring, long-shot chance of a huge gain is the grease that lubricates the machinery of innovation. Secondly, risk is exchanged (but never eliminated) every time a stock is bought or sold. The buyer purchases the primary risk that this stock may go down. Meanwhile, the seller still retains a residual risk—the chance that the stock he just sold may go up!
中文投机在两个层面上有益。第一，没有投机，未经验证的新公司（例如亚马逊，或更早的爱迪生电灯公司）就无法筹得扩张所需资本。以小概率博取巨额收益的诱惑，是让创新机器运转的润滑油。第二，每次股票买卖都会交换风险，却从不消灭风险。买方承担股票可能下跌的主要风险；与此同时，卖方仍保留一种剩余风险——他刚卖出的股票可能上涨。
† A margin account enables you to buy stocks using money you borrow from the brokerage firm. By investing with borrowed money, you make more when your stocks go up—but you can be wiped out when they go down. The collateral for the loan is the value of the investments in your account—so you must put up more money if that value falls below the amount you borrowed. For more information about margin accounts, see www.sec.gov/investor/ pubs/margin.htm, www.sia.com/publications/pdf/MarginsA.pdf, and www. nyse.com/pdfs/2001_factbook_09.pdf.
中文保证金账户允许你使用从经纪公司借来的钱购买股票。借钱投资会在股票上涨时放大利润，也会在股票下跌时让你损失殆尽。贷款的抵押品是账户中投资品的价值；因此，一旦该价值跌到低于借款要求的水平，你就必须补交更多资金。原文随后列出了美国证监会、证券业协会和纽约证券交易所有关保证金账户的资料网址。
* Read Graham’s sentence again, and note what this greatest of investing experts is saying: The future of security prices is never predictable. And as you read ahead in the book, notice how everything else Graham tells you is designed to help you grapple with that truth. Since you cannot predict the behavior of the markets, you must learn how to predict and control your own behavior.
中文请再读一遍格雷厄姆的话，注意这位最伟大的投资专家在说什么：证券价格的未来永远不可预测。继续阅读本书时，你会发现格雷厄姆的其他教导，都是在帮助你面对这一事实。既然无法预测市场行为，你就必须学会预判并控制自己的行为。
* How well did Graham’s forecast pan out? At first blush, it seems, very well: From the beginning of 1972 through the end of 1981, stocks earned an annual average return of 6.5%. (Graham did not specify the time period for his forecast, but it’s plausible to assume that he was thinking of a 10-year time horizon.) However, inflation raged at 8.6% annually over this period, eating up the entire gain that stocks produced. In this section of his chapter, Graham is summarizing what is known as the “Gordon equation,” which essentially holds that the stock market’s future return is the sum of the current dividend yield plus expected earnings growth. With a dividend yield of just under 2% in early 2003, and long-term earnings growth of around 2%, plus inflation at a bit over 2%, a future average annual return of roughly 6% is plausible. (See the commentary on Chapter 3.)
中文格雷厄姆的预测后来表现如何？乍看之下相当准确：1972年初至1981年末，股票年均回报为6.5%。（格雷厄姆没有说明预测期限，但可以合理推测他考虑的是十年。）然而，这段时期通胀率高达年均8.6%，吃掉了股票带来的全部收益。本节其实是在概述后来被称为“戈登方程”的方法：股市未来回报大体等于当前股息收益率加预期盈利增长率。2003年初股息收益率略低于2%，长期盈利实际增长约2%，再加上略高于2%的通胀，未来年均回报约6%是合理估计。（参见第3章评论。）
* Since 1997, when Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (or TIPS) were introduced, stocks have no longer been the automatically superior choice for investors who expect inflation to increase. TIPS, unlike other bonds, rise in value if the Consumer Price Index goes up, effectively immunizing the investor against losing money after inflation. Stocks carry no such guarantee and, in fact, are a relatively poor hedge against high rates of inflation. (For more details, see the commentary to Chapter 2.)
中文自1997年美国推出通胀保值国债（TIPS）后，对于预期通胀上升的投资者来说，股票不再自动是更优选择。与其他债券不同，TIPS的价值会随消费者价格指数上升，实际上能保护投资者免受通胀后的实际购买力损失。股票没有这种保证；事实上，面对高通胀时，股票是一种相对较差的对冲工具。（详见第2章评论。）
* Today, the most widely available alternatives to the Dow Jones Industrial Average are the Standard & Poor’s 500-stock index (the “S & P”) and the Wilshire 5000 index. The S & P focuses on 500 large, well-known companies that make up roughly 70% of the total value of the U.S. equity market. The Wilshire 5000 follows the returns of nearly every significant, publicly traded stock in America, roughly 6,700 in all; but, since the largest companies account for most of the total value of the index, the return of the Wilshire 5000 is usually quite similar to that of the S & P 500. Several low-cost mutual funds enable investors to hold the stocks in these indexes as a single, convenient portfolio. (See Chapter 9.)
中文今天，道琼斯工业平均指数最常见的替代指标，是标准普尔500指数和威尔希尔5000指数。标普500聚焦500家大型知名公司，约占美国股票市场总价值的70%。威尔希尔5000追踪美国几乎每一只重要上市股票的回报，总数约6700只；但由于最大的公司占指数总价值的大部分，威尔希尔5000的回报通常与标普500很相似。投资者可通过若干低成本共同基金，以一个方便的组合持有这些指数中的股票。（参见第9章。）

* In “selling short” (or “shorting”) a stock, you make a bet that its share price will go down, not up. Shorting is a three-step process: First, you borrow shares from someone who owns them; then you immediately sell the borrowed shares; finally, you replace them with shares you buy later. If the stock drops, you will be able to buy your replacement shares at a lower price. The difference between the price at which you sold your borrowed shares and the price you paid for the replacement shares is your gross profit (reduced by dividend or interest charges, along with brokerage costs). However, if the stock goes up in price instead of down, your potential loss is unlimited—making short sales unacceptably speculative for most individual investors.
中文“卖空”一只股票，就是押注其股价会下跌而不是上涨。卖空分三步：先向股票持有人借入股份；随即卖出借来的股份；最后在以后买入股份归还。如果股价下跌，你能以更低价格买回；卖出借股所得与买回成本之差，就是毛利润，还要扣除股息或利息以及经纪费用。但如果股价不跌反涨，潜在亏损没有上限，因此对大多数个人投资者来说，卖空具有不可接受的投机性。
† In the late 1980s, as hostile corporate takeovers and leveraged buyouts multiplied, Wall Street set up institutional arbitrage desks to profit from any errors in pricing these complex deals. They became so good at it that the easy profits disappeared and many of these desks have been closed down. Although Graham does discuss it again (see pp. 174–175), this sort of trading is no longer feasible or appropriate for most people, since only multimillion-dollar trades are large enough to generate worthwhile profits. Wealthy individuals and institutions can utilize this strategy through hedge funds that specialize in merger or “event” arbitrage.
中文20世纪80年代末，随着敌意收购和杠杆收购增多，华尔街设立了机构套利部门，利用复杂交易中的定价错误获利。它们后来变得非常擅长，以至于容易获得的利润消失，许多部门也被关闭。尽管格雷厄姆后来再次谈到这一方法（见第174—175页），它对大多数人已不再可行或合适，因为只有数百万美元规模的交易才足以产生值得追求的利润。富裕个人和机构可通过专做并购套利或“事件套利”的对冲基金采用该策略。
* The Rothschild family, led by Nathan Mayer Rothschild, was the dominant power in European investment banking and brokerage in the nineteenth century. For a brilliant history, see Niall Ferguson, The House of Rothschild: Money’s Prophets, 1798–1848 (Viking, 1998).
中文以内森·迈耶·罗斯柴尔德为首的罗斯柴尔德家族，是19世纪欧洲投资银行和经纪业的主导力量。精彩的历史记述可参见尼尔·弗格森《罗斯柴尔德家族：金钱的先知，1798—1848》（维京出版社，1998年）。

Chapter 2The Investor and Inflation第2章 投资者与通货膨胀

本章导读格雷厄姆在本章处理一个当时（1970 年代初）人人关心的问题：通货膨胀会不会侵蚀投资者的财富？普通股是不是对抗通胀的天然良药？华尔街的流行看法是“债券天生不可取，股票天生更优”，他不接受这种绝对化的结论，而是用 1915 到 1970 年共 55 年的数据（表 2-1）来检验。他先承认通胀是常态，并假定未来每年约 3% 的通胀率；按这个速度，通胀会吃掉免税债券利息的一半，但只要投资者只花掉税后利息的一半，本金的购买力仍能保持。接着他追问：股票能不能做得更好？过去 55 年股票年均回报约 8%（4% 价格上涨加 4% 股息），确实胜过债券，却并不高于 1971 年高等级债券的收益率；至于未来能否更好，他的回答是“断然的不”。论证分两层：第一，通胀与股票盈利、股价之间没有紧密的时间关联，1966 到 1970 年生活成本上涨 22%，股票盈利和股价反而下跌；第二，过去 20 年美国企业的资本收益率不升反降，通胀并没有提高原有资本的盈利能力，反倒是工资涨幅超过生产率、企业债务膨胀近五倍等因素在拖累真实盈利。因此他认为，以 1971 年末的价格买入道指类股票，合理的预期总回报只有 8% 左右；而且“它们会波动”（老摩根名言），过度相信通胀假说的人会把牛市误读为继续买入的理由，“那条路通向悲伤”。他还简评了黄金、收藏品和房地产，都不理想。结论回到第 1 章：既不能全押债券，也不能全押股票，股票只是“两害相权取其轻”中较轻的那一个。

Inflation, and the fight against it, has been very much in the public’s mind in recent years. The shrinkage in the purchasing power of the dollar in the past, and particularly the fear (or hope by speculators) of a serious further decline in the future, has greatly influenced the thinking of Wall Street. It is clear that those with a fixed dollar income will suffer when the cost of living advances, and the same applies to a fixed amount of dollar principal. Holders of stocks, on the other hand, have the possibility that a loss of the dollar’s purchasing power may be offset by advances in their dividends and the prices of their shares.

完整译文近些年来，通货膨胀以及如何对抗通胀，一直是公众高度关心的问题。美元过去购买力的缩水，尤其是人们对未来可能进一步严重贬值的恐惧（或者投机者对此抱有的期待），深刻影响了华尔街的思考。生活成本上涨时，领取固定美元收入的人显然会受损；持有固定金额美元本金的人同样如此。另一方面，股票持有人则有一种可能：股息和股价上涨，或许能抵消美元购买力下降造成的损失。

very much in the public’s mind深受公众关注，为公众所挂心shrinkage缩水，缩减purchasing power购买力cost of living生活成本advances上涨（本书常用；此处为动词）principal本金

On the basis of these undeniable facts many financial authorities have concluded that (1) bonds are an inherently undesirable form of investment, and (2) consequently, common stocks are by their very nature more desirable investments than bonds. We have heard of charitable institutions being advised that their portfolios should consist 100% of stocks and zero percent of bonds.* This is quite a reversal from the earlier days when trust investments were restricted by law to high-grade bonds (and a few choice preferred stocks).

完整译文基于这些无可否认的事实，许多金融权威得出结论：（1）债券天生是一种不理想的投资；（2）因此，普通股就其本性而言比债券更值得投资。我们甚至听说，有人建议慈善机构把投资组合全部放在股票上，一点债券也不要持有。这与早年的做法完全相反——那时许多州的法律规定，信托资金只能投资高等级债券，在某些情况下也可少量投资优质优先股。

financial authorities金融界的权威人士inherently undesirable本质上不可取的by their very nature就其本性而言charitable institutions慈善机构trust investments信托投资choice preferred stocks精选的优先股（choice 作形容词：上乘的）

Our readers must have enough intelligence to recognize that even high-quality stocks cannot be a better purchase than bonds under all conditions—i.e., regardless of how high the stock market may be and how low the current dividend return compared with the rates available on bonds. A statement of this kind would be as absurd as was the contrary one—too often heard years ago—that any bond is safer than any stock. In this chapter we shall try to apply various measurements to the inflation factor, in order to reach some conclusions as to the extent to which the investor may wisely be influenced by expectations regarding future rises in the price level.

完整译文读者应有足够的判断力，明白即使是高质量股票，也不可能在任何条件下都比债券更值得买——不能无视股市已经多高，也不能无视当前股息收益率相对债券利率已经多低。这样的断言，就像多年前经常听到的相反说法“任何债券都比任何股票安全”一样荒谬。本章将用多种尺度衡量通胀因素，以判断投资者在多大程度上可以合理地让未来物价上涨预期影响自己的决策。

A statement of this kind would be as absurd as was the contrary one—too often heard years ago—that any bond is safer than any stock.

这样一种说法，就像与之相反的那种说法——多年前太常听到的“任何债券都比任何股票安全”——一样荒谬。

In this matter, as in so many others in finance, we must base our views of future policy on a knowledge of past experience. Is inflation something new for this country, at least in the serious form it has taken since 1965? If we have seen comparable (or worse) inflations in living experience, what lessons can be learned from them in confronting the inflation of today? Let us start with Table 2-1, a condensed historical tabulation that contains much information about changes in the general price level and concomitant changes in the earnings and market value of common stocks. Our figures will begin with 1915, and thus cover 55 years, presented at five-year intervals. (We use 1946 instead of 1945 to avoid the last year of wartime price controls.)

完整译文在这个问题上，同金融领域许多问题一样，我们必须根据历史经验来制定未来政策。通胀对美国来说是新事物吗，至少1965年以来这种较严重的通胀是新的吗？如果在有生之年已经见过相当甚至更严重的通胀，我们面对今天的通胀时能从中学到什么？先看表2-1。这份压缩的历史统计包含了总体价格水平的变化，以及普通股盈利和市场价值同时发生的变化。数据从1915年开始，覆盖55年，以五年为间隔列示。（我们使用1946年而非1945年，以避开战时价格管制的最后一年。）

base our views of future policy on把我们对未来策略的看法建立在……之上（base A on B）in living experience在活着的人的亲身经历中condensed浓缩的，精简的tabulation表格，列表concomitant伴随的，相应的at five-year intervals每隔五年wartime price controls战时价格管制

The first thing we notice is that we have had inflation in the past—lots of it. The largest five-year dose was between 1915 and 1920, when the cost of living nearly doubled. This compares with the advance of 15% between 1965 and 1970. In between, we have had three periods of declining prices and then six of advances at varying rates, some rather small. On this showing, the investor should clearly allow for the probability of continuing or recurrent inflation to come.

完整译文首先可以看到，过去确实发生过通胀，而且幅度不小。最严重的五年是1915—1920年，生活成本几乎翻了一倍；相比之下，1965—1970年只上涨15%。两者之间，价格曾有三个时期下降，另有六个时期以不同速度上涨，其中一些涨幅很小。由此看来，投资者显然应把未来持续或反复出现通胀的可能性考虑进去。

dose一剂（此处比喻一轮通胀）at varying rates以不同的速度On this showing从这些数据来看，据此allow for把……考虑在内，预留余地recurrent反复出现的

Can we tell what the rate of inflation is likely to be? No clear answer is suggested by our table; it shows variations of all sorts. It would seem sensible, however, to take our cue from the rather consistent record of the past 20 years. The average annual rise in the consumer price level for this period has been 2.5%; that for 1965–1970 was 4.5%; that for 1970 alone was 5.4%. Official government policy has been strongly against large-scale inflation, and there are some reasons to believe that Federal policies will be more effective in the future than in recent years.* We think it would be reasonable for an investor at this point to base his thinking and decisions on a probable (far from certain) rate of future inflation of, say, 3% per annum. (This would compare with an annual rate of about 2½% for the entire period 1915–1970.)1

完整译文我们能判断未来通胀率大约是多少吗？表格没有给出明确答案，因为历史变化多种多样。不过，参考过去20年相当稳定的记录似乎合理：这段时期消费价格年均上涨2.5%，1965—1970年为4.5%，仅1970年就为5.4%。政府的正式政策坚决反对大规模通胀，也有一些理由相信，今后的联邦政策会比近几年更有效。我们认为，此时投资者可以把未来通胀率约3%——这只是可能值，远非确定值——作为思考和决策的基础。（1915—1970年全时期年均通胀约2.5%。）

variations of all sorts各种各样的变化take our cue from从……得到提示，以……为依据consumer price level消费者物价水平Federal policies联邦政府的政策far from certain远非确定say比如说，假定（插入语）per annum每年（拉丁语）

What would be the implications of such an advance? It would eat up, in higher living costs, about one-half the income now obtainable on good medium-term tax-free bonds (or our assumed after-tax equivalent from high-grade corporate bonds). This would be a serious shrinkage, but it should not be exaggerated. It would not mean that the true value, or the purchasing power, of the investor’s fortune need be reduced over the years. If he spent half his interest income after taxes he would maintain this buying power intact, even against a 3% annual inflation.

完整译文如果物价按这个速度上涨，会有什么后果？生活成本增加会吃掉当时优质中期免税债券收入的大约一半（或高等级公司债券税后等值收入的一半）。这确实是严重缩水，却不应夸大。它并不意味着投资者财富的真实价值或购买力必然逐年减少。如果他只花掉税后利息收入的一半，即使每年通胀3%，仍能保持本金购买力不变。

译者补充（非原文）若税后利息为6%，通胀为3%，把3%用于生活、留下3%继续积累，名义本金大致能随物价增长，购买力可近似维持；若把6%全花掉，本金名义金额不变，实际购买力就会逐年下降。这里是简化关系，未计税率和利率变化。

But the next question, naturally, is, “Can the investor be reasonably sure of doing better by buying and holding other things than high-grade bonds, even at the unprecedented rate of return offered in 1970–1971?” Would not, for example, an all-stock program be preferable to a part-bond, part-stock program? Do not common stocks have a built-in protection against inflation, and are they not almost certain to give a better return over the years than will bonds? Have not in fact stocks treated the investor far better than have bonds over the 55-year period of our study?

完整译文接下来的问题自然是：“即使1970—1971年的高等级债券提供了前所未有的高收益，投资者是否仍可以相当确定地通过买入并持有其他资产做得更好？”例如，全股票策略会不会优于股票加债券的组合？普通股难道没有内置的抗通胀能力，长期回报难道不是几乎肯定优于债券？在本章研究的55年里，股票事实上不是远比债券更善待投资者吗？

unprecedented空前的，前所未有的all-stock program全股票的投资方案preferable to比……更可取built-in内在的，自带的than will bonds比债券（将带来的回报）（倒装，补全为 than bonds will give）

Do not common stocks have a built-in protection against inflation, and are they not almost certain to give a better return over the years than will bonds?

普通股不是自带抵御通胀的保护吗？长期来看，它们不是几乎肯定能比债券带来更高的回报吗？

这一段连续四个否定疑问句（Would not…? Do not…? Have not…?）都是修辞性反问，代表流行观点，作者接下来要反驳；句末 than will bonds 是助动词提前的倒装，补全是 than bonds will give。

The answer to these questions is somewhat complicated. Common stocks have indeed done better than bonds over a long period of time in the past. The rise of the DJIA from an average of 77 in 1915 to an average of 753 in 1970 works out at an annual compounded rate of just about 4%, to which we may add another 4% for average dividend return. (The corresponding figures for the S & P composite are about the same.) These combined figures of 8% per year are of course much better than the return enjoyed from bonds over the same 55-year period. But they do not exceed that now offered by high-grade bonds. This brings us to the next logical question: Is there a persuasive reason to believe that common stocks are likely to do much better in future years than they have in the last five and one-half decades?

完整译文这些问题的答案比较复杂。过去很长时期内，普通股确实优于债券。道琼斯工业平均指数从1915年的平均77点升至1970年的平均753点，复合年增长率约4%；再加上平均约4%的股息收益，总回报约为每年8%。（标普综合指数的相应数字大致相同。）这当然远高于同期债券回报，但并没有超过当时高等级债券已经提供的收益。于是又产生一个合乎逻辑的问题：有什么有力理由相信，未来普通股会比过去55年表现得好得多？

works out at算下来是annual compounded rate年复合增长率corresponding相应的，对应的S & P composite标准普尔综合指数persuasive有说服力的five and one-half decades五十五年（五个半十年）

Our answer to this crucial question must be a flat no. Common stocks may do better in the future than in the past, but they are far from certain to do so. We must deal here with two different time elements in investment results. The first covers what is likely to occur over the long-term future—say, the next 25 years. The second applies to what is likely to happen to the investor—both financially and psychologically—over short or intermediate periods, say five years or less. His frame of mind, his hopes and apprehensions, his satisfaction or discontent with what he has done, above all his decisions what to do next, are all determined not in the retrospect of a lifetime of investment but rather by his experience from year to year.

完整译文对这个关键问题，我们只能明确回答：没有。普通股未来可能比过去更好，却远非必然如此。投资结果中必须区分两个时间尺度。第一个是长期未来，例如接下来25年可能发生什么；第二个是较短或中等时期，例如五年以内，投资者在财务和心理上可能经历什么。他的心态、希望与忧虑、对过去操作的满意或不满，尤其是下一步该做什么的决定，并不是在回顾一生投资后形成的，而是受逐年经历支配。

a flat no断然的否定time elements时间因素frame of mind心态apprehensions忧虑，担心discontent不满above all最重要的是in the retrospect of在对……的回顾中

His frame of mind, his hopes and apprehensions, his satisfaction or discontent with what he has done, above all his decisions what to do next, are all determined not in the retrospect of a lifetime of investment but rather by his experience from year to year.

他的心态、他的希望与忧虑、他对自己所作所为的满意或不满，尤其是他关于下一步该怎么做的决定，都不是在回顾一生投资时才被决定的，而是由他一年又一年的切身经历所决定的。

主语是四个并列的名词短语（frame of mind / hopes and apprehensions / satisfaction or discontent / decisions），谓语 are all determined 直到句子后半才出现；not … but rather … 对比“一生的回顾”与“逐年的经历”，点出投资者的心理是被短期经验左右的。

On this point we can be categorical. There is no close time connection between inflationary (or deflationary) conditions and the movement of common-stock earnings and prices. The obvious example is the recent period, 1966–1970. The rise in the cost of living was 22%, the largest in a five-year period since 1946–1950. But both stock earnings and stock prices as a whole have declined since 1965. There are similar contradictions in both directions in the record of previous five-year periods.

完整译文在这一点上，我们可以说得很明确：通胀或通缩环境与普通股盈利和价格的变动，在时间上并没有紧密联系。最明显的例子是1966—1970年：生活成本上涨22%，是1946—1950年以来最大的五年涨幅；但从1965年起，整体股票盈利和股价都下降了。此前各个五年时期的记录中，也能看到方向相反的类似矛盾。

译者补充（非原文）通胀与股票并非同时同幅移动。企业能否把成本上涨转嫁给客户、工资和原料涨得多快、估值起点多高，都会影响股票结果。因此“有通胀”不能单独推出“股票短期一定涨”。

categorical斩钉截铁的，明确无疑的deflationary通货紧缩的as a whole整体上declined下跌（本书常用）contradictions矛盾之处

Inflation and Corporate Earnings

通货膨胀与公司盈利

Another and highly important approach to the subject is by a study of the earnings rate on capital shown by American business. This has fluctuated, of course, with the general rate of economic activity, but it has shown no general tendency to advance with wholesale prices or the cost of living. Actually this rate has fallen rather markedly in the past twenty years in spite of the inflation of the period. (To some degree the decline was due to the charging of more liberal depreciation rates. See Table 2-2.) Our extended studies have led to the conclusion that the investor cannot count on much above the recent five-year rate earned on the DJIA group—about 10% on net tangible assets (book value) behind the shares.2Since the market value of these issues is well above their book value—say, 900 market vs. 560 book in mid-1971—the earnings on current market price work out only at some 6¼%. (This relationship is generally expressed in the reverse, or “times earnings,” manner—e.g., that the DJIA price of 900 equals 18 times the actual earnings for the 12 months ended June 1971.)

完整译文另一个非常重要的研究角度，是观察美国企业资本的盈利率。它当然会随总体经济活动起伏，但并没有表现出随批发价格或生活成本普遍上升的趋势。事实上，尽管这20年存在通胀，资本盈利率反而显著下降。（其中一部分缘于企业采用了更宽松、金额更高的折旧计提，见表2-2。）我们的长期研究结论是：投资者不能指望道指公司最近五年的水平——其股票背后的有形净资产（账面价值）回报率约10%——还能高出很多。由于这些股票的市值明显高于账面价值，例如1971年中市场价值900而账面价值560，按当前市价计算的盈利收益率只有约6.25%。这种关系通常反过来用“市盈率倍数”表达，例如道指900点等于截至1971年6月过去12个月实际盈利的18倍。

译者补充（非原文）假设公司每股账面净资产100元、赚10元，账面回报率为10%；若股价160元，买方对应的盈利收益率只有10÷160＝6.25%。企业资本回报不错，不等于按任何市场价格买入都能得到同样回报。

Our figures gear in directly with the suggestion in the previous chapter* that the investor may assume an average dividend return of about 3.5% on the market value of his stocks, plus an appreciation of, say, 4% annually resulting from reinvested profits. (Note that each dollar added to book value is here assumed to increase the market price by about $1.60.)

完整译文这些数字与上一章的假设直接吻合：投资者可以预计股票市值带来约3.5%的平均股息收益，再加上留存利润再投资造成的约4%年升值。（请注意，这里假设账面价值每增加1美元，市场价格会增加约1.60美元。）

gear in directly with与……直接吻合，正好衔接appreciation增值reinvested profits再投资的利润

The reader will object that in the end our calculations make no allowance for an increase in common-stock earnings and values to result from our projected 3% annual inflation. Our justification is the absence of any sign that the inflation of a comparable amount in the past has had any direct effect on reported per-share earnings. The cold figures demonstrate that all the large gain in the earnings of the DJIA unit in the past 20 years was due to a proportionately large growth of invested capital coming from reinvested profits. If inflation had operated as a separate favorable factor, its effect would have been to increase the “value” of previously existing capital; this in turn should increase the rate of earnings on such old capital and therefore on the old and new capital combined. But nothing of the kind actually happened in the past 20 years, during which the wholesale price level has advanced nearly 40%. (Business earnings should be influenced more by wholesale prices than by “consumer prices.”) The only way that inflation can add to common stock values is by raising the rate of earnings on capital investment. On the basis of the past record this has not been the case.

完整译文读者可能会反驳：我们的计算最终没有把预计每年3%的通胀会推动普通股盈利和价值上升考虑进去。理由是，过去幅度相近的通胀没有显示出对每股报告盈利产生直接影响。冷冰冰的数字表明，道指单位过去20年的盈利大幅增加，全部来自留存利润再投资带来的投入资本同比例增长。如果通胀本身是一项独立的有利因素，它理应提高原有资本的“价值”，进而提高旧资本的盈利率，也提高新旧资本合计的盈利率。但过去20年批发价格上涨近40%，这种情况并未发生。（企业盈利受批发价格的影响应大于消费价格。）通胀只有在提高投入资本回报率时，才能增加普通股价值；历史记录并不支持它做到了这一点。

If inflation had operated as a separate favorable factor, its effect would have been to increase the “value” of previously existing capital; this in turn should increase the rate of earnings on such old capital and therefore on the old and new capital combined.

In the economic cycles of the past, good business was accompanied by a rising price level and poor business by falling prices. It was generally felt that “a little inflation” was helpful to business profits. This view is not contradicted by the history of 1950–1970, which reveals a combination of generally continued prosperity and generally rising prices. But the figures indicate that the effect of all this on the earning power of common-stock capital (“equity capital”) has been quite limited; in fact it has not even served to maintain the rate of earnings on the investment. Clearly there have been important offsetting influences which have prevented any increase in the real profitability of American corporations as a whole. Perhaps the most important of these have been (1) a rise in wage rates exceeding the gains in productivity, and (2) the need for huge amounts of new capital, thus holding down the ratio of sales to capital employed.

完整译文过去的经济周期中，景气通常伴随价格上涨，萧条则伴随价格下跌，人们普遍认为“温和通胀”有助于企业利润。1950—1970年的历史并不否定这一看法，因为这段时期大体同时出现持续繁荣和价格上涨。但数字表明，这些因素对普通股资本即“权益资本”的盈利能力影响很有限，甚至没有维持住投入资本的盈利率。显然，一些重要的抵消因素阻止了美国公司整体实际盈利能力上升。其中最重要的可能是：（1）工资增速超过生产率提升；（2）企业需要投入巨额新资本，因而压低了销售额与所用资本之比。

good business经济景气，生意兴旺contradicted被反驳，与……相矛盾earning power盈利能力equity capital股本，权益资本offsetting influences起抵消作用的因素wage rates工资水平holding down压低capital employed占用的资本

Our figures in Table 2-2 indicate that so far from inflation having benefited our corporations and their shareholders, its effect has been quite the opposite. The most striking figures in our table are those for the growth of corporate debt between 1950 and 1969. It is surprising how little attention has been paid by economists and by Wall Street to this development. The debt of corporations has expanded nearly fivefold while their profits before taxes a little more than doubled. With the great rise in interest rates during this period, it is evident that the aggregate corporate debt is now an adverse economic factor of some magnitude and a real problem for many individual enterprises. (Note that in 1950 net earnings after interest but before income tax were about 30% of corporate debt, while in 1969 they were only 13.2% of debt. The 1970 ratio must have been even less satisfactory.) In sum it appears that a significant part of the 11% being earned on corporate equities as a whole is accomplished by the use of a large amount of new debt costing 4% or less after tax credit. If our corporations had maintained the debt ratio of 1950, their earnings rate on stock capital would have fallen still lower, in spite of the inflation.

完整译文表2-2的数据表明，通胀非但没有造福公司及其股东，效果反而相反。表中最醒目的是1950—1969年公司债务的增长。经济学家和华尔街对此关注之少令人惊讶：公司债务扩大近五倍，税前利润却只增加一倍多。同期利率大幅上升，因此公司总体债务如今已成为影响不小的不利经济因素，也是许多企业的现实难题。（1950年，扣除利息后的税前净利润约等于公司债务的30%；1969年只相当于13.2%，1970年可能更差。）总的看来，公司整体约11%的股权回报中，有相当一部分是通过大量新增债务取得的，而这些债务在税收抵扣后的成本不超过4%。如果公司维持1950年的负债比例，即使存在通胀，股票资本回报率还会更低。

The stock market has considered that the public-utility enterprises have been a chief victim of inflation, being caught between a great advance in the cost of borrowed money and the difficulty of raising the rates charged under the regulatory process. But this may be the place to remark that the very fact that the unit costs of electricity, gas, and telephone services have advanced so much less than the general price index puts these companies in a strong strategic position for the future.3 They are entitled by law to charge rates sufficient for an adequate return on their invested capital, and this will probably protect their shareholders in the future as it has in the inflations of the past.

完整译文股市一直认为，公用事业企业是通胀的主要受害者，因为一方面借款成本大幅上升，另一方面受监管程序限制，收费标准又难以上调。不过，这里值得指出：电力、燃气和电话服务的单位价格涨幅远低于总体价格指数，这一事实反而使这些公司在未来占据有利的战略位置。法律允许它们收取足以使投入资本获得适当回报的费率，这在过去通胀期保护了股东，未来也很可能继续如此。

All of the above brings us back to our conclusion that the investor has no sound basis for expecting more than an average overall return of, say, 8% on a portfolio of DJIA-type common stocks purchased at the late 1971 price level. But even if these expectations should prove to be understated by a substantial amount, the case would not be made for an all-stock investment program. If there is one thing guaranteed for the future, it is that the earnings and average annual market value of a stock portfolio will not grow at the uniform rate of 4%, or any other figure. In the memorable words of the elder J. P. Morgan, “They will fluctuate.”* This means, first, that the common-stock buyer at today’s prices—or tomorrow’s—will be running a real risk of having unsatisfactory results therefrom over a period of years. It took 25 years for General Electric (and the DJIA itself) to recover the ground lost in the 1929–1932 debacle. Besides that, if the investor concentrates his portfolio on common stocks he is very likely to be led astray either by exhilarating advances or by distressing declines. This is particularly true if his reasoning is geared closely to expectations of further inflation. For then, if another bull market comes along, he will take the big rise not as a danger signal of an inevitable fall, not as a chance to cash in on his handsome profits, but rather as a vindication of the inflation hypothesis and as a reason to keep on buying common stocks no matter how high the market level nor how low the dividend return. That way lies sorrow.

完整译文以上分析把我们带回原来的结论：投资者没有充分依据期待，在1971年末价格水平买入类似道指的一组普通股，能获得高于约8%的平均总回报。即使这一预期后来被证明严重低估，也不足以证明全股票策略合理。未来如果有什么可以肯定，就是股票组合的盈利和年均市值不会按4%或任何其他固定速度均匀增长。用老J·P·摩根那句令人难忘的话说：“它们会波动。”这首先意味着，以今天或明天价格买入普通股的人，确实面临连续数年结果不佳的风险。通用电气和道指用了25年才收复1929—1932年崩盘造成的失地。此外，如果投资者把组合集中于普通股，他很可能被令人兴奋的上涨或痛苦的下跌带偏，尤其当他的逻辑紧紧围绕未来通胀预期时。若又一轮牛市来临，他会把大涨视为通胀假说得到验证，因而不论市场多高、股息收益多低都继续买，而不是把它当作下跌风险的信号或兑现丰厚利润的机会。这条路通向悲伤。

译者补充（非原文）长期平均回报并不描述实际路径。即使25年年均回报令人满意，中间也可能先下跌40%、多年不创新高；投资者若在压力下卖出，就拿不到那个长期平均数。

Alternatives to Common Stocks as Inflation Hedges

普通股以外的通胀对冲选择

The standard policy of people all over the world who mistrust their currency has been to buy and hold gold. This has been against the law for American citizens since 1935—luckily for them. In the past 35 years the price of gold in the open market has advanced from $35 per ounce to $48 in early 1972—a rise of only 35%. But during all this time the holder of gold has received no income return on his capital, and instead has incurred some annual expense for storage. Obviously, he would have done much better with his money at interest in a savings bank, in spite of the rise in the general price level.

完整译文世界各地不信任本国货币的人，传统做法是买入并持有黄金。自1935年起，美国公民这样做属于违法——从结果看，这对他们倒是幸运的。过去35年，公开市场黄金价格从每盎司35美元升至1972年初的48美元，只上涨35%；而持有者期间没有任何收入，还要每年支付储存费用。显然，即使总体物价上涨，把钱存在银行赚利息也会好得多。

The near-complete failure of gold to protect against a loss in the purchasing power of the dollar must cast grave doubt on the ability of the ordinary investor to protect himself against inflation by putting his money in “things.”* Quite a few categories of valuable objects have had striking advances in market value over the years—such as diamonds, paintings by masters, first editions of books, rare stamps and coins, etc. But in many, perhaps most, of these cases there seems to be an element of the artificial or the precarious or even the unreal about the quoted prices. Somehow it is hard to think of paying $67,500 for a U.S. silver dollar dated 1804 (but not even minted that year) as an “investment operation.”4 We acknowledge we are out of our depth in this area. Very few of our readers will find the swimming safe and easy there.

完整译文黄金几乎完全没能防止美元购买力损失，这使人们有充分理由怀疑：普通投资者能否靠把钱放进“实物”来抵御通胀。多类贵重物品的市场价值多年间确实大幅上涨，例如钻石、大师画作、初版本书籍、珍稀邮票和钱币等。但在许多甚至多数情况下，这些报价似乎含有某种人为、脆弱乃至不真实的成分。很难把花67,500美元买一枚标注1804年、实际并非当年铸造的美国银元称为“投资操作”。我们承认自己不熟悉这个领域，而很少有读者能在这片水域安全轻松地游泳。

The outright ownership of real estate has long been considered as a sound long-term investment, carrying with it a goodly amount of protection against inflation. Unfortunately, real-estate values are also subject to wide fluctuations; serious errors can be made in location, price paid, etc.; there are pitfalls in salesmen’s wiles. Finally, diversification is not practical for the investor of moderate means, except by various types of participations with others and with the special hazards that attach to new flotations—not too different from common-stock ownership. This too is not our field. All we should say to the investor is, “Be sure it’s yours before you go into it.”

完整译文直接持有房地产长期以来被视为稳健的长期投资，并能在很大程度上防御通胀。遗憾的是，房地产价值也会大幅波动；地点、买价等方面都可能犯严重错误；推销人员的花言巧语也暗藏陷阱。最后，对资金一般的投资者来说，分散持有并不现实，除非通过同他人共同参与的各种形式；新发行项目还会带来特殊风险，与持有普通股没有太大不同。这同样不是我们的专长。我们只能提醒投资者：“涉足之前，先确定它真正适合你、也真正属于你。”
