Conclusion

结论

Naturally, we return to the policy recommended in our previous chapter. Just because of the uncertainties of the future the investor cannot afford to put all his funds into one basket—neither in the bond basket, despite the unprecedentedly high returns that bonds have recently offered; nor in the stock basket, despite the prospect of continuing inflation.

完整译文自然，我们仍回到上一章建议的政策。正因为未来充满不确定，投资者不能把全部资金放在一个篮子里：即使债券近期提供了空前高的回报，也不能全放在债券篮子；即使未来可能持续通胀，也不能全放在股票篮子。

译者补充（非原文）这里的两类资产配置是一种“对预测错误的保险”，不是说股票天然抗通胀、债券天然安全。二者在不同情景下各有失效方式，组合的目的正是避免一个判断错误摧毁全部资金。

Just because of正是因为（此处 just 表强调）cannot afford to承担不起……，不能……put all his funds into one basket把所有资金放进一个篮子里unprecedentedly空前地

The more the investor depends on his portfolio and the income therefrom, the more necessary it is for him to guard against the unexpected and the disconcerting in this part of his life. It is axiomatic that the conservative investor should seek to minimize his risks. We think strongly that the risks involved in buying, say, a telephone-company bond at yields of nearly 7½% are much less than those involved in buying the DJIA at 900 (or any stock list equivalent thereto). But the possibility of large-scale inflation remains, and the investor must carry some insurance against it. There is no certainty that a stock component will insure adequately against such inflation, but it should carry more protection than the bond component.

完整译文投资者越依赖自己的投资组合及其收入，就越有必要防范生活中这一部分出现意外和令人不安的情况。保守投资者应尽量降低风险，这是不言自明的。我们坚信，以接近7.5%收益率买入电话公司债券，风险远低于在900点买入道指或等价股票组合。但大规模通胀的可能性仍在，投资者必须为此保留某种保险。股票部分能否充分对冲通胀并不确定，但它应当比债券部分提供更多保护。

It must be evident to the reader that we have no enthusiasm for common stocks at these levels (892 for the DJIA). For reasons already given we feel that the defensive investor cannot afford to be without an appreciable proportion of common stocks in his portfolio, even if we regard them as the lesser of two evils—the greater being the risks in an all-bond holding.

完整译文读者应该看得很清楚：在当前水平（道指892点），我们对普通股没有热情。但基于已经说明的理由，我们认为防御型投资者不能让组合中缺少相当比例的普通股。即使把股票视为“两害相权取其轻”，更大的那个风险仍是只持有债券。

基于前面已经给出的理由，我们认为防御型投资者的组合里不能没有相当比例的普通股，哪怕我们把股票视为两害中较轻的一害——较重的那一害，是全部持有债券的风险。

Notes · 注释（贾森·兹威格）

* By the late 1990s, this advice—which can be appropriate for a foundation or endowment with an infinitely long investment horizon—had spread to individual investors, whose life spans are finite. In the 1994 edition of his influential book, Stocks for the Long Run, finance professor Jeremy Siegel of the Wharton School recommended that “risk-taking” investors should buy on margin, borrowing more than a third of their net worth to sink 135% of their assets into stocks. Even government officials got in on the act: In February 1999, the Honorable Richard Dixon, state treasurer of Maryland, told the audience at an investment conference: “It doesn’t make any sense for anyone to have any money in a bond fund.”
中文到20世纪90年代末，这种建议——对于投资期限可以近乎无限的基金会或捐赠基金或许合适——已经扩散到寿命有限的个人投资者。沃顿商学院金融学教授杰里米·西格尔在1994年版《股市长线法宝》中建议，“愿意承担风险”的投资者应使用保证金，借入超过净资产三分之一的资金，把相当于自身资产135%的金额投入股票。连政府官员也加入其中：1999年2月，马里兰州财务主管理查德·迪克森在投资会议上说：“任何人把任何钱放在债券基金里都毫无道理。”
* This is one of Graham’s rare misjudgments. In 1973, just two years after President Richard Nixon imposed wage and price controls, inflation hit 8.7%, its highest level since the end of World War II. The decade from 1973 through 1982 was the most inflationary in modern American history, as the cost of living more than doubled.
中文这是格雷厄姆少见的误判之一。1973年，就在理查德·尼克松总统实行工资与物价管制两年后，通胀达到8.7%，创二战结束以来最高水平。1973—1982年是美国现代史上通胀最严重的十年，生活成本增加了一倍以上。
* See p. 25.
中文参见第25页。
* John Pierpont Morgan was the most powerful financier of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Because of his vast influence, he was constantly asked what the stock market would do next. Morgan developed a mercifully short and unfailingly accurate answer: “It will fluctuate.” See Jean Strouse, Morgan: American Financier (Random House, 1999), p. 11.
中文约翰·皮尔庞特·摩根是19世纪末和20世纪初最有权势的金融家。由于影响巨大，他不断被问及股市下一步会怎样。摩根形成了一个极短且永远准确的回答：“它会波动。”参见吉恩·斯特劳斯《摩根：美国金融家》（兰登书屋，1999年），第11页。
* The investment philosopher Peter L. Bernstein feels that Graham was “dead wrong” about precious metals, particularly gold, which (at least in the years after Graham wrote this chapter) has shown a robust ability to out-pace inflation. Financial adviser William Bernstein agrees, pointing out that a tiny allocation to a precious-metals fund (say, 2% of your total assets) is too small to hurt your overall returns when gold does poorly. But, when gold does well, its returns are often so spectacular—sometimes exceeding 100% in a year—that it can, all by itself, set an otherwise lackluster portfolio glittering. However, the intelligent investor avoids investing in gold directly, with its high storage and insurance costs; instead, seek out a well-diversified mutual fund specializing in the stocks of precious-metal companies and charging below 1% in annual expenses. Limit your stake to 2% of your total financial assets (or perhaps 5% if you are over the age of 65).
中文投资思想家彼得·L·伯恩斯坦认为，格雷厄姆对贵金属、尤其黄金的判断“完全错误”；至少在本章写成以后，黄金表现出强劲的跑赢通胀能力。金融顾问威廉·伯恩斯坦也同意，并指出，把总资产中很小的一部分——例如2%——配置给贵金属基金，黄金表现不佳时不足以明显伤害总体回报；而黄金表现出色时，单年回报有时超过100%，足以独自点亮原本平淡的组合。不过，聪明的投资者应避免直接持有黄金及其高昂储存、保险费用，而可寻找充分分散、专门投资贵金属公司的共同基金，年费低于1%；仓位限制在金融资产的2%（65岁以上者或可至5%）。

CHAPTER 03

一个世纪的股市历史：1972年初的股价水平

A Century of Stock-Market History

一百年市场史能告诉我们什么，又不能替我们预测什么？

Chapter 3A Century of Stock-Market History: The Level of Stock Prices in Early 1972第3章 一个世纪的股市历史：1972 年初的股价水平

精读增强副本：英文原文完整保留；每个正文块新增完整中文译文；“译者补充（非原文）”仅用于解释概念和数字，不属于格雷厄姆或茨威格原文。
本章导读投资者的股票组合只是整个股市的一个小小截面，所以格雷厄姆主张先了解股市的百年历史——尤其是价格的大起大落，以及股价与盈利、股息之间不断变化的关系。本章用图表浓缩 1871 年以来的数据：1900–1970 年分成三段——3 到 5 年一轮的规律周期、从“新时代”牛市到 1929 年崩盘再到 1949 年的低迷期、以及道指从 162 点涨到 995 点的史上最大牛市。最值得记住的是战后公众态度的大逆转：市盈率从 6.3 倍升到 22.9 倍，股息率从 7% 以上降到 3%，而同期债券利率却在上升。接着他坦率回顾自己四次对市场水平的判断：1948 年说不贵（对了），1953 年建议谨慎（过于保守），1959 年说危险（部分对），1964 年说太高（对了）。他承认这些判断未必比“坚持一贯而有节制的股票策略、别想战胜市场”这类平淡忠告更有用，并引亚里士多德的话说明：金融分析的精确度介于数学家与演说家之间。对 1972 年初（道指约 900），他的推理是：三年平均市盈率虽不算高，但股票收益率与债券收益率之比却是战后各年中最差的——1948 年股票股息率是债券利率的两倍，如今债券反而是股票的两倍多。因此他重申 1964 年的结论：从保守投资的角度看，这个水平并不吸引人，市场对不到一年前的惨痛教训视而不见更是令人不安的信号；投资者应回到 1964 年的三条方针：不借钱买股票、不提高股票比例、必要时把股票压缩到不超过一半。

The investor’s portfolio of common stocks will represent a small cross-section of that immense and formidable institution known as the stock market. Prudence suggests that he have an adequate idea of stock-market history, in terms particularly of the major fluctuations in its price level and of the varying relationships between stock prices as a whole and their earnings and dividends. With this background he may be in a position to form some worthwhile judgment of the attractiveness or dangers of the level of the market as it presents itself at different times. By a coincidence, useful statistical data on prices, earnings, and dividends go back just 100 years, to 1871. (The material is not nearly as full or dependable in the first half-period as in the second, but it will serve.) In this chapter we shall present the figures, in highly condensed form, with two objects in view. The first is to show the general manner in which stocks have made their underlying advance through the many cycles of the past century. The second is to view the picture in terms of successive ten-year averages, not only of stock prices but of earnings and dividends as well, to bring out the varying relationship between the three important factors. With this wealth of material as a background we shall pass to a consideration of the level of stock prices at the beginning of 1972.

完整译文投资者持有的普通股组合，只是股票市场这个庞大而令人生畏的机构中的一个小切片。谨慎要求他对股市历史有足够认识，尤其要了解价格水平的重大波动，以及整体股价与盈利、股息之间不断变化的关系。有了这样的背景，他才可能对不同时点的市场水平究竟具有吸引力还是暗藏危险，作出一些有价值的判断。巧合的是，有用的价格、盈利和股息统计恰好可追溯100年，始于1871年。（前50年的资料远不如后50年完整可靠，但仍可使用。）本章将高度压缩地列示这些数字，目的有二：第一，展示过去一个世纪的多轮周期中，股票整体怎样实现基础性的长期上涨；第二，用连续十年平均数同时观察股价、盈利和股息，显出三项重要因素之间变化不定的关系。以这些丰富材料为背景，我们再考察1972年初的股价水平。

The long-term history of the stock market is summarized in two tables and a chart. Table 3-1 sets forth the low and high points of nineteen bear- and bull-market cycles in the past 100 years. We have used two indexes here. The first represents a combination of an early study by the Cowles Commission going back to 1870, which has been spliced on to and continued to date in the well-known Standard & Poor’s composite index of 500 stocks. The second is the even more celebrated Dow Jones Industrial Average (the DJIA, or “the Dow”), which dates back to 1897; it contains 30 companies, of which one is American Telephone & Telegraph and the other 29 are large industrial enterprises.1

TABLE 3-1 Major Stock-Market Swings Between 1871 and 1971

完整译文表3-1　1871—1971年股市的重大涨跌。

Swings大幅波动

Chart I, presented by courtesy of Standard & Poor’s, depicts the market fluctuations of its 425-industrial-stock index from 1900 through 1970. (A corresponding chart available for the DJIA will look very much the same.) The reader will note three quite distinct patterns, each covering about a third of the 70 years. The first runs from 1900 to 1924, and shows for the most part a series of rather similar market cycles lasting from three to five years. The annual advance in this period averaged just about 3%. We move on to the “New Era” bull market, culminating in 1929, with its terrible aftermath of collapse, followed by quite irregular fluctuations until 1949. Comparing the average level of 1949 with that of 1924, we find the annual rate of advance to be a mere 1½%; hence the close of our second period found the public with no enthusiasm at all for common stocks. By the rule of opposites the time was ripe for the beginning of the greatest bull market in our history, presented in the last third of our chart. This phenomenon may have reached its culmination in December 1968 at 118 for Standard & Poor’s 425 industrials (and 108 for its 500-stock composite). As Table 3-1 shows, there were fairly important setbacks between 1949 and 1968 (especially in 1956–57 and 1961–62), but the recoveries therefrom were so rapid that they had to be denominated (in the long- accepted semantics) as recessions in a single bull market, rather than as separate market cycles. Between the low level of 162 for “the Dow” in mid-1949 and the high of 995 in early 1966, the advance had been more than sixfold in 17 years—which is at the average compounded rate of 11% per year, not counting dividends of, say, 3½% per annum. (The advance for the Standard & Poor’s composite index was somewhat greater than that of the DJIA—actually from 14 to 96.)

完整译文图1由标准普尔提供，描绘其425只工业股指数在1900—1970年间的波动。（道指的对应图形会十分相似。）读者会看到三个很不相同的模式，各覆盖约23年。第一段从1900到1924年，主要是一连串相当相似、持续三至五年的市场周期，期间年均上涨约3%。接着是最终在1929年见顶的“新时代”牛市及其惨烈崩溃，随后市场不规则波动至1949年。1949年平均水平同1924年相比，年均涨幅仅1.5%；因此第二阶段结束时，公众对普通股毫无兴趣。按照物极必反的规律，此时恰好孕育了美国史上最大牛市，即图中最后三分之一。该现象也许在1968年12月达到顶峰，当时标普425工业股指数为118，500综合指数为108。表3-1显示，1949—1968年间也有相当重要的回落，尤其1956—1957年和1961—1962年；但复苏太快，按照长期通行的说法，只能称为同一轮牛市中的调整，而不是独立周期。道指从1949年中的162点升至1966年初的995点，17年上涨逾六倍，复合年均涨幅11%，还未计每年约3.5%的股息。标普综合指数涨幅更大，从14升至96。

These 14% and better returns were documented in 1963, and later, in a much publicized study.* 2 It created a natural satisfaction on Wall Street with such fine achievements, and a quite illogical and dangerous conviction that equally marvelous results could be expected for common stocks in the future. Few people seem to have been bothered by the thought that the very extent of the rise might indicate that it had been overdone. The subsequent decline from the 1968 high to the 1970 low was 36% for the Standard & Poor’s composite (and 37% for the DJIA), the largest since the 44% suffered in 1939–1942, which had reflected the perils and uncertainties after Pearl Harbor. In the dramatic manner so characteristic of Wall Street, the low level of May 1970 was followed by a massive and speedy recovery of both averages, and the establishment of a new all-time high for the Standard & Poor’s industrials in early 1972. The annual rate of price advance between 1949 and 1970 works out at about 9% for the S & P composite (or the industrial index), using the average figures for both years. That rate of climb was, of course, much greater than for any similar period before 1950. (But in the last decade the rate of advance was much lower—5¼% for the S & P composite index and only the once familiar 3% for the DJIA.)

完整译文这些14%甚至更高的回报，在1963年及以后一项广受宣传的研究中得到记录。这使华尔街自然为辉煌成绩感到满意，却也产生一种不合逻辑且危险的信念：未来普通股仍可带来同样惊人的结果。很少有人担心，涨幅本身如此巨大可能意味着市场已经涨过头。后来标普综合指数从1968年高点跌至1970年低点，跌幅36%，道指跌37%，是1939—1942年因珍珠港事件后的危险与不确定性而下跌44%以来最大跌幅。以华尔街惯有的戏剧性方式，1970年5月低点后两大指数迅速大幅复苏，标普工业股指数在1972年初创下历史新高。按1949和1970两年的平均数计算，标普综合或工业指数价格年均上涨约9%，当然远高于1950年前任何相似时期。不过最近十年涨速已低得多：标普综合指数年均5.25%，道指则只有过去熟悉的3%。

We present a conspectus of this kind in our Table 3-2 (p. 71). It is a good deal to expect from the reader that he study all these figures with care, but for some we hope they will be interesting and instructive.

Let us comment on them as follows: The full decade figures smooth out the year-to-year fluctuations and leave a general picture of persistent growth. Only two of the nine decades after the first show a decrease in earnings and average prices (in 1891–1900 and 1931–1940), and no decade after 1900 shows a decrease in average dividends. But the rates of growth in all three categories are quite variable. In general the performance since World War II has been superior to that of earlier decades, but the advance in the 1960s was less pronounced than that of the 1950s. Today’s investor cannot tell from this record what percentage gain in earnings dividends and prices he may expect in the next ten years, but it does supply all the encouragement he needs for a consistent policy of common-stock investment.

完整译文我们作如下评论：完整十年的数据抚平了逐年波动，留下持续增长的总体图景。第一个十年之后的九个十年中，只有两个十年的盈利和平均价格下降，即1891—1900年与1931—1940年；1900年以后，没有一个十年的平均股息下降。但三类数据的增长速度差异很大。总体而言，二战后的表现优于早期年代，不过20世纪60年代的增长不如50年代显著。今天的投资者无法据此知道未来十年盈利、股息和价格会增长多少，却能从中得到坚持普通股投资政策所需的全部鼓励。

However, a point should be made here that is not disclosed in our table. The year 1970 was marked by a definite deterioration in the overall earnings posture of our corporations. The rate of profit on invested capital fell to the lowest percentage since the World War years. Equally striking is the fact that a considerable number of companies reported net losses for the year; many became “financially troubled,” and for the first time in three decades there were quite a few important bankruptcy proceedings. These facts as much as any others have prompted the statement made above* that the great boom era may have come to an end in 1969–1970.

A striking feature of Table 3-2 is the change in the price/earnings ratios since World War II.† In June 1949 the S & P composite index sold at only 6.3 times the applicable earnings of the past 12 months; in March 1961 the ratio was 22.9 times. Similarly, the dividend yield on the S & P index had fallen from over 7% in 1949 to only 3.0% in 1961, a contrast heightened by the fact that interest rates on high-grade bonds had meanwhile risen from 2.60% to 4.50%. This is certainly the most remarkable turnabout in the public’s attitude in all stock-market history.

To people of long experience and innate caution the passage from one extreme to another carried a strong warning of trouble ahead. They could not help thinking apprehensively of the 1926–1929 bull market and its tragic aftermath. But these fears have not been confirmed by the event. True, the closing price of the DJIA in 1970 was the same as it was 6½ years earlier, and the much heralded “Soaring Sixties” proved to be mainly a march up a series of high hills and then down again. But nothing has happened either to business or to stock prices that can compare with the bear market and depression of 1929–1932.

完整译文对于经验丰富且天性谨慎的人，从一个极端走到另一个极端，是对未来麻烦的强烈警告。他们不免忧虑地想到1926—1929年牛市及其悲剧后果。然而，后来事实没有证实这些恐惧。诚然，1970年末道指与六年半前处于同一水平，备受吹捧的“腾飞的60年代”主要只是翻过一连串高山后又走下来；但无论企业还是股价，都没有发生可与1929—1932年熊市和大萧条相比的灾难。

The Stock-Market Level in Early 1972

1972 年初的股市水平

With a century-long conspectus of stock, prices, earnings, and dividends before our eyes, let us try to draw some conclusions about the level of 900 for the DJIA and 100 for the S & P composite index in January 1972.

完整译文眼前已有一个世纪的股价、盈利和股息概览，现在让我们尝试判断：1972年1月道指900点、标普综合指数100点处于什么水平。

In each of our former editions we have discussed the level of the stock market at the time of writing, and endeavored to answer the question whether it was too high for conservative purchase. The reader may find it informing to review the conclusions we reached on these earlier occasions. This is not entirely an exercise in self-punishment. It will supply a sort of connecting tissue that links the various stages of the stock market in the past twenty years and also a taken-from-life picture of the difficulties facing anyone who tries to reach an informed and critical judgment of current market levels. Let us, first, reproduce the summary of the 1948, 1953, and 1959 analyses that we gave in the 1965 edition:

完整译文此前每一版中，我们都讨论写作当时的股市水平，并试图回答它是否高得不适合保守买入。回顾这些早期结论，可能会使读者有所收获；这也不完全是在自我惩罚。它既能把过去20年股市各阶段连接起来，也能用真实经历展示：任何想对当前市场水平作出有依据、带批判性判断的人，会面临怎样的困难。先重录1965年版中对1948、1953和1959年分析的总结：

In 1948 we applied conservative standards to the Dow Jones level of 180, and found no difficulty in reaching the conclusion that “it was not too high in relation to underlying values.” When we approached this problem in 1953 the average market level for that year had reached 275, a gain of over 50% in five years. We asked ourselves the same question—namely, “whether in our opinion the level of 275 for the Dow Jones Industrials was or was not too high for sound investment.” In the light of the subsequent spectacular advance, it may seem strange to have to report that it was by no means easy for us to reach a definitive conclusion as to the attractiveness of the 1953 level. We did say, positively enough, that “from the standpoint of value indications—our chief investment guide—the conclusion about 1953 stock prices must be favorable.” But we were concerned about the fact that in 1953, the averages had advanced for a longer period than in most bull markets of the past, and that its absolute level was historically high. Setting these factors against our favorable value judgment, we advised a cautious or compromise policy. As it turned out, this was not a particularly brilliant counsel. A good prophet would have foreseen that the market level was due to advance an additional 100% in the next five years. Perhaps we should add in self-defense that few if any of those whose business was stock-market forecasting—as ours was not—had any better inkling than we did of what lay ahead.

完整译文1948年，我们用保守标准考察道指180点，很容易得出结论：“相对于内在价值，它并不太高。”1953年再研究这一问题时，全年平均水平已达275点，五年上涨逾50%。我们仍问：道指275点对稳健投资而言是否过高？鉴于后来惊人的上涨，现在说起来也许奇怪：我们当时很难对1953年的吸引力下定论。我们确实明确表示，从价值迹象这一首要投资指南看，1953年股价应得到有利结论；但也担心市场已连续上涨得比过去多数牛市更久，绝对点位在历史上也很高。把这些担忧与有利的价值判断相权衡，我们建议谨慎或折中策略。结果证明，这并非特别高明的建议。优秀预言家本应看出，随后五年市场还会再涨100%。为自己辩护一句：那些以预测股市为职业的人——我们并非如此——似乎也没有谁比我们更了解前路。

At the beginning of 1959 we found the DJIA at an all-time high of 584. Our lengthy analysis made from all points of view may be summarized in the following (from page 59 of the 1959 edition): “In sum, we feel compelled to express the conclusion that the present level of stock prices is a dangerous one. It may well be perilous because prices are already far too high. But even if this is not the case the market’s momentum is such as inevitably to carry it to unjustifiable heights. Frankly, we cannot imagine a market of the future in which there will never be any serious losses, and in which, every tyro will be guaranteed a large profit on his stock purchases.”

The caution we expressed in 1959 was somewhat better justified by the sequel than was our corresponding attitude in 1954. Yet it was far from fully vindicated. The DJIA advanced to 685 in 1961; then fell a little below our 584 level (to 566) later in the year; advanced again to 735 in late 1961; and then declined in near panic to 536 in May 1962, showing a loss of 27% within the brief period of six months. At the same time there was a far more serious shrinkage in the most popular “growth stocks”—as evidenced by the striking fall of the indisputable leader, International Business Machines, from a high of 607 in December 1961 to a low of 300 in June 1962.

完整译文1959年的谨慎态度，后来得到的支持比我们1954年的谨慎更多，却远未完全证实。道指1961年升至685，随后年内跌至略低于584的566，又在1961年末升至735，接着近乎恐慌地跌至1962年5月的536，短短六个月损失27%。同时，最热门的“成长股”缩水更严重；无可争议的龙头IBM从1961年12月高点607跌至1962年6月低点300，就是醒目例证。

This period saw a complete debacle in a host of newly launched common stocks of small enterprises—the so-called hot issues—which had been offered to the public at ridiculously high prices and then had been further pushed up by needless speculation to levels little short of insane. The recovery and new ascent of common-stock prices was indeed remarkable and created a corresponding revision of Wall Street sentiment. At the low level of June 1962 predictions had appeared predominantly bearish, and after the partial recovery to the end of that year they were mixed, leaning to the skeptical side. But at the outset of 1964 the natural optimism of brokerage firms was again manifest; nearly all the forecasts were on the bullish side, and they so continued through the 1964 advance.

We then approached the task of appraising the November 1964 levels of the stock market (892 for the DJIA). After discussing it learnedly from numerous angles we reached three main conclusions. The first was that “old standards (of valuation) appear inapplicable; new standards have not yet been tested by time.” The second was that the investor “must base his policy on the existence of major uncertainties. The possibilities compass the extremes, on the one hand, of a protracted and further advance in the market’s level—say by 50%, or to 1350 for the DJIA; or, on the other hand, of a largely unheralded collapse of the same magnitude, bringing the average in the neighborhood of, say, 450" (p. 63). The third was expressed in much more definite terms. We said: “Speaking bluntly, if the 1964 price level is not too high how could we say that any price level is too high?” And the chapter closed as follows:

完整译文随后我们评估1964年11月的市场水平（道指892点）。从许多角度进行学术式讨论后，得到三个主要结论。第一，“旧的估值标准似乎已经不适用，新的标准尚未经受时间检验。”第二，投资者“必须把政策建立在重大不确定性确实存在的基础上。可能性覆盖两个极端：一边是市场长期继续上涨，比如再涨50%，使道指达到1350；另一边是一次几乎毫无预警、幅度相同的崩盘，把指数带到约450。”第三个结论说得更明确：“直截了当地说，如果1964年的价格还不算高，我们又怎能说任何价格水平算高？”该章最后写道：

WHAT COURSE TO FOLLOW

Investors should not conclude that the 1964 market level is dangerous merely because they read it in this book. They must weigh our reasoning against the contrary reasoning they will hear from most competent and experienced people on Wall Street. In the end each one must make his own decision and accept responsibility therefor. We suggest, however, that if the investor is in doubt as to which course to pursue he should choose the path of caution. The principles of investment, as set forth herein, would call for the following policy under 1964 conditions, in order of urgency:

Investors who for some time have been following a bona fide dollar-cost averaging plan can in logic elect either to continue their periodic purchases unchanged or to suspend them until they feel the market level is no longer dangerous. We should advise rather strongly against the initiation of a new dollar-averaging plan at the late 1964 levels, since many investors would not have the stamina to pursue such a scheme if the results soon after initiation should appear highly unfavorable.

This time we can say that our caution was vindicated. The DJIA advanced about 11% further, to 995, but then fell irregularly to a low of 632 in 1970, and finished that year at 839. The same kind of debacle took place in the price of “hot issues”—i.e., with declines running as much as 90%—as had happened in the 1961–62 setback. And, as pointed out in the Introduction, the whole financial picture appeared to have changed in the direction of less enthusiasm and greater doubts. A single fact may summarize the story: The DJIA closed 1970 at a level lower than six years before—the first time such a thing had happened since 1944.

完整译文这一次，可以说我们的谨慎得到验证。道指又上涨约11%至995，但随后曲折跌至1970年的632低点，并以839结束该年。热门新股也像1961—1962年回落时一样崩盘，最大跌幅达90%。正如导言所说，整体金融图景似乎已转向热情减退、疑虑增加。一个事实足以概括：1970年末道指低于六年前，这是1944年以来首次出现。

Such were our efforts to evaluate former stock-market levels. Is there anything we and our readers can learn from them? We considered the market level favorable for investment in 1948 and 1953 (but too cautiously in the latter year), “dangerous” in 1959 (at 584 for DJIA), and “too high” (at 892) in 1964. All of these judgments could be defended even today by adroit arguments. But it is doubtful if they have been as useful as our more pedestrian counsels—in favor of a consistent and controlled common-stock policy on the one hand, and discouraging endeavors to “beat the market” or to “pick the winners” on the other.

完整译文以上就是我们评估过去市场水平的努力。我们和读者能学到什么？1948年和1953年，我们认为市场适合投资（后一年过于谨慎）；1959年道指584点时称其“危险”；1964年892点时称其“过高”。即使今天，善辩的人也能替所有判断找到理由。但这些判断是否真像那些更朴素的建议一样有用，值得怀疑：一方面坚持连贯、受控的普通股政策，另一方面不要试图“战胜市场”或“挑出赢家”。

Nonetheless we think our readers may derive some benefit from a renewed consideration of the level of the stock market—this time as of late 1971—even if what we have to say will prove more interesting than practically useful, or more indicative than conclusive. There is a fine passage near the beginning of Aristotle’s Ethics that goes: “It is the mark of an educated mind to expect that amount of exactness which the nature of the particular subject admits. It is equally unreasonable to accept merely probable conclusions from a mathematician and to demand strict demonstration from an orator.” The work of a financial analyst falls somewhere in the middle between that of a mathematician and of an orator.

完整译文尽管如此，我们仍认为读者重新考虑股市水平会有一些益处——这次以1971年末为准——即使结论可能趣味大于实用、提示意义大于定论。亚里士多德《伦理学》开篇附近有一段精彩的话：“有教养的头脑，会只期待特定主题的性质所允许的那种精确程度。接受数学家仅仅可能的结论，与要求演说家作严格证明，同样不合理。”金融分析师的工作处在数学家与演说家之间。

The 3-year price/earnings ratio for the market was lower in October 1971 than at year-end 1963 and 1968. It was about the same as in 1958, but much higher than in the early years of the long bull market. This important indicator, taken by itself, could not be construed to indicate that the market was especially high in January 1972. But when the interest yield on high-grade bonds is brought into the picture, the implications become much less favorable. The reader will note from our table that the ratio of stock returns (earnings/price) to bond returns has grown worse during the entire period, so that the January 1972 figure was less favorable to stocks, by this criterion, than in any of the previous years examined. When dividend yields are compared with bond yields we find that the relationship was completely reversed between 1948 and 1972. In the early year stocks yielded twice as much as bonds; now bonds yield twice as much, and more, than stocks.

In terms of historical market swings the 1971 picture would still appear to be one of irregular recovery from the bad setback suffered in 1969–1970. In the past such recoveries have ushered in a new stage of the recurrent and persistent bull market that began in 1949. (This was the expectation of Wall Street generally during 1971.) After the terrible experience suffered by the public buyers of low-grade common-stock offerings in the 1968–1970 cycle, it is too early (in 1971) for another twirl of the new-issue merry-go-round. Hence that dependable sign of imminent danger in the market is lacking now, as it was at the 892 level of the DJIA in November 1964, considered in our previous edition. Technically, then, the outlook would appear to favor another substantial rise far beyond the 900 DJIA level before the next serious setback or collapse. But we cannot quite leave the matter there, as perhaps we should. To us, the early-1971-market’s disregard of the harrowing experiences of less than a year before is a disquieting sign. Can such heedlessness go unpunished? We think the investor must be prepared for difficult times ahead—perhaps in the form of a fairly quick replay of the 1969–1970 decline, or perhaps in the form of another bull-market fling, to be followed by a more catastrophic collapse.3

完整译文从历史市场波动看，1971年的图景仍像是从1969—1970年严重下跌中不规则复苏。过去，这种复苏会开启1949年开始的反复而持续的牛市新阶段。（1971年华尔街普遍如此预期。）公众在1968—1970年周期买入低等级新股后遭遇惨痛经历，到1971年再启动一轮新股旋转木马还太早。因此，那个可靠的临近危险信号当时并未出现，就像上一版考察的1964年11月道指892点时也没有。纯从技术走势看，前景似乎支持道指在下一次严重回落或崩盘前远远涨过900点。但我们无法就此打住，尽管理应如此。1971年初市场竟无视不到一年前的痛苦经历，在我们看来令人不安。这种健忘会不受惩罚吗？我们认为投资者必须为艰难时期作准备：可能很快重演1969—1970年的下跌，也可能先再来一轮牛市狂欢，随后发生更具灾难性的崩盘。

CHAPTER 04

一般投资组合策略：防御型投资者

General Portfolio Policy: The Defensive Investor

防御型投资者怎样在股票与债券之间建立可执行的纪律？

Chapter 4General Portfolio Policy: The Defensive Investor第4章 一般投资组合策略：防御型投资者

精读增强副本：英文原文完整保留；每个正文块新增完整中文译文；“译者补充（非原文）”仅用于解释概念和数字，不属于格雷厄姆或茨威格原文。
本章导读本章为防御型投资者制定总体的投资组合策略。格雷厄姆先纠正一个流行观念：回报率并不与所冒的风险成正比，而应取决于投资者愿意并能够投入多少“聪明的努力”——省心的被动投资者只能拿最低回报，勤奋精明的进取型投资者才能拿最高回报。接着是股债配置的核心问题：股票仓位始终保持在 25%–75% 之间，标准是对半开。传统上应在熊市低价时加仓、在高位时减仓，但这与人性背道而驰，连共同基金也做不到；既然市场已脱离旧有边界，作者在 1972 年初既不建议股票超过一半，也难以建议远低于一半，于是提出机械的 50–50 方案：股票涨到 55% 就卖出十一分之一转入债券，跌到 45% 则反向操作。耶鲁大学放弃 35% 公式的例子说明大牛市对公式化投资的“致命”影响，但 50–50 的价值恰恰在于简单、方向正确，并能阻止投资者在高位越陷越深。债券部分逐一讨论应税与免税、长期与短期的选择，以及储蓄债券、政府直接和间接债务、市政债券、公司债券各自的特点；他劝普通投资者远离高收益的低等级债券，并用美国煤气电力公司债券被低价赎回的例子揭露赎回条款“正面我赢、反面你输”的不公，建议牺牲一点收益换取不可赎回的保障。最后两节论证：不可转换的优先股在形式上先天不良，只能在廉价时买，且按税法更适合公司而非个人持有；收益债券本是比优先股更合理的形式，却因铁路重组的历史包袱被冷落——华尔街的习惯与偏见往往比新条件更顽固。

The basic characteristics of an investment portfolio are usually determined by the position and characteristics of the owner or owners. At one extreme we have had savings banks, life-insurance companies, and so-called legal trust funds. A generation ago their investments were limited by law in many states to high-grade bonds and, in some cases, high-grade preferred stocks. At the other extreme we have the well-to-do and experienced businessman, who will include any kind of bond or stock in his security list provided he considers it an attractive purchase.

完整译文投资组合的基本特征，通常取决于所有者的处境和特点。一个极端是储蓄银行、寿险公司和所谓法定信托基金。一代人以前，许多州的法律把它们的投资限制在高等级债券，有时也允许高等级优先股。另一个极端是富裕且经验丰富的商人：只要认为买价有吸引力，他会把任何种类的债券或股票纳入证券清单。

position处境，状况（此处指财务状况，不是“头寸”）At one extreme在一个极端legal trust funds法定信托基金（受法律约束只能持有指定证券的信托）high-grade高等级的，优质的preferred stocks优先股well-to-do富裕的provided只要，如果（连词）

It has been an old and sound principle that those who cannot afford to take risks should be content with a relatively low return on their invested funds. From this there has developed the general notion that the rate of return which the investor should aim for is more or less proportionate to the degree of risk he is ready to run. Our view is different. The rate of return sought should be dependent, rather, on the amount of intelligent effort the investor is willing and able to bring to bear on his task. The minimum return goes to our passive investor, who wants both safety and freedom from concern. The maximum return would be realized by the alert and enterprising investor who exercises maximum intelligence and skill. In 1965 we added: “In many cases there may be less real risk associated with buying a ‘bargain issue’ offering the chance of a large profit than with a conventional bond purchase yielding about 4½%.” This statement had more truth in it than we ourselves suspected, since in subsequent years even the best long-term bonds lost a substantial part of their market value because of the rise in interest rates.

完整译文一个古老而稳健的原则是：承受不起风险的人，应满足于投资资金获得相对较低的回报。由此发展出一种普遍观念：投资者追求的回报率，应大致与他愿意承担的风险成正比。我们的看法不同。目标回报率更应取决于投资者愿意并能够投入多少理性努力。既想安全又不愿操心的被动投资者，只能得到最低回报；保持警觉、积极进取并最大限度运用智慧和技巧的人，才可能获得最高回报。1965年我们补充说：“很多时候，购买可能带来较大利润的廉价证券，真实风险反而低于购买收益率约4.5%的常规债券。”后来即使最优质长期债券也因利率上升而大幅贬值，说明这句话比我们当时意识到的更正确。

译者补充（非原文）作者区分的是“需要承担的风险”和“通过研究发现的机会”。高回报不必来自盲目承担更高风险，也可能来自投入更多能力，以低价买入有充分价值支撑的资产；但若没有相应能力，积极操作只会增加错误。

sound稳健的，合理的be content with满足于proportionate to与……成比例ready to run愿意承担（run a risk 冒风险）bring to bear on投入到，施加于freedom from concern无忧无虑，省心enterprising进取型的（本书中与 defensive 相对）bargain issue廉价股，便宜的证券（issue 本书中指证券）yielding收益率为suspected料想到

The rate of return sought should be dependent, rather, on the amount of intelligent effort the investor is willing and able to bring to bear on his task.

The Basic Problem of Bond-Stock Allocation

债券与股票配置的基本问题

We have already outlined in briefest form the portfolio policy of the defensive investor.* He should divide his funds between high-grade bonds and high-grade common stocks.

完整译文我们已经以最简略的形式概述防御型投资者的组合政策：资金应分配在高等级债券和高等级普通股之间。

outlined概述in briefest form以最简略的形式

We have suggested as a fundamental guiding rule that the investor should never have less than 25% or more than 75% of his funds in common stocks, with a consequent inverse range of between 75% and 25% in bonds. There is an implication here that the standard division should be an equal one, or 50–50, between the two major investment mediums. According to tradition the sound reason for increasing the percentage in common stocks would be the appearance of the “bargain price” levels created in a protracted bear market. Conversely, sound procedure would call for reducing the common-stock component below 50% when in the judgment of the investor the market level has become dangerously high.

完整译文我们建议一项基本指导规则：普通股占比永远不低于25%、也不高于75%；债券占比相应反向处于75%至25%之间。这隐含着，两类主要投资工具的标准配置应为各50%。按照传统，只有长期熊市造成“廉价水平”时，才有充分理由提高普通股比例；反过来，当投资者判断市场已高得危险，合理做法是把股票比例降到50%以下。

These copybook maxims have always been easy to enunciate and always difficult to follow—because they go against that very human nature which produces that excesses of bull and bear markets. It is almost a contradiction in terms to suggest as a feasible policy for the average stockowner that he lighten his holdings when the market advances beyond a certain point and add to them after a corresponding decline. It is because the average man operates, and apparently must operate, in opposite fashion that we have had the great advances and collapses of the past; and—this writer believes—we are likely to have them in the future.

完整译文这些教科书式格言从来都容易说、难以做，因为它们与制造牛熊市极端行情的人性正面冲突。建议普通股持有人在市场涨过某一点后减仓、相应下跌后加仓，几乎像在提出一项自相矛盾、难以执行的政策。正因为普通人实际采取、似乎也注定采取相反做法，过去才会出现大涨与崩盘；本书作者相信，未来也仍会如此。

If the division between investment and speculative operations were as clear now as once it was, we might be able to envisage investors as a shrewd, experienced group who sell out to the heedless, hapless speculators at high prices and buy back from them at depressed levels. This picture may have had some verisimilitude in bygone days, but it is hard to identify it with financial developments since 1949. There is no indication that such professional operations as those of the mutual funds have been conducted in this fashion. The percentage of the portfolio held in equities by the two major types of funds—“balanced” and “common-stock”—has changed very little from year to year. Their selling activities have been largely related to endeavors to switch from less to more promising holdings.

If, as we have long believed, the stock market has lost contact with its old bounds, and if new ones have not yet been established, then we can give the investor no reliable rules by which to reduce his common-stock holdings toward the 25% minimum and rebuild them later to the 75% maximum. We can urge that in general the investor should not have more than one-half in equities unless he has strong confidence in the soundness of his stock position and is sure that he could view a market decline of the 1969–70 type with equanimity. It is hard for us to see how such strong confidence can be justified at the levels existing in early 1972. Thus we would counsel against a greater than 50% apportionment to common stocks at this time. But, for complementary reasons, it is almost equally difficult to advise a reduction of the figure well below 50%, unless the investor is disquieted in his own mind about the current market level, and will be satisfied also to limit his participation in any further rise to, say, 25% of his total funds.

完整译文如果像我们长期相信的那样，股市已脱离旧有边界，而新边界尚未建立，我们就无法给投资者一套可靠规则，告诉他何时把股票降到25%，又何时重建至75%。一般而言，除非投资者强烈相信自己的股票仓位稳健，并确定自己能平静看待1969—1970年那种下跌，否则股票不应超过一半。在1972年初的市场水平上，我们很难看出这种强烈信心有何充分依据，因此不建议股票超过50%。但出于相反而互补的理由，也几乎同样难建议把股票大幅降至50%以下；除非投资者内心确实对当前市场不安，而且愿意把参与未来上涨的资金限制为总额约25%。

We are thus led to put forward for most of our readers what may appear to be an oversimplified 50–50 formula. Under this plan the guiding rule is to maintain as nearly as practicable an equal division between bond and stock holdings. When changes in the market level have raised the common-stock component to, say, 55%, the balance would be restored by a sale of one-eleventh of the stock portfolio and the transfer of the proceeds to bonds. Conversely, a fall in the common-stock proportion to 45% would call for the use of one-eleventh of the bond fund to buy additional equities.

完整译文于是，我们为多数读者提出一个可能显得过于简单的50∶50公式。规则是尽可能维持债券与股票各占一半。市场上涨使股票比例达到55%时，就卖出股票组合的十一分之一，把所得转入债券，从而恢复平衡。反过来，股票比例跌到45%时，就动用债券资金的十一分之一增购股票。

Yale University followed a somewhat similar plan for a number of years after 1937, but it was geared around a 35% “normal holding” in common stocks. In the early 1950s, however, Yale seems to have given up its once famous formula, and in 1969 held 61% of its portfolio in equities (including some convertibles). (At that time the endowment funds of 71 such institutions, totaling $7.6 billion, held 60.3% in common stocks.) The Yale example illustrates the almost lethal effect of the great market advance upon the once popular formula approach to investment. Nonetheless we are convinced that our 50–50 version of this approach makes good sense for the defensive investor. It is extremely simple; it aims unquestionably in the right direction; it gives the follower the feeling that he is at least making some moves in response to market developments; most important of all, it will restrain him from being drawn more and more heavily into common stocks as the market rises to more and more dangerous heights.

完整译文耶鲁大学从1937年后曾多年采用类似计划，只是以普通股35%作为“正常持仓”。不过到20世纪50年代初，耶鲁似乎放弃了这套曾经著名的公式；1969年其组合中股票占61%（包括部分可转换证券）。（当时71家机构合计76亿美元的捐赠基金，普通股平均占60.3%。）耶鲁的例子说明，大牛市对一度流行的公式化投资方法产生了近乎致命的影响。尽管如此，我们仍确信，50∶50版本对防御型投资者很合理：它极其简单，方向无疑正确，让执行者感觉自己至少在对市场变化作出行动；最重要的是，它会阻止投资者随市场涨到越来越危险的高度而不断加重股票仓位。

While our proposed 50–50 division is undoubtedly the simplest “all-purpose program” devisable, it may not turn out to be the best in terms of results achieved. (Of course, no approach, mechanical or otherwise, can be advanced with any assurance that it will work out better than another.) The much larger income return now offered by good bonds than by representative stocks is a potent argument for favoring the bond component. The investor’s choice between 50% or a lower figure in stocks may well rest mainly on his own temperament and attitude. If he can act as a cold-blooded weigher of the odds, he would be likely to favor the low 25% stock component at this time, with the idea of waiting until the DJIA dividend yield was, say, two-thirds of the bond yield before he would establish his median 50–50 division between bonds and stocks. Starting from 900 for the DJIA and dividends of $36 on the unit, this would require either a fall in taxable bond yields from 7½% to about 5.5% without any change in the present return on leading stocks, or a fall in the DJIA to as low as 660 if there is no reduction in bond yields and no increase in dividends. A combination of intermediate changes could produce the same “buying point.” A program of that kind is not especially complicated; the hard part is to adopt it and to stick to it not to mention the possibility that it may turn out to have been much too conservative.

完整译文我们提出的50∶50无疑是最简单的“通用方案”，但按最终结果看未必最好。（当然，任何机械或非机械方法都无法保证优于其他方法。）当时优质债券的收入回报远高于代表性股票，这是偏重债券的有力理由。选择股票占50%还是更低，可能主要取决于投资者的性格和态度。如果他能冷静权衡概率，当时很可能偏向股票只占25%，并等待道指股息收益率达到债券收益率的约三分之二，再建立居中的50∶50配置。从道指900点、每单位股息36美元出发，这要求：若主要股票收益不变，应税债券收益率从7.5%降到约5.5%；或者若债券收益率不降、股息不增，道指跌至约660点。多项中间变化的组合也能形成同一“买点”。这套方案并不特别复杂；难的是开始执行并坚持，更别说它最终还可能被证明过于保守。

The Bond Component

债券部分

The choice of issues in the bond component of the investor’s portfolio will turn about two main questions: Should he buy taxable or tax-free bonds, and should he buy shorter- or longer-term maturities? The tax decision should be mainly a matter of arithmetic, turning on the difference in yields as compared with the investor’s tax bracket. In January 1972 the choice in 20-year maturities was between obtaining, say, 7½% on “grade Aa” corporate bonds and 5.3% on prime tax-free issues. (The term “municipals” is generally applied to all species of tax-exempt bonds, including state obligations.) There was thus for this maturity a loss in income of some 30% in passing from the corporate to the municipal field. Hence if the investor was in a maximum tax bracket higher than 30% he would have a net saving after taxes by choosing the municipal bonds; the opposite, if his maximum tax was less than 30%. A single person starts paying a 30% rate when his income after deductions passes $10,000; for a married couple the rate applies when combined taxable income passes $20,000. It is evident that a large proportion of individual investors would obtain a higher return after taxes from good municipals than from good corporate bonds.

完整译文组合中债券品种的选择围绕两个主要问题：买应税债券还是免税债券？买较短期限还是较长期限？税收选择主要是算术问题，要把收益率差异与投资者税率档位相比较。1972年1月，20年期债券可以在约7.5%的Aa级公司债与5.3%的优质免税债之间选择。（“市政债券”通常泛指全部免税债券，包括州政府债务。）从公司债转向市政债，收入约减少30%。因此，若投资者最高边际税率高于30%，选择市政债后的税后收入更高；若税率低于30%，结论相反。单身者扣除后收入超过1万美元、夫妻合并应税收入超过2万美元时开始适用30%税率。显然，相当多个人投资者从优质市政债获得的税后回报高于优质公司债。

译者补充（非原文）比较应看税后收益。若公司债收益7.5%、边际税率40%，税后只有4.5%；免税市政债5.3%反而更高。若税率20%，公司债税后6%，则应税债更有利。税法和信用风险会变，数字不能直接照搬到今天。

The choice of longer versus shorter maturities involves quite a different question, viz.: Does the investor want to assure himself against a decline in the price of his bonds, but at the cost of (1) a lower annual yield and (2) loss of the possibility of an appreciable gain in principal value? We think it best to discuss this question in Chapter 8, The Investor and Market Fluctuations.

For a period of many years in the past the only sensible bond purchases for individuals were the U.S. savings issues. Their safety was—and is—unquestioned; they gave a higher return than other bond investments of first quality; they had a money-back option and other privileges which added greatly to their attractiveness. In our earlier editions we had an entire chapter entitled “U.S. Savings Bonds: A Boon to Investors.”

As we shall point out, U.S. savings bonds still possess certain unique merits that make them a suitable purchase by any individual investor. For the man of modest capital—with, say, not more than $10,000 to put into bonds—we think they are still the easiest and the best choice. But those with larger funds may find other mediums more desirable.

1. U.S. SAVINGS BONDS, SERIES E AND SERIES H. We shall first summarize their important provisions, and then discuss briefly the numerous advantages of these unique, attractive, and exceedingly convenient investments. The Series H bonds pay interest semi-annually, as do other bonds. The rate is 4.29% for the first year, and then a flat 5.10% for the next nine years to maturity. Interest on the Series E bonds is not paid out, but accrues to the holder through increase in redemption value. The bonds are sold at 75% of their face value, and mature at 100% in 5 years 10 months after purchase. If held to maturity the yield works out at 5%, compounded semi-annually. If redeemed earlier, the yield moves up from a minimum of 4.01% in the first year to an average of 5.20% in the next 45/6 years.

完整译文1．美国E系列与H系列储蓄债券。先概述重要条款，再简要讨论这些独特、诱人且极为便利的投资工具的多项优势。H系列像其他债券一样每半年付息，第一年利率4.29%，随后九年至到期固定为5.10%。E系列不把利息付出，而是通过赎回价值增加为持有人累积。债券按面值75%出售，买入后5年10个月以100%面值到期；持有至到期，按半年复利计算收益率为5%。若提前赎回，收益率从第一年的最低4.01%，逐步提高到以后4又5/6年平均5.20%。

Interest on the bonds is subject to Federal income tax, but is exempt from state income tax. However, Federal income tax on the Series E bonds may be paid at the holder’s option either annually as the interest accrues (through higher redemption value), or not until the bond is actually disposed of.

完整译文债券利息须缴联邦所得税，但免征州所得税。不过E系列利息的联邦所得税可由持有人选择：随赎回价值逐年增加而每年缴纳，或等实际处置债券时再缴。

Owners of Series E bonds may cash them in at any time (shortly after purchase) at their current redemption value. Holders of Series H bonds have similar rights to cash them in at par value (cost). Series E bonds are exchangeable for Series H bonds, with certain tax advantages. Bonds lost, destroyed, or stolen may be replaced without cost. There are limitations on annual purchases, but liberal provisions for co-ownership by family members make it possible for most investors to buy as many as they can afford. Comment: There is no other investment that combines (1) absolute assurance of principal and interest payments, (2) the right to demand full “money back” at any time, and (3) guarantee of at least a 5% interest rate for at least ten years. Holders of the earlier issues of Series E bonds have had the right to extend their bonds at maturity, and thus to continue to accumulate annual values at successively higher rates. The deferral of income-tax payments over these long periods has been of great dollar advantage; we calculate it has increased the effective net-after-tax rate received by as much as a third in typical cases. Conversely, the right to cash in the bonds at cost price or better has given the purchasers in former years of low interest rates complete protection against the shrinkage in principal value that befell many bond investors; otherwise stated, it gave them the possibility of benefiting from the rise in interest rates by switching their low-interest holdings into very-high-coupon issues on an even-money basis.

完整译文E系列持有人在买入后不久起，随时可按当前赎回价值兑现；H系列持有人也有类似权利，可按面值即成本兑现。E系列可换成H系列，并享有一定税收优势。遗失、毁坏或被盗的债券可免费补发。虽然每年购买有限额，但家庭成员共同持有的宽松规定，使多数投资者几乎能按承受能力购买。评论：没有其他投资同时具备：（1）本金和利息支付的绝对保障；（2）随时要求全额“退款”的权利；（3）至少十年、至少5%利率的保证。早期E系列持有人到期时可延长债券，继续按逐步提高的利率累积年度价值。长期递延所得税带来巨大金额优势；按我们计算，典型情况下可使实际税后净收益率提高多达三分之一。反过来，按成本或更高价格兑现的权利，使过去低利率年份的买家完全避开许多债券投资者遭受的本金缩水；换句话说，他们可以按等额本金把低息持仓换成高票息证券，从利率上升中受益。

2. OTHER UNITED STATES BONDS. A profusion of these issues exists, covering a wide variety of coupon rates and maturity dates. All of them are completely safe with respect to payment of interest and principal. They are subject to Federal income taxes but free from state income tax. In late 1971 the long-term issues—over ten years—showed an average yield of 6.09%, intermediate issues (three to five years) returned 6.35%, and short issues returned 6.03%.

It is interesting to note also that in many cases the indirect obligations of the U.S. government yield appreciably more than its direct obligations of the same maturity. As we write, an offering appears of 7.05% of “Certificates Fully Guaranteed by the Secretary of Transportation of the Department of Transportation of the United States.” The yield was fully 1% more than that on direct obligations of the U.S., maturing the same year (1986). The certificates were actually issued in the name of the Trustees of the Penn Central Transportation Co., but they were sold on the basis of a statement by the U.S. Attorney General that the guarantee “brings into being a general obligation of the United States, backed by its full faith and credit.” Quite a number of indirect obligations of this sort have been assumed by the U.S. government in the past, and all of them have been scrupulously honored.

完整译文另一个有趣现象是：许多情况下，美国政府的间接债务收益率明显高于同期限直接债务。写作时市场正发行一种收益率7.05%的“由美国运输部部长全额担保的凭证”，比同在1986年到期的美国直接债务高整整1个百分点。凭证实际以宾夕法尼亚中央运输公司受托人名义发行，但销售依据是美国司法部长声明：该担保“形成由美国充分信用支持的一般债务”。过去美国政府承担过不少这类间接债务，并全都严格履约。

The reader may wonder why all this hocus-pocus, involving an apparently “personal guarantee” by our Secretary of Transportation, and a higher cost to the taxpayer in the end. The chief reason for the indirection has been the debt limit imposed on government borrowing by the Congress. Apparently guarantees by the government are not regarded as debts—a semantic windfall for shrewder investors. Perhaps the chief impact of this situation has been the creation of tax-free Housing Authority bonds, enjoying the equivalent of a U.S. guarantee, and virtually the only tax-exempt issues that are equivalent to government bonds. Another type of government-backed issues is the recently created New Community Debentures, offered to yield 7.60% in September 1971.

3. STATE AND MUNICIPAL BONDS. These enjoy exemption from Federal income tax. They are also ordinarily free of income tax in the state of issue but not elsewhere. They are either direct obligations of a state or subdivision, or “revenue bonds” dependent for interest payments on receipts from a toll road, bridge, building lease, etc. Not all tax-free bonds are strongly enough protected to justify their purchase by a defensive investor. He may be guided in his selection by the rating given to each issue by Moody’s or Standard & Poor’s. One of three highest ratings by both services—Aaa (AAA), Aa (AA), or A—should constitute a sufficient indication of adequate safety. The yield on these bonds will vary both with the quality and the maturity, with the shorter maturities giving the lower return. In late 1971 the issues represented in Standard & Poor’s municipal bond index averaged AA in quality rating, 20 years in maturity, and 5.78% in yield. A typical offering of Vineland, N.J., bonds, rated AA for A and gave a yield of only 3% on the one-year maturity, rising to 5.8% to the 1995 and 1996 maturities.1

完整译文3．州政府与市政债券。这些债券免征联邦所得税，通常在发行州也免州所得税，但在其他州不一定免税。它们要么是州或下属行政单位的直接债务，要么是依靠收费公路、桥梁、建筑租金等收入付息的“收益债券”。并非所有免税债券的保障都强到足以让防御型投资者购买。他可参考穆迪或标准普尔评级；两家机构给出的最高三档之一——Aaa（AAA）、Aa（AA）或A——应足以表明安全性适当。收益率同时随质量与期限变化，期限越短通常回报越低。1971年末，标普市政债指数的平均评级为AA、期限20年、收益率5.78%。新泽西州瓦恩兰一批评级AA的典型债券，一年期收益率仅3%，1995和1996年到期品种则升至5.8%。

Those in high income-tax brackets can undoubtedly obtain a better net yield from good tax-free issues than from taxable ones. For others the early 1972 range of taxable yield would seem to be from 5.00% on U.S. savings bonds, with their special options, to about 7½% on high-grade corporate issues.

Higher-Yielding Bond Investments

完整译文收益率更高的债券投资。

Higher-Yielding收益率更高的

By sacrificing quality an investor can obtain a higher income return from his bonds. Long experience has demonstrated that the ordinary investor is wiser to keep away from such high-yield bonds. While, taken as a whole, they may work out somewhat better in terms of overall return than the first-quality issues, they expose the owner to too many individual risks of untoward developments, ranging from disquieting price declines to actual default. (It is true that bargain opportunities occur fairly often in lower-grade bonds, but these require special study and skill to exploit successfully.)*

完整译文牺牲质量，投资者可以从债券获得更高收入。长期经验表明，普通投资者远离这类高收益债更明智。从整体看，它们的总回报也许略优于最高等级债券，却让持有人暴露于过多单项不利风险，从令人不安的价格下跌直到真正违约。（较低等级债券确实时常出现廉价机会，但成功利用需要专门研究和技巧。）

译者补充（非原文）高收益是对风险的补偿，不是额外赠品。若一篮子债券票息多2个百分点，但一次违约造成40%损失，单只债券的一次失败就会吞掉多年利差；普通投资者若不能分散和分析，账面高收益可能并未带来更高总回报。

Perhaps we should add here that the limits imposed by Congress on direct bond issues of the United States have produced at least two sorts of “bargain opportunities” for investors in the purchase of government-backed obligations. One is provided by the tax-exempt “New Housing” issues, and the other by the recently created (taxable) “New Community debentures.” An offering of New Housing issues in July 1971 yielded as high as 5.8%, free from both Federal and state taxes, while an issue of (taxable) New Community debentures sold in September 1971 yielded 7.60%. Both obligations have the “full faith and credit” of the United States government behind them and hence are safe without question. And—on a net basis—they yield considerably more than ordinary United States bonds.†

以储蓄存款代替债券

An investor may now obtain as high an interest rate from a savings deposit in a commercial or savings bank (or from a bank certificate of deposit) as he can from a first-grade bond of short maturity. The interest rate on bank savings accounts may be lowered in the future, but under present conditions they are a suitable substitute for short-term bond investment by the individual.

Call Provisions

赎回条款

In previous editions we had a fairly long discussion of this aspect of bond financing, because it involved a serious but little noticed injustice to the investor. In the typical case bonds were callable fairly soon after issuance, and at modest premiums—say 5%—above the issue price. This meant that during a period of wide fluctuations in the underlying interest rates the investor had to bear the full brunt of unfavorable changes and was deprived of all but a meager participation in favorable ones.

完整译文此前版本用相当篇幅讨论债券赎回条款，因为其中存在一种严重却很少被注意的、对投资者不公的安排。典型债券发行后不久，公司就可按只比发行价高一点的价格——例如溢价5%——赎回。利率大幅波动时，这意味着投资者必须完全承受不利变化，却只能得到有利变化带来的少量收益。

bond financing债券融资little noticed很少被注意到的callable可赎回的（发行人有权提前按约定价格买回）modest premiums不高的溢价bear the full brunt of首当其冲地承受deprived of被剥夺all but除了……以外的一切meager微薄的

This meant that during a period of wide fluctuations in the underlying interest rates the investor had to bear the full brunt of unfavorable changes and was deprived of all but a meager participation in favorable ones.

这意味着，在基础利率大幅波动的时期，投资者不得不承受不利变化的全部冲击，而对有利的变化却几乎分享不到什么好处。

that 从句里先是一个长状语 during a period of … interest rates，然后才是主语 the investor 和两个并列谓语 had to bear … and was deprived of …。all but a meager participation 字面是“除了微薄的参与之外的一切（都被剥夺）”，即只能沾到一点点好处；ones 代指 changes。

EXAMPLE: Our standard example has been the issue of American Gas & Electric 100-year 5% debentures, sold to the public at 101 in 1928. Four years later, under near-panic conditions, the price of these good bonds fell to 62½, yielding 8%. By 1946, in a great reversal, bonds of this type could be sold to yield only 3%, and the 5% issue should have been quoted at close to 160. But at that point the company took advantage of the call provision and redeemed the issue at a mere 106.

完整译文例子：我们常用美国煤气电力公司1928年面向公众按101发行的百年期5%债券。四年后，在近乎恐慌的环境下，这些优质债券跌至62.5，收益率达到8%。到1946年形势彻底反转，同类债券只能提供3%收益，因此这只5%债券理论报价应接近160。但公司此时利用赎回条款，仅按106把债券赎回。

The call feature in these bond contracts was a thinly disguised instance of “heads I win, tails you lose.” At long last, the bond-buying institutions refused to accept this unfair arrangement; in recent years most long-term high-coupon issues have been protected against redemption for ten years or more after issuance. This still limits their possible price rise, but not inequitably.

In practical terms, we advise the investor in long-term issues to sacrifice a small amount of yield to obtain the assurance of noncallability—say for 20 or 25 years. Similarly, there is an advantage in buying a low-coupon bond* at a discount rather than a high-coupon bond selling at about par and callable in a few years. For the discount—e.g., of a 3½% bond at 63½%, yielding 7.85%—carries full protection against adverse call action.

完整译文从实务看，我们建议长期债券投资者牺牲少量收益率，以换取例如20或25年不得赎回的保障。类似地，以折价买入低票息债券，比按面值附近买入几年后即可赎回的高票息债更有利。例如票息3.5%的债券以面值63.5%买入，收益率7.85%；这部分折价能完全保护持有人免受不利赎回。

Straight—i.e., Nonconvertible—Preferred Stocks

纯粹的（即不可转换的）优先股

Certain general observations should be made here on the subject of preferred stocks. Really good preferred stocks can and do exist, but they are good in spite of their investment form, which is an inherently bad one. The typical preferred shareholder is dependent for his safety on the ability and desire of the company to pay dividends on its common stock. Once the common dividends are omitted, or even in danger, his own position becomes precarious, for the directors are under no obligation to continue paying him unless they also pay on the common. On the other hand, the typical preferred stock carries no share in the company’s profits beyond the fixed dividend rate. Thus the preferred holder lacks both the legal claim of the bondholder (or creditor) and the profit possibilities of a common shareholder (or partner).

完整译文谈到不可转换优先股，需要作几点一般观察。真正优质的优先股确实存在，但它们之所以优质，是克服了这种证券形式天生的缺陷。典型优先股股东的安全，取决于公司是否有能力也有意愿给普通股支付股息。一旦普通股停息，甚至只是面临停息危险，优先股处境就变得不稳，因为董事在不给普通股分红时，通常也没有义务继续给优先股分红。另一方面，典型优先股除固定股息外，不能分享公司更多利润。因此，优先股持有人既没有债券持有人即债权人的法律请求权，也没有普通股股东即合伙人的盈利上行空间。

译者补充（非原文）优先股处在尴尬中间地带：公司困难时，它不像债券那样有刚性付息和到期还本权；公司繁荣时，它的收益又通常被固定股息封顶。因此只有发行人极强或价格折让足够大时，风险回报才可能合理。

These weaknesses in the legal position of preferred stocks tend to come to the fore recurrently in periods of depression. Only a small percentage of all preferred issues are so strongly entrenched as to maintain an unquestioned investment status through all vicissitudes. Experience teaches that the time to buy preferred stocks is when their price is unduly depressed by temporary adversity. (At such times they may be well suited to the aggressive investor but too unconventional for the defensive investor.)

完整译文优先股法律地位的这些弱点，会在经济萧条期反复暴露。全部优先股中，只有很少一部分保障足够牢固，能经受各种变化仍保持无可疑问的投资级地位。经验表明，购买优先股的时机，是暂时不利局面使价格过度低迷之时。（此时它们可能适合积极型投资者，却对防御型投资者过于非常规。）

In other words, they should be bought on a bargain basis or not at all. We shall refer later to convertible and similarly privileged issues, which carry some special possibilities of profits. These are not ordinarily selected for a conservative portfolio.

完整译文换句话说，只能按廉价条件买入，否则就根本不要买。后文会讨论可转换证券及带类似权利的品种，它们具备一些特殊获利可能；通常并不适合保守组合。

Another peculiarity in the general position of preferred stocks deserves mention. They have a much better tax status for corporation buyers than for individual investors. Corporations pay income tax on only 15% of the income they receive in dividends, but on the full amount of their ordinary interest income. Since the 1972 corporate rate is 48%, this means that $100 received as preferred-stock dividends is taxed only $7.20, whereas $100 received as bond interest is taxed $48. On the other hand, individual investors pay exactly the same tax on preferred-stock investments as on bond interest, except for a recent minor exemption. Thus, in strict logic, all investment-grade preferred stocks should be bought by corporations, just as all tax-exempt bonds should be bought by investors who pay income tax.*

完整译文优先股整体地位还有一个特点值得说明：公司买家享有的税收待遇远优于个人。公司收到的股息收入只有15%需缴所得税，普通利息收入却全部计税。1972年公司税率48%，意味着收到100美元优先股股息只缴税7.20美元，而100美元债券利息要缴48美元。个人投资者除近来一项很小的免税额外，优先股与债券利息适用完全相同的税。因此严格说来，所有投资级优先股都应由公司购买，就像所有免税债券都应由需要缴所得税的投资者购买。

peculiarity特殊之处deserves mention值得一提tax status税收待遇corporate rate公司所得税税率exemption免税额in strict logic严格按逻辑来说investment-grade投资级的

Security Forms

证券形式

The bond form and the preferred-stock form, as hitherto discussed, are well-understood and relatively simple matters. A bondholder is entitled to receive fixed interest and payment of principal on a definite date. The owner of a preferred stock is entitled to a fixed dividend, and no more, which must be paid before any common dividend. His principal value does not come due on any specified date. (The dividend may be cumulative or noncumulative. He may or may not have a vote.)

完整译文前文讨论的债券和优先股形式容易理解，也相对简单。债券持有人有权在明确日期收取固定利息并收回本金；优先股持有人有权获得固定股息，不多也不少，而且必须先于任何普通股股息支付。其本金价值没有指定到期日。（股息可累积也可不累积；持有人可能有投票权，也可能没有。）

hitherto迄今为止，到目前为止is entitled to有权获得come due到期cumulative累积的（未付股息累积到以后补发）have a vote有投票权

The above describes the standard provisions and, no doubt, the majority of bond and preferred issues, but there are innumerable departures from these forms. The best-known types are convertible and similar issues, and income bonds. In the latter type, interest does not have to be paid unless it is earned by the company. (Unpaid interest may accumulate as a charge against future earnings, but the period is often limited to three years.)

完整译文以上是标准条款，无疑适用于多数债券和优先股，但偏离标准的形式不计其数。最著名的是可转换及类似证券，还有收益债券。对后一种债券，除非公司赚到足够利润，否则不必付息。（未付利息可以累积并从未来盈利中支付，但累积期通常限制为三年。）

innumerable无数的departures from偏离，变体income bonds收益债券（只在公司有盈利时才付息的债券）a charge against对……的扣减，从……中优先扣除

Income bonds should be used by corporations much more extensively than they are. Their avoidance apparently arises from a mere accident of economic history—namely, that they were first employed in quantity in connection with railroad reorganizations, and hence they have been associated from the start with financial weakness and poor investment status. But the form itself has several practical advantages, especially in comparison with and in substitution for the numerous (convertible) preferred-stock issues of recent years. Chief of these is the deductibility of the interest paid from the company’s taxable income, which in effect cuts the cost of that form of capital in half. From the investor’s standpoint it is probably best for him in most cases that he should have (1) an unconditional right to receive interest payments when they are earned by the company, and (2) a right to other forms of protection than bankruptcy proceedings if interest is not earned and paid. The terms of income bonds can be tailored to the advantage of both the borrower and the lender in the manner best suited to both. (Conversion privileges can, of course, be included.) The acceptance by everybody of the inherently weak preferred-stock form and the rejection of the stronger income-bond form is a fascinating illustration of the way in which traditional institutions and habits often tend to persist on Wall Street despite new conditions calling for a fresh point of view. With every new wave of optimism or pessimism, we are ready to abandon history and time-tested principles, but we cling tenaciously and unquestioningly to our prejudices.

完整译文公司本应比现在更广泛地使用收益债券。它之所以被回避，显然只是经济史的偶然：这种工具最初大规模用于铁路重组，从一开始就与财务薄弱和较差投资地位联系在一起。但形式本身具有多项实际优点，尤其可与近年来大量可转换优先股比较并取而代之。最大优点是已付利息可从公司应税收入中扣除，实际上把这种资本的成本减半。从投资者角度，多数情况下最好拥有：（1）公司赚到相应利润时，无条件收取利息的权利；（2）若没有赚到或支付利息，除申请破产外还享有其他保护。收益债券条款可按最适合双方的方式定制，使借款人和出借人都受益，当然也可加入转换权。所有人都接受天生薄弱的优先股形式，却排斥更强的收益债券，生动说明：即使新环境要求更新观点，华尔街的传统制度和习惯仍会延续。每当新一轮乐观或悲观来临，我们随时准备抛弃历史和久经考验的原则，却顽固而不假思索地抱住偏见。

译者补充（非原文）收益债券的利息与“赚到利润”挂钩，降低公司在低谷期的刚性负担；但对投资者而言，必须明确“赚到”的会计定义、未付利息能否累积，以及不付息时有哪些保护。形式名称本身不能代替条款审查。

* While Graham’s logic remains valid, the numbers have changed. Corporations can currently deduct 70% of the income they receive from dividends, and the standard corporate tax rate is 35%. Thus, a corporation would pay roughly $24.50 in tax on $100 in dividends from preferred stock versus $35 in tax on $100 in interest income. Individuals pay the same rate of income tax on dividend income that they do on interest income, so preferred stock offers them no tax advantage.

CHAPTER 05

防御型投资者与普通股

The Defensive Investor and Common Stocks

不追求频繁判断时，普通股该用哪些标准筛选？

Chapter 5The Defensive Investor and Common Stocks第5章 防御型投资者与普通股

精读增强副本：英文原文完整保留；每个正文块新增完整中文译文；“译者补充（非原文）”仅用于解释概念和数字，不属于格雷厄姆或茨威格原文。
本章导读本章回答一个具体问题：防御型投资者应当怎样持有普通股。格雷厄姆先回顾 1949 年他为股票辩护的两条理由——抵御通货膨胀对购买力的侵蚀、长期回报高于债券——随即提醒：只要买价过高，这两个优势就会化为乌有，1929 年之后市场花了 25 年才爬回原来的高点，而 1957 年以来股票的股息率已经低于债券利率。即便对 1971 年末 900 点的道指毫无热情，他仍坚持防御型投资者不能没有相当比例的股票，这是“两害相权取其轻”。接着他提出四条选股规则：适度分散（10 到 30 只）；只买大型、知名、财务稳健的公司；有长期连续派息的记录；买价不超过过去七年平均利润的 25 倍、最近一年利润的 20 倍。第四条实际上把几乎所有成长股都排除在外，他用 IBM 和德州仪器的暴涨暴跌说明理由：成长股的高价里含有沉重的投机成分，普通人不能指望靠它们创造奇迹。随后几节讨论组合的定期检视（只托付给信誉最好的机构）、定期定额投资法，以及寡妇、医生、年轻人三个处境不同的投资者，结论是：该买什么证券，取决于投资者的知识、经验和性格，而不是财力。章末两条附注最值得记住：一是“风险”只应指真正实现的亏损、公司状况恶化或买价过高，暂时的市价波动不算风险；二是“财务稳健”可以量化为普通股账面价值至少占总资本的一半（铁路和公用事业为 30%），“大型”大致相当于 5000 万美元的资产或营业额。

Investment Merits of Common Stocks

普通股的投资价值

In our first edition (1949) we found it necessary at this point to insert a long exposition of the case for including a substantial common-stock component in all investment portfolios.* Common stocks were generally viewed as highly speculative and therefore unsafe; they had declined fairly substantially from the high levels of 1946, but instead of attracting investors to them because of their reasonable prices, this fall had had the opposite effect of undermining confidence in equity securities. We have commented on the converse situation that has developed in the ensuing 20 years, whereby the big advance in stock prices made them appear safe and profitable investments at record high levels which might actually carry with them a considerable degree of risk.†

完整译文在第一版（1949年）中，我们认为有必要在这里用较长篇幅说明：为什么所有投资组合都应包含相当比例的普通股。当时，普通股普遍被视为高度投机、因而不安全；它们已经从1946年的高位明显下跌，但这次下跌并未因价格变得合理而吸引投资者，反而削弱了人们对权益证券的信心。我们也评论过随后20年出现的相反情况：股价大涨，使股票在创纪录高位看起来既安全又有利可图，而这些高位其实可能伴随相当大的风险。

We have commented on the converse situation that has developed in the ensuing 20 years, whereby the big advance in stock prices made them appear safe and profitable investments at record high levels which might actually carry with them a considerable degree of risk.

我们已经评论过随后 20 年里出现的相反局面：股价大幅上涨，使股票在创纪录的高位上看起来像是安全而有利可图的投资，而这种高位实际上可能带有相当大的风险。

whereby 引导定语从句修饰 situation，意为“通过这种方式”；made them appear … investments 是 make + 宾语 + 动词原形的结构；句末的 which 指代 record high levels，而不是 investments。

The argument we made for common stocks in 1949 turned on two main points. The first was that they had offered a considerable degree of protection against the erosion of the investor’s dollar caused by inflation, whereas bonds offered no protection at all. The second advantage of common stocks lay in their higher average return to investors over the years. This was produced both by an average dividend income exceeding the yield on good bonds and by an underlying tendency for market value to increase over the years in consequence of the reinvestment of undistributed profits.

完整译文我们在1949年提出的支持普通股的论点主要基于两点。第一，它们为投资者提供了相当程度的保护，使其免受通货膨胀导致的美元贬值影响，而债券则完全无法提供这种保护。普通股的第二个优势在于其多年来为投资者带来的更高平均回报。这既源于其平均股息收入超过优质债券的收益率，也源于未分配利润再投资导致市值随年份增长的趋势。

While these two advantages have been of major importance—and have given common stocks a far better record than bonds over the long-term past—we have consistently warned that these benefits could be lost by the stock buyer if he pays too high a price for his shares. This was clearly the case in 1929, and it took 25 years for the market level to climb back to the ledge from which it had abysmally fallen in 1929–1932.* Since 1957 common stocks have once again, through their high prices, lost their traditional advantage in dividend yield over bond interest rates.† It remains to be seen whether the inflation factor and the economic-growth factor will make up in the future for this significantly adverse development.

It should be evident to the reader that we have no enthusiasm for common stocks in general at the 900 DJIA level of late 1971. For reasons already given* we feel that the defensive investor cannot afford to be without an appreciable proportion of common stocks in his portfolio, even if he must regard them as the lesser of two evils—the greater being the risks attached to an all-bond holding.

4. The investor should impose some limit on the price he will pay for an issue in relation to its average earnings over, say, the past seven years. We suggest that this limit be set at 25 times such average earnings, and not more than 20 times those of the last twelve-month period. But such a restriction would eliminate nearly all the strongest and most popular companies from the portfolio. In particular, it would ban virtually the entire category of “growth stocks,” which have for some years past been the favorites of both speculators and institutional investors. Growth Stocks and the Defensive Investor

成长股与防御型投资者

The term “growth stock” is applied to one which has increased its per-share earnings in the past at well above the rate for common stocks generally and is expected to continue to do so in the future. (Some authorities would say that a true growth stock should be expected at least to double its per-share earnings in ten years—i.e., to increase them at a compounded annual rate of over 7.1%.)† Obviously stocks of this kind are attractive to buy and to own, provided the price paid is not excessive. The problem lies there, of course, since growth stocks have long sold at high prices in relation to current earnings and at much higher multiples of their average profits over a past period. This has introduced a speculative element of considerable weight in the growth-stock picture and has made successful operations in this field a far from simple matter.

完整译文“成长股”一词用于指代那些过去每股收益增长率远高于普通股平均水平，且预计未来将继续如此增长的股票。（一些权威人士认为，真正的成长股应至少能在十年内使其每股收益翻倍——即复合年增长率超过7.1%。）† 显然，只要支付的价格不过高，这类股票就值得购买和持有。问题恰恰在于此，因为成长股长期以来相对于当前收益的售价就很高，相对于过去一段时间的平均利润的倍数则更高。这给成长股图景引入了相当重的投机成分，使得在该领域的成功操作绝非易事。

The leading growth issue has long been International Business Machines, and it has brought phenomenal rewards to those who bought it years ago and held on to it tenaciously. But we have already pointed out* that this “best of common stocks” actually lost 50% of its market price in a six-months’ decline during 1961–62 and nearly the same percentage in 1969–70. Other growth stocks have been even more vulnerable to adverse developments; in some cases not only has the price fallen back but the earnings as well, thus causing a double discomfiture to those who owned them. A good second example for our purpose is Texas Instruments, which in six years rose from 5 to 256, without paying a dividend, while its earnings increased from 40 cents to $3.91 per share. (Note that the price advanced five times as fast as the profits; this is characteristic of popular common stocks.) But two years later the earnings had dropped off by nearly 50% and the price by four-fifths, to 49.†

完整译文国际商业机器公司（IBM）长期以来一直是领先的成长股，它为那些多年前买入并坚韧持有的投资者带来了惊人的回报。但我们已经指出*，这只“最好的普通股”实际上在1961-62年的六个月下跌中损失了50%的市值，在1969-70年也损失了几乎相同的比例。其他成长股对不利发展的脆弱性甚至更大；在某些情况下，不仅价格回落，收益也下降了，从而给持有者造成了双重打击。我们目的的一个很好的第二个例子是德州仪器（Texas Instruments），它在六年内从5美元涨到256美元，期间未支付股息，而其收益从每股40美分增加到3.91美元。（注意，价格增长速度是利润的五倍；这是热门普通股的典型特征。）但两年后，收益下降了近50%，价格下跌了五分之四，跌至49美元。†

The reader will understand from these instances why we regard growth stocks as a whole as too uncertain and risky a vehicle for the defensive investor. Of course, wonders can be accomplished with the right individual selections, bought at the right levels, and later sold after a huge rise and before the probable decline. But the average investor can no more expect to accomplish this than to find money growing on trees. In contrast we think that the group of large companies that are relatively unpopular, and therefore obtainable at reasonable earnings multipliers,* offers a sound if unspectacular area of choice by the general public. We shall illustrate this idea in our chapter on portfolio selection.

完整译文读者从这些例子中可以理解，为什么我们将成长股整体视为对防御型投资者来说过于不确定和冒险的工具。当然，通过正确的个股选择，在合适的价位买入，并在大幅上涨后、可能下跌前卖出，确实可以创造奇迹。但普通投资者指望做到这一点，无异于指望树上长钱。相比之下，我们认为，那些相对不受欢迎的大型公司群体，因此可以在合理的收益倍数*获得，为公众提供了一个稳健（尽管不引人注目）的选择领域。我们将在投资组合选择章节中阐述这一理念。

It is now standard practice to submit all security lists for periodic inspection in order to see whether their quality can be improved. This, of course, is a major part of the service provided for clients by investment counselors. Nearly all brokerage houses are ready to make corresponding suggestions, without special fee, in return for the commission business involved. Presumably our defensive investor should obtain—at least once a year—the same kind of advice regarding changes in his portfolio as he sought when his funds were first committed. Since he will have little expertness of his own on which to rely, it is essential that he entrust himself only to firms of the highest reputation; otherwise he may easily fall into incompetent or unscrupulous hands. It is important, in any case, that at every such consultation he make clear to his adviser that he wishes to adhere closely to the four rules of common-stock selection given earlier in this chapter. Incidentally, if his list has been competently selected in the first instance, there should be no need for frequent or numerous changes.†

完整译文我们的防御型投资者应该至少每年获得一次关于其投资组合变更的建议，就像他在资金首次投入时寻求的那样。由于他几乎没有自己的专业知识可以依赖，因此至关重要的是他只委托给声誉最高的公司；否则，他很容易落入无能或不道德的人手中。在任何情况下，重要的是，在每次这样的咨询中，他都要向顾问明确表示，他希望严格遵守本章前面给出的普通股选择的四条规则。顺便说一句，如果他的清单最初是经过精心挑选的，那么就不需要频繁或大量的变更。†

Dollar-Cost Averaging

定期定额投资法

The New York Stock Exchange has put considerable effort into popularizing its “monthly purchase plan,” under which an investor devotes the same dollar amount each month to buying one or more common stocks. This is an application of a special type of “formula investment” known as dollar-cost averaging. During the predominantly rising-market experience since 1949 the results from such a procedure were certain to be highly satisfactory, especially since they prevented the practitioner from concentrating his buying at the wrong times.

完整译文纽约证券交易所投入大量精力推广“月度购买计划”：投资者每月用相同金额购买一只或多只普通股。这是“公式化投资”的一种特殊形式，称为“定期定额投资”。1949年以来市场以上涨为主，这种方法的结果自然十分令人满意，尤其因为它阻止执行者在错误时点集中买入。

译者补充（非原文）定期定额减少的是择时依赖，不是资产本身的风险。每月投入1000元，价格10元时买100份、5元时买200份，低价自动买得更多；但若所买公司永久恶化，持续投入仍会扩大损失，所以它不能替代分散和质量筛选。

monthly purchase plan月度购买计划devotes投入formula investment公式化投资dollar-cost averaging定期定额投资法（美元成本平均法）predominantly主要地practitioner实践者

In Lucile Tomlinson’s comprehensive study of formula investment plans,1 the author presented a calculation of the results of dollar-cost averaging in the group of stocks making up the Dow Jones industrial index. Tests were made covering 23 ten-year purchase periods, the first ending in 1929, the last in 1952. Every test showed a profit either at the close of the purchase period or within five years thereafter. The average indicated profit at the end of the 23 buying periods was 21.5%, exclusive of dividends received. Needless to say, in some instances there was a substantial temporary depreciation at market value. Miss Tomlinson ends her discussion of this ultrasimple investment formula with the striking sentence: “No one has yet discovered any other formula for investing which can be used with so much confidence of ultimate success, regardless of what may happen to security prices, as Dollar Cost Averaging.”

完整译文露西尔·汤姆林森对公式化投资计划作过全面研究，并计算了对道指成分股实行定期定额投资的结果。测试覆盖23个为期十年的买入期，第一个结束于1929年，最后一个结束于1952年。每次测试都在买入期结束时或随后五年内实现盈利。23个买入期结束时，平均账面利润为21.5%，尚未计入收到的股息。当然，有些时期的市场价值曾暂时大幅缩水。汤姆林森在讨论这套极其简单的公式时，以一句醒目的话作结：“迄今还没有人发现另一种投资公式，能像定期定额投资一样，不论证券价格怎样变化，都可以如此有把握地期待最终成功。”

It may be objected that dollar-cost averaging, while sound in principle, is rather unrealistic in practice, because few people are so situated that they can have available for common-stock investment the same amount of money each year for, say, 20 years. It seems to me that this apparent objection has lost much of its force in recent years. Common stocks are becoming generally accepted as a necessary component of a sound savings-investment program. Thus, systematic and uniform purchases of common stocks may present no more psychological and financial difficulties than similar continuous payments for United States savings bonds and for life insurance—to which they should be complementary. The monthly amount may be small, but the results after 20 or more years can be impressive and important to the saver.

完整译文有人可能会反对说，尽管定期定额投资法在原则上是合理的，但在实践中却相当不切实际，因为很少有人能处于这样一种境地，即每年都能拿出相同数额的资金用于普通股投资，比如说持续20年。在我看来，这种看似合理的反对意见在近年来已失去了大部分效力。普通股正逐渐被普遍接受为健全储蓄投资计划的一个必要组成部分。因此，系统且均匀地购买普通股，在心理和财务上带来的困难，并不比定期连续购买美国储蓄债券和人寿保险更大——它们本应互为补充。每月的金额可能很小，但20年或更长时间后的结果可能令人印象深刻，对储蓄者而言也至关重要。

The Investor’s Personal Situation

投资者的个人状况

At the beginning of this chapter we referred briefly to the position of the individual portfolio owner. Let us return to this matter, in the light of our subsequent discussion of general policy. To what extent should the type of securities selected by the investor vary with his circumstances? As concrete examples representing widely different conditions, we shall take: (1) a widow left $200,000 with which to support herself and her children; (2) a successful doctor in mid-career, with savings of $100,000 and yearly accretions of $10,000; and (3) a young man earning $200 per week and saving $1,000 a year.*

For the widow, the problem of living on her income is a very difficult one. On the other hand the need for conservatism in her investments is paramount. A division of her fund about equally between United States bonds and first-grade common stocks is a compromise between these objectives and corresponds to our general prescription for the defensive investor. (The stock component may be placed as high as 75% if the investor is psychologically prepared for this decision, and if she can be almost certain she is not buying at too high a level. Assuredly this is not the case in early 1972.)

完整译文对这位寡妇来说，依靠投资收入维持生活十分困难；另一方面，她的投资又必须把保守放在首位。把资金大致平均分配在美国债券与一流普通股之间，是兼顾这两个目标的折中，也符合我们对防御型投资者的一般建议。（股票比例可高至75%，前提是她在心理上已为此作好准备，而且几乎能够确定买价并不过高；1972年初显然不具备后一条件。）

译者补充（非原文）本例中的“寡妇”是原书年代用来代表依靠资产收入生活、承受亏损能力较低的人，并非说投资策略由性别决定。现代读者应把判断变量换成支出刚性、收入来源、投资期限和承受波动的能力。

We do not preclude the possibility that the widow may qualify as an enterprising investor, in which case her objectives and methods will be quite different. The one thing the widow must not do is to take speculative chances in order to “make some extra income.” By this we mean trying for profits or high income without the necessary equipment to warrant full confidence in overall success. It would be far better for her to draw $2,000 per year out of her principal, in order to make both ends meet, than to risk half of it in poorly grounded, and therefore speculative, ventures.

完整译文我们不排除这位寡妇具备积极型投资者的条件；若是如此，她的目标和方法会完全不同。但她绝不能为了“多赚一点收入”而冒险投机，也就是在缺乏足够知识和能力、无法对总体成功抱有充分信心时，仍去追求利润或高收益。为了收支平衡，她宁可每年从本金取出2,000美元，也不要把一半本金投入缺少可靠依据、因而属于投机的项目。

The prosperous doctor has none of the widow’s pressures and compulsions, yet we believe that his choices are pretty much the same. Is he willing to take a serious interest in the business of investment? If he lacks the impulse or the flair, he will do best to accept the easy role of the defensive investor. The division of his portfolio should then be no different from that of the “typical” widow, and there would be the same area of personal choice in fixing the size of the stock component. The annual savings should be invested in about the same proportions as the total fund.

完整译文这位富裕的医生没有寡妇面对的压力和迫切需要，但我们认为他的选择大致相同。他是否愿意认真投入投资这门事情？若缺乏这种意愿或天赋，最好接受防御型投资者的轻松角色。此时其组合配置应与“典型”寡妇无异，股票部分的比例也有同样的个人选择空间；每年新增储蓄应大致按总资金的同一比例配置。

The average doctor may be more likely than the average widow to elect to become an enterprising investor, and he is perhaps more likely to succeed in the undertaking. He has one important handicap, however—the fact that he has less time available to give to his investment education and to the administration of his funds. In fact, medical men have been notoriously unsuccessful in their security dealings. The reason for this is that they usually have an ample confidence in their own intelligence and a strong desire to make a good return on their money, without the realization that to do so successfully requires both considerable attention to the matter and something of a professional approach to security values.

完整译文普通医生比寡妇更有可能选择成为进取型投资者，并且他或许更有可能取得成功。然而，他有一个重要的劣势——他没有足够的时间用于投资教育和资金管理。事实上，医务人员在证券交易中历来表现不佳。原因在于，他们通常对自己的智力充满信心，并强烈希望获得良好的投资回报，却未能意识到要成功做到这一点，既需要投入大量精力，也需要对证券价值采取某种专业态度。

Finally, the young man who saves $1,000 a year—and expects to do better gradually—finds himself with the same choices, though for still different reasons. Some of his savings should go automatically into Series E bonds. The balance is so modest that it seems hardly worthwhile for him to undergo a tough educational and temperamental discipline in order to qualify as an aggressive investor. Thus a simple resort to our standard program for the defensive investor would be at once the easiest and the most logical policy.
