Let us not ignore human nature at this point. Finance has a fascination for many bright young people with limited means. They would like to be both intelligent and enterprising in the placement of their savings, even though investment income is much less important to them than their salaries. This attitude is all to the good. There is a great advantage for the young capitalist to begin his financial education and experience early. If he is going to operate as an aggressive investor he is certain to make some mistakes and to take some losses. Youth can stand these disappointments and profit by them. We urge the beginner in security buying not to waste his efforts and his money in trying to beat the market. Let him study security values and initially test out his judgment on price versus value with the smallest possible sums.

完整译文在此我们不可忽视人性。金融对许多聪明但资金有限的年轻人具有吸引力。他们希望在储蓄配置上既明智又进取，尽管投资收入对他们的重要性远不如工资。这种态度完全是有益的。年轻的资本家尽早开始金融教育和积累经验具有巨大优势。如果他打算作为进取型投资者运作，他肯定会犯一些错误并遭受一些损失。年轻人能够承受这些失望并从中获益。我们敦促证券购买初学者不要浪费精力和金钱去试图战胜市场。让他研究证券价值，并用尽可能小的金额初步测试自己对价格与价值的判断。

Thus we return to the statement, made at the outset, that the kind of securities to be purchased and the rate of return to be sought depend not on the investor’s financial resources but on his financial equipment in terms of knowledge, experience, and temperament.

完整译文这样，我们又回到本章开头的说法：投资者应购买什么证券、追求怎样的回报率，并不取决于他的财力，而取决于他在知识、经验和性格方面具备怎样的投资素养。

Note on the Concept of “Risk”

关于“风险”概念的说明

It is conventional to speak of good bonds as less risky than good preferred stocks and of the latter as less risky than good common stocks. From this was derived the popular prejudice against common stocks because they are not “safe,” which was demonstrated in the Federal Reserve Board’s survey of 1948. We should like to point out that the words “risk” and “safety” are applied to securities in two different senses, with a resultant confusion in thought.

完整译文通常人们会说，优质债券的风险低于优质优先股，而优质优先股的风险又低于优质普通股。由此产生了对普通股的普遍偏见，认为它们不“安全”；美联储委员会1948年的调查就反映了这一点。我们要指出，“风险”和“安全”用于证券时具有两种不同含义，因而造成了思维混乱。

译者补充（非原文）本节区分报价波动与永久损失。优质分散组合从100万元暂时跌到75万元而企业价值未坏，属于波动；若公司资不抵债、盈利能力永久受损，或投资者因杠杆被迫在75万元卖出，才转化为真实损失。

conventional约定俗成的，惯常的preferred stocks优先股prejudice偏见Federal Reserve Board美联储理事会senses含义（此处不是“感觉”）resultant由此产生的

A bond is clearly proved unsafe when it defaults its interest or principal payments. Similarly, if a preferred stock or even a common stock is bought with the expectation that a given rate of dividend will be continued, then a reduction or passing of the dividend means that it has proved unsafe. It is also true that an investment contains a risk if there is a fair possibility that the holder may have to sell at a time when the price is well below cost.

完整译文债券若不能支付利息或本金，显然就证明它不安全。类似地，如果买入优先股甚至普通股时，预期某一股息率会持续，而后来股息减少或取消，也说明它不安全。若持有人很可能被迫在价格远低于成本时卖出，这项投资同样含有风险。

defaults违约，未能支付interest or principal payments利息或本金的支付a given rate of dividend某一既定的股息率passing of the dividend停发股息（pass a dividend 是行话）a fair possibility相当大的可能well below cost远低于成本

Nevertheless, the idea of risk is often extended to apply to a possible decline in the price of a security, even though the decline may be of a cyclical and temporary nature and even though the holder is unlikely to be forced to sell at such times. These chances are present in all securities, other than United States savings bonds, and to a greater extent in the general run of common stocks than in senior issues as a class. But we believe that what is here involved is not a true risk in the useful sense of the term. The man who holds a mortgage on a building might have to take a substantial loss if he were forced to sell it at an unfavorable time. That element is not taken into account in judging the safety or risk of ordinary real-estate mortgages, the only criterion being the certainty of punctual payments. In the same way the risk attached to an ordinary commercial business is measured by the chance of its losing money, not by what would happen if the owner were forced to sell.

完整译文然而，人们常把风险概念扩大到证券价格可能下跌，即使这种下跌只是周期性、暂时性的，而且持有人不大可能在那时被迫卖出。除美国储蓄债券外，所有证券都有这种可能；整体而言，普通股比优先受偿证券更明显。但我们认为，这并不是“风险”一词在有用意义上的真正风险。持有某栋建筑抵押贷款的人，若被迫在不利时点卖出，也可能遭受重大损失；但判断普通房地产抵押贷款是否安全时，并不考虑这种因素，唯一标准是能否按时收到款项。同样，衡量普通商业经营的风险，是看它是否可能亏钱，而不是看业主若被迫出售会发生什么。

That element is not taken into account in judging the safety or risk of ordinary real-estate mortgages, the only criterion being the certainty of punctual payments.

在判断普通房地产抵押贷款是否安全、有无风险时，这一因素并不被考虑在内，唯一的标准是能否确定按时收到还款。

逗号后的 the only criterion being … 是独立主格结构（名词 + 现在分词），相当于一个补充说明的分句 and the only criterion is …。

In Chapter 8 we shall set forth our conviction that the bona fide investor does not lose money merely because the market price of his holdings declines; hence the fact that a decline may occur does not mean that he is running a true risk of loss. If a group of well-selected common-stock investments shows a satisfactory overall return, as measured through a fair number of years, then this group investment has proved to be “safe.” During that period its market value is bound to fluctuate, and as likely as not it will sell for a while under the buyer’s cost. If that fact makes the investment “risky,” it would then have to be called both risky and safe at the same time. This confusion may be avoided if we apply the concept of risk solely to a loss of value which either is realized through actual sale, or is caused by a significant deterioration in the company’s position—or, more frequently perhaps, is the result of the payment of an excessive price in relation to the intrinsic worth of the security.2

完整译文第8章将说明我们的信念：真正的投资者不会仅因持仓市价下跌就已经亏钱；因此，价格可能下跌并不意味着他正承受真正的损失风险。如果一组精心选择的普通股在相当多年里取得令人满意的总体回报，这组投资就证明是“安全”的。期间市值必然波动，也很可能一度低于买入成本。若仅凭这一点就说它“有风险”，那它便同时既有风险又安全。要避免这种混乱，可以只把“风险”用于以下价值损失：通过实际卖出而实现的损失；公司状况严重恶化造成的损失；或者更常见地，相对于证券内在价值支付过高价格所造成的损失。

译者补充（非原文）“股价下跌不等于已经亏钱”并不意味着跌幅可以忽略。需要重新检查：企业基本面是否恶化、买入估值是否原本过高、持有期和现金需求是否改变。只有这些事实未变，暂时下跌才主要是市场报价问题。

set forth阐述conviction坚定的看法bona fide真正的（拉丁语）is bound to必然会as likely as not很可能，多半solely仅仅realized实现的（账面亏损通过实际卖出变成真实亏损）deterioration恶化intrinsic worth内在价值

Many common stocks do involve risks of such deterioration. But it is our thesis that a properly executed group investment in common stocks does not carry any substantial risk of this sort and that therefore it should not be termed “risky” merely because of the element of price fluctuation. But such risk is present if there is danger that the price may prove to have been clearly too high by intrinsic-value standards—even if any subsequent severe market decline may be recouped many years later.

完整译文许多普通股确实存在公司状况恶化的风险。但我们的主张是：执行得当、成组持有的普通股投资，不会带有这种重大的实质风险，因此不能仅仅因为价格会波动就称其“有风险”。不过，如果按内在价值标准衡量，买价可能明显过高，那么风险确实存在——即使后来发生的严重市场下跌在许多年后最终被收复。

thesis论点properly executed执行得当的group investment组合式投资termed被称为may prove to have been事后可能证明曾经是recouped挽回，收复

Note on the Category of “Large, Prominent, and Conservatively Financed Corporations”

关于“大型、知名、财务稳健的公司”这一类别的说明

The quoted phrase in our caption was used earlier in the chapter to describe the kind of common stocks to which defensive investors should limit their purchases—provided also that they had paid continuous dividends for a considerable number of years. A criterion based on adjectives is always ambiguous. Where is the dividing line for size, for prominence, and for conservatism of financial structure? On the last point we can suggest a specific standard that, though arbitrary, is in line with accepted thinking. An industrial company’s finances are not conservative unless the common stock (at book value) represents at least half of the total capitalization, including all bank debt.3 For a railroad or public utility the figure should be at least 30%.

完整译文本节标题中的那组词，前面曾用来说明防御型投资者应把购买范围限制在哪类普通股上；此外，这些公司还应有相当多年连续分红的记录。以形容词作标准总有歧义：规模多大算“大型”？怎样算“知名”？财务结构多保守才够？最后一点可以给出一个虽带任意性、却符合公认思路的具体标准：工业公司的普通股账面价值若不足总资本（包括全部银行债务）的一半，其财务就不能算保守。铁路或公用事业公司的这一比例至少应为30%。

caption标题（此处指本节的小标题）dividing line分界线arbitrary武断的，随意划定的in line with符合accepted thinking公认的看法at book value按账面价值total capitalization总资本（股本加长期债务）public utility公用事业公司

The words “large” and “prominent” carry the notion of substantial size combined with a leading position in the industry. Such companies are often referred to as “primary”; all other common stocks are then called “secondary,” except that growth stocks are ordinarily placed in a separate class by those who buy them as such. To supply an element of concreteness here, let us suggest that to be “large” in present-day terms a company should have $50 million of assets or do $50 million of business.* Again to be “prominent” a company should rank among the first quarter or first third in size within its industry group.

完整译文“大型”和“知名”意味着规模可观，并在行业中处于领先地位。这类公司常被称为“一线公司”；其他普通股则称为“二线股”，不过购买成长股的人通常把成长股另列一类。为使标准更具体，我们建议：按当时水平，一家公司若要算“大型”，资产或营业额应达到5000万美元；若要算“知名”，其规模应位居所属行业前四分之一或前三分之一。

carry the notion of含有……的意思primary一线的，主要的secondary二线的，次要的as such作为这样的东西（即当作成长股来买）concreteness具体性in present-day terms按当今的标准do $50 million of business做到 5000 万美元的营业额rank among位居……之列

It would be foolish, however, to insist upon such arbitrary criteria. They are offered merely as guides to those who may ask for guidance. But any rule which the investor may set for himself and which does no violence to the common-sense meanings of “large” and “prominent” should be acceptable. By the very nature of the case there must be a large group of companies that some will and others will not include among those suitable for defensive investment. There is no harm in such diversity of opinion and action. In fact, it has a salutary effect upon stock-market conditions, because it permits a gradual differentiation or transition between the categories of primary and secondary stock issues.

完整译文不过，死守这些任意标准是愚蠢的。它们只是给需要指引的人提供参考。投资者为自己制定的任何规则，只要不违背“大型”和“知名”的常识含义，都可以接受。事情的性质决定了，必然有一大批公司会被一些人纳入防御型投资范围，却被另一些人排除。这种意见和行动的差异没有坏处；事实上，它对股市状况有益，因为它让一线与二线股票之间形成渐进的区分和过渡。

criteria标准（criterion 的复数）does no violence to不违背common-sense meanings常识意义By the very nature从……的本质来看（by the very nature of the case：就事情本身的性质而言）salutary有益的differentiation区分

By the very nature of the case there must be a large group of companies that some will and others will not include among those suitable for defensive investment.

从事情的本质来看，必然有一大批公司，有些人会把它们列入适合防御型投资的名单，另一些人则不会。

that 是定语从句的关系代词，充当 include 的宾语；从句里有两个并列主语 some will 和 others will not，共用一个动词 include，理解时把 that 补回 include 后面：some will include them and others will not include them among …。

* At the beginning of 1949, the average annual return produced by stocks over the previous 20 years was 3.1%, versus 3.9% for long-term Treasury bonds—meaning that $10,000 invested in stocks would have grown to $18,415 over that period, while the same amount in bonds would have turned into $21,494. Naturally enough, 1949 turned out to be a fabulous time to buy stocks: Over the next decade, the Standard & Poor’s 500-stock index gained an average of 20.1% per year, one of the best long-term returns in the history of the U.S. stock market.

(When you say you intend to own stocks “for the long run,” do you realize just how long the long run can be—or that many investors who bought in 1929 were no longer even alive by 1954?) However, for patient investors who reinvested their income, stock returns were positive over this otherwise dismal period, simply because dividend yields averaged more than 5.6% per year. According to professors Elroy Dimson, Paul Marsh, and Mike Staunton of London Business School, if you had invested $1 in U.S. stocks in 1900 and spent all your dividends, your stock portfolio would have grown to $198 by 2000. But if you had reinvested all your dividends, your stock portfolio would have been worth $16,797! Far from being an afterthought, dividends are the greatest force in stock investing.

† Why do the “high prices” of stocks affect their dividend yields? A stock’s yield is the ratio of its cash dividend to the price of one share of common stock. If a company pays a $2 annual dividend when its stock price is $100 per share, its yield is 2%. But if the stock price doubles while the dividend stays constant, the dividend yield will drop to 1%. In 1959, when the trend Graham spotted in 1957 became noticeable to everyone, most Wall Street pundits declared that it could not possibly last. Never before had stocks yielded less than bonds; after all, since stocks are riskier than bonds, why would anyone buy them at all unless they pay extra dividend income to compensate for their greater risk? The experts argued that bonds would outyield stocks for a few months at most, and then things would revert to “normal.” More than four decades later, the relationship has never been normal again; the yield on stocks has (so far) continuously stayed below the yield on bonds.

CHAPTER 06

积极型投资者的投资组合策略：反面做法

Portfolio Policy for the Enterprising Investor: Negative Approach

积极并不等于冒进：哪些证券和做法应该先排除？

独立精读增强版：保留英文原文、段落 ID、词汇提示、长难句、图片及注释结构；新增完整中文译文。扩展解释均标注“译者补充（非原文）”。

Chapter 6Portfolio Policy for the Enterprising Investor: Negative Approach第6章 积极型投资者的投资组合策略：反面做法

本章导读这一章是写给积极型投资者的“反面清单”。格雷厄姆认为，对这类投资者最有用的概括恰恰是否定性的：先告诉他不要做什么。出发点与防御型投资者一样——高等级债券加上按合理价格买入的高等级普通股，任何偏离都得有充分的理由。随后他逐一排除三类诱惑。第一是二级（低等级）债券和优先股：按足价买入，只多拿 1%–2% 的收益，却要承担本金大幅缩水的风险，所谓“生意人的投资”是个谬论；这类证券在坏市场里几乎无一幸免地急跌，等好日子回来大多又会恢复，所以正确的做法不是按面值买，而是耐心等到 70 左右的折价再买。1946–47 年十只铁路收益债券在业绩改善的情况下一年内跌去三分之一，就是最好的证据。第二是外国政府债券：1914 年以来记录糟糕，出了问题债权人没有任何强制执行的手段，捷克斯洛伐克 8% 债券几十年间在 117 与 6 之间反复过山车、最终跌到 8，就是缩影。第三是新发行证券，尤其是牛市里小公司的普通股首发：新股背后有专门的推销力量，而且总是在对卖方最有利的时候出售；随着牛市推进，发行公司越来越差、定价越来越离谱，等到无名小公司的新股卖得比有长期记录的中型公司还贵，牛市就快到头了，随后的崩盘常让新股跌去 75% 以上。最值得记住的一句话是：用这种方式每赚一美元，最后只赔两美元就算走运。

The “aggressive” investor should start from the same base as the defensive investor, namely, a division of his funds between high-grade bonds and high-grade common stocks bought at reasonable prices.* He will be prepared to branch out into other kinds of security commitments, but in each case he will want a well-reasoned justification for the departure. There is a difficulty in discussing this topic in orderly fashion, because there is no single or ideal pattern for aggressive operations. The field of choice is wide; the selection should depend not only on the individual’s competence and equipment but perhaps equally well upon his interests and preferences.

aggressive进取型的，积极型的（本章与 enterprising 同义）branch out into扩展到，涉足security commitments证券投资头寸（commitment 本书常指投入的资金）well-reasoned justification有充分理由的论证departure偏离（此处指偏离基本策略，不是“出发”）in orderly fashion有条理地competence and equipment能力与条件（equipment 此处指知识、工具等“装备”）

“积极型”投资者应和防御型投资者从同一起点出发：把资金分配在高等级债券与以合理价格买入的高等级普通股之间。他可以扩展到其他证券，但每一次偏离基础配置，都必须有经过充分推理的理由。这个主题难以按单一顺序讲述，因为积极操作不存在唯一或理想模式。可选领域很广，选择既取决于个人能力和条件，也同样取决于兴趣与偏好。

The most useful generalizations for the enterprising investor are of a negative sort. Let him leave high-grade preferred stocks to corporate buyers. Let him also avoid inferior types of bonds and preferred stocks unless they can be bought at bargain levels—which means ordinarily at prices at least 30% under par for high-coupon issues, and much less for the lower coupons.* He will let someone else buy foreign-government bond issues, even though the yield may be attractive. He will also be wary of all kinds of new issues, including convertible bonds and preferreds that seem quite tempting and common stocks with excellent earnings confined to the recent past.

Let him also avoid inferior types of bonds and preferred stocks unless they can be bought at bargain levels—which means ordinarily at prices at least 30% under par for high-coupon issues, and much less for the lower coupons.

他还应避开质量较差的债券和优先股，除非能以廉价买到——通常这意味着，高票息的债券价格至少要低于面值 30%，而票息较低的债券还要便宜得多。

Let him + 动词是格雷厄姆爱用的第三人称祈使句，相当于“他应该……”。破折号后的 which 指代 bargain levels；句末 and much less for the lower coupons 是省略句，补全是 and (at prices) much less (than that) for the lower coupons——低票息债券对利率更敏感，所以要求更大的折价。

对积极型投资者最有用的一般原则，多半是负面的：高等级优先股留给公司投资者；低等级债券和优先股也应避开，除非能以便宜货价格买到——高票息证券通常至少应低于面值30%，低票息证券还应折价更多。外国政府债券即使收益诱人，也让别人去买。各种新发行证券同样要警惕，包括看似吸引人的可转换债券和优先股，以及只在最近几年盈利出色的普通股。

For standard bond investments the aggressive investor would do well to follow the pattern suggested to his defensive confrere, and make his choice between high-grade taxable issues, which can now be selected to yield about 7¼%, and good-quality tax-free bonds, which yield up to 5.30% on longer maturities.†

would do well to最好……，明智的做法是……confrere同行，同伴（法语借词）taxable issues应税债券longer maturities较长的到期期限

在标准债券投资上，积极型投资者最好遵循给防御型投资者的模式，在高等级应税债券和优质免税债券中选择；当时前者收益率约7.25%，期限较长的后者最高约5.30%。

Second-Grade Bonds and Preferred Stocks

二级债券与优先股

Since in late-1971 it is possible to find first-rate corporate bonds to yield 7¼%, and even more, it would not make much sense to buy second-grade issues merely for the higher return they offer. In fact corporations with relatively poor credit standing have found it virtually impossible to sell “straight bonds”—i.e., nonconvertibles—to the public in the past two years. Hence their debt financing has been done by the sale of convertible bonds (or bonds with warrants attached), which place them in a separate category. It follows that virtually all the nonconvertible bonds of inferior rating represent older issues which are selling at a large discount. Thus they offer the possibility of a substantial gain in principal value under favorable future conditions—which would mean here a combination of an improved credit rating for the company and lower general interest rates.

second-grade issues二级债券（信用等级较低的债券）credit standing信用状况straight bonds普通债券（不附带转换权等条款）i.e.即（拉丁语 id est 的缩写）nonconvertibles不可转换债券warrants attached附带认股权证It follows that由此可以推出at a large discount大幅折价principal value本金价值

1971年末，一流公司债收益率已达7.25%甚至更高，仅为多一点收益而买二级债券并不合理。过去两年，信用较差的公司实际上很难向公众出售“普通债券”，即不可转换债券，因此只能发行可转换债券或附权证债券，属于另一类别。于是几乎所有评级较低的不可转换债券都是大幅折价的老券。在未来信用评级改善且整体利率下降的有利组合下，它们可能取得可观本金升值。

But even in the matter of price discounts and resultant chance of principal gain, the second-grade bonds are in competition with better issues. Some of the well-entrenched obligations with “old-style” coupon rates (2½% to 4%) sold at about 50 cents on the dollar in 1970. Examples: American Telephone & Telegraph 2 5/8s, due 1986 sold at 51; Atchison Topeka & Santa Fe RR 4s, due 1995, sold at 51; McGraw-Hill 3 7/8s, due 1992, sold at 50½.

resultant由此产生的well-entrenched obligations地位稳固的债券（obligation 此处指债务证券）coupon rates票面利率50 cents on the dollar每 1 美元面值卖 50 美分，即面值的一半2 5/8s票息 2⅝% 的债券（词尾 -s 表示“该票息的债券”）RR铁路公司（Railroad 的缩写）

但即使考虑折价与本金升值机会，二级债券也要与更优质的债券竞争。1970年，一些地位稳固、票息仍是旧式水平（2.5%至4%）的债券，只卖面值约一半。例如：American Telephone & Telegraph 1986年到期的2又5/8%债券卖51；Atchison Topeka & Santa Fe Railroad 1995年到期的4%债券卖51；McGraw-Hill 1992年到期的3又7/8%债券卖50又1/2。

Hence under conditions of late-1971 the enterprising investors can probably get from good-grade bonds selling at a large discount all that he should reasonably desire in the form of both income and chance of appreciation.

因此在1971年末的条件下，积极型投资者从大幅折价的优质债券中，大概已能同时获得合理所需的收入与升值机会。

Throughout this book we refer to the possibility that any well-defined and protracted market situation of the past may return in the future. Hence we should consider what policy the aggressive investor might have to choose in the bond field if prices and yields of high-grade issues should return to former normals. For this reason we shall reprint here our observations on that point made in the 1965 edition, when high-grade bonds yielded only 4½%.

protracted持续很久的former normals以前的正常水平reprint重印，再次刊出

本书反复提醒：过去任何界限清楚、持续较久的市场状态，将来都可能重现。因此还应考虑，若高等级债券的价格和收益率回到从前的常态，积极型投资者该采取何种债券策略。为此重印1965年版的意见；当时高等级债券收益率只有4.5%。

Something should be said now about investing in second-grade issues, which can readily be found to yield any specified return up to 8% or more. The main difference between first- and second- grade bonds is usually found in the number of times the interest charges have been covered by earnings. Example: In early 1964 Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul and Pacific 5% income debenture bonds, at 68, yielded 7.35%. But the total interest charges of the road, before income taxes, were earned only 1.5 times in 1963, against our requirement of 5 times for a well-protected railroad issue.1

现在应谈谈二级债券投资，这类证券很容易找到收益率达到8%甚至更高的品种。一、二级债券的主要差别，通常在盈利对利息费用的保障倍数。例如1964年初，Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul and Pacific的5%收益债券价格68，收益率7.35%；但该铁路1963年税前盈利仅为总利息费用的1.5倍，远低于我们对保障良好铁路债券所要求的5倍。

Many investors buy securities of this kind because they “need income” and cannot get along with the meager return offered by top-grade issues. Experience clearly shows that it is unwise to buy a bond or a preferred which lacks adequate safety merely because the yield is attractive.* (Here the word “merely” implies that the issue is not selling at a large discount and thus does not offer an opportunity for a substantial gain in principal value.) Where such securities are bought at full prices—that is, not many points under 100 * —the chances are very great that at some future time the holder will see much lower quotations. For when bad business comes, or just a bad market, issues of this kind prove highly susceptible to severe sinking spells; often interest or dividends are suspended or at least endangered, and frequently there is a pronounced price weakness even though the operating results are not at all bad.

For when bad business comes, or just a bad market, issues of this kind prove highly susceptible to severe sinking spells; often interest or dividends are suspended or at least endangered, and frequently there is a pronounced price weakness even though the operating results are not at all bad.

因为一旦经营不景气来临——哪怕只是市场行情不好——这类证券就极易出现严重的急跌；利息或股息常常被暂停支付，或至少受到威胁，而且即便经营业绩并不差，价格也往往明显疲软。

许多投资者因为“需要收入”、无法接受最高等级证券的微薄回报，便购买这类证券。经验清楚表明，仅因收益率诱人，就购买安全性不足的债券或优先股并不明智。（“仅因”表示证券没有大幅折价，也没有取得可观本金收益的机会。）若按接近全价买入，即没有比100低很多，将来看到大幅更低报价的概率很高。经营恶化或市场不佳时，这类证券极易暴跌；利息或股息常会暂停或面临危险，即使经营结果并不差，价格也经常明显走弱。

As a specific illustration of this characteristic of second-quality senior issues, let us summarize the price behavior of a group of ten railroad income bonds in 1946–47. These comprise all of those which sold at 96 or more in 1946, their high prices averaging 102½. By the following year the group had registered low prices averaging only 68, a loss of one-third of the market value in a very short time. Peculiarly enough, the railroads of the country were showing much better earnings in 1947 than in 1946; hence the drastic price decline ran counter to the business picture and was a reflection of the selloff in the general market. But it should be pointed out that the shrinkage in these income bonds was proportionately larger than that in the common stocks in the Dow Jones industrial list (about 23%). Obviously the purchaser of these bonds at a cost above 100 could not have expected to participate to any extent in a further rise in the securities market. The only attractive feature was the income yield, averaging about 4.25% (against 2.50% for first-grade bonds, an advantage of 1.75% in annual income). Yet the sequel showed all too soon and too plainly that for the minor advantage in annual income the buyer of these second-grade bonds was risking the loss of a substantial part of his principal.

senior issues优先证券（债券和优先股，受偿顺序在普通股之前）railroad income bonds铁路收益债券Peculiarly enough奇怪的是ran counter to与……背道而驰business picture经营状况selloff抛售shrinkage缩水proportionately按比例来说participate to any extent in在任何程度上分享sequel后续发展，后来的结果all too soon太快了（all too 强调“过于”）

以1946—1947年十只铁路收益债券说明二级优先证券的特性：它们是1946年所有价格达到96以上的同类债券，最高价平均102又1/2；到下一年，最低价平均仅68，短期损失三分之一市值。奇怪的是，1947年铁路盈利远好于1946年，因此暴跌并非经营恶化，而是跟随大盘抛售；其跌幅比例还高于道琼斯工业股约23%的下跌。按高于100买入的人显然不可能期待市场继续上涨时取得多少额外收益。唯一吸引点是平均约4.25%的收益率，而一级债券为2.50%，每年只多1.75%。后来的结果很快说明：为这点额外年收入，买家承担了损失大量本金的风险。

The above example permits us to pay our respects to the popular fallacy that goes under the sobriquet of a “businessman’s investment.” That involves the purchase of a security showing a larger yield than is obtainable on a high-grade issue and carrying a correspondingly greater risk. It is bad business to accept an acknowledged possibility of a loss of principal in exchange for a mere 1 or 2% of additional yearly income. If you are willing to assume some risk you should be certain that you can realize a really substantial gain in principal value if things go well. Hence a second-grade 5.5 or 6% bond selling at par is almost always a bad purchase. The same issue at 70 might make more sense—and if you are patient you will probably be able to buy it at that level.

上面的例子让我们得以“领教”一下那个被冠以“生意人的投资”之美名的流行谬论。

上述例子也揭示了所谓“商人式投资”的流行谬误：买入收益率高于高等级证券、风险也相应更高的证券。为每年仅多1%或2%的收入，就接受本金可能损失，是一笔坏生意。若愿承担风险，就应确保一旦情况顺利，本金有机会获得真正可观的增值。因此，面值附近的二级5.5%或6%债券几乎总是糟糕购买；同一债券若卖70则可能合理，而且只要耐心，多半能等到这个价格。

译者补充（非原文）：关键不是“高收益一定不能买”，而是收益补偿是否与本金风险对称。面值100买入最多只收回100，本金上行有限；70买入既有较高当期收益率，也有信用改善后回到面值的30点空间。

Second-grade bonds and preferred stocks possess two contradictory attributes which the intelligent investor must bear clearly in mind. Nearly all suffer severe sinking spells in bad markets. On the other hand, a large proportion recover their position when favorable conditions return, and these ultimately “work out all right.” This is true even of (cumulative) preferred stocks that fail to pay dividends for many years. There were a number of such issues in the early 1940s, as a consequence of the long depression of the 1930s. During the postwar boom period of 1945–1947 many of these large accumulations were paid off either in cash or in new securities, and the principal was often discharged as well. As a result, large profits were made by people who, a few years previously, had bought these issues when they were friendless and sold at low prices.2

二级债券与优先股有两项互相矛盾的特征，聪明投资者必须牢记：几乎都在坏市场中严重下跌；但有利环境恢复后，很大一部分又会回到原位，最终“得到妥善解决”。多年不派息的累积优先股也可能如此。20世纪30年代长期萧条后，40年代初有不少这类证券；1945—1947年战后繁荣中，许多累计欠付股息以现金或新证券补清，本金也常获偿还。几年前趁无人问津、价格很低时买入的人因此赚取巨额利润。

It may well be true that, in an overall accounting, the higher yields obtainable on second-grade senior issues will prove to have offset those principal losses that were irrecoverable. In other words, an investor who bought all such issues at their offering prices might conceivably fare as well, in the long run, as one who limited himself to first-quality securities; or even somewhat better.3

从总体核算看，二级优先证券较高的收益率，可能确实足以抵消无法挽回的本金损失。换言之，把所有这类证券都按发行价买入的人，长期结果理论上可能不逊于只买最高等级证券的人，甚至略好。

But for practical purposes the question is largely irrelevant. Regardless of the outcome, the buyer of second-grade issues at full prices will be worried and discommoded when their price declines precipitately. Furthermore, he cannot buy enough issues to assure an “average” result, nor is he in a position to set aside a portion of his larger income to offset or “amortize” those principal losses which prove to be permanent. Finally, it is mere common sense to abstain from buying securities at around 100 if long experience indicates that they can probably be bought at 70 or less in the next weak market.

但实践中这个问题大致无关紧要。无论最终结果如何，按全价买二级证券的人在价格暴跌时都会焦虑不便。他也无法买入足够多品种来保证获得“平均”结果，更无法从较高收入中专门留出一部分，抵消或“摊销”永久本金损失。既然长期经验表明下一次弱市很可能以70或更低价格买到，那么不在100附近买入只是常识。

Foreign Government Bonds

外国政府债券

All investors with even small experience know that foreign bonds, as a whole, have had a bad investment history since 1914. This was inevitable in the light of two world wars and an intervening world depression of unexampled depth. Yet every few years market conditions are sufficiently favorable to permit the sale of some new foreign issues at a price of about par. This phenomenon tells us a good deal about the working of the average investor’s mind—and not only in the field of bonds.

in the light of鉴于，考虑到intervening其间发生的（介于两次大战之间）unexampled空前的at a price of about par以接近面值的价格a good deal about很多关于……的情况（a good deal：很多）

稍有经验的投资者都知道，1914年以来外国债券作为整体投资记录糟糕。经历两次世界大战及其间深度空前的全球萧条，这难以避免。然而每隔几年，市场条件又会好到让一些新外国债券按面值附近售出。这个现象很能说明普通投资者如何思考，而且不只限于债券领域。

We have no concrete reason to be concerned about the future history of well-regarded foreign bonds such as those of Australia or Norway. But we do know that, if and when trouble should come, the owner of foreign obligations has no legal or other means of enforcing his claim. Those who bought Republic of Cuba 4½s as high as 117 in 1953 saw them default their interest and then sell as low as 20 cents on the dollar in 1963. The New York Stock Exchange bond list in that year also included Belgian Congo 5¼s at 36, Greek 7s at 30, and various issues of Poland as low as 7. How many readers have any idea of the repeated vicissitudes of the 8% bonds of Czechoslovakia, since they were first offered in this country in 1922 at 96½? They advanced to 112 in 1928, declined to 67 3/4 in 1932, recovered to 106 in 1936, collapsed to 6 in 1939, recovered (unbelievably) to 117 in 1946, fell promptly to 35 in 1948, and sold as low as 8 in 1970!

我们没有具体理由担忧澳大利亚或挪威等信誉良好外国债券的未来。但一旦出事，外国债权人没有法律或其他手段强制索偿。1953年有人以117买入古巴共和国4.5%债券，后来利息违约，1963年最低只卖面值20%。当年纽交所还列有Belgian Congo 5.25%债券36、Greek 7%债券30，波兰多种债券最低7。又有多少读者知道捷克斯洛伐克8%债券自1922年按96又1/2在美国发行后反复经历什么？1928年涨至112，1932年跌至67又3/4，1936年回到106，1939年崩到6，1946年不可思议地恢复到117，1948年迅速跌至35，1970年最低又到8！

Years ago an argument of sorts was made for the purchase of foreign bonds here on the grounds that a rich creditor nation such as ours was under moral obligation to lend abroad. Time, which brings so many revenges, now finds us dealing with an intractable balance-of-payments problem of our own, part of which is ascribable to the large-scale purchase of foreign bonds by American investors seeking a small advantage in yield. For many years past we have questioned the inherent attractiveness of such investments from the standpoint of the buyer; perhaps we should add now that the latter would benefit both his country and himself if he declined these opportunities.

多年前有人主张购买外国债券，理由是美国作为富裕债权国在道义上有义务向海外放贷。时间带来讽刺性的报复，如今美国自己面对棘手的国际收支问题，其中部分正源于美国投资者为多一点收益而大规模购买外国债券。我们多年来一直怀疑这种投资对买家本身是否有内在吸引力；现在或许还应补充，拒绝这些机会既有利于买家，也有利于国家。

New Issues Generally

新发行证券的一般情况

It might seem ill-advised to attempt any broad statements about new issues as a class, since they cover the widest possible range of quality and attractiveness. Certainly there will be exceptions to any suggested rule. Our one recommendation is that all investors should be wary of new issues—which means, simply, that these should be subjected to careful examination and unusually severe tests before they are purchased.

ill-advised不明智的as a class作为一个类别subjected to接受，经受（检验）

新发行证券的质量和吸引力范围极广，对整个类别作宽泛断言似乎不妥，任何规则当然都有例外。我们唯一的建议是：所有投资者都应警惕新发行证券，也就是买入前必须仔细审查，并接受格外严格的检验。

There are two reasons for this double caveat. The first is that new issues have special salesmanship behind them, which calls therefore for a special degree of sales resistance.* The second is that most new issues are sold under “favorable market conditions”—which means favorable for the seller and consequently less favorable for the buyer.†

double caveat双重警告（caveat 拉丁语，警告、告诫）salesmanship推销术，推销力量calls therefore for因此需要（call for：需要）sales resistance抵御推销的能力

需要双重警惕有两个原因。第一，新发行背后有特别强的推销力量，因此买家也需有特别强的抗推销能力。第二，大多数新发行在“有利市场环境”中出售——对卖方有利，也就对买方较不利。

The effect of these considerations becomes steadily more important as we go down the scale from the highest-quality bonds through second-grade senior issues to common-stock flotations at the bottom. A tremendous amount of financing, consisting of the repayment of existing bonds at call price and their replacement by new issues with lower coupons, was done in the past. Most of this was in the category of high-grade bonds and preferred stocks. The buyers were largely financial institutions, amply qualified to protect their interests. Hence these offerings were carefully priced to meet the going rate for comparable issues, and high-powered salesmanship had little effect on the outcome. As interest rates fell lower and lower the buyers finally came to pay too high a price for these issues, and many of them later declined appreciably in the market. This is one aspect of the general tendency to sell new securities of all types when conditions are most favorable to the issuer; but in the case of first-quality issues the ill effects to the purchaser are likely to be unpleasant rather than serious.

go down the scale沿着等级往下走common-stock flotations普通股的发行上市（flotation：发行、上市）call price赎回价（call 本书中常指提前赎回）amply qualified完全有能力going rate现行利率high-powered高压的，强力的came to pay最终付出了appreciably明显地ill effects不良后果

从最高等级债券一路向下，到二级优先证券，再到底部的普通股新发行，这两点影响会越来越重要。过去曾有巨量再融资：公司按赎回价偿还旧债，再用低票息新债取代，多数属于高等级债券和优先股，买家主要是有充分能力保护自身利益的金融机构。因此定价会仔细贴近同类证券市场收益率，强势推销影响很小。随着利率持续下降，买家最终仍为这些证券付得太高，后来不少价格显著下跌。这同样体现发行人总在最有利时出售新证券；但对最高等级证券买家而言，后果通常只是令人不快，而非严重损失。

The situation proves somewhat different when we study the lower-grade bonds and preferred stocks sold during the 1945–46 and 1960–61 periods. Here the effect of the selling effort is more apparent, because most of these issues were probably placed with individual and inexpert investors. It was characteristic of these offerings that they did not make an adequate showing when judged by the performance of the companies over a sufficient number of years. They did look safe enough, for the most part, if it could be assumed that the recent earnings would continue without a serious setback. The investment bankers who brought out these issues presumably accepted this assumption, and their salesmen had little difficulty in persuading themselves and their customers to a like effect. Nevertheless it was an unsound approach to investment, and one likely to prove costly.

selling effort推销力度placed with配售给inexpert不内行的make an adequate showing表现合格，交出像样的成绩investment bankers投资银行家brought out推出（发行）to a like effect得出同样的结论（like 此处是形容词“同样的”）unsound不稳健的

1945—1946和1960—1961年出售的低等级债券与优先股则不同。推销影响更明显，因为买家大多是个人和缺乏经验的投资者。这些证券若用足够多年经营记录衡量，通常无法证明安全；只有假设最近盈利永远不会严重下降，看起来才算安全。承销投行大概接受了这个假设，销售人员也不难说服自己和客户。但这种投资方法并不稳健，很可能代价高昂。

Bull-market periods are usually characterized by the transformation of a large number of privately owned businesses into companies with quoted shares. This was the case in 1945–46 and again beginning in 1960. The process then reached extraordinary proportions until brought to a catastrophic close in May 1962. After the usual “swearing-off” period of several years the whole tragicomedy was repeated, step by step, in 1967–1969.*

quoted shares有市场报价的股票（即上市交易的股票）extraordinary proportions非同寻常的规模catastrophic close灾难性的收场swearing-off发誓戒除（指市场暂时不再热衷新股）tragicomedy悲喜剧

牛市常把大量私人企业变成公开上市公司。1945—1946年如此，1960年起又再次如此，规模一路发展得异乎寻常，直到1962年5月灾难性结束。经过通常几年“发誓再也不碰”的阶段，1967—1969年整出悲喜剧又逐步重演。

New Common-Stock Offerings

新发行的普通股

The following paragraphs are reproduced unchanged from the 1959 edition, with comment added:

reproduced unchanged原封不动地转载

以下段落原样取自1959年版，并另加评论：

Common-stock financing takes two different forms. In the case of companies already listed, additional shares are offered pro rata to the existing stockholders. The subscription price is set below the current market, and the “rights” to subscribe have an initial money value.* The sale of the new shares is almost always under-written by one or more investment banking houses, but it is the general hope and expectation that all the new shares will be taken by the exercise of the subscription rights. Thus the sale of additional common stock of listed companies does not ordinarily call for active selling effort on the part of distributing firms.

pro rata按比例（拉丁语）subscription price认购价rights认股权，配股权（可以转让，所以有货币价值）under-written承销（underwrite 的过去分词，此处带连字符）investment banking houses投资银行（house 本书中指券商、金融机构）exercise of the subscription rights行使认购权distributing firms分销机构（负责承销的券商）

普通股融资有两种形式。已经上市的公司按持股比例向现有股东增发，认购价低于市价，认购“权利”初始具有现金价值。新股几乎总由一家或多家投行承销，但各方通常希望并预期全部新股由股东行使认购权买走。因此，上市公司增发普通股一般不需要经销机构大力推销。

The second type is the placement with the public of common stock of what were formerly privately owned enterprises. Most of this stock is sold for the account of the controlling interests to enable them to cash in on a favorable market and to diversify their own finances. (When new money is raised for the business it comes often via the sale of preferred stock, as previously noted.) This activity follows a well-defined pattern, which by the nature of the security markets must bring many losses and disappointments to the public. The dangers arise both from the character of the businesses that are thus financed and from the market conditions that make the financing possible.

placement with the public向公众配售for the account of由……出售并归其所得（即卖的是控股股东的老股）controlling interests控股股东（interest 此处指权益持有人）cash in on趁机变现，从中捞一笔diversify their own finances分散自己的财产well-defined pattern清晰的模式thus financed以这种方式融资的

第二种是把原属私人的企业普通股卖给公众。多数股份由控制股东出售，以便在有利市场套现并分散个人资产。（企业筹集新资金时，往往如前所述发行优先股。）这种活动模式清楚，因证券市场本性必给公众带来许多损失与失望；危险既来自融资企业本身，也来自使融资得以进行的市场条件。

In the early part of the century a large proportion of our leading companies were introduced to public trading. As time went on, the number of enterprises of first rank that remained closely held steadily diminished; hence original common-stock flotations have tended to be concentrated more and more on relatively small concerns. By an unfortunate correlation, during the same period the stock-buying public has been developing an ingrained preference for the major companies and a similar prejudice against the minor ones. This prejudice, like many others, tends to become weaker as bull markets are built up; the large and quick profits shown by common stocks as a whole are sufficient to dull the public’s critical faculty, just as they sharpen its acquisitive instinct. During these periods, also, quite a number of privately owned concerns can be found that are enjoying excellent results—although most of these would not present too impressive a record if the figures were carried back, say, ten years or more.

introduced to public trading被引入公开交易（即上市）of first rank一流的closely held股权集中在少数人手里的（未上市的）concerns企业，公司（本书中 concern 常作此义）By an unfortunate correlation不幸的是，与此同时还有一种相关现象ingrained根深蒂固的prejudice against对……的偏见dull the public’s critical faculty使公众的判断力变迟钝（dull 作动词）acquisitive instinct占有的本能，贪欲carried back往前追溯

This prejudice, like many others, tends to become weaker as bull markets are built up; the large and quick profits shown by common stocks as a whole are sufficient to dull the public’s critical faculty, just as they sharpen its acquisitive instinct.

这种偏见和许多别的偏见一样，会随着牛市的形成而逐渐减弱；普通股整体上带来的又快又大的利润，足以让公众的判断力变得迟钝，正如它们让公众的贪欲变得敏锐一样。

分号前后是两个独立分句。后半句 dull（使迟钝）与 sharpen（使敏锐）构成一组反义对照，just as 引出对比：同一件事（快钱）既钝化了理性，又磨利了贪心；its 指 the public’s。

20世纪初，许多领先公司开始公开交易。此后仍由少数人持有的一流企业越来越少，首次公开发行普通股逐渐集中于相对较小的企业。不幸的是，同期购股公众形成对大公司的根深蒂固偏爱，以及对小公司的相应偏见。牛市发展时，这种偏见会减弱：普通股整体快速获取巨额利润，既麻痹公众判断力，又强化占有欲。此时还能找到不少经营成果极佳的私人企业，不过若把数据追溯十年或更久，多数记录就没那么出色。

When these factors are put together the following consequences emerge: Somewhere in the middle of the bull market the first common-stock flotations make their appearance. These are priced not unattractively, and some large profits are made by the buyers of the early issues. As the market rise continues, this brand of financing grows more frequent; the quality of the companies becomes steadily poorer; the prices asked and obtained verge on the exorbitant. One fairly dependable sign of the approaching end of a bull swing is the fact that new common stocks of small and nondescript companies are offered at prices somewhat higher than the current level for many medium-sized companies with a long market history. (It should be added that very little of this common-stock financing is ordinarily done by banking houses of prime size and reputation.)*

make their appearance登场，出现not unattractively并非没有吸引力（双重否定，即定价还算合理）brand of这一类的（brand 此处不是“品牌”）verge on the exorbitant接近离谱（verge on：濒于；exorbitant：过高的）dependable sign可靠的信号bull swing牛市行情nondescript平庸的，不起眼的market history上市交易的历史banking houses of prime size and reputation规模和声誉一流的投资银行

这些因素结合后会出现固定结果：牛市中段开始出现第一批普通股新发行，定价尚算有吸引力，早期买家取得大额利润。随着市场继续上涨，发行越来越多，公司质量持续下降，要价和成交价接近离谱。牛市将近尾声一个相当可靠的信号是：规模小、缺乏特色的新公司股票，发行价竟高于许多有长期交易历史的中型公司。（这类发行通常很少由规模最大、声誉最高的投行承做。）

The heedlessness of the public and the willingness of selling organizations to sell whatever may be profitably sold can have only one result—price collapse. In many cases the new issues lose 75% and more of their offering price. The situation is worsened by the aforementioned fact that, at bottom, the public has a real aversion to the very kind of small issue that it bought so readily in its careless moments. Many of these issues fall, proportionately, as much below their true value as they formerly sold above it.

heedlessness轻率，漫不经心whatever may be profitably sold任何能卖出去赚钱的东西aforementioned前面提到的at bottom归根结底（也可理解为“在市场底部时”）aversion to对……的厌恶careless moments疏忽大意的时候

公众轻率，加上销售机构愿意卖出任何有利可图的东西，只会带来一个结果：价格崩塌。许多新股会损失发行价75%以上。更糟的是，公众内心其实厌恶自己一时轻率买下的这类小股票；不少证券后来低于真实价值的程度，和先前高估程度一样严重。

An elementary requirement for the intelligent investor is an ability to resist the blandishments of salesmen offering new common-stock issues during bull markets. Even if one or two can be found that can pass severe tests of quality and value, it is probably bad policy to get mixed up in this sort of business. Of course the salesman will point to many such issues which have had good-sized market advances—including some that go up spectacularly the very day they are sold. But all this is part of the speculative atmosphere. It is easy money. For every dollar you make in this way you will be lucky if you end up by losing only two.

elementary requirement基本要求blandishments花言巧语，甜言蜜语get mixed up in卷入，掺和market advances市场价格上涨（advance 本书常用义）the very day就在……当天（very 强调）easy money轻松赚来的钱end up by losing最后落得赔了

For every dollar you make in this way you will be lucky if you end up by losing only two.

用这种方式每赚到一美元，最后如果只赔掉两美元，你就算走运了。

For every dollar you make 表示“每赚一美元”的对应关系，不是“为了……”；end up by losing 意为“最后落得赔钱”。这是格雷厄姆典型的冷幽默：预期结果不是赚，而是赔两倍。

聪明投资者一项基本能力，是抵抗牛市中新股推销员的诱惑。即使能找到一两只通过严格质量和价值检验的股票，卷入这种生意多半仍非良策。销售员当然会指出许多上市后大涨的新股，有些发行当天就暴涨。但这些都是投机氛围的一部分，是看似轻松的钱。用这种方式每赚1美元，最后若只亏2美元就算幸运。

Some of these issues may prove excellent buys—a few years later, when nobody wants them and they can be had at a small fraction of their true worth.

prove excellent buys证明是极好的买入对象（buy 作名词）can be had at可以按……的价格买到a small fraction of……的一小部分

几年后，当无人问津、价格只有真实价值很小一部分时，其中某些股票倒可能成为绝佳买点。

译者补充（非原文）：这里的正面机会来自时间错配：牛市时按故事高价发行，崩跌后市场又可能把尚有真实价值的企业一并抛售。积极型投资者应等待价格远低于保守价值，而不是在发行时追逐热度。

as follows如下

1965年版继续这样讨论：

While the broader aspects of the stock market’s behavior since 1949 have not lent themselves well to analysis based on long experience, the development of new common-stock flotations proceeded exactly in accordance with ancient prescription. It is doubtful whether we ever before had so many new issues offered, of such low quality, and with such extreme price collapses, as we experienced in 1960–1962.4 The ability of the stock market as a whole to disengage itself rapidly from that disaster is indeed an extraordinary phenomenon, bringing back long-buried memories of the similar invulnerability it showed to the great Florida real-estate collapse in 1925.

lent themselves well to适合于（lend oneself to：适用于）in accordance with ancient prescription完全按照老剧本（prescription 本义“处方”，此处指老套路）It is doubtful whether很难说是否……disengage itself rapidly from迅速摆脱long-buried尘封已久的invulnerability刀枪不入，不受伤害的特性Florida real-estate collapse1925 年佛罗里达房地产泡沫崩盘

It is doubtful whether we ever before had so many new issues offered, of such low quality, and with such extreme price collapses, as we experienced in 1960–1962.

我们以前是否曾经有过像 1960 到 1962 年那样的时期——新股发行数量如此之多、质量如此之低、价格崩跌如此之惨——是很值得怀疑的。

so many … of such low quality … with such extreme … 三个 so/such 短语并列，共同与句末的 as we experienced in 1960–1962 搭配，构成 so/such … as 的比较结构；had … offered 是“有……被发行”的使役用法。

1949年以来股市整体行为不太适合依据长期经验分析，但普通股新发行的发展完全遵循古老剧本。1960—1962年，新发行数量之多、质量之差、价格崩塌之极端，恐怕前所未见。股市整体竟能迅速摆脱这场灾难，确实非同寻常，让人想起它对1925年佛罗里达房地产大崩盘同样表现出的刀枪不入。

Must there be a return of the new-stock-offering madness before the present bull market can come to its definitive close? Who knows? But we do know that an intelligent investor will not forget what happened in 1962 and will let others make the next batch of quick profits in this area and experience the consequent harrowing losses.

definitive close最终的、决定性的结束consequent随之而来的harrowing惨痛的，令人痛苦的

当前牛市是否一定要等新股发行狂潮重现才会真正结束？没人知道。但聪明投资者不会忘记1962年发生过什么，会让别人去赚下一批快钱，也让他们承受随后惨痛损失。

We followed these paragraphs in the 1965 edition by citing “A Horrible Example,” namely, the sale of stock of Aetna Maintenance Co. at $9 in November 1961. In typical fashion the shares promptly advanced to $15; the next year they fell to 2 3/8, and in 1964 to 7/8. The later history of this company was on the extraordinary side, and illustrates some of the strange metamorphoses that have taken place in American business, great and small, in recent years. The curious reader will find the older and newer history of this enterprise in Appendix 5.

In typical fashion按惯常的模式on the extraordinary side颇不寻常（on the … side：偏于……）metamorphoses变形，蜕变（metamorphosis 的复数）great and small大大小小的（后置修饰 American business）

1965年版在这些段落后举了一个“可怕案例”：Aetna Maintenance Co.股票1961年11月按9美元出售，典型地很快涨至15美元，次年跌到2又3/8美元，1964年跌至7/8美元。公司后来的历史更为奇异，也说明近年美国大小企业发生的一些古怪变形。好奇读者可在附录5看到它的新旧历史。

It is by no means difficult to provide even more harrowing examples taken from the more recent version of “the same old story,” which covered the years 1967–1970. Nothing could be more pat to our purpose than the case of AAA Enterprises, which happens to be the first company then listed in Standard & Poor’s Stock Guide. The shares were sold to the public at $14 in 1968, promptly advanced to 28, but in early 1971 were quoted at a dismal 25¢. (Even this price represented a gross overvaluation of the enterprise, since it had just entered the bankruptcy court in a hopeless condition.) There is so much to be learned, and such important warnings to be gleaned, from the story of this flotation that we have reserved it for detailed treatment below, in Chapter 17.

the same old story老一套，老故事pat to our purpose正合我们的用意（pat：恰当的）Standard & Poor’s Stock Guide标准普尔《股票指南》quoted at报价为dismal惨淡的gross overvaluation严重高估bankruptcy court破产法院gleaned收集，拾取（原指拾麦穗）

1967—1970年新版“老故事重演”中，更惨痛的例子并不难找。最贴合本章目的的是AAA Enterprises，当时恰列在《标准普尔股票指南》第一家公司。股票1968年按14美元向公众出售，很快涨到28美元，1971年初却只有惨淡的0.25美元。（即便这个价格仍严重高估，因为公司刚在毫无希望的状态下进入破产法院。）这次发行有太多教训和重要警告，因此留到第17章详述。

Notes · 注释（贾森·兹威格）

* Here Graham has made a slip of the tongue. After insisting in Chapter 1 that the definition of an “enterprising” investor depends not on the amount of risk you seek, but the amount of work you are willing to put in, Graham falls back on the conventional notion that enterprising investors are more “aggressive.” The rest of the chapter, however, makes clear that Graham stands by his original definition. (The great British economist John Maynard Keynes appears to have been the first to use the term “enterprise” as a synonym for analytical investment.)
这里格雷厄姆口误了。第1章刚坚持“积极型”投资者取决于愿投入多少工作，而不是愿承担多少风险，他却又退回传统说法，把积极型投资者称为更“激进”。不过本章其余内容清楚表明，他仍坚持原定义。（英国经济学家约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯似乎最早用“enterprise”指代分析型投资。）
* “High-coupon issues” are corporate bonds paying above-average interest rates (in today’s markets, at least 8%) or preferred stocks paying large dividend yields (10% or more). If a company must pay high rates of interest in order to borrow money, that is a fundamental signal that it is risky. For more on high-yield or “junk” bonds, see pp. 145–147.
“高票息证券”指利率高于平均的公司债（在今日市场至少8%）或股息率很高的优先股（10%以上）。公司必须支付高利率才能借款，本身就是风险较高的根本信号。高收益或“垃圾”债券详见第145—147页。
† As of early 2003, the equivalent yields are roughly 5.1% on high-grade corporate bonds and 4.7% on 20-year tax-free municipal bonds. To update these yields, see www.bondsonline.com/asp/news/composites/html or www.bloomberg.com/markets/rates.html and www.bloomberg.com/markets/ psamuni.html.
截至2003年初，对应收益率约为高等级公司债5.1%、20年期免税市政债4.7%。原注所列网站可用于更新。
* For a recent example that painfully reinforces Graham’s point, see p. 146 below.
一个近年的惨痛例子进一步印证格雷厄姆观点，见下文第146页。
* Bond prices are quoted in percentages of “par value,” or 100. A bond priced at “85” is selling at 85% of its principal value; a bond originally offered for $10,000, but now selling at 85, will cost $8,500. When bonds sell below 100, they are called “discount” bonds; above 100, they become “premium” bonds.
债券价格按“面值”100的百分比报价。报价85表示本金面值的85%；原面值10,000美元的债券按85交易，价格为8,500美元。低于100称“折价债券”，高于100称“溢价债券”。
* New issues of common stock—initial public offerings or IPOs—normally are sold with an “underwriting discount” (a built-in commission) of 7%. By contrast, the buyer’s commission on older shares of common stock typically ranges below 4%. Whenever Wall Street makes roughly twice as much for selling something new as it does for selling something old, the new will get the harder sell.
新发行普通股即IPO通常含7%的“承销折扣”（内置佣金）；旧普通股买方佣金通常低于4%。华尔街卖新东西赚的钱约为旧东西两倍时，新东西自然会被更卖力推销。
† Recently, finance professors Owen Lamont of the University of Chicago and Paul Schultz of the University of Notre Dame have shown that corporations choose to offer new shares to the public when the stock market is near a peak. For technical discussion of these issues, see Lamont’s “Evaluating Value Weighting: Corporate Events and Market Timing” and Schultz’s “Pseudo Market Timing and the Long-Run Performance of IPOs” at http:// papers.ssrn.com.
芝加哥大学Owen Lamont与圣母大学Paul Schultz的研究表明，公司会在股市接近高点时选择向公众发行新股。技术讨论参见两人的相关论文。
* In the two years from June 1960, through May 1962, more than 850 companies sold their stock to the public for the first time—an average of more than one per day. In late 1967 the IPO market heated up again; in 1969 an astonishing 781 new stocks were born. That oversupply helped create the bear markets of 1969 and 1973–1974. In 1974 the IPO market was so dead that only nine new stocks were created all year; 1975 saw only 14 stocks born. That undersupply, in turn, helped feed the bull market of the 1980s, when roughly 4,000 new stocks flooded the market—helping to trigger the over-enthusiasm that led to the 1987 crash. Then the cycle swung the other way again as IPOs dried up in 1988–1990. That shortage contributed to the bull market of the 1990s—and, right on cue, Wall Street got back into the business of creating new stocks, cranking out nearly 5,000 IPOs. Then, after the bubble burst in 2000, only 88 IPOs were issued in 2001—the lowest annual total since 1979. In every case, the public has gotten burned on IPOs, has stayed away for at least two years, but has always returned for another scalding. For as long as stock markets have existed, investors have gone through this manic-depressive cycle. In America’s first great IPO boom, back in 1825, a man was said to have been squeezed to death in the stampede of speculators trying to buy shares in the new Bank of Southwark; the wealthiest buyers hired thugs to punch their way to the front of the line. Sure enough, by 1829, stocks had lost roughly 25% of their value.
1960年6月至1962年5月两年间，超过850家公司首次公开发行，平均每天超过一家。1967年末IPO再度升温，1969年惊人地诞生781只新股；供给过剩助推1969及1973—1974年熊市。1974年全年仅9只新股，1975年14只；供给不足又助推80年代牛市，当时约4,000只新股涌入，过度热情帮助触发1987年崩盘。1988—1990年IPO枯竭，短缺助长90年代牛市，随后华尔街又制造近5,000宗IPO。2000年泡沫破裂后，2001年只有88宗，为1979年以来最低。每次公众被IPO烫伤后至少离场两年，却总会回来再被烫。股市存在多久，这种躁狂—抑郁循环就存在多久。1825年美国首次IPO大潮中，据说一名男子被争购新Bank of Southwark股票的人群挤死，富豪雇打手挤到队首；到1829年，股票果然损失约25%。
* Here Graham is describing rights offerings, in which investors who already own a stock are asked to pony up even more money to maintain the same proportional interest in the company. This form of financing, still widespread in Europe, has become rare in the United States, except among closed-end funds.
格雷厄姆描述的是配股：现有股东需再投入资金，才能维持在公司的相同比例权益。这种融资在欧洲仍普遍，在美国除封闭式基金外已很少见。
* In Graham’s day, the most prestigious investment banks generally steered clear of the IPO business, which was regarded as an undignified exploitation of naïve investors. By the peak of the IPO boom in late 1999 and early 2000, however, Wall Street’s biggest investment banks had jumped in with both feet. Venerable firms cast off their traditional prudence and behaved like drunken mud wrestlers, scrambling to foist ludicrously overvalued stocks on a desperately eager public. Graham’s description of how the IPO process works is a classic that should be required reading in investment-banking ethics classes, if there are any.
格雷厄姆时代，最有声望的投行通常避开IPO，因为它被视为对天真投资者的不体面利用。但1999年末至2000年初IPO狂潮顶峰，华尔街最大投行全面加入。老牌机构抛弃传统谨慎，像醉醺醺的泥浆摔跤手一样争相把荒谬高估的股票塞给急切公众。格雷厄姆对IPO流程的描述堪称经典，应成为投行伦理课必读材料——如果真有这种课。

本章导读这一章是第 6 章“反面做法”的对应篇：说完积极型投资者不该做什么，格雷厄姆转而讲他可以做什么。债券方面只简短回顾了第 4 章提到的几种政府担保的特殊债券，重点放在普通股。他把积极型投资者的股票操作分成四类——低买高卖、买成长股、买廉价股、买特殊情况——然后逐一考察。对“择时”，他坦言过去 20 年的市场走势已无法用任何机械公式把握，只能把 25%–75% 的股票仓位区间留给有强烈看法的人自己定夺。对“成长股”，他用威森伯格年鉴里 120 只成长型基金的十年业绩（平均 108%，与标普综合指数的 105% 相差无几）说明：连专业机构都赚不到超额回报，个人更不必去买市盈率高于 20 倍的成长股；成长股最大的问题是股价波动剧烈，而靠单一公司发大财的人几乎都是内部人。随后他正面推荐三条路：一是“相对不受欢迎的大公司”，用道指低市盈率股 1937–1969 年的回测证明便宜的大公司长期跑赢，同时提醒克莱斯勒这类利润剧烈波动的公司会让市盈率信号失真；二是“廉价股”，定义为估算价值至少比市价高 50% 的证券，最易识别的一种是股价低于净营运资本的股票，此外还讨论了被市场冷落的二线公司；三是“特殊情况”即套利与重组，但只适合极少数人。最后回到根本立场：投资者必须在防御型与积极型之间二选一，没有“半个商人”的中间地带；由此推出一个看似苛刻的结论——二线股只应在不超过评估价值三分之二的廉价水平买入。

General Market Policy—Formula Timing

总体市场策略——公式化择时

We reserve for the next chapter our discussion of the possibilities and limitations of a policy of entering the market when it is depressed and selling out in the advanced stages of a boom. For many years in the past this bright idea appeared both simple and feasible, at least from first inspection of a market chart covering its periodic fluctuations. We have already admitted ruefully that the market’s action in the past 20 years has not lent itself to operations of this sort on any mathematical basis. The fluctuations that have taken place, while not inconsiderable in extent, would have required a special talent or “feel” for trading to take advantage of them. This is something quite different from the intelligence which we are assuming in our readers, and we must exclude operations based on such skill from our terms of reference.

The 50–50 plan, which we proposed to the defensive investor and described on p. 90, is about the best specific or automatic formula we can recommend to all investors under the conditions of 1972. But we have retained a broad leeway between the 25% minimum and the 75% maximum in common stocks, which we allow to those investors who have strong convictions about either the danger or the attractiveness of the general market level. Some 20 years ago it was possible to discuss in great detail a number of clear-cut formulas for varying the percentage held in common stocks, with confidence that these plans had practical utility.1 The times seem to have passed such approaches by, and there would be little point in trying to determine new levels for buying and selling out of the market patterns since 1949. That is too short a period to furnish any reliable guide to the future.*

在1972年环境下，我们向防御型投资者建议的50—50计划，大约是最适合所有投资者的具体自动公式。不过普通股比例仍可在25%至75%间宽幅变化，供那些对整体市场危险或吸引力有强烈判断的人使用。约20年前，还能详细讨论多种清晰的股债比例调整公式，并相信它们有实用价值。时代似乎已越过这种方法；试图根据1949年以来的市场模式重新确定买卖水平意义不大，因为这段时期太短，无法可靠指引未来。

Growth-Stock Approach

成长股方法

Every investor would like to select the stocks of companies that will do better than the average over a period of years. A growth stock may be defined as one that has done this in the past and is expected to do so in the future.2 Thus it seems only logical that the intelligent investor should concentrate upon the selection of growth stocks. Actually the matter is more complicated, as we shall try to show.

每位投资者都想挑出未来多年表现优于平均的公司股票。成长股可定义为过去已经胜过平均、未来也预期继续胜过平均的股票。于是聪明投资者似乎理应集中挑选成长股；但事情实际上更复杂。

There are two catches to this simple idea. The first is that common stocks with good records and apparently good prospects sell at correspondingly high prices. The investor may be right in his judgment of their prospects and still not fare particularly well, merely because he has paid in full (and perhaps overpaid) for the expected prosperity. The second is that his judgment as to the future may prove wrong. Unusually rapid growth cannot keep up forever; when a company has already registered a brilliant expansion, its very increase in size makes a repetition of its achievement more difficult. At some point the growth curve flattens out, and in many cases it turns downward.

这个简单想法有两个陷阱。第一，记录好、前景看似好的普通股会卖得相应昂贵。即使前景判断正确，投资者也可能因已为预期繁荣付足价格甚至多付而表现平平。第二，对未来的判断可能错误。异常高速增长不可能永远持续；公司已经大幅扩张后，规模本身会让重复过去成就更困难。增长曲线终会变平，许多时候还会向下。

译者补充（非原文）：好公司若被市场按完美前景定价，经营只要“非常好但不够完美”，股价仍可能下跌。增长判断与买入价格必须同时成立，缺一不可。

It is obvious that if one confines himself to a few chosen instances, based on hindsight, he could demonstrate that fortunes can readily be either made or lost in the growth-stock field. How can one judge fairly of the overall results obtainable here? We think that reasonably sound conclusions can be drawn from a study of the results achieved by the investment funds specializing in the growth-stock approach. The authoritative manual entitled Investment Companies, published annually by Arthur Wiesenberger & Company, members of the New York Stock Exchange, computes the annual performance of some 120 such “growth funds” over a period of years. Of these, 45 have records covering ten years or more. The average overall gain for these companies—unweighted for size of fund—works out at 108% for the decade 1961–1970, compared with 105% for the S & P composite and 83% for the DJIA.3 In the two years 1969 and 1970 the majority of the 126 “growth funds” did worse than either index. Similar results were found in our earlier studies. The implication here is that no outstanding rewards came from diversified investment in growth companies as compared with that in common stocks generally.*

There is no reason at all for thinking that the average intelligent investor, even with much devoted effort, can derive better results over the years from the purchase of growth stocks than the investment companies specializing in this area. Surely these organizations have more brains and better research facilities at their disposal than you do. Consequently we should advise against the usual type of growth-stock commitment for the enterprising investor.* This is one in which the excellent prospects are fully recognized in the market and already reflected in a current price-earnings ratio of, say, higher than 20. (For the defensive investor we suggested an upper limit of purchase price at 25 times average earnings of the past seven years. The two criteria would be about equivalent in most cases.)†

The striking thing about growth stocks as a class is their tendency toward wide swings in market price. This is true of the largest and longest-established companies—such as General Electric and International Business Machines—and even more so of newer and smaller successful companies. They illustrate our thesis that the main characteristic of the stock market since 1949 has been the injection of a highly speculative element into the shares of companies which have scored the most brilliant successes, and which themselves would be entitled to a high investment rating. (Their credit standing is of the best, and they pay the lowest interest rates on their borrowings.) The investment caliber of such a company may not change over a long span of years, but the risk characteristics of its stock will depend on what happens to it in the stock market. The more enthusiastic the public grows about it, and the faster its advance as compared with the actual growth in its earnings, the riskier a proposition it becomes.*

成长股作为一类，最突出特点是市价波动很大。General Electric、IBM等最大最成熟公司如此，更新更小的成功企业更甚。这印证我们的观点：1949年以来股市主要特征，是把高度投机因素注入经营最成功、本应获得高投资评级的公司股票。公司本身的投资品质可能多年不变，但股票风险取决于市场发生什么。公众越狂热，股价上涨越快于实际盈利增长，它就越危险。

But is it not true, the reader may ask, that the really big fortunes from common stocks have been garnered by those who made a substantial commitment in the early years of a company in whose future they had great confidence, and who held their original shares unwaveringly while they increased 100-fold or more in value? The answer is “Yes.” But the big fortunes from single-company investments are almost always realized by persons who have a close relationship with the particular company—through employment, family connection, etc.—which justifies them in placing a large part of their resources in one medium and holding on to this commitment through all vicissitudes, despite numerous temptations to sell out at apparently high prices along the way. An investor without such close personal contact will constantly be faced with the question of whether too large a portion of his funds are in this one medium.* Each decline—however temporary it proves in the sequel—will accentuate his problem; and internal and external pressures are likely to force him to take what seems to be a goodly profit, but one far less than the ultimate bonanza.4

读者也许会问，普通股中真正巨额财富，不正是由早年重仓一家前景极有信心的公司、坚定持有到上涨百倍甚至更多的人取得吗？答案是肯定的。但单一公司投资造就的巨富，几乎总属于与公司有密切关系的人，例如雇员或家族成员；这种关系使他们有理由把大部分资产放在一处，并历经所有变化坚持持有，抵抗途中高价卖出的诱惑。没有这种联系的投资者会不断担心单一持仓比例过高。每次下跌，即使后来证明只是暂时，都会加重压力；内外因素很可能迫使他在看似丰厚的利润处卖出，却远低于最终巨额收益。

Three Recommended Fields for “Enterprising Investment”

推荐给“积极型投资”的三个领域

To obtain better than average investment results over a long pull requires a policy of selection or operation possessing a twofold merit: (1) It must meet objective or rational tests of underlying soundness; and (2) it must be different from the policy followed by most investors or speculators. Our experience and study leads us to recommend three investment approaches that meet these criteria. They differ rather widely from one another, and each may require a different type of knowledge and temperament on the part of those who assay it.

长期取得高于平均的投资结果，需要一套具有双重优点的选择或操作政策：（1）基础稳健，能通过客观理性检验；（2）不同于多数投资者或投机者采取的政策。我们的经验与研究建议三种符合标准的方法，它们差别很大，采用者可能需要不同知识和性格。

The Relatively Unpopular Large Company

相对不受欢迎的大公司

If we assume that it is the habit of the market to overvalue common stocks which have been showing excellent growth or are glamorous for some other reason, it is logical to expect that it will undervalue—relatively, at least—companies that are out of favor because of unsatisfactory developments of a temporary nature. This may be set down as a fundamental law of the stock market, and it suggests an investment approach that should prove both conservative and promising.

glamorous光彩夺目的，有魅力的out of favor不受欢迎，失宠unsatisfactory developments不如意的情况of a temporary nature暂时性的set down as记作，视为

若市场习惯高估增长出色或因其他原因光鲜的普通股，那么逻辑上也会相对低估因暂时性不利发展而失宠的公司。这可视为股市一条基本规律，并提示一种既保守又有希望的投资方法。

The key requirement here is that the enterprising investor concentrate on the larger companies that are going through a period of unpopularity. While small companies may also be undervalued for similar reasons, and in many cases may later increase their earnings and share price, they entail the risk of a definitive loss of profitability and also of protracted neglect by the market in spite of better earnings. The large companies thus have a double advantage over the others. First, they have the resources in capital and brain power to carry them through adversity and back to a satisfactory earnings base. Second, the market is likely to respond with reasonable speed to any improvement shown.

entail带来，意味着（某种后果）definitive loss of profitability盈利能力的永久丧失protracted neglect长期被冷落brain power智力资源，人才carry them through adversity帮它们渡过逆境earnings base盈利基础respond with reasonable speed以合理的速度作出反应

关键要求是，积极型投资者应集中于正处在不受欢迎阶段的大公司。小公司也可能因类似原因低估，后来盈利和股价提高；但它们既有盈利永久丧失的风险，也可能即使盈利改善仍被市场长期忽略。大公司有双重优势：其一，有资本和人才渡过逆境、恢复满意盈利；其二，市场通常会较快回应任何改善。

A remarkable demonstration of the soundness of this thesis is found in studies of the price behavior of the unpopular issues in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. In these it was assumed that an investment was made each year in either the six or the ten issues in the DJIA which were selling at the lowest multipliers of their current or previous year’s earnings. These could be called the “cheapest” stocks in the list, and their cheapness was evidently the reflection of relative unpopularity with investors or traders. It was assumed further that these purchases were sold out at the end of holding periods ranging from one to five years. The results of these investments were then compared with the results shown in either the DJIA as a whole or in the highest multiplier (i.e., the most popular) group.

道琼斯工业平均指数中冷门股票的价格研究，显著证明这个观点。研究假定每年买入道指中按当前或上年盈利计算市盈率最低的6只或10只，也就是名单里“最便宜”、显然最不受投资者欢迎的股票，再在持有一至五年后卖出；然后把结果与整个道指或市盈率最高、最热门的组合比较。

The detailed material we have available covers the results of annual purchases assumed in each of the past 53 years.5 In the early period, 1917–1933, this approach proved unprofitable. But since 1933 the method has shown highly successful results. In 34 tests made by Drexel & Company (now Drexel Firestone)* of one-year holding—from 1937 through 1969—the cheap stocks did definitely worse than the DJIA in only three instances; the results were about the same in six cases; and the cheap stocks clearly outperformed the average in 25 years. The consistently better performance of the low-multiplier stocks is shown (Table 7-2) by the average results for successive five-year periods, when compared with those of the DJIA and of the ten high-multipliers.

The concept of buying “unpopular large companies” and its execution on a group basis, as described above, are both quite simple. But in considering individual companies a special factor of opposite import must sometimes to be taken into account. Companies that are inherently speculative because of widely varying earnings tend to sell both at a relatively high price and at a relatively low multiplier in their good years, and conversely at low prices and high multipliers in their bad years. These relationships are illustrated in Table 7-3, covering fluctuations of Chrysler Corp. common. In these cases the market has sufficient skepticism as to the continuation of the unusually high profits to value them conservatively, and conversely when earnings are low or nonexistent. (Note that, by the arithmetic, if a company earns “next to nothing” its shares must sell at a high multiplier of these minuscule profits.)

Companies that are inherently speculative because of widely varying earnings tend to sell both at a relatively high price and at a relatively low multiplier in their good years, and conversely at low prices and high multipliers in their bad years.

那些因为利润剧烈波动而本质上具有投机性的公司，在景气年份往往股价相对较高、市盈率却相对较低；而在不景气的年份则相反：股价低、市盈率高。

关键在于理解 multiplier（市盈率）与 price（股价）为什么反向变动：市场怀疑高利润能否持续，好年景时不肯给高倍数；坏年景时利润接近于零，除数极小，市盈率自然畸高。这正是格雷厄姆说“低市盈率选股法”需要加以修正的地方。

按组买入“不受欢迎的大公司”概念和执行都很简单，但分析个别公司时，有时要考虑作用相反的特殊因素。盈利波动很大的公司天生具有投机性，在好年份往往盈利高、股价也较高，却显示低市盈率；坏年份则股价低、盈利更低，反而市盈率高。表7-3中Chrysler普通股波动说明这种关系。市场对异常高利润能否持续已有怀疑，故只给保守估值；盈利低或接近零时则相反。（算术上，公司若“几乎不赚钱”，任何正股价除以微小盈利都会得到很高市盈率。）

As it happens Chrysler has been quite exceptional in the DJIA list of leading companies, and hence it did not greatly affect the low-multiplier calculations. It would be quite easy to avoid inclusion of such anomalous issues in a low-multiplier list by requiring also that the price be low in relation to past average earnings or by some similar test.

Chrysler在道指领先公司中相当特殊，因此没有显著扭曲低市盈率计算。只要再要求股价相对于过去平均盈利也较低，或加入类似检验，就容易排除这类异常股票。

While writing this revision we tested the results of the DJIA-low-multiplier method applied to a group assumed to be bought at the end of 1968 and revalued on June 30, 1971. This time the figures proved quite disappointing, showing a sharp loss for the low-multiplier six or ten and a good profit for the high-multiplier selections. This one bad instance should not vitiate conclusions based on 30-odd experiments, but its recent happening gives it a special adverse weight. Perhaps the aggressive investor should start with the “low-multiplier” idea, but add other quantitative and qualitative requirements thereto in making up his portfolio.

Purchase of Bargain Issues

买入廉价股

We define a bargain issue as one which, on the basis of facts established by analysis, appears to be worth considerably more than it is selling for. The genus includes bonds and preferred stocks selling well under par, as well as common stocks. To be as concrete as possible, let us suggest that an issue is not a true “bargain” unless the indicated value is at least 50% more than the price. What kind of facts would warrant the conclusion that so great a discrepancy exists? How do bargains come into existence, and how does the investor profit from them?

我们把“便宜证券”定义为：依据分析确认的事实，其价值明显高于售价。这个类别包括远低于面值的债券、优先股和普通股。为尽量具体，若估计价值没有至少比价格高50%，就不算真正“便宜货”。什么事实足以证明如此大差距？便宜货怎样产生，投资者又怎样获利？

译者补充（非原文）：“价值至少比价格高50%”等价于买价不超过估值的约三分之二。例如保守估值150元，价格100元，价值比价格高50%，也留下约三分之一估值幅度的安全边际。

There are two tests by which a bargain common stock is detected. The first is by the method of appraisal. This relies largely on estimating future earnings and then multiplying these by a factor appropriate to the particular issue. If the resultant value is sufficiently above the market price—and if the investor has confidence in the technique employed—he can tag the stock as a bargain. The second test is the value of the business to a private owner. This value also is often determined chiefly by expected future earnings—in which case the result may be identical with the first. But in the second test more attention is likely to be paid to the realizable value of the assets, with particular emphasis on the net current assets or working capital.

识别便宜普通股有两种检验。第一是估值法，主要估算未来盈利，再乘以适合该证券的倍数；若结果充分高于市价且投资者信任方法，就可判定便宜。第二是从私人业主角度衡量企业价值，也常主要由未来预期盈利决定，结果可能与第一种相同；但它通常更重视资产可变现价值，尤其净流动资产或营运资本。

At low points in the general market a large proportion of common stocks are bargain issues, as measured by these standards. (A typical example was General Motors when it sold at less than 30 in 1941, equivalent to only 5 for the 1971 shares. It had been earning in excess of $4 and paying $3.50, or more, in dividends.) It is true that current earnings and the immediate prospects may both be poor, but a levelheaded appraisal of average future conditions would indicate values far above ruling prices. Thus the wisdom of having courage in depressed markets is vindicated not only by the voice of experience but also by application of plausible techniques of value analysis.

in excess of超过immediate prospects近期前景levelheaded头脑冷静的far above ruling prices远高于当时的市价（ruling：通行的、当时的）vindicated得到证实，被证明正确the voice of experience经验之谈plausible合理的，站得住脚的

整体市场低点时，按这些标准，大量普通股都会成为便宜货。（典型例是General Motors 1941年卖不到30美元，折合1971年股份仅5美元；当时每股盈利超过4美元，股息3.50美元以上。）当前盈利和近期前景可能都差，但冷静估计未来平均环境，会得到远高于市价的价值。因此，萧条市场中勇敢买入的智慧，不仅由经验支持，也能由合理价值分析证明。

The same vagaries of the market place that recurrently establish a bargain condition in the general list account for the existence of many individual bargains at almost all market levels. The market is fond of making mountains out of molehills and exaggerating ordinary vicissitudes into major setbacks.* Even a mere lack of interest or enthusiasm may impel a price decline to absurdly low levels. Thus we have what appear to be two major sources of undervaluation: (1) currently disappointing results and (2) protracted neglect or unpopularity.

使整个市场周期性出现便宜状态的反复无常，也让几乎任何市场水平都存在个别便宜货。市场爱小题大做，把普通波折夸张成重大挫败。即使只是缺乏兴趣或热情，也能把价格压到荒谬低位。因此低估主要有两个来源：（1）当前业绩令人失望；（2）长期遭忽略或不受欢迎。

However, neither of these causes, if considered by itself alone, can be relied on as a guide to successful common-stock investment. How can we be sure that the currently disappointing results are indeed going to be only temporary? True, we can supply excellent examples of that happening. The steel stocks used to be famous for their cyclical quality, and the shrewd buyer could acquire them at low prices when earnings were low and sell them out in boom years at a fine profit. A spectacular example is supplied by Chrysler Corporation, as shown by the data in Table 7-3.

但这两个原因单独看都不足以指导成功投资。怎样确认当前失望只是暂时？确有优秀例子。钢铁股曾以周期性著称，精明买家可在盈利低迷时低价买入，繁荣年份高价卖出。表7-3的Chrysler是更惊人的案例。

If this were the standard behavior of stocks with fluctuating earnings, then making profits in the stock market would be an easy matter. Unfortunately, we could cite many examples of declines in earnings and price which were not followed automatically by a handsome recovery of both. One such was Anaconda Wire and Cable, which had large earnings up to 1956, with a high price of 85 in that year. The earnings then declined irregularly for six years; the price fell to 23½ in 1962, and the following year it was taken over by its parent enterprise (Anaconda Corporation) at the equivalent of only 33.

handsome recovery可观的复苏（handsome：数量可观的）Anaconda Wire and Cable安纳康达电线电缆公司irregularly不规则地，时断时续地taken over被收购parent enterprise母公司at the equivalent of以相当于……的价格

若所有盈利波动股都按此模式运行，股市赚钱会很容易。遗憾的是，很多盈利和价格下降后并未自动漂亮复苏。例如Anaconda Wire and Cable在1956年前盈利丰厚，当年最高85美元；随后盈利断续下滑六年，1962年股价跌至23又1/2美元，次年母公司Anaconda Corporation仅按相当于33美元收购。

The many experiences of this type suggest that the investor would need more than a mere falling off in both earnings and price to give him a sound basis for purchase. He should require an indication of at least reasonable stability of earnings over the past decade or more—i.e., no year of earnings deficit—plus sufficient size and financial strength to meet possible setbacks in the future. The ideal combination here is thus that of a large and prominent company selling both well below its past average price and its past average price/earnings multiplier. This would no doubt have ruled out most of the profitable opportunities in companies such as Chrysler, since their low-price years are generally accompanied by high price/earnings ratios. But let us assure the reader now—and no doubt we shall do it again—that there is a world of difference between “hindsight profits” and “real-money profits.” We doubt seriously whether the Chrysler type of roller coaster is a suitable medium for operations by our enterprising investor.

这类经验说明，仅有盈利和股价同时下降，不足以构成稳健买入依据。投资者至少应要求过去十年或更久盈利具有合理稳定性——没有年度亏损——并且企业规模和财务实力足以应对未来挫折。理想组合是一家大型知名公司，股价既远低于过去平均价格，也远低于过去平均市盈率。这无疑会排除Chrysler式机会，因为其低价年份往往伴随高市盈率。但必须提醒：“事后利润”和“真金白银的利润”天差地别。我们严重怀疑Chrysler式过山车适合积极型投资者操作。

We have mentioned protracted neglect or unpopularity as a second cause of price declines to unduly low levels. A current case of this kind would appear to be National Presto Industries. In the bull market of 1968 it sold at a high of 45, which was only 8 times the $5.61 earnings for that year. The per-share profits increased in both 1969 and 1970, but the price declined to only 21 in 1970. This was less than 4 times the (record) earnings in that year and less than its net-current-asset value. In March 1972 it was selling at 34, still only 5½ times the last reported earnings, and at about its enlarged net-current-asset value.

unduly过度地National Presto Industries国民普雷斯托工业公司（美国小家电制造商）at a high of 45最高价 45 美元per-share profits每股利润record创纪录的net-current-asset value净流动资产价值the last reported earnings最近公布的利润

长期被忽视或不受欢迎，是价格过低的第二个原因。National Presto Industries似乎是当时案例：1968年牛市最高45美元，也只有当年每股盈利5.61美元的8倍；1969、1970年每股利润继续增长，股价却在1970年跌至21美元，不到当年创纪录盈利4倍，也低于每股净流动资产。1972年3月卖34美元，仍只有最近盈利5.5倍，约等于已经扩大的每股净流动资产。

Another example of this type is provided currently by Standard Oil of California, a concern of major importance. In early 1972 it was selling at about the same price as 13 years before, say 56. Its earnings had been remarkably steady, with relatively small growth but with only one small decline over the entire period. Its book value was about equal to the market price. With this conservatively favorable 1958–71 record the company has never shown an average annual price as high as 15 times its current earnings. In early 1972 the price/earnings ratio was only about 10.

另一例是重要企业Standard Oil of California。1972年初股价约56美元，与13年前相近。盈利极稳定，增长虽小，整个期间只有一次轻微下降；账面价值约等于市价。尽管1958—1971年记录保守而良好，公司年度平均股价从未高于当年盈利15倍，1972年初市盈率仅约10倍。

A third cause for an unduly low price for a common stock may be the market’s failure to recognize its true earnings picture. Our classic example here is Northern Pacific Railway which in 1946–47 declined from 36 to 13½. The true earnings of the road in 1947 were close to $10 per share. The price of the stock was held down in great part by its $1 dividend. It was neglected also because much of its earnings power was concealed by accounting methods peculiar to railroads.

true earnings picture真实的盈利状况Northern Pacific Railway北太平洋铁路公司the road这家铁路公司（road = railroad）earnings power盈利能力peculiar to……特有的

普通股价格过低的第三个原因，是市场没有识别真实盈利。经典案例Northern Pacific Railway在1946—1947年从36跌至13又1/2美元，1947年真实每股盈利接近10美元。仅1美元股息在很大程度上压住股价；铁路特有会计方法又隐藏了大量盈利能力，因此市场忽视它。

The type of bargain issue that can be most readily identified is a common stock that sells for less than the company’s net working capital alone, after deducting all prior obligations.* This would mean that the buyer would pay nothing at all for the fixed assets—buildings, machinery, etc., or any good-will items that might exist. Very few companies turn out to have an ultimate value less than the working capital alone, although scattered instances may be found. The surprising thing, rather, is that there have been so many enterprises obtainable which have been valued in the market on this bargain basis. A compilation made in 1957, when the market’s level was by no means low, disclosed about 150 of such common stocks. In Table 7-4 we summarize the result of buying, on December 31, 1957, one share of each of the 85 companies in that list for which data appeared in Standard & Poor’s Monthly Stock Guide, and holding them for two years.

最容易识别的便宜证券，是股价低于公司净营运资本本身，且已扣除全部优先义务的普通股。这意味着买家没有为建筑、机器等固定资产或任何商誉支付一分钱。最终价值低于营运资本的公司很少，虽有零星案例。真正惊人的是，市场上曾有那么多企业能按这种便宜标准买到。1957年市场并不低，统计仍发现约150只。表7-4汇总：1957年12月31日各买入其中有《标准普尔月度股票指南》数据的85家公司一股，持有两年。

译者补充（非原文）：计算口径是：现金、应收款、存货等流动资产，减去全部负债、优先股等优先义务。若每股结果为20元而股价15元，买家相当于按低于净流动资产的价格取得企业，固定资产和持续经营能力没有被计价。

By something of a coincidence, each of the groups advanced in the two years to somewhere in the neighborhood of the aggregate net-current-asset value. The gain for the entire “portfolio” in that period was 75%, against 50% for Standard & Poor’s 425 industrials. What is more remarkable is that none of the issues showed significant losses, seven held about even, and 78 showed appreciable gains.

颇为巧合的是，两年后各组都涨到接近合计净流动资产价值。整个“组合”上涨75%，标准普尔425种工业股上涨50%。更惊人的是，没有一只显著亏损；7只大致持平，78只明显上涨。

Our experience with this type of investment selection—on a diversified basis—was uniformly good for many years prior to 1957. It can probably be affirmed without hesitation that it constitutes a safe and profitable method of determining and taking advantage of undervalued situations. However, during the general market advance after 1957 the number of such opportunities became extremely limited, and many of those available were showing small operating profits or even losses. The market decline of 1969–70 produced a new crop of these “sub-working-capital” stocks. We discuss this group in Chapter 15, on stock selection for the enterprising investor.

1957年前多年，我们以分散方式采用这种选择法，经验一贯良好。可以毫不犹豫地说，它是识别并利用低估情形的一种安全、获利方法。但1957年后整体市场上涨，这类机会变得极少，且不少可选公司只微利甚至亏损。1969—1970年下跌又产生一批“低于营运资本”股票，第15章积极型投资者选股会讨论。
