BARGAIN-ISSUE PATTERN IN SECONDARY COMPANIES. We have defined a secondary company as one that is not a leader in a fairly important industry. Thus it is usually one of the smaller concerns in its field, but it may equally well be the chief unit in an unimportant line. By way of exception, any company that has established itself as a growth stock is not ordinarily considered “secondary.”

secondary company二线公司concerns企业，公司（本书常用义）the chief unit主要企业，龙头an unimportant line不重要的行业（line：行业、业务线）By way of exception作为例外

二线公司的便宜证券模式。我们把二线公司定义为：不是某个相当重要行业的领头企业。它通常是本行业较小公司，也可能是不重要行业的主要企业。例外是，已经确立成长股地位的公司通常不视为“二线”。

In the great bull market of the 1920s relatively little distinction was drawn between industry leaders and other listed issues, provided the latter were of respectable size. The public felt that a middle-sized company was strong enough to weather storms and that it had a better chance for really spectacular expansion than one that was already of major dimensions. The depression years 1931–32, however, had a particularly devastating impact on the companies below the first rank either in size or in inherent stability. As a result of that experience investors have since developed a pronounced preference for industry leaders and a corresponding lack of interest most of the time in the ordinary company of secondary importance. This has meant that the latter group have usually sold at much lower prices in relation to earnings and assets than have the former. It has meant further that in many instances the price has fallen so low as to establish the issue in the bargain class.

20世纪20年代大牛市中，只要其他上市公司规模体面，公众很少严格区分行业龙头与它们。人们认为中型公司足以挺过风暴，又比巨头更可能惊人扩张。但1931—1932年萧条对规模或内在稳定性低于一流的公司打击尤其惨重。此后投资者明显偏爱行业龙头，多数时候忽视普通二线公司，导致后者相对于盈利和资产的价格通常低得多，许多甚至跌入便宜货类别。

When investors rejected the stocks of secondary companies, even though these sold at relatively low prices, they were expressing a belief or fear that such companies faced a dismal future. In fact, at least subconsciously, they calculated that any price was too high for them because they were heading for extinction—just as in 1929 the companion theory for the “blue chips” was that no price was too high for them because their future possibilities were limitless. Both of these views were exaggerations and were productive of serious investment errors. Actually, the typical middle-sized listed company is a large one when compared with the average privately owned business. There is no sound reason why such companies should not continue indefinitely in operation, undergoing the vicissitudes characteristic of our economy but earning on the whole a fair return on their invested capital.

投资者即使面对低价也拒绝二线股，表达的是担忧它们前景黯淡；至少潜意识里，他们认为这些公司走向消亡，任何价格都太高，就像1929年对蓝筹股的相反理论是前景无限、任何价格都不高。两种观点都夸张，都会造成严重投资错误。典型上市中型公司与普通私人企业相比其实已很大，没有充分理由认为它不能无限期经营，经历经济波折后总体仍为投入资本赚取合理回报。

This brief review indicates that the stock market’s attitude toward secondary companies tends to be unrealistic and consequently to create in normal times innumerable instances of major undervaluation. As it happens, the World War II period and the postwar boom were more beneficial to the smaller concerns than to the larger ones, because then the normal competition for sales was suspended and the former could expand sales and profit margins more spectacularly. Thus by 1946 the market’s pattern had completely reversed itself from that before the war. Whereas the leading stocks in the Dow Jones Industrial Average had advanced only 40% from the end of 1938 to the 1946 high, Standard & Poor’s index of low-priced stocks had shot up no less than 280% in the same period. Speculators and many self-styled investors—with the proverbial short memories of people in the stock market—were eager to buy both old and new issues of unimportant companies at inflated levels. Thus the pendulum had swung clear to the opposite extreme. The very class of secondary issues that had formerly supplied by far the largest proportion of bargain opportunities was now presenting the greatest number of examples of overenthusiasm and overvaluation. In a different way this phenomenon was repeated in 1961 and 1968—the emphasis now being placed on new offerings of the shares of small companies of less than secondary character, and on nearly all companies in certain favored fields such as “electronics,” “computers,” “franchise” concerns, and others.*

这段回顾表明，股市对二线公司的态度往往不现实，因此正常时期会制造无数严重低估。二战和战后繁荣对小企业反而比大企业更有利，因为正常销售竞争暂停，小企业的销售与利润率能更惊人扩张。到1946年，市场模式已与战前完全反转：1938年末至1946年高点，道指龙头仅涨40%，标准普尔低价股指数却猛涨280%。记忆短暂的投机者和许多自称投资者的人，争购不重要公司的新老股票且价格虚高，钟摆摆到另一极端。过去提供最多便宜机会的二线股，此时反而出现最多过热和高估案例。1961、1968年以不同方式重演：焦点转到比二线还弱的小公司新股，以及“电子”“计算机”“特许经营”等热门领域几乎所有公司。

As was to be expected the ensuing market declines fell most heavily on these overvaluations. In some cases the pendulum swing may have gone as far as definite under valuation.

正如预料，随后市场下跌对这些高估打击最重。有些案例中，钟摆甚至摆到明确低估。

If most secondary issues tend normally to be undervalued, what reason has the investor to believe that he can profit from such a situation? For if it persists indefinitely, will he not always be in the same market position as when he bought the issue? The answer here is somewhat complicated. Substantial profits from the purchase of secondary companies at bargain prices arise in a variety of ways. First, the dividend return is relatively high. Second, the reinvested earnings are substantial in relation to the price paid and will ultimately affect the price. In a five-to seven-year period these advantages can bulk quite large in a well-selected list. Third, a bull market is ordinarily most generous to low-priced issues; thus it tends to raise the typical bargain issue to at least a reasonable level. Fourth, even during relatively featureless market periods a continuous process of price adjustment goes on, under which secondary issues that were undervalued may rise at least to the normal level for their type of security. Fifth, the specific factors that in many cases made for a disappointing record of earnings may be corrected by the advent of new conditions, or the adoption of new policies, or by a change in management.

若多数二线股通常低估，投资者凭什么相信能从中获利？若低估永久持续，市场处境岂非与买入时相同？答案较复杂。按便宜价格买二线公司可通过多种途径取得可观收益。第一，股息收益率较高。第二，相对于买价，留存再投资盈利很大，最终会影响价格；在精心选择的组合中，五至七年后两项优势会相当显著。第三，牛市通常最厚待低价股，会把典型便宜股至少推回合理水平。第四，即使市场平淡，持续的价格调整也会使低估二线股回到同类正常水平。第五，造成盈利失望的具体因素可能因新环境、新政策或管理层更换而纠正。

An important new factor in recent years has been the acquisition of smaller companies by larger ones, usually as part of a diversification program. In these cases the consideration paid has almost always been relatively generous, and much in excess of the bargain levels existing not long before.

近年一个重要新因素，是大公司通常为多元化而收购小公司。收购价几乎总是相当慷慨，远高于不久前的便宜水平。

When interest rates were much lower than in 1970, the field of bargain issues extended to bonds and preferred stocks that sold at large discounts from the amount of their claim. Currently we have a different situation in which even well-secured issues sell at large discounts if carrying coupon rates of, say, 4½% or less. Example: American Telephone & Telegraph 2 5/8s, due 1986, sold as low as 51 in 1970; Deere & Co. 4½s, due 1983, sold as low as 62. These may well turn out to have been bargain opportunities before very long—if ruling interest rates should decline substantially. For a bargain bond issue in the more traditional sense perhaps we shall have to turn once more to the first-mortgage bonds of railroads now in financial difficulties, which sell in the 20s or 30s. Such situations are not for the inexpert investor; lacking a real sense of values in this area, he may burn his fingers. But there is an underlying tendency for market decline in this field to be overdone; consequently the group as a whole offers an especially rewarding invitation to careful and courageous analysis. In the decade ending in 1948 the billion-dollar group of defaulted railroad bonds presented numerous and spectacular opportunities in this area. Such opportunities have been quite scarce since then; but they seem likely to return in the 1970s.*

利率远低于1970年时，便宜证券还包括按远低于债权金额交易的债券和优先股。如今不同：即使保障良好，票息4.5%或更低也会大幅折价。例如AT&T 1986年到期2又5/8%债券1970年最低51；Deere & Co. 1983年到期4.5%债券最低62。若市场利率大降，它们可能很快证明是便宜机会。若找传统意义的便宜债券，或须再次看陷入财务困境、价格20或30多的铁路第一抵押债券。这不适合外行；没有真正价值判断，很容易受伤。但此领域价格下跌常被做过头，整体特别值得谨慎而勇敢地分析。到1948年止十年，价值10亿美元的违约铁路债券曾提供大量惊人机会；此后很少，但70年代似乎会重现。

Special Situations, or “Workouts”

特殊情况，或“重组套利”

Not so long ago this was a field which could almost guarantee an attractive rate of return to those who knew their way around in it; and this was true under almost any sort of general market situation. It was not actually forbidden territory to members of the general public. Some who had a flair for this sort of thing could learn the ropes and become pretty capable practitioners without the necessity of long academic study or apprenticeship. Others have been keen enough to recognize the underlying soundness of this approach and to attach themselves to bright young men who handled funds devoted chiefly to these “special situations.” But in recent years, for reasons we shall develop later, the field of “arbitrages and workouts” became riskier and less profitable. It may be that in years to come conditions in this field will become more propitious. In any case it is worthwhile outlining the general nature and origin of these operations, with one or two illustrative examples.

knew their way around in it熟门熟路forbidden territory禁区a flair for对……的天赋learn the ropes学会门道，摸清诀窍apprenticeship学徒期keen enough to足够敏锐，能……attach themselves to追随，依附于arbitrages and workouts套利与重组（workout：通过重组、清算等解决问题的过程）propitious有利的，吉利的illustrative examples说明性的例子

不久前，熟悉门道的人在这个领域几乎可保证取得有吸引力回报，几乎不受整体市场影响。它也非公众禁区；有天赋者不需长期学术训练或学徒期，也能学会规则、成为相当能干的操作者。另一些敏锐者看出方法稳健，便把资金交给主要处理“特殊情况”的聪明年轻人。但近年“套利与清算”风险上升、利润下降，原因后文会解释。未来条件也许会更有利；无论如何，仍值得概述这类操作的性质、来源和一两个例子。

The typical “special situation” has grown out of the increasing number of acquisitions of smaller firms by large ones, as the gospel of diversification of products has been adopted by more and more managements. It often appears good business for such an enterprise to acquire an existing company in the field it wishes to enter rather than to start a new venture from scratch. In order to make such acquisition possible, and to obtain acceptance of the deal by the required large majority of shareholders of the smaller company, it is almost always necessary to offer a price considerably above the current level. Such corporate moves have been producing interesting profit-making opportunities for those who have made a study of this field, and have good judgment fortified by ample experience.

has grown out of源于，由……发展而来the gospel of diversification多元化的“福音”（gospel：被奉为真理的信条）good business划算的生意from scratch从零开始obtain acceptance of the deal使交易获得接受the required large majority所需的绝大多数（股东）made a study of研究过fortified by ample experience以丰富的经验为后盾

典型“特殊情况”源于大公司收购小公司的数量增加，因为越来越多管理层信奉产品多元化。企业进入新领域时，收购现有公司往往比从零创业更合算。为了完成收购，并获小公司所需绝大多数股东同意，几乎总须报出明显高于当前市价的价格。研究此领域且判断良好、经验充分的人，能从这类公司行动中发现有趣获利机会。

译者补充（非原文）：特殊情况的收益并非单纯押注股价上涨，而是买价、收购对价、成交概率和等待时间之间的差额。若要约50元、股票47元，3元差价必须足以补偿交易失败后可能跌回原价的风险。

A great deal of money was made by shrewd investors not so many years ago through the purchase of bonds of railroads in bankruptcy—bonds which they knew would be worth much more than their cost when the railroads were finally reorganized. After promulgation of the plans of reorganization a “when issued” market for the new securities appeared. These could almost always be sold for considerably more than the cost of the old issues which were to be exchanged therefor. There were risks of nonconsummation of the plans or of unexpected delays, but on the whole such “arbitrage operations” proved highly profitable.

promulgation公布，颁布plans of reorganization重组方案when issued待发行（尚未正式发行的新证券的预先交易）exchanged therefor换成它们（therefor = for that，古旧用法）nonconsummation未能完成arbitrage operations套利操作

若干年前，精明投资者买入破产铁路债券赚了很多钱，因为他们知道铁路最终重组后，债券价值会远高于成本。重组计划公布后，新证券出现“待发行”市场，通常可按明显高于将被交换的旧债成本出售。计划可能无法完成或意外延误，但这类“套利操作”总体利润很高。

There were similar opportunities growing out of the breakup of public-utility holding companies pursuant to 1935 legislation. Nearly all these enterprises proved to be worth considerably more when changed from holding companies to a group of separate operating companies.

breakup拆分public-utility holding companies公用事业控股公司pursuant to依据（法律用语）

1935年立法要求公用事业控股公司拆分，也产生类似机会。几乎所有企业从控股公司变为若干独立运营公司后，总价值都显著提高。

The underlying factor here is the tendency of the security markets to undervalue issues that are involved in any sort of complicated legal proceedings. An old Wall Street motto has been: “Never buy into a lawsuit.” This may be sound advice to the speculator seeking quick action on his holdings. But the adoption of this attitude by the general public is bound to create bargain opportunities in the securities affected by it, since the prejudice against them holds their prices down to unduly low levels.*

legal proceedings法律程序，诉讼Never buy into a lawsuit永远别买有官司的股票quick action快速的行情变动is bound to必然会prejudice偏见

背后因素是，证券市场倾向低估卷入复杂法律程序的证券。华尔街老格言说：“绝不要买入诉讼。”对追求快速行情的投机者也许合理；但公众普遍采取这种态度，必会压低相关证券价格到过分水平，从而制造便宜机会。

The exploitation of special situations is a technical branch of investment which requires a somewhat unusual mentality and equipment. Probably only a small percentage of our enterprising investors are likely to engage in it, and this book is not the appropriate medium for expounding its complications.6

exploitation利用，开发mentality and equipment心态和本领（equipment 此处指知识技能等“装备”）expounding详细阐述complications复杂之处

利用特殊情况是技术性投资分支，需要较不寻常的思维和条件。积极型投资者中大概只有少数会参与，本书也不适合详述其复杂性。

Broader Implications of Our Rules for Investment

我们的投资规则的更广泛含义

Investment policy, as it has been developed here, depends in the first place on a choice by the investor of either the defensive (passive) or aggressive (enterprising) role. The aggressive investor must have a considerable knowledge of security values—enough, in fact, to warrant viewing his security operations as equivalent to a business enterprise. There is no room in this philosophy for a middle ground, or a series of gradations, between the passive and aggressive status. Many, perhaps most, investors seek to place themselves in such an intermediate category; in our opinion that is a compromise that is more likely to produce disappointment than achievement.

warrant使……有正当理由business enterprise商业企业middle ground中间地带gradations渐变的等级intermediate category中间类别compromise折中

本书投资政策首先要求投资者选择防御型（被动）或积极型角色。积极型投资者必须充分了解证券价值，足以把证券操作视为一项商业事业。这套理念不容许被动与积极之间存在中间地带或多个等级。许多、也许多数投资者想把自己放在中间类别；我们认为这种妥协更可能令人失望，而非取得成果。

As an investor you cannot soundly become “half a businessman,” expecting thereby to achieve half the normal rate of business profits on your funds.

soundly稳妥地，合理地half a businessman半个商人thereby由此

作为投资者，你不能稳妥地只做“半个商人”，却期望资金赚到正常商业利润的一半。

It follows from this reasoning that the majority of security owners should elect the defensive classification. They do not have the time, or the determination, or the mental equipment to embark upon investing as a quasi-business. They should therefore be satisfied with the excellent return now obtainable from a defensive portfolio (and with even less), and they should stoutly resist the recurrent temptation to increase this return by deviating into other paths.

elect选择mental equipment头脑上的本领，智力装备quasi-business准企业，类似经营企业的活动stoutly resist坚决抵制deviating into other paths偏离到其他路径上

因此，多数证券持有人应选择防御型。他们没有时间、决心或思维条件，把投资作为准商业活动。应满足于防御型组合目前可取得的优秀回报，甚至接受更低回报，并坚决抵抗反复出现的诱惑，不为提高收益而偏离其他路径。

The enterprising investor may properly embark upon any security operation for which his training and judgment are adequate and which appears sufficiently promising when measured by established business standards.

security operation证券操作adequate足够的，胜任的established business standards公认的商业标准

积极型投资者可以从事任何其训练和判断足以胜任，并按成熟商业标准衡量具有充分吸引力的证券操作。

In our recommendations and caveats for this group of investors we have attempted to apply such business standards. In those for the defensive investor we have been guided largely by the three requirements of underlying safety, simplicity of choice, and promise of satisfactory results, in terms of psychology as well as arithmetic. The use of these criteria has led us to exclude from the field of recommended investment a number of security classes that are normally regarded as suitable for various kinds of investors. These prohibitions were listed in our first chapter on p. 30.

caveats警告，告诫underlying safety内在安全性simplicity of choice选择简单in terms of psychology as well as arithmetic无论从心理上还是从计算上prohibitions禁令

我们给积极型投资者的建议和警告，试图采用这些商业标准。对防御型投资者则主要依据三项要求：基础安全、选择简单、结果令人满意——既在算术上，也在心理上。应用这些标准后，我们把若干通常被认为适合某类投资者的证券排除在推荐范围外；第1章第30页列出了这些禁止事项。

Let us consider a little more fully than before what is implied in these exclusions. We have advised against the purchase at “full prices” of three important categories of securities: (1) foreign bonds, (2) ordinary preferred stocks, and (3) secondary common stocks, including, of course, original offerings of such issues. By “full prices” we mean prices close to par for bonds or preferred stocks, and prices that represent about the fair business value of the enterprise in the case of common stocks. The greater number of defensive investors are to avoid these categories regardless of price; the enterprising investor is to buy them only when obtainable at bargain prices—which we define as prices not more than two-thirds of the appraisal value of the securities.

exclusions排除项full prices全价（接近公允价值的价格）original offerings首次发行（新股）close to par接近面值fair business value公允的企业价值regardless of price不论价格如何appraisal value评估价值

进一步说明这些排除意味着什么。我们反对按“全价”购买三类重要证券：（1）外国债券；（2）普通优先股；（3）二线普通股，当然包括这类股票首次发行。“全价”对债券和优先股指接近面值，对普通股指大约等于企业公平商业价值。大多数防御型投资者无论价格都应避开；积极型投资者只有在便宜价时买，即不超过估计价值三分之二。

译者补充（非原文）：本章统一把“bargain price”理解为显著低于保守估值，而不是只比近期高点便宜。格雷厄姆给出的硬参考是价格不超过估值的三分之二。

What would happen if all investors were guided by our advice in these matters? That question was considered in regard to foreign bonds, on p. 138, and we have nothing to add at this point. Investment-grade preferred stocks would be bought solely by corporations, such as insurance companies, which would benefit from the special income-tax status of stock issues owned by them.

若所有投资者都听从我们的建议，会怎样？外国债券在第138页已讨论，无须补充。投资级优先股将只由保险公司等企业购买，因为它们能享受持有股票的特殊所得税待遇。

The most troublesome consequence of our policy of exclusion is in the field of secondary common stocks. If the majority of investors, being in the defensive class, are not to buy them at all, the field of possible buyers becomes seriously restricted. Furthermore, if aggressive investors are to buy them only at bargain levels, then these issues would be doomed to sell for less than their fair value, except to the extent that they were purchased unintelligently.

Furthermore, if aggressive investors are to buy them only at bargain levels, then these issues would be doomed to sell for less than their fair value, except to the extent that they were purchased unintelligently.

此外，如果进取型投资者只在廉价水平才买它们，那么这些股票就注定要以低于公允价值的价格出售——除非有人不明智地以高价买入。

排除政策最棘手的后果出现在二线普通股。若占多数的防御型投资者完全不买，潜在买家会严重减少；积极型投资者又只在便宜水平买，那么除了被不理性买入时，这些股票似乎注定长期低于公平价值。

This may sound severe and even vaguely unethical. Yet in truth we are merely recognizing what has actually happened in this area for the greater part of the past 40 years. Secondary issues, for the most part, do fluctuate about a central level which is well below their fair value. They reach and even surpass that value at times; but this occurs in the upper reaches of bull markets, when the lessons of practical experience would argue against the soundness of paying the prevailing prices for common stocks.

这听起来严厉，甚至有点不道德。但我们只是承认过去40年大部分时间真实发生的事：二线股多数围绕远低于公平价值的中心水平波动；有时会达到甚至超过公平价值，但通常发生在牛市高处，而实践经验恰好警告不宜按当时价格买普通股。

Thus we are suggesting only that the aggressive investor recognize the facts of life as it is lived by secondary issues and that they accept the central market levels that are normal for that class as their guide in fixing their own levels for purchase.

the facts of life生活的现实（此处双关，指二线股“生存”的实际状况）central market levels市场的中心价位fixing确定

因此，我们只是建议积极型投资者承认二线股现实，把这一类别正常的市场中心水平作为确定自身买价的依据。

There is a paradox here, nevertheless. The average well-selected secondary company may be fully as promising as the average industrial leader. What the smaller concern lacks in inherent stability it may readily make up in superior possibilities of growth. Consequently it may appear illogical to many readers to term “unintelligent” the purchase of such secondary issues at their full “enterprise value.” We think that the strongest logic is that of experience. Financial history says clearly that the investor may expect satisfactory results, on the average, from secondary common stocks only if he buys them for less than their value to a private owner, that is, on a bargain basis.

paradox悖论fully as promising as完全和……一样有前景make up弥补superior possibilities of growth更高的增长可能性term称为（动词）enterprise value企业价值

What the smaller concern lacks in inherent stability it may readily make up in superior possibilities of growth.

小公司在内在稳定性上的欠缺，它可以轻易地用更大的增长潜力来弥补。

宾语提前的强调结构：What the smaller concern lacks in inherent stability 整个从句是 make up 的宾语，正常语序是 it may readily make up what it lacks … in superior possibilities of growth。concern 在本书中指“公司、企业”。

但这里存在悖论：平均而言，精心挑选的二线公司可能与平均行业龙头同样有前途；小公司内在稳定性不足，却容易由更强增长潜力弥补。因此很多读者会觉得，把按完整“企业价值”购买二线股称为“不聪明”并不合逻辑。我们认为经验的逻辑最强：金融史清楚表明，普通外部投资者平均只有以低于私人业主价值、即便宜基础买入二线普通股，才可期待满意结果。

The last sentence indicates that this principle relates to the ordinary outside investor. Anyone who can control a secondary company, or who is part of a cohesive group with such control, is fully justified in buying the shares on the same basis as if he were investing in a “close corporation” or other private business. The distinction between the position, and consequent investment policy, of insiders and of outsiders becomes more important as the enterprise itself becomes less important. It is a basic characteristic of a primary or leading company that a single detached share is ordinarily worth as much as a share in a controlling block. In secondary companies the average market value of a detached share is substantially less than its worth to a controlling owner. Because of this fact, the matter of shareholder-management relations and of those between inside and outside shareholders tends to be much more important and controversial in the case of secondary than in that of primary companies.

outside investor外部投资者cohesive group紧密团结的群体fully justified in完全有理由close corporation封闭型公司（股东少、股票不公开交易的公司）primary or leading company一线或龙头公司a single detached share单独一股零散股份controlling block构成控股权的一批股份controlling owner控股股东shareholder-management relations股东与管理层的关系

最后一句说明，这项原则针对普通外部投资者。能控制二线公司、或属于有控制权的一致行动团体者，完全有理由按投资非上市公司或私人企业的方式买股。企业越不重要，内部人与外部人的处境和投资政策差异越重要。龙头公司基本特征是，一股零散股份通常与控制性持股中的一股价值相同；二线公司中，零散股份平均市值明显低于对控制者的价值。因此股东—管理层关系以及内外股东关系，在二线公司往往更重要、更有争议。

At the end of Chapter 5 we commented on the difficulty of making any hard and fast distinction between primary and secondary companies. The many common stocks in the boundary area may properly exhibit an intermediate price behavior. It would not be illogical for an investor to buy such an issue at a small discount from its indicated or appraisal value, on the theory that it is only a small distance away from a primary classification and that it may acquire such a rating unqualifiedly in the not too distant future.

hard and fast distinction严格明确的区分boundary area边界地带indicated or appraisal value估算或评估价值unqualifiedly毫无保留地in the not too distant future在不太遥远的将来

第5章末提到，一线与二线公司很难划定硬性界限。处于边界的大量普通股可以合理呈现中间价格行为。投资者按略低于指示或估计价值买入并不违背逻辑，因为公司离一线地位不远，可能在不久后毫无保留地取得该评级。

Thus the distinction between primary and secondary issues need not be made too precise; for, if it were, then a small difference in quality must produce a large differential in justified purchase price. In saying this we are admitting a middle ground in the classification of common stocks, although we counseled against such a middle ground in the classification of investors. Our reason for this apparent inconsistency is as follows: No great harm comes from some uncertainty of viewpoint regarding a single security, because such cases are exceptional and not a great deal is at stake in the matter. But the investor’s choice as between the defensive or the aggressive status is of major consequence to him, and he should not allow himself to be confused or compromised in this basic decision.

need not be made too precise不必划得太精确if it were如果真那样做的话（虚拟语气）justified purchase price合理的买入价counseled against劝告不要apparent inconsistency表面上的不一致at stake处于危险中，利害攸关compromised妥协，动摇（此处指在决定上打折扣）

因此一线与二线证券的界限不必过度精确，否则微小质量差异就会造成巨大合理买价差异。这里我们承认普通股分类存在中间地带，虽曾反对投资者分类的中间地带。原因是：对单只证券看法稍有不确定，危害不大，因为案例少、利害有限；但投资者选择防御型还是积极型，对本人意义重大，不应在这个基本决定上混乱或妥协。

* As already noted (see p. 96, footnote †), the New Housing Authority and New Community bonds are no longer issued.
如前注所述（见第96页脚注），New Housing Authority与New Community债券已不再发行。
† Today these “lower-quality bonds” in the “special situation” area are known as distressed or defaulted bonds. When a company is in approaching) bankruptcy, its common stock becomes essentially worthless, since U.S. bankruptcy law entitles bondholders to a much stronger legal claim than shareholders. But if the company reorganizes successfully and comes out of bankruptcy, the bondholders often receive stock in the new firm, and the value of the bonds usually recovers once the company is able to pay interest again. Thus the bonds of a troubled company can perform almost as well as the common stock of a healthy company. In these special situations, as Graham puts it, “no true distinction exists between bonds and common stocks.”(or
今天，特殊情况领域的这类“低质量债券”称困境债券或违约债券。公司接近或进入破产时，普通股基本一文不值，因为美国破产法给予债券持有人远强于股东的权利。但若公司成功重组退出破产，债权人常获得新公司股票，恢复付息后债券价值通常回升。因此困境公司债券表现可能近似健康公司普通股；正如格雷厄姆所说，特殊情况下“债券与普通股没有真正区别”。
* Note very carefully what Graham is saying here. Writing in 1972, he contends that the period since 1949—a stretch of more than 22 years—is too short a period from which to draw reliable conclusions! With his mastery of mathematics, Graham never forgets that objective conclusions require very long samples of large amounts of data. The charlatans who peddle “time-tested” stock-picking gimmicks almost always base their findings on smaller samples than Graham would ever accept. (Graham often used 50-year periods to analyze past data.)
请特别留意：格雷厄姆1972年写作时认为，1949年以来超过22年的时期仍短得不足以得出可靠结论。精通数学的他始终记得，客观结论需要大量数据和很长样本。推销“久经时间考验”选股技巧的骗子，所用样本几乎总小于格雷厄姆会接受的规模；他常用50年数据。
† Today, the enterprising investor can assemble such a list over the Internet by visiting such websites as www.morningstar.com (try the Stock Quickrank tool), www.quicken.com/investments/stocks/search/full, and http://yahoo. marketguide.com.
今天积极型投资者可通过互联网股票筛选工具建立这类名单；原注列举Morningstar、Quicken与Yahoo等网站。
* Over the 10 years ending December 31, 2002, funds investing in large growth companies—today’s equivalent of what Graham calls “growth funds”—earned an annual average of 5.6%, underperforming the overall stock market by an average of 3.7 percentage points per year. However, “large value” funds investing in more reasonably priced big companies also underperformed the market over the same period (by a full percentage point per year). Is the problem merely that growth funds cannot reliably select stocks that will outperform the market in the future? Or is it that the high costs of running the average fund (whether it buys growth or “value” companies) exceed any extra return the managers can earn with their stock picks? To update fund performance by type, see www.morningstar.com, “Category Returns.” For an enlightening reminder of how perishable the performance of different investment styles can be, see www.callan.com/resource/periodic_ table/pertable.pdf.
截至2002年12月31日十年，投资大型成长公司的基金年均回报5.6%，每年平均落后整体股市3.7个百分点；但投资价格较合理大公司的“大盘价值”基金同期也落后市场整整1个百分点。问题也许不只在成长基金难以挑出未来赢家，还在普通基金的高运营成本超过经理选股能创造的超额收益。不同投资风格的表现也很容易消逝。
* Graham makes this point to remind you that an “enterprising” investor is not one who takes more risk than average or who buys “aggressive growth” stocks; an enterprising investor is simply one who is willing to put in extra time and effort in researching his or her portfolio.
格雷厄姆提醒：“积极型”不是承担高于平均的风险，也不是买“激进成长股”，而只是愿意投入更多时间和精力研究组合。
† Notice that Graham insists on calculating the price/earnings ratio based on a multiyear average of past earnings. That way, you lower the odds that you will overestimate a company’s value based on a temporarily high burst of profitability. Imagine that a company earned $3 per share over the past 12 months, but an average of only 50 cents per share over the previous six years. Which number—the sudden $3 or the steady 50 cents—is more likely to represent a sustainable trend? At 25 times the $3 it earned in the most recent year, the stock would be priced at $75. But at 25 times the average earnings of the past seven years ($6 in total earnings, divided by seven, equals 85.7 cents per share in average annual earnings), the stock would be priced at only $21.43. Which number you pick makes a big difference. Finally, it’s worth noting that the prevailing method on Wall Street today—basing price/earnings ratios primarily on “next year’s earnings”—would be anathema to Graham. How can you value a company based on earnings it hasn’t even generated yet? That’s like setting house prices based on a rumor that Cinderella will be building her new castle right around the corner.
格雷厄姆坚持用多年平均历史盈利计算市盈率，以降低暂时利润暴增导致高估的概率。假设公司最近一年每股赚3美元，前六年平均仅0.50美元，哪个更可持续？按最近3美元的25倍，股价75美元；七年总盈利6美元，年均0.857美元，按25倍只值21.43美元。选哪个数字影响巨大。今天华尔街主要用“明年盈利”算市盈率，这会令格雷厄姆厌恶：公司尚未赚到的盈利怎能用于估值？这像听说灰姑娘要在附近建城堡，就据此定房价。
* Recent examples hammer Graham’s point home. On September 21, 2000, Intel Corp., the maker of computer chips, announced that it expected its revenues to grow by up to 5% in the next quarter. At first blush, that sounds great; most big companies would be delighted to increase their sales by 5% in just three months. But in response, Intel’s stock dropped 22%, a one-day loss of nearly $91 billion in total value. Why? Wall Street’s analysts had expected Intel’s revenue to rise by up to 10%. Similarly, on February 21, 2001, EMC Corp., a data-storage firm, announced that it expected its revenues to grow by at least 25% in 2001—but that a new caution among customers “may lead to longer selling cycles.” On that whiff of hesitation, EMC’s shares lost 12.8% of their value in a single day.
近年案例印证此点。2000年9月21日Intel预计下季收入最多增长5%，多数大公司会很满意，但股价一天跌22%、市值损失近910亿美元，因为分析师预期增长最多10%。2001年2月21日，数据存储公司EMC预计全年收入至少增长25%，只补充客户更谨慎“可能延长销售周期”，股票一天就跌12.8%。
* Today’s equivalent of investors “who have a close relationship with the particular company” are so-called control persons—senior managers or directors who help run the company and own huge blocks of stock. Executives like Bill Gates of Microsoft or Warren Buffett of Berkshire Hathaway have direct control over a company’s destiny—and outside investors want to see these chief executives maintain their large shareholdings as a vote of confidence. But less-senior managers and rank-and-file workers cannot influence the company’s share price with their individual decisions; thus they should not put more than a small percentage of their assets in their own employer’s stock. As for outside investors, no matter how well they think they know the company, the same objection applies.
今天与公司“关系密切”的投资者相当于控制人，即参与管理并持有大量股份的高管或董事。Microsoft的Bill Gates、Berkshire Hathaway的Warren Buffett能直接影响公司命运，外部投资者也希望其维持大量持股以表信心。但较低级经理和普通员工无法靠个人决定影响股价，不应把超过很小比例的资产放在雇主股票中；外部投资者无论自认多了解公司也一样。

买入道指中最便宜股票的策略如今昵称“Dogs of the Dow”（道指狗股法）。

But Pfizer’s shares surged ahead when research later showed that there was no cause for alarm; the stock gained roughly a third over the next two years. A company with an ordinary record cannot, without confusing the term, be called a growth company or a “growth stock” merely because its proponent expects it to do better than the average in the future. It is just a “promising company.” Graham is making a subtle but important point: If the definition of a growth stock is a company that will thrive in the future, then that’s not a definition at all, but wishful thinking. It’s like calling a sports team “the champions” before the season is over. This wishful thinking persists today; among mutual funds, “growth” portfolios describe their holdings as companies with “above-average growth potential” or “favorable prospects for earnings growth.” A better definition might be companies whose net earnings per share have increased by an annual average of at least 15% for at least five years running. (Meeting this definition in the past does not ensure that a company will meet it in the future.)

CHAPTER 08

投资者与市场波动

The Investor and Market Fluctuations

如何利用“市场先生”，而不是被他的情绪操纵？

Chapter 8The Investor and Market Fluctuations第8章 投资者与市场波动

本章导读这是全书最核心的章节之一。格雷厄姆先承认：只要持有股票，价格波动就无法避免，投资者必须在财务和心理上都做好准备。想从波动中获利有两条路：择时（预测涨跌）和估价（低于价值时买、高于价值时卖）。他断言，把重心放在预测上的人最终会变成投机者；道氏理论和 1950 年代的公式化投资计划都证明，一种方法一旦流行，恰好就是它开始失灵的时候。随后他转向投资者自己的组合：应当事先接受持仓上涨 50% 又回落三分之一的“大概率”，并用机械的股债比例调整给自己“找点事做”，以免被牛市情绪裹挟。本章的理论核心是“企业估值与股市估值”的区分：上市股东有双重身份，既是企业的部分所有者，又握着一张随时可卖的纸。由此引出一个悖论——公司越优秀、溢价越高，股价就越依赖市场情绪、波动越剧烈（IBM、施乐的暴跌即是例证），因此保守投资者不妨集中于价格不超过有形资产价值三分之一以上的股票。A. & P. 的故事展示了市场如何在 1938 年把一家大企业以低于净流动资产的价格“白送”，又在 1961 年以 30 倍市盈率追捧它。接着是著名的“市场先生”寓言：市场每天报价，你可以利用它，也可以完全不理它；报价是给你的选择权，不是命令。全章结论只有一句：价格波动对真正的投资者只有一种意义——大跌时提供买入机会，大涨时提供卖出机会；其余时间盯住股息和经营业绩就够了。最后一部分讨论债券：即使本息安全无虞，长期债券价格也会随利率大幅波动，投资者要么接受波动，要么选储蓄债券，并可仿效银行按“摊余成本”记账。

To the extent that the investor’s funds are placed in high-grade bonds of relatively short maturity—say, of seven years or less—he will not be affected significantly by changes in market prices and need not take them into account. (This applies also to his holdings of U.S. savings bonds, which he can always turn in at his cost price or more.) His longer-term bonds may have relatively wide price swings during their lifetimes, and his common-stock portfolio is almost certain to fluctuate in value over any period of several years.

如果投资者把资金放在期限较短的高等级债券中，比如七年以内的债券，那么市场价格变化对他的影响不会太大，也不必特别理会。（美国储蓄债券也是如此，因为他随时可以按不低于成本的价格兑回。）期限较长的债券在存续期内，价格可能大幅起落；而普通股组合只要持有数年，市值几乎肯定会发生波动。

The investor should know about these possibilities and should be prepared for them both financially and psychologically. He will want to benefit from changes in market levels—certainly through an advance in the value of his stock holdings as time goes on, and perhaps also by making purchases and sales at advantageous prices. This interest on his part is inevitable, and legitimate enough. But it involves the very real danger that it will lead him into speculative attitudes and activities. It is easy for us to tell you not to speculate; the hard thing will be for you to follow this advice. Let us repeat what we said at the outset: If you want to speculate do so with your eyes open, knowing that you will probably lose money in the end; be sure to limit the amount at risk and to separate it completely from your investment program.

advance上涨（本书常用）on his part就他而言，他这方面的legitimate正当的，合理的speculative投机性的at the outset一开始with your eyes open清醒地，明知后果地the amount at risk承担风险的金额investment program投资计划

投资者应当知道这些情况可能发生，并在财务和心理上都做好准备。他当然希望从市场水平的变化中获益：随着时间推移，持有的股票升值；也可能在有利的价格上买进和卖出。这样的愿望无法避免，也完全正当。危险在于，它很容易把人引向投机心态和投机行为。劝你不要投机很容易，真正难的是让你照做。我们再重复开篇的忠告：如果你想投机，就要清醒地去做，明白自己最终很可能亏钱；务必限制投入投机的金额，并把它与投资计划彻底分开。

We shall deal first with the more important subject of price changes in common stocks, and pass later to the area of bonds. In Chapter 3 we supplied a historical survey of the stock market’s action over the past hundred years. In this section we shall return to that material from time to time, in order to see what the past record promises the investor—in either the form of long-term appreciation of a portfolio held relatively unchanged through successive rises and declines, or in the possibilities of buying near bear-market lows and selling not too far below bull-market highs.

我们先讨论更重要的普通股价格变化，之后再谈债券。第3章回顾了过去一百年的股市走势。本节还会不时引用那些资料，看看历史记录能给投资者带来什么：是让一个大体不动的组合经历一轮又一轮涨跌后获得长期升值，还是在熊市低位附近买入、在离牛市高点不太远的地方卖出。

Market Fluctuations as a Guide to Investment Decisions

以市场波动指导投资决策

Since common stocks, even of investment grade, are subject to recurrent and wide fluctuations in their prices, the intelligent investor should be interested in the possibilities of profiting from these pendulum swings. There are two possible ways by which he may try to do this: the way of timing and the way of pricing. By timing we mean the endeavor to anticipate the action of the stock market—to buy or hold when the future course is deemed to be upward, to sell or refrain from buying when the course is downward. By pricing we mean the endeavor to buy stocks when they are quoted below their fair value and to sell them when they rise above such value. A less ambitious form of pricing is the simple effort to make sure that when you buy you do not pay too much for your stocks. This may suffice for the defensive investor, whose emphasis is on long-pull holding; but as such it represents an essential minimum of attention to market levels.1

investment grade投资级的are subject to容易受到，难免有recurrent反复出现的pendulum swings钟摆式的摆动timing择时pricing估价（按价格高低决定买卖）endeavor努力，尝试refrain from避免，克制不做quoted报价fair value公允价值，合理价值long-pull holding长期持有

即使是投资级普通股，价格也会反复出现大幅波动，所以聪明的投资者自然会关心怎样从这种钟摆式摆动中获益。办法有两种：择时和估价。所谓择时，是预测市场下一步怎么走：认为将上涨时买入或持有，认为将下跌时卖出或暂缓买入。所谓估价，是在股价低于合理价值时买入，高于合理价值时卖出。还有一种没那么进取的估价法：买入时只求不为股票付出过高的价格。对重在长期持有的防御型投资者来说，这样也许就够了；但至少要对整体价格水平保持这点基本关注。

译者补充（非原文）：例：你判断一家公司的合理价值约为100元，70元买入属于估价；因为猜明天会涨而在任何价格买入，则属于择时。格雷厄姆更信任前者。

We are convinced that the intelligent investor can derive satisfactory results from pricing of either type. We are equally sure that if he places his emphasis on timing, in the sense of forecasting, he will end up as a speculator and with a speculator’s financial results. This distinction may seem rather tenuous to the layman, and it is not commonly accepted on Wall Street. As a matter of business practice, or perhaps of thoroughgoing conviction, the stock brokers and the investment services seem wedded to the principle that both investors and speculators in common stocks should devote careful attention to market forecasts.

derive获得end up as最终成为tenuous牵强的，站不住脚的layman外行thoroughgoing conviction彻底的信念wedded to执着于，固守investment services投资咨询服务机构

我们相信，按上述任一种估价方式行事，聪明的投资者都能得到令人满意的结果。我们同样确信，如果他把重点放在预测意义上的择时，最终就会变成投机者，并得到投机者通常得到的财务结果。在外行看来，这个区别也许很勉强，华尔街也不普遍接受。无论出于商业惯例，还是出于根深蒂固的信念，股票经纪人和投资咨询机构似乎都认定：普通股投资者和投机者都应认真研究市场预测。

The farther one gets from Wall Street, the more skepticism one will find, we believe, as to the pretensions of stock-market forecasting or timing. The investor can scarcely take seriously the innumerable predictions which appear almost daily and are his for the asking. Yet in many cases he pays attention to them and even acts upon them. Why? Because he has been persuaded that it is important for him to form some opinion of the future course of the stock market, and because he feels that the brokerage or service forecast is at least more dependable than his own.11

我们认为，离华尔街越远，人们就越怀疑股市预测或择时所声称的本领。几乎每天都有无数预测免费送到投资者眼前，他很难把这些东西当真。可事实上，很多人不仅会看，还会据此行动。为什么？因为他们已经相信，自己必须对股市未来走势形成某种判断；同时又觉得，经纪商或咨询机构的预测至少比自己的判断可靠。

We lack space here to discuss in detail the pros and cons of market forecasting. A great deal of brain power goes into this field, and undoubtedly some people can make money by being good stock-market analysts. But it is absurd to think that the general public can ever make money out of market forecasts. For who will buy when the general public, at a given signal, rushes to sell out at a profit? If you, the reader, expect to get rich over the years by following some system or leadership in market forecasting, you must be expecting to try to do what countless others are aiming at, and to be able to do it better than your numerous competitors in the market. There is no basis either in logic or in experience for assuming that any typical or average investor can anticipate market movements more successfully than the general public, of which he is himself a part.

篇幅有限，我们无法在这里详谈市场预测的利弊。这个领域投入了大量聪明才智，毫无疑问，确实有人能凭借出色的市场分析赚钱。但若认为广大公众都能靠市场预测赚钱，那就荒唐了：当所有人收到同一个信号、一起想获利卖出时，谁来接盘？如果你打算长期追随某套预测系统或某位领袖而致富，就等于认定自己能和无数抱有相同目标的人做同一件事，并且做得比众多竞争者更好。无论从逻辑还是经验看，都没有理由认为一个普通投资者能比公众整体更准确地预判市场，而他自己本来就是公众的一员。

There is one aspect of the “timing” philosophy which seems to have escaped everyone’s notice. Timing is of great psychological importance to the speculator because he wants to make his profit in a hurry. The idea of waiting a year before his stock moves up is repugnant to him. But a waiting period, as such, is of no consequence to the investor. What advantage is there to him in having his money uninvested until he receives some (presumably) trustworthy signal that the time has come to buy? He enjoys an advantage only if by waiting he succeeds in buying later at a sufficiently lower price to offset his loss of dividend income. What this means is that timing is of no real value to the investor unless it coincides with pricing—that is, unless it enables him to repurchase his shares at substantially under his previous selling price.

择时理念有一点似乎一直没人注意。择时对投机者的心理意义很大，因为他急于赚钱，无法忍受买入后等上一年才上涨。但等待本身对投资者并不重要。为了等到某个据说可靠的买入信号而让资金闲置，对他有什么好处？只有当等待使他日后能以足够低的价格买入，低价带来的好处又超过等待期间损失的股息时，他才真正占到便宜。换句话说，择时只有与估价重合才对投资者有实际价值，也就是让他能以显著低于此前卖出价的价格买回股票。

译者补充（非原文）：等待本身不会创造收益。假设卖出后空等一年，损失4元股息；只有后来买回时便宜超过4元，等待才有经济意义。

In this respect the famous Dow theory for timing purchases and sales has had an unusual history.* Briefly, this technique takes its signal to buy from a special kind of “breakthrough” of the stock averages on the up side, and its selling signal from a similar breakthrough on the down side. The calculated—not necessarily actual—results of using this method showed an almost unbroken series of profits in operations from 1897 to the early 1960s. On the basis of this presentation the practical value of the Dow theory would have appeared firmly established; the doubt, if any, would apply to the dependability of this published “record” as a picture of what a Dow theorist would actually have done in the market.

Dow theory道氏理论（依据道琼斯指数走势判断趋势的技术分析理论）breakthrough突破（指数突破前期高点或低点）stock averages股票平均指数on the up side向上unbroken series连续不断的一系列operations操作，交易（本书常用）if any如果有的话dependability可靠性

著名的道氏理论用来决定买卖时机，其历史颇不寻常。简而言之，这套方法把股价平均指数向上的某种特殊“突破”视为买入信号，把向下的类似突破视为卖出信号。按计算得出的结果（不一定等于真实交易结果），从1897年到20世纪60年代初，运用此法几乎连续获利。照这份记录看，道氏理论的实用价值似乎已经得到坚实证明；若还有疑问，也只在于公开的“业绩记录”是否真的反映了一名道氏理论信徒会在市场中怎样操作。

A closer study of the figures indicates that the quality of the results shown by the Dow theory changed radically after 1938—a few years after the theory had begun to be taken seriously on Wall Street. Its spectacular achievement had been in giving a sell signal, at 306, about a month before the 1929 crash and in keeping its followers out of the long bear market until things had pretty well righted themselves, at 84, in 1933. But from 1938 on the Dow theory operated mainly by taking its practitioners out at a pretty good price but then putting them back in again at a higher price. For nearly 30 years thereafter, one would have done appreciably better by just buying and holding the DJIA.2

仔细研究数据可以发现，道氏理论的成绩在1938年以后发生了根本变化，而那正是华尔街开始认真看待这套理论的几年后。它最精彩的表现，是在1929年股灾前约一个月、指数处于306点时发出卖出信号，并让追随者避开漫长熊市，直到1933年市场在84点附近基本恢复正常。然而1938年以后，这套理论主要是让使用者以还不错的价格卖出，随后又以更高的价格买回来。此后近30年，单纯买入并持有道琼斯工业平均指数，成绩会明显更好。

In our view, based on much study of this problem, the change in the Dow-theory results is not accidental. It demonstrates an inherent characteristic of forecasting and trading formulas in the fields of business and finance. Those formulas that gain adherents and importance do so because they have worked well over a period, or sometimes merely because they have been plausibly adapted to the statistical record of the past. But as their acceptance increases, their reliability tends to diminish. This happens for two reasons: First, the passage of time brings new conditions which the old formula no longer fits. Second, in stock-market affairs the popularity of a trading theory has itself an influence on the market’s behavior which detracts in the long run from its profit-making possibilities. (The popularity of something like the Dow theory may seem to create its own vindication, since it would make the market advance or decline by the very action of its followers when a buying or selling signal is given. A “stampede” of this kind is, of course, much more of a danger than an advantage to the public trader.)

我们深入研究过这个问题，认为道氏理论成绩的变化并非偶然。它揭示了商业和金融领域各种预测公式与交易公式的内在特点：一套公式会赢得追随者和影响力，是因为它曾在一段时期内奏效，有时甚至只是因为它看起来很好地拟合了过去的数据。但接受它的人越多，可靠性往往越低。原因有二。第一，时间会带来旧公式无法适应的新条件。第二，在股市里，某套交易理论一旦流行，本身就会改变市场行为，长期获利空间反而被削弱。（道氏理论一类的方法看似可能“自我实现”：买卖信号一出，追随者的集体行动就推动市场上涨或下跌。但对普通交易者而言，这种蜂拥而动造成的危险远大于好处。）

译者补充（非原文）：一套公开规则如果要求所有人在同一信号下买入，大家的抢买会先把价格推高；后来者能赚到的差价自然变小。

Buy-Low–Sell-High Approach

低买高卖法

We are convinced that the average investor cannot deal successfully with price movements by endeavoring to forecast them. Can he benefit from them after they have taken place—i.e., by buying after each major decline and selling out after each major advance? The fluctuations of the market over a period of many years prior to 1950 lent considerable encouragement to that idea. In fact, a classic definition of a “shrewd investor” was “one who bought in a bear market when everyone else was selling, and sold out in a bull market when everyone else was buying.” If we examine our Chart I, covering the fluctuations of the Standard & Poor’s composite index between 1900 and 1970, and the supporting figures in Table 3-1 (p.66), we can readily see why this viewpoint appeared valid until fairly recent years.

我们确信，普通投资者无法靠预测价格走势成功应对波动。那么，能否等波动发生后再利用它，即每次大跌后买入、每次大涨后卖出？1950年以前许多年的市场起落，确实很支持这个想法。经典的“精明投资者”甚至被定义为：“熊市里人人卖出时买入，牛市里人人买入时卖出的人。”只要查看图表I所列1900至1970年标准普尔综合指数的波动，以及表3-1中的相关数据，就不难理解为什么直到较近的年代，这种看法一直显得合理。

Between 1897 and 1949 there were ten complete market cycles, running from bear-market low to bull-market high and back to bear-market low. Six of these took no longer than four years, four ran for six or seven years, and one—the famous “new-era” cycle of 1921–1932—lasted eleven years. The percentage of advance from the lows to highs ranged from 44% to 500%, with most between about 50% and 100%. The percentage of subsequent declines ranged from 24% to 89%, with most found between 40% and 50%. (It should be remembered that a decline of 50% fully offsets a preceding advance of 100%.)

market cycles市场周期new-era“新时代”（指 1920 年代人们认为经济已进入永久繁荣的新时代）ranged from范围从……到……subsequent随后的offsets抵消preceding之前的

1897至1949年间，市场经历了十个完整周期：从熊市低点升至牛市高点，再回到熊市低点。其中六个周期不超过四年，四个持续六至七年；著名的1921至1932年“新时代”周期则长达十一年。从低点到高点的涨幅在44%至500%之间，多数约为50%至100%；此后的跌幅在24%至89%之间，多数为40%至50%。（要记住，先上涨100%，随后下跌50%，就会把此前涨幅全部抹去。）

Nearly all the bull markets had a number of well-defined characteristics in common, such as (1) a historically high price level, (2) high price/earnings ratios, (3) low dividend yields as against bond yields, (4) much speculation on margin, and (5) many offerings of new common-stock issues of poor quality. Thus to the student of stock-market history it appeared that the intelligent investor should have been able to identify the recurrent bear and bull markets, to buy in the former and sell in the latter, and to do so for the most part at reasonably short intervals of time. Various methods were developed for determining buying and selling levels of the general market, based on either value factors or percentage movements of prices or both.

几乎所有牛市都有若干清晰的共同特征，例如：价格处于历史高位；市盈率偏高；相对于债券收益率，股息率偏低；保证金投机盛行；大量质量低劣的普通股新股上市。因此，研究股市历史的人会觉得，聪明的投资者理应能够识别反复出现的熊市与牛市，在前者买入、后者卖出，而且多数时候两次行动之间不会相隔太久。人们也设计了各种方法，用价值因素、股价涨跌幅，或两者结合来确定整体市场的买卖水平。

But we must point out that even prior to the unprecedented bull market that began in 1949, there were sufficient variations in the successive market cycles to complicate and sometimes frustrate the desirable process of buying low and selling high. The most notable of these departures, of course, was the great bull market of the late 1920s, which threw all calculations badly out of gear.* Even in 1949, therefore, it was by no means a certainty that the investor could base his financial policies and procedures mainly on the endeavor to buy at low levels in bear markets and to sell out at high levels in bull markets.

unprecedented史无前例的variations变化，差异frustrate挫败，使无法实现（此处不是“使沮丧”）departures偏离（常规的情况）threw all calculations badly out of gear使所有的计算完全失灵（out of gear：脱离齿轮，失调）by no means绝不a certainty确定的事

但我们必须指出，即使在1949年开始的空前牛市之前，各轮市场周期之间也已经存在足够多的差异，使“低买高卖”变得复杂，有时甚至完全失效。最突出的偏离当然是20世纪20年代末的大牛市，它把所有计算都打乱了。所以，即使在1949年，投资者也绝不能确信自己可以把财务政策和操作方法主要建立在“熊市低位买入、牛市高位卖出”上。

It turned out, in the sequel, that the opposite was true. The market’s behavior in the past 20 years has not followed the former pattern, nor obeyed what once were well-established danger signals, nor permitted its successful exploitation by applying old rules for buying low and selling high. Whether the old, fairly regular bull-and-bear-market pattern will eventually return we do not know. But it seems unrealistic to us for the investor to endeavor to base his present policy on the classic formula—i.e., to wait for demonstrable bear-market levels before buying any common stocks. Our recommended policy has, however, made provision for changes in the proportion of common stocks to bonds in the portfolio, if the investor chooses to do so, according as the level of stock prices appears less or more attractive by value standards.*

后来的事实恰好证明相反的一面。过去20年的市场没有沿袭旧模式，也不听从过去那些公认的危险信号；用旧规则低买高卖，也无法稳定获利。旧日相对规律的牛熊周期会不会回来，我们不知道。但若投资者仍把当前策略建立在经典公式上，即非要等到市场明显进入熊市低位才买任何普通股，我们认为并不现实。不过，我们建议的策略允许投资者在愿意的情况下，根据股价按价值标准看起来较便宜还是较昂贵，调整组合中股票与债券的比例。

Formula Plans

公式化投资计划

In the early years of the stock-market rise that began in 1949–50 considerable interest was attracted to various methods of taking advantage of the stock market’s cycles. These have been known as “formula investment plans.” The essence of all such plans—except the simple case of dollar averaging—is that the investor automatically does some selling of common stocks when the market advances substantially. In many of them a very large rise in the market level would result in the sale of all common-stock holdings; others provided for retention of a minor proportion of equities under all circumstances.

formula investment plans公式化投资计划essence本质，要点dollar averaging定期定额投资法（即 dollar-cost averaging）provided for规定retention保留equities股票，股权under all circumstances在任何情况下

1949至1950年开始的股市上涨初期，利用市场周期的各种方法引起了广泛兴趣，人们称之为“公式投资计划”。除简单的定期定额投资外，这些计划的共同核心是：市场大幅上涨时，投资者自动卖掉一部分普通股。许多方案规定，市场涨得非常高时要卖掉全部股票；另一些则要求无论如何都保留一小部分权益资产。

This approach had the double appeal of sounding logical (and conservative) and of showing excellent results when applied retrospectively to the stock market over many years in the past. Unfortunately, its vogue grew greatest at the very time when it was destined to work least well. Many of the “formula planners” found themselves entirely or nearly out of the stock market at some level in the middle 1950s. True, they had realized excellent profits, but in a broad sense the market “ran away” from them thereafter, and their formulas gave them little opportunity to buy back a common-stock position.*

double appeal双重吸引力retrospectively回溯地，用过去的数据回测vogue流行，风行destined注定realized实现（利润）ran away（市场）一路上涨、把他们甩在后面position头寸，持仓

这种办法有双重吸引力：听起来既合乎逻辑又保守，而且把它套用到过去多年的市场数据上，成绩十分出色。遗憾的是，它最流行的时候，恰好也是注定最不好用的时候。20世纪50年代中期，许多采用公式的人在某个点位已经完全或几乎完全退出股市。他们确实实现了可观利润，但此后市场大体上一路跑远，而公式几乎没给他们重新建立股票仓位的机会。

There is a similarity between the experience of those adopting the formula-investing approach in the early 1950s and those who embraced the purely mechanical version of the Dow theory some 20 years earlier. In both cases the advent of popularity marked almost the exact moment when the system ceased to work well. We have had a like discomfiting experience with our own “central value method” of determining indicated buying and selling levels of the Dow Jones Industrial Average. The moral seems to be that any approach to moneymaking in the stock market which can be easily described and followed by a lot of people is by its terms too simple and too easy to last.† Spinoza’s concluding remark applies to Wall Street as well as to philosophy: “All things excellent are as difficult as they are rare.”

20世纪50年代初采用公式投资的人，与约20年前采用纯机械版道氏理论的人，经历十分相似：两套系统都在走红的那一刻附近开始失灵。我们自己的“中央价值法”用于判断道琼斯工业平均指数买卖水平，也有过同样令人难堪的经历。教训似乎是：任何能轻易讲清、又能被很多人照着做的股市赚钱方法，正因为太简单、太容易，便很难长久。斯宾诺莎的结语既适用于哲学，也适用于华尔街：“一切卓越之物，既困难又稀少。”

译者补充（非原文）：这不是说简单方法一定无效，而是说“人人照做还能持续获得超额收益”很难成立。分散、低成本等简单原则不依赖别人接盘，性质不同。

Market Fluctuations of the Investor’s Portfolio

投资者投资组合的市场波动

Every investor who owns common stocks must expect to see them fluctuate in value over the years. The behavior of the DJIA since our last edition was written in 1964 probably reflects pretty well what has happened to the stock portfolio of a conservative investor who limited his stock holdings to those of large, prominent, and conservatively financed corporations. The overall value advanced from an average level of about 890 to a high of 995 in 1966 (and 985 again in 1968), fell to 631 in 1970, and made an almost full recovery to 940 in early 1971. (Since the individual issues set their high and low marks at different times, the fluctuations in the Dow Jones group as a whole are less severe than those in the separate components.) We have traced through the price fluctuations of other types of diversified and conservative common-stock portfolios and we find that the overall results are not likely to be markedly different from the above. In general, the shares of second-line companies* fluctuate more widely than the major ones, but this does not necessarily mean that a group of well-established but smaller companies will make a poorer showing over a fairly long period. In any case the investor may as well resign himself in advance to the probability rather than the mere possibility that most of his holdings will advance, say, 50% or more from their low point and decline the equivalent one-third or more from their high point at various periods in the next five years.†

In any case the investor may as well resign himself in advance to the probability rather than the mere possibility that most of his holdings will advance, say, 50% or more from their low point and decline the equivalent one-third or more from their high point at various periods in the next five years.

无论如何，投资者不妨事先就认命地接受这样一个大概率事件——而不只是“可能”——即在未来五年的不同时期，他的大部分持仓会从低点上涨 50% 或更多，又从高点下跌相当于三分之一或更多。

骨架是 resign himself to the probability that…（认命地接受……的大概率），中间插入 rather than the mere possibility 作对比；that 从句是 probability 的同位语。注意 in advance 是“事先”，而后面的 advance 是动词“上涨”。一跌三分之一恰好抵消一涨 50%，所以说 the equivalent。

每个持有普通股的投资者，都必须预料到它们的价值会随年份波动。自本书上一版于1964年写成以来，道琼斯工业平均指数的表现，大概很能代表保守投资者组合的经历；这类投资者只持有规模大、声誉好、财务稳健的公司。指数平均水平从约890点升到1966年的995点高位（1968年又到985点），1970年跌至631点，1971年初又几乎完全恢复到940点。（个股达到高低点的时间不同，所以道指整体的波动小于各成分股分别出现的波动。）我们也追踪了其他类型的分散化保守股票组合，整体结果大致相近。通常，二线公司的股价比大公司波动更大，但这不表示一组经营扎实的中小公司长期表现一定更差。无论如何，投资者最好事先接受一种“很可能发生”的情况，而不只是把它看成一种可能：未来五年里，他的大多数持仓都可能从低点上涨50%甚至更多，也可能从高点下跌相当于三分之一甚至更多。

译者补充（非原文）：10元涨50%会到15元；15元再跌三分之一（5元），恰好回到10元。上涨50%与随后下跌33.3%在金额上互相抵消。

A serious investor is not likely to believe that the day-to-day or even month-to-month fluctuations of the stock market make him richer or poorer. But what about the longer-term and wider changes? Here practical questions present themselves, and the psychological problems are likely to grow complicated. A substantial rise in the market is at once a legitimate reason for satisfaction and a cause for prudent concern, but it may also bring a strong temptation toward imprudent action. Your shares have advanced, good! You are richer than you were, good! But has the price risen too high, and should you think of selling? Or should you kick yourself for not having bought more shares when the level was lower? Or—worst thought of all—should you now give way to the bull-market atmosphere, become infected with the enthusiasm, the overconfidence and the greed of the great public (of which, after all, you are a part), and make larger and dangerous commitments? Presented thus in print, the answer to the last question is a self-evident no, but even the intelligent investor is likely to need considerable will power to keep from following the crowd.

严肃的投资者大概不会认为，股市每天甚至每月的涨跌让自己变富或变穷。但时间更长、幅度更大的变化又该怎么看？这时实际问题会出现，心理问题也会复杂起来。市场大涨，既有充分理由令人高兴，也有理由让人谨慎；同时，它还可能诱使人做出不明智的行动。你的股票涨了，很好！你比以前富了，很好！但价格是否已经太高，该不该卖？还是该责怪自己低位时没多买？又或者，最糟的是，你会不会向牛市气氛投降，感染大众的兴奋、过度自信和贪婪，投入更多资金并承担危险？写在纸上，最后一个问题的答案显然是“不”；但即使聪明的投资者，也需要很强的意志力才能不随大流。

It is for these reasons of human nature, even more than by calculation of financial gain or loss, that we favor some kind of mechanical method for varying the proportion of bonds to stocks in the investor’s portfolio. The chief advantage, perhaps, is that such a formula will give him something to do. As the market advances he will from time to time make sales out of his stockholdings, putting the proceeds into bonds; as it declines he will reverse the procedure. These activities will provide some outlet for his otherwise too-pent-up energies. If he is the right kind of investor he will take added satisfaction from the thought that his operations are exactly opposite from those of the crowd.*

It is for these reasons of human nature, even more than by calculation of financial gain or loss, that we favor some kind of mechanical method for varying the proportion of bonds to stocks in the investor’s portfolio.

正是出于这些人性上的原因——甚至更甚于对财务得失的计算——我们才主张用某种机械的方法来调整投资组合中债券与股票的比例。

It is … that … 是强调句，被强调的是原因状语 for these reasons of human nature；even more than by calculation… 是插入的比较，说明人性因素比盈亏计算更重要。favor 在这里是动词“赞成、主张”。

正因为人性如此，而不仅是出于盈亏计算，我们赞成用某种机械方法调整组合中债券与股票的比例。它最大的好处也许只是让投资者“有事可做”。市场上涨时，他不时卖出一部分股票，把所得转入债券；市场下跌时，再反向操作。这些动作能给无处释放的冲动找个出口。如果他确实是合格的投资者，还会因为自己的操作恰好与大众相反而多一份满足。

译者补充（非原文）：例如把股债目标定为50:50。股票上涨后占到60%，就卖一部分股票、补债券，恢复50:50；下跌时反向操作。这就是再平衡。

Business Valuations versus Stock-Market Valuations

企业估值与股市估值

The impact of market fluctuations upon the investor’s true situation may be considered also from the standpoint of the shareholder as the part owner of various businesses. The holder of marketable shares actually has a double status, and with it the privilege of taking advantage of either at his choice. On the one hand his position is analogous to that of a minority shareholder or silent partner in a private business. Here his results are entirely dependent on the profits of the enterprise or on a change in the underlying value of its assets. He would usually determine the value of such a private-business interest by calculating his share of the net worth as shown in the most recent balance sheet. On the other hand, the common-stock investor holds a piece of paper, an engraved stock certificate, which can be sold in a matter of minutes at a price which varies from moment to moment—when the market is open, that is—and often is far removed from the balance-sheet value.*

要理解市场波动对投资者真实处境的影响，还可以从股东是多家企业部分所有者的角度来看。持有可交易股票的人其实有双重身份，并有权选择利用其中任何一种。一方面，他类似于非上市企业的小股东或沉默合伙人；投资结果完全取决于企业利润或基础资产价值的变化。通常，他会依据最新资产负债表显示的净资产，计算自己在这家私人企业中的权益价值。另一方面，普通股投资者手中又有一张股票凭证，只要市场开门，几分钟内就能按不断变化的价格卖掉；这个价格往往与账面价值相去甚远。

The development of the stock market in recent decades has made the typical investor more dependent on the course of price quotations and less free than formerly to consider himself merely a business owner. The reason is that the successful enterprises in which he is likely to concentrate his holdings sell almost constantly at prices well above their net asset value (or book value, or “balance-sheet value”). In paying these market premiums the investor gives precious hostages to fortune, for he must depend on the stock market itself to validate his commitments.†

price quotations市场报价net asset value净资产价值book value账面价值market premiums市场溢价gives precious hostages to fortune把珍贵的人质交到命运手里（典出培根，指一旦付出就受制于运气）validate证实……正当、有效

近几十年股市的发展，使典型投资者比过去更依赖每天的报价，也更难只把自己看成企业所有者。原因是，他最可能集中持有的成功企业，股价几乎总是显著高于净资产价值（也叫账面价值或资产负债表价值）。投资者支付这种市场溢价，就把一项宝贵的东西交给了命运作人质：他必须依赖市场日后继续认可自己当初付出的价格。

译者补充（非原文）：若账面价值每股20元、你以100元买入，其中80元依赖市场继续认可公司的盈利和前景；预期稍变，溢价便可能快速收缩。

This is a factor of prime importance in present-day investing, and it has received less attention than it deserves. The whole structure of stock-market quotations contains a built-in contradiction. The better a company’s record and prospects, the less relationship the price of its shares will have to their book value. But the greater the premium above book value, the less certain the basis of determining its intrinsic value—i.e., the more this “value” will depend on the changing moods and measurements of the stock market. Thus we reach the final paradox, that the more successful the company, the greater are likely to be the fluctuations in the price of its shares. This really means that, in a very real sense, the better the quality of a common stock, the more speculative it is likely to be—at least as compared with the unspectacular middle-grade issues.* (What we have said applies to a comparison of the leading growth companies with the bulk of well-established concerns; we exclude from our purview here those issues which are highly speculative because the businesses themselves are speculative.)

of prime importance头等重要的built-in contradiction内在的矛盾record业绩记录（本书常用）premium溢价intrinsic value内在价值paradox悖论unspectacular不起眼的middle-grade中等质量的the bulk of大部分concerns企业，公司（本书常用）purview讨论范围，视野

Thus we reach the final paradox, that the more successful the company, the greater are likely to be the fluctuations in the price of its shares.

于是我们得到了最后这个悖论：公司越成功，其股价的波动反而可能越大。

the more…, the greater… 是“越……越……”结构；后半句 the greater are likely to be the fluctuations 是倒装，正常语序为 the fluctuations … are likely to be the greater。that 引导的从句是 paradox 的同位语，解释悖论的内容。

这是当代投资中极重要、却没有得到足够重视的因素。股市报价体系里存在一个内在矛盾：公司的历史表现和前景越好，股价与账面价值的关系往往越弱；股价高出账面价值越多，内在价值的判断基础就越不确定，也就是说，这个“价值”越依赖市场不断变化的情绪和衡量尺度。于是出现最终的悖论：公司越成功，股价波动可能越大。从一个很实际的意义说，普通股质量越好，投机性反而可能越强，至少与那些不耀眼的中等质量股票相比是如此。（这里比较的是领先成长公司与大量经营稳健的普通企业；那些因业务本身具有投机性而高度投机的股票，不在讨论范围内。）

译者补充（非原文）：“好公司”不等于“任何价格都值得买”。企业仍然优秀，股价也可能因为先前估值过高而腰斩。

The argument made above should explain the often erratic price behavior of our most successful and impressive enterprises. Our favorite example is the monarch of them all—International Business Machines. The price of its shares fell from 607 to 300 in seven months in 1962–63; after two splits its price fell from 387 to 219 in 1970. Similarly, Xerox—an even more impressive earnings gainer in recent decades—fell from 171 to 87 in 1962–63, and from 116 to 65 in 1970. These striking losses did not indicate any doubt about the future long-term growth of IBM or Xerox; they reflected instead a lack of confidence in the premium valuation that the stock market itself had placed on these excellent prospects.

erratic不稳定的，飘忽不定的monarch君主（比喻龙头老大）splits股票分拆（拆股）Xerox施乐公司（复印机巨头）earnings gainer盈利增长者striking惊人的premium valuation溢价估值

上述论点可以解释，为什么最成功、最令人印象深刻的企业，其股价也常常反复无常。我们最常用的例子是其中的王者——国际商业机器公司（IBM）。1962至1963年的七个月里，它的股价从607跌到300；经历两次拆股后，1970年又从387跌到219。同样，过去几十年盈利增长更惊人的施乐，1962至1963年从171跌到87，1970年又从116跌到65。这些巨大跌幅并不表示人们怀疑IBM或施乐的长期增长前景，而是市场对自己此前为这些优秀前景给出的高溢价失去了信心。

The previous discussion leads us to a conclusion of practical importance to the conservative investor in common stocks. If he is to pay some special attention to the selection of his portfolio, it might be best for him to concentrate on issues selling at a reasonably close approximation to their tangible-asset value—say, at not more than one-third above that figure. Purchases made at such levels, or lower, may with logic be regarded as related to the company’s balance sheet, and as having a justification or support independent of the fluctuating market prices. The premium over book value that may be involved can be considered as a kind of extra fee paid for the advantage of stock-exchange listing and the marketability that goes with it.

of practical importance有实际意义的approximation近似值tangible-asset value有形资产价值with logic合乎逻辑地justification合理依据independent of不依赖于stock-exchange listing在证券交易所上市marketability可交易性，变现能力

前面的讨论给保守型普通股投资者带来一项实用结论：如果他要特别用心挑选组合，最好把注意力放在价格与有形资产价值相当接近的股票上，比如股价不高于有形资产价值的三分之一以上。在这一水平或更低价格买入，可以合理地认为有资产负债表作依据，支撑它的理由不依赖不断变化的市场报价。高出账面价值的那部分溢价，则可看成购买交易所挂牌和流动性所付的一笔额外费用。

A caution is needed here. A stock does not become a sound investment merely because it can be bought at close to its asset value. The investor should demand, in addition, a satisfactory ratio of earnings to price, a sufficiently strong financial position, and the prospect that its earnings will at least be maintained over the years. This may appear like demanding a lot from a modestly priced stock, but the prescription is not hard to fill under all but dangerously high market conditions. Once the investor is willing to forgo brilliant prospects—i.e., better than average expected growth—he will have no difficulty in finding a wide selection of issues meeting these criteria.

A caution一点告诫sound稳健的，可靠的ratio of earnings to price盈利与价格之比（市盈率的倒数）modestly priced价格适中的the prescription is not hard to fill这张“处方”不难配齐（fill a prescription：按方配药）all but除……以外的一切forgo放弃criteria标准（criterion 的复数）

这里必须提醒一句：一只股票能以接近资产价值的价格买到，并不自动成为稳健投资。投资者还应要求盈利相对于价格足够可观，财务状况足够强健，并且未来多年盈利至少能够维持。对一只价格不高的股票提出这些要求，听起来似乎很多；但只要市场没有危险地高估，符合条件的股票并不难找。一旦投资者肯放弃耀眼前景，也就是不再强求高于平均水平的预期增长，他就不难找到一大批满足这些标准的股票。

In our chapters on the selection of common stocks (Chapters 14 and 15) we shall give data showing that more than half of the DJIA issues met our asset-value criterion at the end of 1970. The most widely held investment of all—American Tel. & Tel.—actually sells below its tangible-asset value as we write. Most of the light-and- power shares, in addition to their other advantages, are now (early 1972) available at prices reasonably close to their asset values.

在第14章和第15章讨论普通股选择时，我们会给出数据，说明1970年末，道琼斯工业平均指数的成分股中有一半以上符合我们的资产价值标准。持有人最多的股票——美国电话电报公司——在本书写作时甚至低于有形资产价值交易。大多数电力和照明公用事业股除了其他优点外，在1972年初的价格也相当接近其资产价值。

The investor with a stock portfolio having such book values behind it can take a much more independent and detached view of stock-market fluctuations than those who have paid high multipliers of both earnings and tangible assets. As long as the earning power of his holdings remains satisfactory, he can give as little attention as he pleases to the vagaries of the stock market. More than that, at times he can use these vagaries to play the master game of buying low and selling high.

如果投资者组合中的股票有这样的账面价值作后盾，他看待股市波动时，就能比那些按盈利和有形资产的高倍数买入的人更独立、更冷静。只要所持公司的盈利能力保持令人满意，他完全可以少理会市场的反复无常。不仅如此，有时他还可以利用这些反复，玩好低买高卖这场主人的游戏。

The A. & P. Example

A. & P. 公司的例子

At this point we shall introduce one of our original examples, which dates back many years but which has a certain fascination for us because it combines so many aspects of corporate and investment experience. It involves the Great Atlantic & Pacific Tea Co. Here is the story:

dates back追溯到，源自fascination吸引力Great Atlantic & Pacific Tea Co.大西洋与太平洋茶叶公司（A&P，当时美国最大的连锁杂货商）

下面介绍一个我们早年提出的案例。它年代久远，却一直令我们着迷，因为其中汇集了企业经营和投资经历的许多面向。主角是大西洋与太平洋茶叶公司（A. & P.）。故事如下。

A. & P. shares were introduced to trading on the “Curb” market, now the American Stock Exchange, in 1929 and sold as high as 494. By 1932 they had declined to 104, although the company’s earnings were nearly as large in that generally catastrophic year as previously. In 1936 the range was between 111 and 131. Then in the business recession and bear market of 1938 the shares fell to a new low of 36.

introduced to trading开始挂牌交易Curb“路边”市场（纽约场外交易市场的旧称，因早年在街边交易得名）American Stock Exchange美国证券交易所catastrophic灾难性的recession经济衰退

A. & P.股票于1929年在当时的“场外交易市场”（后来成为美国证券交易所）开始交易，最高到494。到1932年，股价已跌至104，尽管在那个普遍灾难性的年份，公司盈利仍几乎和从前一样高。1936年的波动区间是111至131。随后，在1938年的经济衰退和熊市中，股价跌到36的新低。

That price was extraordinary. It meant that the preferred and common were together selling for $126 million, although the company had just reported that it held $85 million in cash alone and a working capital (or net current assets) of $134 million. A. & P. was the largest retail enterprise in America, if not in the world, with a continuous and impressive record of large earnings for many years. Yet in 1938 this outstanding business was considered on Wall Street to be worth less than its current assets alone—which means less as a going concern than if it were liquidated. Why? First, because there were threats of special taxes on chain stores; second, because net profits had fallen off in the previous year; and, third, because the general market was depressed. The first of these reasons was an exaggerated and eventually groundless fear; the other two were typical of temporary influences.

这个价格异乎寻常。当时优先股和普通股合计市值只有1.26亿美元，而公司刚刚报告，仅现金就有8500万美元，营运资本（即流动资产净额）为1.34亿美元。A. & P.是美国、甚至可能是世界最大的零售企业，多年来持续取得可观利润，记录令人瞩目。可1938年的华尔街竟认为，这家优秀企业的价值低于其流动资产本身，也就是认为它作为持续经营企业，还不如清算拆卖值钱。为什么？第一，连锁商店面临被征收特别税的威胁；第二，上年净利润下降；第三，整体市场低迷。第一个理由是被夸大的恐惧，后来证明毫无根据；后两个则是典型的暂时性影响。

译者补充（非原文）：把公司想成一个装有1.34亿美元净流动资产的盒子，市场却只给整个盒子标价1.26亿美元；当时的报价甚至没有计入持续经营和未来盈利的价值。

Let us assume that the investor had bought A. & P. common in 1937 at, say, 12 times its five-year average earnings, or about 80. We are far from asserting that the ensuing decline to 36 was of no importance to him. He would have been well advised to scrutinize the picture with some care, to see whether he had made any miscalculations. But if the results of his study were reassuring—as they should have been—he was entitled then to disregard the market decline as a temporary vagary of finance, unless he had the funds and the courage to take advantage of it by buying more on the bargain basis offered.

假设一名投资者在1937年以A. & P.过去五年平均利润的12倍买入普通股，价格约为80。我们绝不是说，随后跌到36对他毫无意义。他理应认真复查情况，看看自己是否算错了什么。但如果复查结果令人安心——本来就应如此——他就有权把这次下跌看成金融市场暂时的反常而不予理会；若他还有资金和勇气，也可以利用市场给出的便宜价格继续买入。

Sequel and Reflections

后续发展与反思

The following year, 1939, A. & P. shares advanced to 117½, or three times the low price of 1938 and well above the average of 1937. Such a turnabout in the behavior of common stocks is by no means uncommon, but in the case of A. & P. it was more striking than most. In the years after 1949 the grocery chain’s shares rose with the general market until in 1961 the split-up stock (10 for 1) reached a high of 70½ which was equivalent to 705 for the 1938 shares.

turnabout急剧转变，反转by no means uncommon绝非罕见grocery chain连锁杂货店split-up stock分拆后的股票10 for 1一拆十（1 股拆成 10 股）equivalent to相当于

第二年，也就是1939年，A. & P.股价升到117.5，是1938年低点的三倍，也远高于1937年的平均价格。普通股出现这种急转并不罕见，但A. & P.的幅度格外醒目。1949年以后，这家连锁杂货商的股票随大市上涨；到1961年，经过1拆10后的股票最高达到70.5，相当于1938年口径下的705。

This price of 70½ was remarkable for the fact it was 30 times the earnings of 1961. Such a price/earnings ratio—which compares with 23 times for the DJIA in that year—must have implied expectations of a brilliant growth in earnings. This optimism had no justification in the company’s earnings record in the preceding years, and it proved completely wrong. Instead of advancing rapidly, the course of earnings in the ensuing period was generally downward. The year after the 70½ high the price fell by more than half to 34. But this time the shares did not have the bargain quality that they showed at the low quotation in 1938. After varying sorts of fluctuations the price fell to another low of 21½ in 1970 and 18 in 1972—having reported the first quarterly deficit in its history.

remarkable for因……而引人注目30 times the earnings盈利的 30 倍（即市盈率 30 倍）justification依据bargain quality廉价股的特质quotation报价varying sorts of各种各样的quarterly deficit季度亏损

70.5这个价格之所以惊人，是因为它相当于1961年盈利的30倍，而当年道琼斯工业平均指数约为23倍。如此高的市盈率，必然隐含了对盈利高速增长的期待。但公司前几年的盈利记录并不支持这种乐观，后来也证明它完全错误。此后盈利没有快速增长，整体反而一路下降。创下70.5高点的次年，股价腰斩至34；可这一次，股票已经不具备1938年低价时的便宜品质。经历各种波动后，1970年又跌到21.5，1972年跌到18；公司也报告了历史上第一次季度亏损。

We see in this history how wide can be the vicissitudes of a major American enterprise in little more than a single generation, and also with what miscalculations and excesses of optimism and pessimism the public has valued its shares. In 1938 the business was really being given away, with no takers; in 1961 the public was clamoring for the shares at a ridiculously high price. After that came a quick loss of half the market value, and some years later a substantial further decline. In the meantime the company was to turn from an outstanding to a mediocre earnings performer; its profit in the boom-year 1968 was to be less than in 1958; it had paid a series of confusing small stock dividends not warranted by the current additions to surplus; and so forth. A. & P. was a larger company in 1961 and 1972 than in 1938, but not as well-run, not as profitable, and not as attractive.*

We see in this history how wide can be the vicissitudes of a major American enterprise in little more than a single generation, and also with what miscalculations and excesses of optimism and pessimism the public has valued its shares.

从这段历史中我们看到，一家美国大企业在仅仅一代人多一点的时间里，兴衰变迁可以有多么剧烈；也看到公众在给它的股票估价时，犯下了怎样的误判，又有过怎样过度的乐观与悲观。

see 后面接两个并列的宾语从句：how wide can be the vicissitudes…（倒装，正常语序 how wide the vicissitudes can be）和 with what miscalculations … the public has valued its shares（介词短语 with what… 提前，正常语序是 the public has valued its shares with what miscalculations…）。两处倒装都是为了把强调的部分放在前面。

这段历史让我们看到，一家美国大企业在短短一代人的时间里会经历多么剧烈的变迁，也让人看到公众在给股票估值时如何算错，以及乐观和悲观如何走向极端。1938年，这家企业几乎白送却无人问津；1961年，公众又争抢着以荒唐的高价买它。随后市值迅速损失一半，几年后又进一步大跌。与此同时，公司从出色的盈利者变成平庸者；繁荣的1968年，利润还低于1958年；它连续发放令人困惑的小额股票股利，但当期留存收益的增加并不足以支持这些做法，诸如此类。1961年和1972年的A. & P.规模都比1938年大，但经营不如从前，盈利更差，吸引力也更低。

There are two chief morals to this story. The first is that the stock market often goes far wrong, and sometimes an alert and courageous investor can take advantage of its patent errors. The other is that most businesses change in character and quality over the years, sometimes for the better, perhaps more often for the worse. The investor need not watch his companies’ performance like a hawk; but he should give it a good, hard look from time to time.

这个故事有两条主要教训。第一，股市经常犯很大的错；有时，警觉而勇敢的投资者可以利用这些明显错误。第二，大多数企业的性质和质量会随时间改变，有时变好，可能更多时候是变差。投资者不必像鹰一样时刻盯着公司，但应当隔一段时间认真、严格地检查一次经营表现。

Let us return to our comparison between the holder of marketable shares and the man with an interest in a private business. We have said that the former has the option of considering himself merely as the part owner of the various businesses he has invested in, or as the holder of shares which are salable at any time he wishes at their quoted market price.

现在回到可交易股票持有人与私人企业权益持有人的比较。前者可以只把自己看成所投资企业的部分所有者，也可以把自己看成持有一批随时能按市场报价卖出的股票；这两种身份由他选择。

But note this important fact: The true investor scarcely ever is forced to sell his shares, and at all other times he is free to disregard the current price quotation. He need pay attention to it and act upon it only to the extent that it suits his book, and no more.* Thus the investor who permits himself to be stampeded or unduly worried by unjustified market declines in his holdings is perversely transforming his basic advantage into a basic disadvantage. That man would be better off if his stocks had no market quotation at all, for he would then be spared the mental anguish caused him by other persons’ mistakes of judgment.†

scarcely ever几乎从不He need pay他只需（need 作情态动词，后接动词原形）to the extent that在……的程度上suits his book符合他的打算、对他有利（习语）stampeded被裹挟着惊慌行动perversely反常地，不合情理地spared免受mental anguish精神上的痛苦

但请注意这个重要事实：真正的投资者几乎从来不会被迫卖出股票；在其他任何时候，他都可以不理当前报价。只有当价格符合他自己的账本和利益、值得采取行动时，他才需要关注，除此之外不必多管。因此，如果投资者因为毫无根据的市场下跌而惊慌失措或过度担忧，便是反常地把自己的基本优势变成了基本劣势。若他的股票根本没有市场报价，反倒可能更好，因为那样就不会因别人的判断错误而承受精神折磨。

译者补充（非原文）：报价是一项选择权，不是一道命令。只要没有融资追缴、生活开支或其他原因逼你卖，别人今天的低报价不会自动变成你的已实现损失。

Incidentally, a widespread situation of this kind actually existed during the dark depression days of 1931–1933. There was then a psychological advantage in owning business interests that had no quoted market. For example, people who owned first mortgages on real estate that continued to pay interest were able to tell themselves that their investments had kept their full value, there being no market quotations to indicate otherwise. On the other hand, many listed corporation bonds of even better quality and greater underlying strength suffered severe shrinkages in their market quotations, thus making their owners believe they were growing distinctly poorer. In reality the owners were better off with the listed securities, despite the low prices of these. For if they had wanted to, or were compelled to, they could at least have sold the issues—possibly to exchange them for even better bargains. Or they could just as logically have ignored the market’s action as temporary and basically meaningless. But it is self-deception to tell yourself that you have suffered no shrinkage in value merely because your securities have no quoted market at all.

1931至1933年大萧条最黑暗的日子里，这种情况确实广泛存在。当时，持有没有市场报价的企业权益，反而有一种心理优势。例如，房地产第一顺位抵押贷款仍在付息，持有人便能告诉自己投资价值丝毫未减，因为没有报价显示相反结果。另一方面，许多上市公司债券明明质量更高、基础更稳固，市场报价却大幅缩水，使持有人觉得自己明显变穷了。实际上，尽管价格很低，上市证券持有人处境反而更好：如果愿意或不得不卖，他们至少可以出售，也许还能换成更便宜、更优质的证券；同样合理的做法，是把市场波动视为暂时且基本没有意义而不予理会。不过，只因证券没有公开报价，就告诉自己价值毫无缩水，也是一种自欺。

Returning to our A. & P. shareholder in 1938, we assert that as long as he held on to his shares he suffered no loss in their price decline, beyond what his own judgment may have told him was occasioned by a shrinkage in their underlying or intrinsic value. If no such shrinkage had occurred, he had a right to expect that in due course the market quotation would return to the 1937 level or better—as in fact it did the following year. In this respect his position was at least as good as if he had owned an interest in a private business with no quoted market for its shares. For in that case, too, he might or might not have been justified in mentally lopping off part of the cost of his holdings because of the impact of the 1938 recession—depending on what had happened to his company.

再看1938年的A. & P.股东。我们认为，只要他继续持股，股价下跌本身并没有让他遭受损失；真正可能构成损失的，只是他根据自己的判断确认企业基础价值或内在价值已经缩水。如果内在价值没有下降，他就有理由期待市场报价终会回到1937年的水平或更高；事实是，第二年就做到了。在这一点上，他的处境至少不比持有一家没有市场报价的私人企业权益差。后一种情况下，他同样需要根据公司实际发生的变化，判断1938年经济衰退是否足以让自己在心里减记一部分持有成本。

Critics of the value approach to stock investment argue that listed common stocks cannot properly be regarded or appraised in the same way as an interest in a similar private enterprise, because the presence of an organized security market “injects into equity ownership the new and extremely important attribute of liquidity.” But what this liquidity really means is, first, that the investor has the benefit of the stock market’s daily and changing appraisal of his holdings, for whatever that appraisal may be worth, and, second, that the investor is able to increase or decrease his investment at the market’s daily figure—if he chooses. Thus the existence of a quoted market gives the investor certain options that he does not have if his security is unquoted. But it does not impose the current quotation on an investor who prefers to take his idea of value from some other source.

价值投资的批评者认为，上市普通股不能像类似私人企业的权益那样看待或估价，因为有组织的证券市场“给股权所有权注入了流动性这一全新且极其重要的属性”。但流动性的真实含义只是两点：第一，投资者每天都能得到市场对持仓的不同估价，至于这种估价值多少，是另一回事；第二，如果他愿意，可以按当天价格增加或减少投资。公开市场给了投资者一些非上市证券没有的选择权，却没有强迫那些从其他来源判断价值的人接受当前报价。

Let us close this section with something in the nature of a parable. Imagine that in some private business you own a small share that cost you $1,000. One of your partners, named Mr. Market, is very obliging indeed. Every day he tells you what he thinks your interest is worth and furthermore offers either to buy you out or to sell you an additional interest on that basis. Sometimes his idea of value appears plausible and justified by business developments and prospects as you know them. Often, on the other hand, Mr. Market lets his enthusiasm or his fears run away with him, and the value he proposes seems to you a little short of silly.

Often, on the other hand, Mr. Market lets his enthusiasm or his fears run away with him, and the value he proposes seems to you a little short of silly.

但另一方面，市场先生也常常被自己的热情或恐惧冲昏头脑，他提出的价值在你看来简直近乎荒唐。
