If, as it appears, the member firms as a whole had allowed their overhead and other expenses to increase at a rate that could not sustain even a mild reduction in volume during part of a year, this does not speak well for either their business acumen or their financial conservatism.

如果像表面看来的那样，会员公司整体上听任管理费用和其他开支的增长速度达到了这样的地步——连一年中某段时间成交量的温和下降都承受不了——那这对它们的经营头脑和财务稳健性都不是什么好评价。

as it appears 是插入语；had allowed … to increase at a rate that … 中 rate 后面带一个 that 定语从句；speak well for 意为“说明……好”，否定之后就是“说明……不怎么样”。

1969年经纪公司最初出现财务问题时，人们归咎于交易量增加，声称业务太多压垮设施、推高管理费用，并造成大量结算问题。这大概是历史上第一次有重要企业因为生意多到做不过来而破产。1970年，经纪公司倒闭增多，主因又被说成“交易量下降”。可1970年纽约证交所成交29.37亿股，是历史最高纪录，比1965年前任何一年都高一倍以上，这个抱怨颇为奇怪。到1964年结束的十五年牛市中，年均成交“只有”7.12亿股，不及1970年的四分之一，经纪业却经历了史上最繁荣的时期。看来会员公司整体让管理费等支出增长到连一年中短暂、温和的成交减少都承受不起，这既不能说明经营有方，也谈不上财务保守。

A third explanation of the financial trouble finally emerged out of a mist of concealment, and we suspect that it is the most plausible and significant of the three. It seems that a good part of the capital of certain brokerage houses was held in the form of common stocks owned by the individual partners. Some of these seem to have been highly speculative and carried at inflated values. When the market declined in 1969 the quotations of such securities fell drastically and a substantial part of the capital of the firms vanished with them.2 In effect the partners were speculating with the capital that was supposed to protect the customers against the ordinary financial hazards of the brokerage business, in order to make a double profit thereon. This was inexcusable; we refrain from saying more.

emerged out of a mist of concealment从遮遮掩掩的迷雾中浮现出来plausible可信的，说得通的a good part of很大一部分partners合伙人carried at inflated values以虚高的价值入账quotations报价，市价In effect实际上hazards风险thereon在其上（指用那笔资本）inexcusable不可原谅的

第三种解释终于从遮掩的迷雾中浮现，我们怀疑它最可信也最重要。某些经纪公司的大部分资本，似乎以合伙人个人持有的普通股形式存在；其中一些股票投机性很强，还按虚高价值入账。1969年市场下跌，这些证券的报价暴跌，公司相当一部分资本也随之消失。实际上，合伙人为了赚取双重利润，拿本应用来保护客户免受经纪业务普通财务风险的资本去投机。这无法原谅，我们不再多说。

The investor should use his intelligence not only in formulating his financial policies but also in the associated details. These include the choice of a reputable broker to execute his orders. Up to now it was sufficient to counsel our readers to deal only with a member of the New York Stock Exchange, unless he had compelling reasons to use a nonmember firm. Reluctantly, we must add some further advice in this area. We think that people who do not carry margin accounts—and in our vocabulary this means all nonprofessional investors—should have the delivery and receipt of their securities handled by their bank. When giving a buying order to your brokers you can instruct them to deliver the securities bought to your bank against payment therefor by the bank; conversely, when selling you can instruct your bank to deliver the securities to the broker against payment of the proceeds. These services will cost a little extra but they should be well worth the expense in terms of safety and peace of mind. This advice may be disregarded, as no longer called for, after the investor is sure that all the problems of stock-exchange firms have been disposed of, but not before.*

投资者不仅制定财务政策时要动脑，处理相关细节也一样，包括选择信誉可靠的经纪人执行指令。过去，我们只需建议读者除非有迫切理由，否则只与纽约证交所会员交易。如今不得不再加一条。我们认为，不开保证金账户的人——按本书用语即所有非专业投资者——应由银行处理证券的交收。发出买入指令时，可要求经纪人把证券交给银行，由银行付款；卖出时，要求银行把证券交给经纪人并收取价款。这会多花一点费用，但换来的安全和安心值得。只有当投资者确信证券公司的全部问题已经解决后，这项建议才可不再采用，在此之前不行。

Investment Bankers

投资银行家

The term “investment banker” is applied to a firm that engages to an important extent in originating, underwriting, and selling new issues of stocks and bonds. (To underwrite means to guarantee to the issuing corporation, or other issuer, that the security will be fully sold.) A number of the brokerage houses carry on a certain amount of underwriting activity. Generally this is confined to participating in underwriting groups formed by leading investment bankers. There is an additional tendency for brokerage firms to originate and sponsor a minor amount of new-issue financing, particularly in the form of smaller issues of common stocks when a bull market is in full swing.

engages to an important extent in在很大程度上从事originating发起（证券发行）underwriting承销new issues新发行的证券（issue 此处兼有“发行”与“证券”之义）issuing corporation发行公司underwriting groups承销团new-issue financing新股融资in full swing如火如荼，全面展开

“投资银行”指在相当程度上从事股票和债券新发行的创设、承销和销售的公司。（承销即向发行公司或其他发行人保证证券将全部售出。）许多经纪公司也做一部分承销，通常只是参加领先投资银行组织的承销团。经纪公司也越来越会发起和主办少量新融资，尤其在牛市火热时承销规模较小的普通股新发行。

Investment banking is perhaps the most respectable department of the Wall Street community, because it is here that finance plays its constructive role of supplying new capital for the expansion of industry. In fact, much of the theoretical justification for maintaining active stock markets, notwithstanding their frequent speculative excesses, lies in the fact that organized security exchanges facilitate the sale of new issues of bonds and stocks. If investors or speculators could not expect to see a ready market for a new security offered them, they might well refuse to buy it.

constructive role建设性作用theoretical justification理论依据notwithstanding尽管speculative excesses投机过度facilitate促进，便利a ready market现成的市场，随时可以买卖的市场

投资银行或许是华尔街最体面的部门，因为金融在这里发挥建设性作用，为工业扩张提供新资本。事实上，尽管活跃股市常有投机过度，维持它的很多理论依据正在于：有组织的证券交易所方便了新债券和股票的出售。如果投资者或投机者不能期待新证券日后有活跃市场，可能根本不愿买。

The relationship between the investment banker and the investor is basically that of the salesman to the prospective buyer. For many years past the great bulk of the new offerings in dollar value has consisted of bond issues that were purchased in the main by financial institutions such as banks and insurance companies. In this business the security salesmen have been dealing with shrewd and experienced buyers. Hence any recommendations made by the investment bankers to these customers have had to pass careful and skeptical scrutiny. Thus these transactions are almost always effected on a businesslike footing.

prospective buyer潜在买家new offerings新发行的证券in the main主要地skeptical scrutiny怀疑的审视effected完成，实施（不是 affected）on a businesslike footing以公事公办的方式

投资银行与投资者的关系，基本是销售者与潜在买家的关系。过去多年，按金额计算，绝大多数新发证券是债券，主要由银行、保险公司等金融机构购买。证券销售员面对的是精明而经验丰富的买家，所以投资银行提出的建议必须经受谨慎而怀疑的审查，交易几乎总在商业化基础上完成。

But a different situation obtains in a relationship between the individual security buyer and the investment banking firms, including the stockbrokers acting as underwriters. Here the purchaser is frequently inexperienced and seldom shrewd. He is easily influenced by what the salesman tells him, especially in the case of common-stock issues, since often his unconfessed desire in buying is chiefly to make a quick profit. The effect of all this is that the public investor’s protection lies less in his own critical faculty than in the scruples and ethics of the offering houses.3

obtains存在，通行（不及物动词，此处不是“获得”）underwriters承销商unconfessed未言明的，不肯承认的critical faculty批判性的判断力scruples良知，顾忌offering houses发行证券的机构

The effect of all this is that the public investor’s protection lies less in his own critical faculty than in the scruples and ethics of the offering houses.

这一切造成的结果是，公众投资者的保护与其说来自他自己的判断力，不如说来自发行机构的良知和职业道德。

lies less in A than in B 是“与其说在于 A，不如说在于 B”的比较结构；critical faculty 指批判性的判断能力，scruples 指做事时良心上的顾忌。

个人证券买家与投资银行（包括充当承销商的股票经纪人）之间却不同。买家往往缺乏经验，也很少精明，容易受销售员影响，普通股新发行尤其如此，因为他买入时没有说出口的愿望，常常只是迅速获利。结果，公众投资者得到多少保护，较少取决于自己的批判能力，更多取决于发行机构的操守和道德。

译者补充（非原文）：承销商的职责是把新证券卖出去；买方的职责是判断价格与风险。即使披露充分，两者目标也不相同。

It is a tribute to the honesty and competence of the underwriting firms that they are able to combine fairly well the discordant roles of adviser and salesman. But it is imprudent for the buyer to trust himself to the judgment of the seller. In 1959 we stated at this point: “The bad results of this unsound attitude show themselves recurrently in the underwriting field and with notable effects in the sale of new common stock issues during periods of active speculation.” Shortly thereafter this warning proved urgently needed. As already pointed out, the years 1960–61 and, again, 1968–69 were marked by an unprecedented outpouring of issues of lowest quality, sold to the public at absurdly high offering prices and in many cases pushed much higher by heedless speculation and some semi-manipulation. A number of the more important Wall Street houses have participated to some degree in these less than creditable activities, which demonstrates that the familiar combination of greed, folly, and irresponsibility has not been exorcized from the financial scene.

a tribute to是对……的褒扬，足以证明discordant roles相互冲突的角色imprudent不明智的trust himself to把自己托付给recurrently反复地Shortly thereafter此后不久unprecedented outpouring空前的大量涌出heedless不顾后果的semi-manipulation半操纵（市场）less than creditable不太光彩的exorcized驱除（原义是驱魔）

承销公司能把顾问与销售员这两个互有冲突的角色结合得相当好，说明它们总体诚实而有能力；但买家把判断交给卖家，仍是不谨慎。1959年我们在这里写道：“这种不健全态度带来的恶果，在承销领域反复出现；投机活跃时期销售普通股新股时尤其明显。”不久后，这个警告就显得十分紧迫。正如前文所说，1960至1961年、以及1968至1969年，最低质量的新股以前所未有的规模涌出，以荒唐高价卖给公众；许多股票又被轻率投机和某些半操纵行为推得更高。若干重要华尔街公司也不同程度参与了这些不光彩活动，说明贪婪、愚蠢和不负责任这组熟悉的组合，从未被逐出金融世界。

The intelligent investor will pay attention to the advice and recommendations received from investment banking houses, especially those known by him to have an excellent reputation; but he will be sure to bring sound and independent judgment to bear upon these suggestions—either his own, if he is competent, or that of some other type of adviser.*

bring sound and independent judgment to bear upon用稳健而独立的判断来审视（bring … to bear upon：把……施加于）competent有能力的，胜任的

聪明的投资者会认真听取投资银行的建议，尤其是自己知道信誉卓著的机构；但他一定会用健全而独立的判断检验这些意见。若自己有能力，就亲自判断；否则应找另一类顾问。

Other Advisers

其他顾问

It is a good old custom, especially in the smaller towns, to consult one’s local banker about investments. A commercial banker may not be a thoroughgoing expert on security values, but he is experienced and conservative. He is especially useful to the unskilled investor, who is often tempted to stray from the straight and unexciting path of a defensive policy and needs the steadying influence of a prudent mind. The more alert and aggressive investor, seeking counsel in the selection of security bargains, will not ordinarily find the commercial banker’s viewpoint to be especially suited to his own objectives.†

thoroughgoing彻底的，十足的tempted to stray from受诱惑而偏离unexciting乏味的steadying influence稳定人心的影响prudent审慎的alert机敏的security bargains廉价证券

咨询当地银行家是一项良好传统，小城镇尤其如此。商业银行家未必是证券价值的彻底专家，但经验丰富而且保守。对缺乏技巧的投资者格外有用：后者常想偏离防御型策略那条正直却不刺激的道路，需要谨慎头脑帮助稳定。更警觉、更积极、希望咨询便宜证券选择的投资者，通常会发现商业银行家的视角不太适合自己的目标。

We take a more critical attitude toward the widespread custom of asking investment advice from relatives or friends. The inquirer always thinks he has good reason for assuming that the person consulted has superior knowledge or experience. Our own observation indicates that it is almost as difficult to select satisfactory lay advisers as it is to select the proper securities unaided. Much bad advice is given free.

widespread普遍的inquirer求教者the person consulted被请教的人（过去分词作后置定语）lay advisers外行顾问（lay：非专业的）unaided不靠别人帮助

我们对向亲友征求投资意见这一普遍习惯，态度更为批评。提问者总觉得自己有充分理由相信，对方知识或经验更胜一筹。但按我们的观察，挑到令人满意的业余顾问，几乎和不借助别人而挑对证券一样难。许多坏建议都是免费的。

Summary

小结

Investors who are prepared to pay a fee for the management of their funds may wisely select some well-established and well-recommended investment-counsel firm. Alternatively, they may use the investment department of a large trust company or the supervisory service supplied on a fee basis by a few of the leading New York Stock Exchange houses. The results to be expected are in no wise exceptional, but they are commensurate with those of the average well-informed and cautious investor.

well-recommended口碑好的，广受推荐的trust company信托公司supervisory service账户监管服务on a fee basis收费的in no wise绝不（wise 此处是古旧用法，意为“方式”）commensurate with与……相称

愿意付费请人管理资金的投资者，可以明智地选择历史悠久、口碑良好的投资顾问公司；也可以使用大型信托公司的投资部门，或少数领先纽约证交所会员公司按费提供的监督服务。预期结果绝不会不同寻常，但会与一个知识充足、谨慎的普通投资者相称。

Most security buyers obtain advice without paying for it specifically. It stands to reason, therefore, that in the majority of cases they are not entitled to and should not expect better than average results. They should be wary of all persons, whether customers’ brokers or security salesmen, who promise spectacular income or profits. This applies both to the selection of securities and to guidance in the elusive (and perhaps illusive) art of trading in the market.

It stands to reason理所当然wary of提防spectacular惊人的elusive难以捉摸的illusive虚幻的（与 elusive 谐音双关）

多数证券买家取得建议时不另行付费。因此，按理说，他们通常没有资格、也不应期待高于平均的结果。无论客户经纪人还是证券销售员，只要许诺惊人收入或利润，都应警惕。这既适用于选证券，也适用于那门捉摸不定、甚至只是幻象的市场交易“艺术”。

Defensive investors, as we have defined them, will not ordinarily be equipped to pass independent judgment on the security recommendations made by their advisers. But they can be explicit—and even repetitiously so—in stating the kind of securities they want to buy. If they follow our prescription they will confine themselves to high-grade bonds and the common stocks of leading corporations, preferably those that can be purchased at individual price levels that are not high in the light of experience and analysis. The security analyst of any reputable stock-exchange house can make up a suitable list of such common stocks and can certify to the investor whether or not the existing price level therefor is a reasonably conservative one as judged by past experience.

equipped to具备……的能力repetitiously so甚至反复地这样（so 代指 explicit）prescription处方，建议high-grade高等级的reputable声誉良好的make up编制（名单）certify证明，确认therefor为此，就其而言（旧式副词，不是 therefore）

按我们的定义，防御型投资者通常没有能力独立判断顾问推荐的证券，但可以明确、甚至反复说明自己想买什么。若遵循本书方案，就只限于高等级债券和领先公司的普通股；最好还能在根据历史经验和分析看来并不昂贵的个别价位买入。任何信誉良好的交易所会员公司，其证券分析师都能列出合适股票，并确认当前价格按过去经验判断是否足够保守。

The aggressive investor will ordinarily work in active cooperation with his advisers. He will want their recommendations explained in detail, and he will insist on passing his own judgment upon them. This means that the investor will gear his expectations and the character of his security operations to the development of his own knowledge and experience in the field. Only in the exceptional case, where the integrity and competence of the advisers have been thoroughly demonstrated, should the investor act upon the advice of others without understanding and approving the decision made.

insist on坚持gear his expectations调整他的期望（gear … to：使与……相适应）security operations证券操作integrity正直，诚信act upon依照……行事

Only in the exceptional case, where the integrity and competence of the advisers have been thoroughly demonstrated, should the investor act upon the advice of others without understanding and approving the decision made.

只有在例外的情况下——顾问的诚信和能力已经得到充分证明——投资者才可以在没有理解并认可所作决定的情况下，按别人的建议行事。

Only 引导的状语放在句首，主句要用部分倒装 should the investor act；where 引导的非限定性定语从句修饰 case；the decision made 中 made 是过去分词作后置定语。

积极型投资者通常会与顾问主动合作。他要求详细解释建议，并坚持自己作出判断。这意味着，他会让回报预期和证券操作的性质，与自己在该领域逐步增长的知识和经验相匹配。只有极少数情况下，即顾问的诚信和能力已经得到充分证明，投资者才可以在没有理解并赞同决策的情况下，直接照别人的建议行动。

There have always been unprincipled stock salesmen and fly by-night stock brokers, and—as a matter of course—we have advised our readers to confine their dealings, if possible, to members of the New York Stock Exchange. But we are reluctantly compelled to add the extra-cautious counsel that security deliveries and payments be made through the intermediary of the investor’s bank. The distressing Wall Street brokerage-house picture may have cleared up completely in a few years, but in late 1971 we still suggest, “Better safe than sorry.”

unprincipled没有原则的，不择手段的fly by-night靠不住的、随时跑路的（通常写作 fly-by-night）as a matter of course理所当然地extra-cautious格外谨慎的intermediary中介distressing令人痛心的Better safe than sorry小心不吃亏（谚语：宁可稳妥，不要后悔）

不讲原则的股票销售员和来去匆匆的经纪商一直都有，所以我们照例建议读者尽可能只与纽约证交所会员交易。但如今不得不加一条格外谨慎的建议：证券交付与付款应通过投资者的银行办理。华尔街经纪公司的困境几年后也许会完全消失，但在1971年末，我们仍主张：“谨慎总比后悔好。”

Notes · 注释（贾森·兹威格）

* The list of sources for investment advice remains as “miscellaneous” as it was when Graham wrote. A survey of investors conducted in late 2002 for the Securities Industry Association, a Wall Street trade group, found that 17% of investors depended most heavily for investment advice on a spouse or friend; 2% on a banker; 16% on a broker; 10% on financial periodicals; and 24% on a financial planner. The only difference from Graham’s day is that 8% of investors now rely heavily on the Internet and 3% on financial television. (See www.sia.com.)
投资建议来源仍像格雷厄姆写作时一样“杂乱”。美国证券业协会2002年末调查发现，17%的投资者最依赖配偶或朋友，2%依赖银行家，16%依赖经纪人，10%依赖金融刊物，24%依赖理财规划师。与格雷厄姆时代相比，新增的是8%高度依赖互联网，3%依赖财经电视。
* The character of investment counseling firms and trust banks has not changed, but today they generally do not offer their services to investors with less than $1 million in financial assets; in some cases, $5 million or more is required. Today thousands of independent financial-planning firms perform very similar functions, although (as analyst Robert Veres puts it) the mutual fund has replaced blue-chip stocks as the investment of choice and diversification has replaced “quality” as the standard of safety.
投资顾问公司和信托银行的性质没有改变，但如今一般不为金融资产少于100万美元的人服务，有时门槛是500万美元甚至更高。现在有数千家独立理财规划公司执行相似职能。不过，正如分析师罗伯特·维雷斯所说，共同基金取代蓝筹股成为首选投资，分散化也取代“质量”成为安全标准。
* Overall, Graham was as tough and cynical an observer as Wall Street has ever seen. In this rare case, however, he was not nearly cynical enough. Wall Street may have higher ethical standards than some businesses (smuggling, prostitution, Congressional lobbying, and journalism come to mind) but the investment world nevertheless has enough liars, cheaters, and thieves to keep Satan’s check-in clerks frantically busy for decades to come.
总体而言，格雷厄姆是华尔街最严厉、最冷峻的观察者之一；但这一次，他还不够怀疑。华尔街的道德标准也许高于某些行业，可投资界仍有足够多的骗子、作弊者和窃贼，能让撒旦的登记员忙上几十年。
† The thousands of people who bought stocks in the late 1990s in the belief that Wall Street analysts were providing unbiased and valuable advice have learned, in a painful way, how right Graham is on this point.
20世纪90年代末，成千上万人相信华尔街分析师会提供无偏见、有价值的建议而买入股票，后来以痛苦方式明白了格雷厄姆这句话有多正确。
† ‡ Interestingly, this stinging criticism, which in his day Graham was directing at full-service brokers, ended up applying to discount Internet brokers in the late 1990s. These firms spent millions of dollars on flashy advertising that goaded their customers into trading more and trading faster. Most of those customers ended up picking their own pockets, instead of paying someone else to do it for them—and the cheap commissions on that kind of transaction are a poor consolation for the result. More traditional brokerage firms, meanwhile, began emphasizing financial planning and “integrated asset management,” instead of compensating their brokers only on the basis of how many commissions they could generate.
有意思的是，格雷厄姆当年针对全服务经纪商的尖锐批评，最终也适用于90年代末的互联网折扣券商。它们花费数百万美元制作耀眼广告，刺激客户交易得更多、更快。多数客户最后是自己掏空自己的口袋，而不是付钱让别人来做；便宜佣金对此只是微不足道的安慰。与此同时，传统经纪公司开始强调理财规划和“综合资产管理”，不再只按经纪人创造的佣金付酬。
* This remains true, although many of Wall Street’s best analysts hold the title of chartered financial analyst. The CFA certification is awarded by the Association of Investment Management & Research (formerly the Financial Analysts Federation) only after the candidate has completed years of rigorous study and passed a series of difficult exams. More than 50,000 analysts worldwide have been certified as CFAs. Sadly, a recent survey by Professor Stanley Block found that most CFAs ignore Graham’s teachings: Growth potential ranks higher than quality of earnings, risks, and dividend policy in determining P/E ratios, while far more analysts base their buy ratings on recent price than on the long-term outlook for the company. See Stanley Block, “A Study of Financial Analysts: Practice and Theory,” Financial Analysts Journal, July/August, 1999, at www.aimrpubs.org. As Graham was fond of saying, his own books have been read by—and ignored by—more people than any other books in finance.
这点至今仍成立，尽管华尔街许多优秀分析师持有CFA称号。候选人须经过多年严格学习并通过一系列困难考试，才由投资管理与研究协会授予资格，全球已有五万多名CFA。遗憾的是，斯坦利·布洛克教授的调查发现，多数CFA忽视格雷厄姆的教导：决定市盈率时，增长潜力排在盈利质量、风险和股息政策之前；更多分析师依据近期价格而非公司长期前景给出买入评级。格雷厄姆爱说，自己的书被阅读又被忽略的次数，比其他任何金融书都多。
* It is highly unusual today for a security analyst to allow mere commoners to contact him directly. For the most part, only the nobility of institutional investors are permitted to approach the throne of the almighty Wall Street analyst. An individual investor might, perhaps, have some luck calling analysts who work at “regional” brokerage firms headquartered outside of New York City. The investor relations area at the websites of most publicly traded companies will provide a list of analysts who follow the stock. Websites like www.zacks.com and www.multex.com offer access to analysts’ research reports—but the intelligent investor should remember that most analysts do not analyze businesses. Instead, they engage in guesswork about future stock prices.
如今，证券分析师让普通人直接联系极不寻常。通常只有机构投资者这样的“贵族”能接近全能华尔街分析师的宝座。个人投资者联系总部不在纽约的地区券商分析师，也许还有机会。多数上市公司网站的投资者关系页面会列出跟踪该股的分析师；一些网站提供研报。但聪明的投资者要记住，多数分析师并不分析企业，而是在猜未来股价。
† Benjamin Graham was the prime force behind the establishment of the CFA program, which he advocated for nearly two decades before it became a reality.
本杰明·格雷厄姆是推动CFA项目建立的首要力量；在它成为现实前，他倡导了近二十年。
* The two firms Graham had in mind were probably Du Pont, Glore, Forgan & Co. and Goodbody & Co. Du Pont (founded by the heirs to the chemical fortune) was saved from insolvency in 1970 only after Texas entrepreneur H. Ross Perot lent more than $50 million to the firm; Goodbody, the fifth-largest brokerage firm in the United States, would have failed in late 1970 had Merrill Lynch not acquired it. Hayden, Stone & Co. would also have gone under if it had not been acquired. In 1970, no fewer than seven brokerage firms went bust. The farcical story of Wall Street’s frenzied over-expansion in the late 1960s is beautifully told in John Brooks’s The Go-Go Years (John Wiley & Sons, New York, 1999).
格雷厄姆想到的两家公司，可能是杜邦—格洛尔—福根公司与古德博迪公司。1970年，得州企业家H·罗斯·佩罗借给杜邦公司逾5000万美元，它才免于破产；全美第五大经纪公司古德博迪若未被美林收购，也会在1970年末倒闭。海登—斯通公司同样靠收购才没有垮掉。1970年至少七家经纪公司破产。约翰·布鲁克斯《沸腾岁月》精彩讲述了60年代末华尔街疯狂扩张的闹剧。
* Nearly all brokerage transactions are now conducted electronically, and securities are no longer physically “delivered.” Thanks to the establishment of the Securities Investor Protection Corporation, or SIPC, in 1970, investors are generally assured of recovering their full account values if their brokerage firm becomes insolvent. SIPC is a government-mandated consortium of brokers; all the members agree to pool their assets to cover losses incurred by the customers of any firm that becomes insolvent. SIPC’s protection eliminates the need for investors to make payment and take delivery through a bank intermediary, as Graham urges.
如今几乎所有经纪交易都以电子方式完成，证券不再实物“交付”。1970年成立证券投资者保护公司（SIPC）后，经纪公司破产时，投资者通常能收回完整账户价值。SIPC是政府规定成立的经纪商联合体，所有会员汇集资产，弥补任一破产公司的客户损失。这项保护使投资者不再需要按格雷厄姆建议，通过银行中介付款和收取证券。
* Those who heeded Graham’s advice would not have been suckered into buying Internet IPOs in 1999 and 2000.
听从格雷厄姆建议的人，不会在1999和2000年被骗去买互联网公司首次公开发行的股票。
† This traditional role of bankers has for the most part been supplanted by accountants, lawyers, or financial planners.
银行家的这项传统角色，如今大体由会计师、律师或理财规划师取代。

Endnotes · 尾注（本杰明·格雷厄姆）

1. The examinations are given by the Institute of Chartered Financial Analysts, which is an arm of the Financial Analysts Federation. The latter now embraces constituent societies with over 50,000 members.
考试由特许金融分析师学院组织，该学院隶属金融分析师联合会；后者如今包含多个成员协会，总会员超过五万人。
2. The NYSE had imposed some drastic rules of valuation (known as “haircuts”) designed to minimize this danger, but apparently they did not help sufficiently.
纽约证交所曾实施大幅折减估值的规则，称为“haircuts”，旨在降低这种危险；但显然效果仍不充分。
3. New offerings may now be sold only by means of a prospectus prepared under the rules of the Securities and Exchange Commission. This document must disclose all the pertinent facts about the issue and issuer, and it is fully adequate to inform the as to the exact nature of the security offered him. But the very copiousness of the data required usually makes the prospectus of prohibitive length. It is generally agreed that only a small percentage of buying new issues read the prospectus with thoroughness. Thus they are still acting mainly not on their own judgment but on that of the house selling them the security or on the recommendation of the individual salesman or account executive.
如今，新发行只能通过按SEC规则编制的招股说明书销售。文件必须披露证券和发行人的全部相关事实，足以让投资者准确了解所获证券的性质。但要求资料太多，通常使招股书长得令人生畏。公认只有很少新股买家会彻底阅读。因此，他们主要依靠的仍不是自己判断，而是卖方机构、销售员或客户主管的判断。

CHAPTER 11

普通投资者的证券分析：一般方法

Security Analysis for the Lay Investor

非专业投资者怎样抓住决定证券价值的少数关键变量？

Chapter 11Security Analysis for the Lay Investor: General Approach第11章 普通投资者的证券分析：一般方法

本章导读本章是格雷厄姆写给非专业读者的证券分析入门。他先说明分析师做什么：总结企业的经营成果和财务状况、估计未来盈利能力，最后对债券的安全性或股票的吸引力给出判断；随即指出一个令人不安的悖论——数学化的估值恰恰在最不可靠的领域（高市盈率成长股）用得最多，因为估值越依赖对未来的预期，出错的余地就越大。债券分析的核心标准是利息保障倍数（多年平均盈利覆盖利息总支出的倍数），辅以企业规模、股票/权益比率和资产价值等检验。铁路债券的历史证明：凡通过严格安全测试的债券几乎都躲过了财务困境；公用事业债券同样如此，工业债券则稳定性较差。普通股分析的理想做法是估计未来若干年的平均盈利，再乘以适当的“资本化因子”。他用 Value Line 对道指成分股的预测与实际结果对比，发现整体预测尚可而个股偏差很大——这正是基金广泛分散投资的根本原因。影响资本化率的五个因素是长期前景、管理层、财务实力与资本结构、股息记录、当前股息率。本章最著名的是成长股估值公式：价值 = 当期（正常）盈利 ×（8.5 + 2 × 预期年增长率）；他同时警告：按此公式，增长率 8% 以上的公司价值将是无穷大，因此估值必须留出安全边际，预测不可高度信赖。最后他提出“两段式评估法”：先由初级分析师按公式机械地算出仅基于过去业绩的“过去业绩价值”，再由高级分析师根据预期的新情况加以修正并说明理由——这种估值未必足够可靠，但仍值得去做。

Financial analysis is now a well-established and flourishing profession, or semiprofession. The various societies of analysts that make up the National Federation of Financial Analysts have over 13,000 members, most of whom make their living out of this branch of mental activity. Financial analysts have textbooks, a code of ethics, and a quarterly journal.* They also have their share of unresolved problems. In recent years there has been a tendency to replace the general concept of “security analysis” by that of “financial analysis.” The latter phrase has a broader implication and is better suited to describe the work of most senior analysts on Wall Street. It would be useful to think of security analysis as limiting itself pretty much to the examination and evaluation of stocks and bonds, whereas financial analysis would comprise that work, plus the determination of investment policy (portfolio selection), plus a substantial amount of general economic analysis.1 In this chapter we shall use whatever designation is most applicable, with chief emphasis on the work of the security analyst proper.

well-established and flourishing稳固而兴旺的semiprofession半专业性的职业make their living out of以……谋生branch of mental activity脑力活动的一个分支（此处略带调侃地指分析这一行）their share of unresolved problems他们也有自己那一份尚未解决的问题implication含义，意涵senior analysts资深分析师portfolio selection投资组合选择designation名称，称谓the security analyst proper严格意义上的证券分析师（proper 后置，意为“本身、严格意义上的”）

财务分析如今已成为成熟而兴盛的职业，或半职业。组成全国金融分析师联合会的各个分析师协会拥有一万三千多名会员，其中多数靠这项脑力活动谋生。金融分析师有自己的教科书、道德准则和季刊，也有尚未解决的问题。近年出现一种倾向：用范围更广的“财务分析”取代一般所说的“证券分析”，因为前者更适合描述华尔街多数高级分析师的工作。可以把证券分析理解为主要审查和评价股票、债券；财务分析则在此之外，还包括制定投资政策（选择组合）和大量宏观经济分析。本章会按情况选用名称，重点仍是严格意义上的证券分析师工作。

The security analyst deals with the past, the present, and the future of any given security issue. He describes the business; he summarizes its operating results and financial position; he sets forth its strong and weak points, its possibilities and risks; he estimates its future earning power under various assumptions, or as a “best guess.” He makes elaborate comparisons of various companies, or of the same company at various times. Finally, he expresses an opinion as to the safety of the issue, if it is a bond or investment-grade preferred stock, or as to its attractiveness as a purchase, if it is a common stock.

security issue证券（issue 在本书中常指证券、股票）sets forth阐述，列出earning power盈利能力best guess最佳猜测，尽可能合理的估计elaborate comparisons详尽的比较investment-grade preferred stock投资级优先股

证券分析师研究某项证券的过去、现在和未来。他描述企业，概括经营结果和财务状况，列明优势、弱点、机会与风险；在不同假设下估计未来盈利能力，或给出“最佳猜测”；详细比较不同公司，或同一公司在不同时点的情况。最后，如果对象是债券或投资级优先股，他会评价安全性；如果是普通股，则判断是否值得买。

In doing all these things the security analyst avails himself of a number of techniques, ranging from the elementary to the most abstruse. He may modify substantially the figures in the company’s annual statements, even though they bear the sacred imprimatur of the certified public accountant. He is on the lookout particularly for items in these reports that may mean a good deal more or less than they say.

avails himself of利用（avail oneself of）abstruse深奥难懂的sacred imprimatur神圣的认可印记（imprimatur 原指出版许可，此处讽刺会计师签字的权威）on the lookout留意寻找，密切注意a good deal more or less than they say远比字面所说的多或少

完成这些工作时，证券分析师会运用从基础到极其深奥的各种技术。即使公司年报带有注册会计师神圣的认可，他也可能大幅调整其中数字；尤其会寻找那些实际意义远大于或小于表面文字的项目。

The security analyst develops and applies standards of safety by which we can conclude whether a given bond or preferred stock may be termed sound enough to justify purchase for investment. These standards relate primarily to past average earnings, but they are concerned also with capital structure, working capital, asset values, and other matters.

termed被称为sound enough to justify purchase足够稳健、值得买入capital structure资本结构working capital营运资本

证券分析师制定并运用安全标准，以判断某只债券或优先股是否足够稳健、可以作为投资买入。这些标准主要与过去的平均盈利有关，也会考察资本结构、营运资本、资产价值等因素。

In dealing with common stocks the security analyst until recently has only rarely applied standards of value as well defined as were his standards of safety for bonds and preferred stocks. Most of the time he contended himself with a summary of past performances, a more or less general forecast of the future—with particular emphasis on the next 12 months—and a rather arbitrary conclusion. The latter was, and still is, often drawn with one eye on the stock ticker or the market charts. In the past few years, however, much attention has been given by practicing analysts to the problem of valuing growth stocks. Many of these have sold at such high prices in relation to past and current earnings that those recommending them have felt a special obligation to justify their purchase by fairly definite projections of expected earnings running fairly far into the future. Certain mathematical techniques of a rather sophisticated sort have perforce been invoked to support the valuations arrived at.

as well defined as像……一样明确的contended himself with满足于（正确拼法应为 contented himself with）arbitrary武断的，随意的with one eye on一边盯着……stock ticker股票行情自动收录机（显示实时报价的设备）practicing analysts执业分析师felt a special obligation to感到有一种特别的责任去……perforce必然地，不得已地（古雅用语）invoked被援用，被搬出来

Many of these have sold at such high prices in relation to past and current earnings that those recommending them have felt a special obligation to justify their purchase by fairly definite projections of expected earnings running fairly far into the future.

这些股票中有许多相对于过去和当前的盈利卖得如此之贵，以至于推荐它们的人感到有一种特别的义务，要用对未来相当长时期内预期盈利的相当明确的预测，来证明买入它们是合理的。

主干是 such high prices … that …（如此……以至于……）；those recommending them 是“those + 现在分词”结构，意为“推荐这些股票的人”，作 that 从句的主语；running fairly far into the future 是分词短语修饰 projections，指预测延伸到很远的未来。

分析普通股时，直到不久前，证券分析师也很少采用像债券和优先股安全标准那样明确的价值标准。多数时候，他只满足于总结历史表现，对未来作笼统预测，尤其着眼未来十二个月，最后给出颇为武断的结论；这个结论过去如此、现在也常如此，往往一只眼盯着行情机或走势图。近几年，实务分析师开始大量研究成长股估值。许多成长股相对于过去和当前盈利，价格高得惊人；推荐它们的人因此觉得有义务以相当明确、延伸到很远将来的盈利预测，证明买入合理。为支持所得估值，人们不得不运用颇复杂的数学技术。

We shall deal with these techniques, in foreshortened form, a little later. However, we must point out a troublesome paradox here, which is that the mathematical valuations have become most prevalent precisely in those areas where one might consider them least reliable. For the more dependent the valuation becomes on anticipations of the future—and the less it is tied to a figure demonstrated by past performance—the more vulnerable it becomes to possible miscalculation and serious error. A large part of the value found for a high-multiplier growth stock is derived from future projections which differ markedly from past performance—except perhaps in the growth rate itself. Thus it may be said that security analysts today find themselves compelled to become most mathematical and “scientific” in the very situations which lend themselves least auspiciously to exact treatment.*

in foreshortened form以精简的形式troublesome paradox令人头疼的悖论prevalent盛行的anticipations预期vulnerable容易受伤害的，脆弱的（后面的 to 隔在 it becomes 之后）miscalculation误算high-multiplier growth stock高市盈率成长股（multiplier 在本书中指市盈率）compelled to被迫lend themselves least auspiciously to exact treatment最不适合精确处理（lend oneself to：适合于；auspiciously：吉利地、顺利地，此处是反讽）

For the more dependent the valuation becomes on anticipations of the future—and the less it is tied to a figure demonstrated by past performance—the more vulnerable it becomes to possible miscalculation and serious error.

因为估值越是依赖对未来的预期——越是不与过去业绩所证实的数字挂钩——它就越容易出现误算和严重错误。

句首 For 是连词“因为”；主干是 the more dependent … the more vulnerable … 的“越……越……”结构，破折号里插入的 and the less it is tied to … 是与 the more dependent 并列的第二个条件。

Thus it may be said that security analysts today find themselves compelled to become most mathematical and “scientific” in the very situations which lend themselves least auspiciously to exact treatment.

因此可以说，今天的证券分析师发现自己恰恰是在最不适合精确处理的情形下，被迫变得最数学化、最“科学”。

find themselves compelled to 意为“发现自己不得不”；the very situations 中的 very 表强调“恰恰是那些”；lend themselves to 意为“适合于”，least auspiciously 是反讽式的委婉说法，等于“最不适合”；“scientific”加引号表示作者的怀疑态度。

稍后会简要讨论这些技术。但这里有个麻烦的悖论：数学估值恰恰在最不可靠的领域最盛行。估值越依赖对未来的预期、越少依托过去业绩已经证明的数字，就越容易受误算和严重错误影响。高倍数成长股的很大部分价值，来自与过去表现显著不同的未来预测，也许只有增长率本身例外。于是，现代证券分析师偏偏在最不适合精确处理的情形下，被迫变得最数学化、最“科学”。

Let us proceed, nonetheless, with our discussion of the more important elements and techniques of security analysis. The present highly condensed treatment is directed to the needs of the nonprofessional investor. At the minimum he should understand what the security analyst is talking about and driving at; beyond that, he should be equipped, if possible, to distinguish between superficial and sound analysis.

highly condensed treatment高度浓缩的论述driving at想要说明的意思（drive at：意在，想说）be equipped具备能力superficial肤浅的

尽管如此，我们仍继续讨论证券分析中较重要的要素和技术。这里高度浓缩的内容面向非专业投资者。最低要求是，他应理解分析师在谈什么、想解决什么；如果可能，还应有能力区分肤浅分析与健全分析。

Security analysis for the lay investor is thought of as beginning with the interpretation of a company’s annual financial report. This is a subject which we have covered for laymen in a separate book, entitled The Interpretation of Financial Statements. 2 We do not consider it necessary or appropriate to traverse the same ground in this chapter, especially since the emphasis in the present book is on principles and attitudes rather than on information and description. Let us pass on to two basic questions underlying the selection of investments. What are the primary tests of safety of a corporate bond or preferred stock? What are the chief factors entering into the valuation of a common stock?

lay investor非专业投资者，外行投资者laymen外行人entitled题为traverse the same ground重复讲同样的内容（字面：走同一片地）pass on to转到，接着谈entering into构成，成为（……的组成因素）

一般认为，普通投资者学习证券分析，应从解释公司年度财务报告开始。我们曾为非专业读者另写《财务报表解读》专门讨论。本章没必要也不适合重复，尤其本书重在原则和态度，不重资料与描述。下面转向投资选择背后的两个基本问题：检验公司债或优先股安全性的主要标准是什么？普通股估值要考虑哪些核心因素？

Bond Analysis

债券分析

The most dependable and hence the most respectable branch of security analysis concerns itself with the safety, or quality, of bond issues and investment-grade preferred stocks. The chief criterion used for corporate bonds is the number of times that total interest charges have been covered by available earnings for some years in the past. In the case of preferred stocks, it is the number of times that bond interest and preferred dividends combined have been covered.

respectable值得尊敬的，体面的concerns itself with关注，研究criterion标准total interest charges利息总支出covered by available earnings被可用盈利所覆盖（利息保障倍数的概念）

证券分析中最可靠、因而最受尊重的分支，是判断债券与投资级优先股的安全性或质量。公司债的主要标准，是过去若干年可用盈利覆盖全部利息费用多少倍；优先股则看盈利覆盖债券利息和优先股股息合计数的倍数。

译者补充（非原文）：若公司多年平均利息税前利润为700万元，年利息100万元，利息覆盖倍数就是7倍。利润下滑时，倍数越高，债权人的缓冲通常越厚。

The exact standards applied will vary with different authorities. Since the tests are at bottom arbitrary, there is no way to determine precisely the most suitable criteria. In the 1961 revision of our textbook, Security Analysis, we recommend certain “coverage” standards, which appear in Table 11-1.*

authorities权威人士at bottom归根结底coverage保障倍数（盈利对利息的覆盖倍数）

不同权威采用的具体标准会有差异。测试归根结底带有主观规定，不可能精确确定哪套指标最合适。我们在1961年修订《证券分析》时，提出了表11-1所列的若干“覆盖倍数”标准。

Our basic test is applied only to the average results for a period of years. Other authorities require also that a minimum coverage be shown for every year considered. We approve a “poorest-year” test as an alternative to the seven-year-average test; it would be sufficient if the bond or preferred stock met either of these criteria.

poorest-year最差年份as an alternative to作为……的替代met either of these criteria满足这两条标准中的任意一条

我们的基本测试只看多年平均结果。其他权威还要求所考察的每一年都达到最低覆盖倍数。我们赞同把“最差年度”测试作为七年平均测试的替代方案；债券或优先股满足其中任一标准即可。

C. 其他类别的债券和优先股

The standards given above are not applicable to (1) public-utility holding companies, (2) financial companies, (3) real-estate companies.

public-utility holding companies公用事业控股公司real-estate companies房地产公司

上述标准不适用于：公用事业控股公司、金融公司和房地产公司。

It may be objected that the large increase in bond interest rates since 1961 would justify some offsetting reduction in the coverage of charges required. Obviously it would be much harder for an industrial company to show a seven-times coverage of interest charges at 8% than at 4½%. To meet this changed situation we now suggest an alternative requirement related to the percent earned on the principal amount of the debt. These figures might be 33% before taxes for an industrial company, 20% for a public utility, and 25% for a railroad. It should be borne in mind here that the rate actually paid by most companies on their total debt is considerably less than the current 8% figures, since they have the benefit of older issues bearing lower coupons. The “poorest year” requirement could be set at about two-thirds of the seven-year requirement.

It may be objected that有人可能会反驳说offsetting reduction相应的降低（offsetting：抵消性的）seven-times coverage七倍的保障倍数To meet this changed situation为应对这一变化了的情况principal amount of the debt债务本金额borne in mind牢记（bear in mind 的过去分词）considerably less than远低于bearing lower coupons票面利率较低的（coupon：票息）

有人可能提出，1961年以来债券利率大幅上升，应允许相应降低所要求的费用覆盖倍数。显然，利率8%时工业公司要做到利息覆盖七倍，比利率4.5%时难得多。为适应变化，我们现在建议增加一项与债务本金收益百分比有关的替代标准：工业公司税前盈利可为债务本金的33%，公用事业20%，铁路25%。还要记住，多数公司全部债务的实际利率明显低于当前8%，因为它们仍受益于早年发行的低息债。“最差年度”的要求，可定为七年标准约三分之二。

In addition to the earnings-coverage test, a number of others are generally applied. These include the following:

earnings-coverage test盈利保障倍数测试

除盈利覆盖测试外，通常还会采用下列几项测试：

1. Size of Enterprise. There is a minimum standard in terms of volume of business for a corporation—varying as between industrials, utilities, and railroads—and of population for a municipality.

volume of business业务规模industrials工业公司municipality市政当局（发行市政债券的市镇）

一、企业规模。公司按业务量设最低标准，工业、公用事业和铁路各不相同；市政发行人则按人口设标准。

2. Stock/Equity Ratio. This is the ratio of the market price of the junior stock issues* to the total face amount of the debt, or the debt plus preferred stock. It is a rough measure of the protection, or “cushion,” afforded by the presence of a junior investment that must first bear the brunt of unfavorable developments. This factor includes the market’s appraisal of the future prospects of the enterprise.

junior stock issues次级股票（受偿顺序排在债券之后的股票）face amount面值总额cushion缓冲垫（比喻对债券的保护）bear the brunt of首当其冲地承受appraisal评估

二、普通股／权益比率。它是次级股票的市场价值与债务面值总额，或债务加优先股面值总额之比。普通股须先承受不利变化的冲击，所以其存在为优先证券提供保护或“缓冲”；这个比率就是粗略衡量缓冲厚度，也包含市场对企业未来前景的评价。

译者补充（非原文）：公司有1亿元债务、普通股市值2亿元，权益缓冲是2倍；若企业价值下跌，先由普通股承担，债券本金才更晚受损。

3. Property Value. The asset values, as shown on the balance sheet or as appraised, were formerly considered the chief security and protection for a bond issue. Experience has shown that in most cases safety resides in the earning power, and if this is deficient the assets lose most of their reputed value. Asset values, however, retain importance as a separate test of ample security for bonds and preferred stocks in three enterprise groups: public utilities (because rates may depend largely on the property investment), real-estate concerns, and investment companies.

chief security主要的担保（security 此处指担保物，不是“证券”）resides in存在于reputed号称的，名义上的rates费率（公用事业的收费标准）real-estate concerns房地产公司（concern 在本书中常指企业）

三、财产价值。过去，资产负债表所列或评估所得的资产价值，被视为债券安全和保障的首要来源。经验表明，多数情况下安全性来自盈利能力；盈利不足，资产所谓的价值往往也会大半消失。不过，对三类企业的债券和优先股，资产价值仍是检验保障是否充足的独立标准：公用事业（费率可能主要取决于财产投资）、房地产企业和投资公司。

At this point the alert investor should ask, “How dependable are tests of safety that are measured by past and present performance, in view of the fact that payment of interest and principal depends upon what the future will bring forth?” The answer can be founded only on experience. Investment history shows that bonds and preferred stocks that have met stringent tests of safety, based on the past, have in the great majority of cases been able to face the vicissitudes of the future successfully. This has been strikingly demonstrated in the major field of railroad bonds—a field that has been marked by a calamitous frequency of bankruptcies and serious losses. In nearly every case the roads that got into trouble had long been overbonded, had shown an inadequate coverage of fixed charges in periods of average prosperity, and would thus have been ruled out by investors who applied strict tests of safety. Conversely, practically every road that has met such tests has escaped financial embarrassment. Our premise was strikingly vindicated by the financial history of the numerous railroads reorganized in the 1940s and in 1950. All of these, with one exception, started their careers with fixed charges reduced to a point where the current coverage of fixed-interest requirements was ample, or at least respectable. The exception was the New Haven Railroad, which in its reorganization year, 1947, earned its new charges only about 1.1 times. In consequence, while all the other roads were able to come through rather difficult times with solvency unimpaired, the New Haven relapsed into trusteeship (for the third time) in 1961.

in view of the fact that鉴于……这一事实bring forth带来，产生stringent严格的vicissitudes变迁，兴衰起伏calamitous灾难性的the roads这些铁路公司（road 此处指 railroad）overbonded债券发行过度的，负债过重的ruled out排除financial embarrassment财务困境（embarrassment 此处不是“尴尬”）premise前提vindicated证实，证明正确earned its new charges only about 1.1 times盈利只有新固定费用的约 1.1 倍solvency unimpaired偿付能力未受损害relapsed into trusteeship再度陷入托管（破产管理）

In nearly every case the roads that got into trouble had long been overbonded, had shown an inadequate coverage of fixed charges in periods of average prosperity, and would thus have been ruled out by investors who applied strict tests of safety.

几乎在每一个案例中，陷入困境的铁路公司都早已负债过重，在一般景气时期的固定费用保障倍数就已经不足，因此本来就会被采用严格安全标准的投资者排除在外。

主语 the roads（此处指 railroads）后面接三个并列谓语 had long been … / had shown … / would thus have been ruled out；最后一个用虚拟语气 would have been，表示“如果投资者当时用了严格标准，本来就会……”。

警觉的投资者此时会问：“利息和本金能否支付取决于未来，按过去和现在表现衡量的安全测试有多可靠？”答案只能来自经验。投资史表明，按过去数据通过严格安全测试的债券和优先股，绝大多数都能成功应对未来变故。铁路债是最鲜明的证明；这个领域破产和重大损失发生得灾难性地频繁。几乎所有陷入困境的铁路公司，早已负债过重，在一般繁荣时期固定费用覆盖也不足，采用严格测试的投资者本会排除它们。反过来，几乎每家通过测试的铁路都避开了财务困境。20世纪40年代和1950年大量重组铁路的财务历史，强有力地证实了这一前提。除一家外，它们重启时都把固定费用降到当期盈利足以充分或至少像样覆盖的水平。例外是纽黑文铁路，1947年重组当年，新固定费用只被盈利覆盖约1.1倍。结果，其他铁路都在艰难时期保持偿付能力，纽黑文却于1961年第三次进入托管。

In Chapter 17 below we shall consider some aspects of the bankruptcy of the Penn Central Railroad, which shook the financial community in 1970. An elementary fact in this case was that the coverage of fixed charges did not meet conservative standards as early as 1965; hence a prudent bond investor would have avoided or disposed of the bond issues of the system long before its financial collapse.

shook the financial community震动了金融界prudent审慎的disposed of处置，卖掉financial collapse财务崩溃

第17章会讨论1970年震动金融界的宾夕法尼亚中央铁路破产。一个基本事实是，该系统固定费用覆盖倍数早在1965年就达不到保守标准；谨慎的债券投资者会在财务崩溃很久前避开或卖掉其债券。

Our observations on the adequacy of the past record to judge future safety apply, and to an even greater degree, to the public utilities, which constitute a major area for bond investment. Receivership of a soundly capitalized (electric) utility company or system is almost impossible. Since Securities and Exchange Commission control was instituted,* along with the breakup of most of the holding-company systems, public-utility financing has been sound and bankruptcies unknown. The financial troubles of electric and gas utilities in the 1930s were traceable almost 100% to financial excesses and mismanagement, which left their imprint clearly on the companies’ capitalization structures. Simple but stringent tests of safety, therefore, would have warned the investor away from the issues that were later to default.

Receivership破产管理（由法院指定接管人管理公司财产）soundly capitalized资本结构稳健的Securities and Exchange Commission美国证券交易委员会（SEC）traceable可追溯至……的financial excesses财务上的过度行为left their imprint留下印记default违约

我们关于过去记录足以判断未来安全性的看法，对债券投资重镇公用事业同样适用，而且程度更高。资本结构稳健的电力公用事业公司或系统几乎不可能进入接管程序。SEC开始监管并拆分大多数控股公司体系后，公用事业融资一直稳健，也没有破产。20世纪30年代电气和燃气公用事业的财务麻烦，几乎全部源自融资过度与管理不善，并清楚留痕在资本结构中。因此，简单而严格的安全测试本可提醒投资者远离后来违约的证券。

Among industrial bond issues the long-term record has been different. Although the industrial group as a whole has shown a better growth of earning power than either the railroads or the utilities, it has revealed a lesser degree of inherent stability for individual companies and lines of business. Thus in the past, at least, there have been persuasive reasons for confining the purchase of industrial bonds and preferred stocks to companies that not only are of major size but also have shown an ability in the past to withstand a serious depression.

inherent stability内在的稳定性lines of business业务领域，行业confining限制在of major size规模很大的withstand经受住

工业债的长期记录不同。工业企业整体盈利增长胜过铁路和公用事业，但单个公司和行业的内在稳定性较差。至少按过去经验，购买工业债和优先股应限于规模大、而且过去证明有能力承受严重萧条的公司，理由很充分。

Few defaults of industrial bonds have occurred since 1950, but this fact is attributable in part to the absence of a major depression during this long period. Since 1966 there have been adverse developments in the financial position of many industrial companies. Considerable difficulties have developed as the result of unwise expansion. On the one hand this has involved large additions to both bank loans and long-term debt; on the other it has frequently produced operating losses instead of the expected profits. At the beginning of 1971 it was calculated that in the past seven years the interest payments of all nonfinancial firms had grown from $9.8 billion in 1963 to $26.1 billion in 1970, and that interest payments had taken 29% of the aggregate profits before interest and taxes in 1971, against only 16% in 1963.3 Obviously, the burden on many individual firms had increased much more than this. Overbonded companies have become all too familiar. There is every reason to repeat the caution expressed in our 1965 edition:

attributable in part to部分归因于adverse developments不利的事态发展unwise expansion不明智的扩张operating losses经营亏损nonfinancial firms非金融企业aggregate profits before interest and taxes息税前利润总额Overbonded债券发行过度的，负债过重的all too familiar太常见了There is every reason to完全有理由

1950年以来工业债违约很少，但部分原因是这段漫长时期没有发生大萧条。1966年后，许多工业公司的财务状况出现不利变化，盲目扩张带来相当困难：一方面银行贷款与长期债务都大增，另一方面经营结果常从预期利润变成亏损。1971年初的计算显示，过去七年里，全部非金融企业利息支出从1963年的98亿美元增至1970年的261亿美元；1971年，利息占企业利息税前利润合计数的29%，1963年仅16%。显然，许多单个企业的负担增长远超平均。负债过重的公司已屡见不鲜。我们完全有理由重复1965年版的警告：

We are not quite ready to suggest that the investor may count on an indefinite continuance of this favorable situation, and hence relax his standards of bond selection in the industrial or any other group.

count on指望indefinite continuance无限期的持续relax his standards放松标准

我们还不能建议投资者相信这种有利局面会无限延续，因而放松工业或其他任何领域的债券选择标准。

Common-Stock Analysis

普通股分析

The ideal form of common-stock analysis leads to a valuation of the issue which can be compared with the current price to determine whether or not the security is an attractive purchase. This valuation, in turn, would ordinarily be found by estimating the average earnings over a period of years in the future and then multiplying that estimate by an appropriate “capitalization factor.”

valuation of the issue对该股票的估值an attractive purchase值得买入的对象in turn进而，反过来capitalization factor资本化因子（把盈利换算成价值的乘数，即市盈率）

理想的普通股分析会得出一项估值，再与当前价格比较，判断证券是否值得买。通常的估值办法，是估计未来若干年的平均盈利，再乘以适当的“资本化倍数”。

The now-standard procedure for estimating future earning power starts with average past data for physical volume, prices received, and operating margin. Future sales in dollars are then projected on the basis of assumptions as to the amount of change in volume and price level over the previous base. These estimates, in turn, are grounded first on general economic forecasts of gross national product, and then on special calculations applicable to the industry and company in question.

physical volume实物销量operating margin营业利润率grounded建立在……的基础上gross national product国民生产总值in question所讨论的，所涉及的

如今估计未来盈利能力的标准程序，从过去的实物销量、售价和营业利润率平均数据出发；再假设销量和价格水平相对基期会怎样变化，预测未来销售额。这些估计先建立在对国民生产总值的一般经济预测上，再结合有关行业和公司的专门计算。

An illustration of this method of valuation may be taken from our 1965 edition and brought up to date by adding the sequel. The Value Line, a leading investment service, makes forecasts of future earnings and dividends by the procedure outlined above, and then derives a figure of “price potentiality” (or projected market value) by applying a valuation formula to each issue based largely on certain past relationships. In Table 11-2 we reproduce the projections for 1967–1969 made in June 1964, and compare them with the earnings, and average market price actually realized in 1968 (which approximates the 1967–1969 period).

这个估值方法可用1965年版的例子说明，并补上后续结果。领先投资服务机构Value Line按上述程序预测未来盈利和股息，再主要依据若干历史关系，对每只股票套用估值公式，得出“价格潜力”（或预计市场价值）。表11-2重列其1964年6月对1967至1969年的预测，并与1968年的实际盈利和平均市场价格比较；1968年大致代表1967至1969这段时期。

The combined forecasts proved to be somewhat on the low side, but not seriously so. The corresponding predictions made six years before had turned out to be overoptimistic on earnings and dividends; but this had been offset by use of a low multiplier, with the result that the “price potentiality” figure proved to be about the same as the actual average price for 1963.

on the low side偏低overoptimistic过于乐观的offset抵消multiplier乘数，市盈率

合计预测结果略偏低，但不算严重。六年前所作的对应预测，在盈利和股息上过度乐观；不过采用的倍数较低，抵销了误差，所以“价格潜力”与1963年的实际平均价格大致相同。

The reader will note that quite a number of the individual forecasts were wide of the mark. This is an instance in support of our general view that composite or group estimates are likely to be a good deal more dependable than those for individual companies. Ideally, perhaps, the security analyst should pick out the three or four companies whose future he thinks he knows the best, and concentrate his own and his clients’ interest on what he forecasts for them. Unfortunately, it appears to be almost impossible to distinguish in advance between those individual forecasts which can be relied upon and those which are subject to a large chance of error. At bottom, this is the reason for the wide diversification practiced by the investment funds. For it is undoubtedly better to concentrate on one stock that you know is going to prove highly profitable, rather than dilute your results to a mediocre figure, merely for diversification’s sake. But this is not done, because it cannot be done dependably. 4 The prevalence of wide diversification is in itself a pragmatic repudiation of the fetish of “selectivity,” to which Wall Street constantly pays lip service.*

For it is undoubtedly better to concentrate on one stock that you know is going to prove highly profitable, rather than dilute your results to a mediocre figure, merely for diversification’s sake. But this is not done, because it cannot be done dependably.

因为，如果你确知某只股票将会带来丰厚利润，把资金集中在它上面无疑好过仅仅为了分散而分散、把成绩稀释成一个平庸的数字。但没有人这样做，因为这没法可靠地做到。

读者会注意到，不少单项预测偏差很大。这支持我们的总体看法：组合或群体估计，通常比单个公司估计可靠得多。理想情况下，分析师也许应挑出三四家自己最了解未来的公司，让自己和客户集中关注这些预测。遗憾的是，事先几乎无法分辨哪些个别预测可靠、哪些很可能大错。这正是投资基金广泛分散的根本原因。若能确定某只股票会带来丰厚利润，集中持有当然比为了分散而把结果稀释到平庸水平更好；但人们不这样做，因为无法可靠地做到。广泛分散的普遍存在，本身就是用实践否定华尔街嘴上不断推崇的“精选”迷信。

译者补充（非原文）：分散化并不是说每家公司都不了解，而是承认“最有把握的预测也可能错”。它用少数赢家覆盖无法事先识别的错误。

Factors Affecting the Capitalization Rate

影响资本化率的因素

Though average future earnings are supposed to be the chief determinant of value, the security analyst takes into account a number of other factors of a more or less definite nature. Most of these will enter into his capitalization rate, which can vary over a wide range, depending upon the “quality” of the stock issue. Thus, although two companies may have the same figure of expected earnings per share in 1973–1975—say $4—the analyst may value one as low as 40 and the other as high as 100. Let us deal briefly with some of the considerations that enter into these divergent multipliers.

chief determinant主要决定因素of a more or less definite nature或多或少明确的capitalization rate资本化率（决定用多少倍盈利来给股票定价的比率）vary over a wide range在很大范围内变动divergent multipliers差异悬殊的市盈率倍数

平均未来盈利虽被视为价值的主要决定因素，证券分析师还会考虑若干相对明确的其他因素。多数因素会进入资本化率；倍数范围可以很宽，取决于股票的“质量”。因此，两家公司1973至1975年的预期每股盈利可能同为4美元，分析师却可能只给一家40美元估值，给另一家100美元。下面简述造成倍数差异的因素。

1. General Long-Term Prospects. No one really knows anything about what will happen in the distant future, but analysts and investors have strong views on the subject just the same. These views are reflected in the substantial differentials between the price/earnings ratios of individual companies and of industry groups. At this point we added in our 1965 edition:

just the same尽管如此，仍然substantial differentials显著的差异price/earnings ratios市盈率

一、一般长期前景。没有人真正知道遥远未来会发生什么，分析师和投资者却照样对此抱有强烈看法。这些看法反映为不同公司和行业市盈率之间的显著差异。1965年版中，我们在这里补充道：

For example, at the end of 1963 the chemical companies in the DJIA were selling at considerably higher multipliers than the oil companies, indicating stronger confidence in the prospects of the former than of the latter. Such distinctions made by the market are often soundly based, but when dictated mainly by past performance they are as likely to be wrong as right.

selling at以……的价格交易soundly based有充分根据的dictated mainly by主要由……决定as likely to be wrong as right对错的可能性各半

例如，1963年末，道指中的化工公司按明显高于石油公司的倍数交易，说明市场对前者前景信心更强。市场作出的这类区别常有合理依据，但若主要由过去表现驱动，出错与正确的概率差不多。

We shall supply here, in Table 11-3, the 1963 year-end material on the chemical and oil company issues in the DJIA, and carry their earnings to the end of 1970. It will be seen that the chemical companies, despite their high multipliers, made practically no gain in earnings in the period after 1963. The oil companies did much better than the chemicals and about in line with the growth implied in their 1963 multipliers.5 Thus our chemical-stock example proved to be one of the cases in which the market multipliers were proven wrong.*

year-end material年末的数据资料carry their earnings to把它们的盈利数据延续到practically no gain几乎没有增长about in line with大致符合implied in隐含在……中

表11-3列出1963年末道指化工股和石油股资料，并把盈利延续到1970年末。可以看到，化工公司虽然倍数很高，1963年后盈利几乎没有增长；石油公司则好得多，大致符合1963年倍数所隐含的增长。所以化工股成为市场倍数判断错误的案例。

2. Management. On Wall Street a great deal is constantly said on this subject, but little that is really helpful. Until objective, quantitative, and reasonably reliable tests of managerial competence are devised and applied, this factor will continue to be looked at through a fog. It is fair to assume that an outstandingly successful company has unusually good management. This will have shown itself already in the past record; it will show up again in the estimates for the next five years, and once more in the previously discussed factor of long-term prospects. The tendency to count it still another time as a separate bullish consideration can easily lead to expensive overvaluations. The management factor is most useful, we think, in those cases in which a recent change has taken place that has not yet had the time to show its significance in the actual figures.

little that is really helpful真正有用的却很少managerial competence管理能力devised设计出looked at through a fog隔着迷雾看（看不清楚）shown itself显现出来count it still another time把它再算一次bullish consideration看涨的考虑因素overvaluations估值过高

二、管理层。华尔街不断谈论管理，却很少说出真正有帮助的东西。只要还没有制定并应用客观、量化而且较可靠的管理能力测试，这个因素就会一直隔着迷雾观察。可以合理假定，格外成功的公司拥有格外优秀的管理层；但这已经反映在历史记录中，也会再次进入未来五年估计和前面讨论的长期前景。若再把管理层作为独立利好计算一次，很容易导致昂贵的高估。我们认为，管理因素最有用的情形，是近期发生了变化，其意义尚未来得及反映在实际数字中。

Two spectacular occurrences of this kind were associated with the Chrysler Motor Corporation. The first took place as far back as 1921, when Walter Chrysler took command of the almost moribund Maxwell Motors, and in a few years made it a large and highly profitable enterprise, while numerous other automobile companies were forced out of business. The second happened as recently as 1962, when Chrysler had fallen far from its once high estate and the stock was selling at its lowest price in many years. Then new interests, associated with Consolidation Coal, took over the reins. The earnings advanced from the 1961 figure of $1.24 per share to the equivalent of $17 in 1963, and the price rose from a low of 38½ in 1962 to the equivalent of nearly 200 the very next year.6

as far back as早在took command of接掌moribund奄奄一息的forced out of business被迫倒闭fallen far from its once high estate从昔日的显赫地位一落千丈（estate：地位、状况）new interests新的利益集团（此处指新的控股方）took over the reins接管了控制权（reins：缰绳）the equivalent of相当于

克莱斯勒汽车公司有过两次这类戏剧性事件。第一次早在1921年，沃尔特·克莱斯勒接管奄奄一息的麦克斯韦汽车，几年内把它变成大型高利润企业，同时许多其他汽车公司被淘汰。第二次在1962年：克莱斯勒早已从昔日高位跌落，股价处在多年最低点；随后与联合煤炭有关的新股东掌舵。每股盈利从1961年的1.24美元升至1963年折合17美元，股价也从1962年低点38.5升至第二年折合近200。

3. Financial Strength and Capital Structure. Stock of a company with a lot of surplus cash and nothing ahead of the common is clearly a better purchase (at the same price) than another one with the same per share earnings but large bank loans and senior securities. Such factors are properly and carefully taken into account by security analysts. A modest amount of bonds or preferred stock, however, is not necessarily a disadvantage to the common, nor is the moderate use of seasonal bank credit. (Incidentally, a top-heavy structure—too little common stock in relation to bonds and preferred—may under favorable conditions make for a huge speculative profit in the common. This is the factor known as “leverage.”)

surplus cash多余的现金nothing ahead of the common没有任何证券排在普通股之前（即没有债务和优先股）senior securities优先证券（债券和优先股）seasonal bank credit季节性银行信贷Incidentally顺便说一句top-heavy structure头重脚轻的资本结构（债务和优先股比重过大）make for促成，导致leverage杠杆

三、财务实力与资本结构。在价格相同、每股盈利相同的情况下，拥有大量多余现金且普通股之前没有优先证券的公司，显然比背负大量银行贷款和高级证券的公司更值得买。证券分析师会恰当而认真地考虑这些因素。不过，适量债券或优先股不一定对普通股不利，适度使用季节性银行信贷也一样。（顺带说，普通股相对债券和优先股太少的头重脚轻结构，在有利条件下可能让普通股产生巨额投机利润，这就是“杠杆”。）

4. Dividend Record. One of the most persuasive tests of high quality is an uninterrupted record of dividend payments going back over many years. We think that a record of continuous dividend payments for the last 20 years or more is an important plus factor in the company’s quality rating. Indeed the defensive investor might be justified in limiting his purchases to those meeting this test.

uninterrupted record从未间断的记录plus factor加分因素quality rating质量评级justified in有理由……

四、股息记录。多年从未中断派息，是最有说服力的高质量检验之一。我们认为，过去二十年或更久持续派息，是公司质量评级的重要加分项。防御型投资者甚至可以合理地把购买范围限于通过此项测试的公司。

5. Current Dividend Rate. This, our last additional factor, is the most difficult one to deal with in satisfactory fashion. Fortunately, the majority of companies have come to follow what may be called a standard dividend policy. This has meant the distribution of about two-thirds of their average earnings, except that in the recent period of high profits and inflationary demands for more capital the figure has tended to be lower. (In 1969 it was 59.5% for the stocks in the Dow Jones average, and 55% for all American corporations.)* Where the dividend bears a normal relationship to the earnings, the valuation may be made on either basis without substantially affecting the result. For example, a typical secondary company with expected average earnings of $3 and an expected dividend of $2 may be valued at either 12 times its earnings or 18 times its dividend, to yield a value of 36 in both cases.

in satisfactory fashion以令人满意的方式come to follow逐渐采用inflationary demands for more capital通胀带来的更多资本需求bears a normal relationship to与……保持正常的关系on either basis以两者中的任一为基础secondary company二线公司to yield a value of得出……的价值

五、当前股息率。这是最后一个附加因素，也是最难令人满意处理的因素。好在多数公司已经遵循一种可称为标准的股息政策：大约派发平均盈利的三分之二；但近年利润高、通胀又要求更多资本，比例趋于下降。（1969年，道指成分股为59.5%，全部美国公司为55%。）如果股息与盈利保持正常关系，用任何一项估值都不会明显改变结果。例如，一家典型二线公司预期平均每股盈利3美元、股息2美元；按12倍盈利或18倍股息估值，结果都是36美元。

However, an increasing number of growth companies are departing from the once standard policy of paying out 60% or more of earnings in dividends, on the grounds that the shareholders’ interests will be better served by retaining nearly all the profits to finance expansion. The issue presents problems and requires careful distinctions. We have decided to defer our discussion of the vital question of proper dividend policy to a later section—Chapter 19—where we shall deal with it as a part of the general problem of management-shareholder relations.

departing from背离paying out派发（股息）on the grounds that理由是retaining留存The issue这个问题（issue 此处指问题，不是证券）defer推迟

但越来越多成长公司偏离过去派发60%以上盈利的标准政策，理由是保留几乎全部利润用于扩张，更符合股东利益。这个问题需要仔细区分。我们决定把适当股息政策这一重要议题留到第19章，作为管理层与股东关系的一部分讨论。

Capitalization Rates for Growth Stocks

成长股的资本化率

Most of the writing of security analysts on formal appraisals relates to the valuation of growth stocks. Our study of the various methods has led us to suggest a foreshortened and quite simple formula for the valuation of growth stocks, which is intended to produce figures fairly close to those resulting from the more refined mathematical calculations. Our formula is:

It is explainable in part by the stock market’s feeling that General Motors’ 1963 earnings—the largest for any corporation in history—can be maintained with difficulty and exceeded only modestly at best. We should have added a caution somewhat as follows: The valuations of expected high-growth stocks are necessarily on the low side, if we were to assume these growth rates will actually be realized. In fact, according to the arithmetic, if a company could be assumed to grow at a rate of 8% or more indefinitely in the future its value would be infinite, and no price would be too high to pay for the shares. What the valuer actually does in these cases is to introduce a margin of safety into his calculations—somewhat as an engineer does in his specifications for a structure. On this basis the purchases would realize his assigned objective (in 1963, a future overall return of 7½% per annum) even if the growth rate actually realized proved substantially less than that projected in the formula. Of course, then, if that rate were actually realized the investor would be sure to enjoy a handsome additional return. There is really no way of valuing a high-growth company (with an expected rate above, say, 8% annually), in which the analyst can make realistic assumptions of both the proper multiplier for the current earnings and the expectable multiplier for the future earnings.

我们本应加上一段提醒：若假设预期高增长确会实现，公式对高增长股票给出的估值必然偏低。按纯数学推演，一家公司若能永远以8%或更高速度增长，其价值会趋于无限，任何股价都不算太高。估值者真正做的，是像工程师设计结构一样，在计算中加入安全边际。按此方法，即使实际增长明显低于公式预测，买入仍可达到预设目标（1963年设定为未来每年总回报7.5%）；若增长真能实现，投资者自然取得可观额外回报。对预期年增长超过约8%的公司，实际上没有一种估值法，能同时对当前盈利的合理倍数和未来盈利可能对应的倍数作出现实假设。

As it happened the actual growth for Xerox and IBM proved very close to the high rates implied from our formula. As just explained, this fine showing inevitably produced a large advance in the price of both issues. The growth of the DJIA itself was also about as projected by the 1963 closing market price. But the moderate rate of 5% did not involve the mathematical dilemma of Xerox and IBM. It turned out that the 23% price rise to the end of 1970, plus the 28% in aggregate dividend return received, gave not far from the 7½% annual overall gain posited in our formula. In the case of the other four companies it may suffice to say that their growth did not equal the expectations implied in the 1963 price and that their quotations failed to rise as much as the DJIA. Warning: This material is supplied for illustrative purposes only, and because of the inescapable necessity in security analysis to project the future growth rate for most companies studied. Let the reader not be misled into thinking that such projections have any high degree of reliability or, conversely, that future prices can be counted on to behave accordingly as the prophecies are realized, surpassed, or disappointed.

We should point out that any “scientific,” or at least reasonably dependable, stock evaluation based on anticipated future results must take future interest rates into account. A given schedule of expected earnings, or dividends, would have a smaller present value if we assume a higher than if we assume a lower interest structure.* Such assumptions have always been difficult to make with any degree of confidence, and the recent violent swings in long-term interest rates render forecasts of this sort almost presumptuous. Hence we have retained our old formula above, simply because no new one would appear more plausible.

任何以未来预期结果为基础、号称“科学”或至少相当可靠的股票估值，都必须考虑未来利率。预期盈利或股息相同，假定利率越高，现值越小；利率越低，现值越大。对利率作有把握的假设从来很难，近期长期利率剧烈摆动，更让这种预测近乎自负。因此，我们保留上述旧公式，只因看不出新公式会更可信。

Industry Analysis

行业分析

Because the general prospects of the enterprise carry major weight in the establishment of market prices, it is natural for the security analyst to devote a great deal of attention to the economic position of the industry and of the individual company in its industry. Studies of this kind can go into unlimited detail. They are sometimes productive of valuable insights into important factors that will be operative in the future and are insufficiently appreciated by the current market. Where a conclusion of that kind can be drawn with a fair degree of confidence, it affords a sound basis for investment decisions.

carry major weight有很大分量go into unlimited detail可以无止境地深入细节productive of能产生……operative起作用的insufficiently appreciated未被充分认识affords提供

企业整体前景在形成市价时分量很重，所以证券分析师自然会投入大量精力研究行业经济地位，以及公司在行业中的位置。这类研究可以无限细化，有时能看出未来会起重要作用、当前市场又未充分认识的因素。若能以相当把握得出这种结论，就为投资决策提供了稳健基础。

Our own observation, however, leads us to minimize somewhat the practical value of most of the industry studies that are made available to investors. The material developed is ordinarily of a kind with which the public is already fairly familiar and that has already exerted considerable influence on market quotations. Rarely does one find a brokerage-house study that points out, with a convincing array of facts, that a popular industry is heading for a fall or that an unpopular one is due to prosper. Wall Street’s view of the longer future is notoriously fallible, and this necessarily applies to that important part of its investigations which is directed toward the forecasting of the course of profits in various industries.

不过，按我们的观察，应适度降低对多数公开行业研究实际价值的评价。材料通常是公众已相当熟悉、也已显著影响市场报价的内容。很少看到券商报告用一整套有说服力的事实指出，热门行业将要衰落，或冷门行业即将繁荣。华尔街对较长期未来的看法出错是出了名的，其研究中预测各行业利润走向的重要部分，自然也逃不过这一点。

We must recognize, however, that the rapid and pervasive growth of technology in recent years is not without major effect on the attitude and the labors of the security analyst. More so than in the past, the progress or retrogression of the typical company in the coming decade may depend on its relation to new products and new processes, which the analyst may have a chance to study and evaluate in advance. Thus there is doubtless a promising area for effective work by the analyst, based on field trips, interviews with research men, and on intensive technological investigation on his own. There are hazards connected with investment conclusions derived chiefly from such glimpses into the future, and not supported by presently demonstrable value. Yet there are perhaps equal hazards in sticking closely to the limits of value set by sober calculations resting on actual results. The investor cannot have it both ways. He can be imaginative and play for the big profits that are the reward for vision proved sound by the event; but then he must run a substantial risk of major or minor miscalculation. Or he can be conservative, and refuse to pay more than a minor premium for possibilities as yet unproved; but in that case he must be prepared for the later contemplation of golden opportunities foregone.

但必须承认，近年来技术快速而广泛的发展，确实深刻影响证券分析师的态度和工作。未来十年，典型公司的进步或倒退，比过去更可能取决于它与新产品、新工艺的关系，而分析师有机会提前研究评价。因此，实地走访、采访研发人员和亲自深入调查技术，为分析师提供了有希望的有效工作领域。主要依据对未来的一瞥、却没有当前可证明价值支撑的投资结论，当然危险；但只守着实际结果和冷静计算划定的价值界限，也可能同样危险。投资者不能两者兼得。他可以发挥想象，追求远见得到事实证明后的巨大利润，但必须承受判断出现大小错误的显著风险；也可以保持保守，只愿为尚未证实的可能性支付少量溢价，但要准备日后看着黄金机会从身边错过。

A Two-Part Appraisal Process

两段式评估法

Let us return for a moment to the idea of valuation or appraisal of a common stock, which we began to discuss above on p. 288. A great deal of reflection on the subject has led us to conclude that this better be done quite differently than is now the established practice. We suggest that analysts work out first what we call the “past-performance value,” which is based solely on the past record. This would indicate what the stock would be worth—absolutely, or as a percentage of the DJIA or of the S & P composite—if it is assumed that its relative past performance will continue unchanged in the future. (This includes the assumption that its relative growth rate, as shown in the last seven years, will also continue unchanged over the next seven years.) This process could be carried out mechanically by applying a formula that gives individual weights to past figures for profitability, stability, and growth, and also for current financial condition. The second part of the analysis should consider to what extent the value based solely on past performance should be modified because of new conditions expected in the future.

回到第288页开始讨论的普通股估值。经过大量思考，我们认为，做法最好与现行惯例相当不同。建议分析师先算出只依据历史记录的“过去业绩价值”。它表示：假设公司相对过去的表现未来不变，这只股票绝对值多少，或相当于道指、标普综合指数的多少百分比。（还假设过去七年显示的相对增长率，未来七年继续不变。）可以用机械公式完成，分别给历史盈利能力、稳定性、增长和当前财务状况赋权。第二步再考虑，因为预期未来会有新情况，纯历史业绩价值应调整多少。

Such a procedure would divide the work between senior and junior analysts as follows: (1) The senior analyst would set up the formula to apply to all companies generally for determining past-performance value. (2) The junior analysts would work up such factors for the designated companies—pretty much in mechanical fashion. (3) The senior analyst would then determine to what extent a company’s performance—absolute or relative—is likely to differ from its past record, and what change should be made in the value to reflect such anticipated changes. It would be best if the senior analyst’s report showed both the original valuation and the modified one, with his reasons for the change.

set up the formula建立公式work up整理出，算出designated指定的pretty much in mechanical fashion差不多以机械的方式absolute or relative绝对的或相对的anticipated changes预期的变化

这套程序可把工作分给高级与初级分析师：第一，高级分析师建立适用于所有公司、计算历史业绩价值的一般公式；第二，初级分析师用相当机械的方式，为指定公司整理各项因素；第三，高级分析师判断公司未来的绝对或相对表现可能在多大程度上偏离过去，并确定应怎样调整价值。高级分析师的报告最好同时列出原始估值、修正估值和修改理由。

Is a job of this kind worth doing? Our answer is in the affirmative, but our reasons may appear somewhat cynical to the reader. We doubt whether the valuations so reached will prove sufficiently dependable in the case of the typical industrial company, great or small. We shall illustrate the difficulties of this job in our discussion of Aluminum Company of America (ALCOA) in the next chapter. Nonetheless it should be done for such common stocks. Why? First, many security analysts are bound to make current or projected valuations, as part of their daily work. The method we propose should be an improvement on those generally followed today. Secondly, because it should give useful experience and insight to the analysts who practice this method. Thirdly, because work of this kind could produce an invaluable body of recorded experience—as has long been the case in medicine—that may lead to better methods of procedure and a useful knowledge of its possibilities and limitations. The public-utility stocks might well prove an important area in which this approach will show real pragmatic value. Eventually the intelligent analyst will confine himself to those groups in which the future appears reasonably predictable,* or where the margin of safety of past-performance value over current price is so large that he can take his chances on future variations—as he does in selecting well-secured senior securities.

Eventually the intelligent analyst will confine himself to those groups in which the future appears reasonably predictable, or where the margin of safety of past-performance value over current price is so large that he can take his chances on future variations—as he does in selecting well-secured senior securities.

最终，聪明的分析师会把自己限制在这样一些股票群体中：要么其未来看起来相当可以预测，要么其过去业绩价值高出当前价格的安全边际大到足以让他去冒未来变动的风险——就像他在挑选有充分保障的优先证券时那样。

这项工作值得做吗？我们回答值得，但理由在读者看来也许有些冷峻。我们怀疑，对典型工业公司，无论大小，这样得到的估值都未必足够可靠。下一章讨论美国铝业时，会说明困难。尽管如此，普通股仍应做这项工作。第一，许多分析师日常本来就必须给出当前或预测估值，我们的方法应比常用方法有所改进。第二，实践会给分析师带来有用经验和洞察。第三，它能像医学长期积累病例那样，形成极有价值的记录，帮助改进程序，并认识方法的能力和局限。公用事业股也许是这套方法能显示真正实用价值的重要领域。最终，聪明的分析师会把自己限于未来较能合理预测的行业，或历史业绩价值相对当前价格的安全边际大到足以承受未来变化的股票，就像挑选有充分保障的高级证券一样。

In subsequent chapters we shall supply concrete examples of the application of analytical techniques. But they will only be illustrations. If the reader finds the subject interesting he should pursue it systematically and thoroughly before he considers himself qualified to pass a final buy-or-sell judgment of his own on a security issue.

pursue it systematically系统地钻研它qualified to有资格pass a final buy-or-sell judgment做出最终的买卖判断

随后几章会给出分析技术的具体应用，但都只是例子。若读者觉得这个主题有兴趣，应先系统、深入地学习，再认为自己有资格对一项证券独立作出最终买卖判断。

Notes · 注释（贾森·兹威格）

* The National Federation of Financial Analysts is now the Association for Investment Management and Research; its “quarterly” research publication, the Financial Analysts Journal, now appears every other month.
全国金融分析师联合会如今是投资管理与研究协会；其“季刊”《金融分析师杂志》现为双月刊。
* The higher the growth rate you project, and the longer the future period over which you project it, the more sensitive your forecast becomes to the slightest error. If, for instance, you estimate that a company earning $1 per share can raise that profit by 15% a year for the next 15 years, its earnings would end up at $8.14. If the market values the company at 35 times earnings, the stock would finish the period at roughly $285. But if earnings grow at 14% instead of 15%, the company would earn $7.14 at the end of the period—and, in the shock of that shortfall, investors would no longer be willing to pay 35 times earnings. At, say, 20 times earnings, the stock would end up around $140 per share, or more than 50% less. Because advanced mathematics gives the appearance of precision to the inherently iffy process of foreseeing the future, investors must be highly skeptical of anyone who claims to hold any complex computational key to basic financial problems. As Graham put it: “In 44 years of Wall Street experience and study, I have never seen dependable calculations made about common-stock values, or related investment policies, that went beyond simple arithmetic or the most elementary algebra. Whenever calculus is brought in, or higher algebra, you could take it as a warning signal that the operator was trying to substitute theory for experience, and usually also to give to speculation the deceptive guise of investment.” (See p. 570.)
预测的增长率越高、期限越长，微小误差造成的影响越大。假设公司每股赚1美元，未来15年每年增长15%，期末盈利为8.14美元；若市场给35倍市盈率，股价约285美元。但若实际增长14%，期末盈利只有7.14美元；预期落空后，投资者也许只肯给20倍，股价约140美元，少一半以上。高级数学会给本来不确定的未来预测披上精确外衣，所以凡有人声称用复杂计算掌握基本金融问题的钥匙，投资者都应高度怀疑。格雷厄姆说，自己44年华尔街经历中，从未见过超出简单算术或初等代数、又可靠的普通股价值计算；一旦有人用微积分或高等代数，往往是在用理论替代经验，并给投机套上投资的迷惑外观。
* In 1972, an investor in corporate bonds had little choice but to assemble his or her own portfolio. Today, roughly 500 mutual funds invest in corporate bonds, creating a convenient, well-diversified bundle of securities. Since it is not feasible to build a diversified bond portfolio on your own unless you have at least $100,000, the typical intelligent investor will be best off simply buying a low-cost bond fund and leaving the painstaking labor of credit research to its managers. For more on bond funds, see the commentary on Chapter 4.
1972年，公司债投资者几乎只能自己组组合。如今约有500只共同基金投资公司债，方便地提供分散化组合。个人若没有至少10万美元，很难自行建立分散债券组合；典型聪明投资者最好买低成本债券基金，把繁琐信用研究交给经理。更多内容见第4章评论。
* By “junior stock issues” Graham means shares of common stock. Preferred stock is considered “senior” to common stock because the company must pay all dividends on the preferred before paying any dividends on the common.
格雷厄姆所说“次级股票”指普通股。优先股地位高于普通股，因为公司必须先付清优先股股息，才能向普通股派息。
* After investors lost billions of dollars on the shares of recklessly assembled utility companies in 1929–1932, Congress authorized the SEC to regulate the issuance of utility stocks under the Public Utility Holding Company Act of 1935.
1929至1932年，投资者在胡乱拼装的公用事业公司股票上损失数十亿美元；国会随后通过1935年《公用事业控股公司法》，授权SEC监管公用事业股票发行。
* In more recent years, most mutual funds have almost robotically mimicked the Standard & Poor’s 500-stock index, lest any different holdings cause their returns to deviate from that of the index. In a countertrend, some fund companies have launched what they call “focused” portfolios, which own 25 to 50 stocks that the managers declare to be their “best ideas.” That leaves investors wondering whether the other funds run by the same managers contain their worst ideas. Considering that most of the “best idea” funds do not markedly outperform the averages, investors are also entitled to wonder whether the managers’ ideas are even worth having in the first place. For indisputably skilled investors like Warren Buffett, wide diversification would be foolish, since it would water down the concentrated force of a few great ideas. But for the typical fund manager or individual investor, not diversifying is foolish, since it is so difficult to select a limited number of stocks that will include most winners and exclude most losers. As you own more stocks, the damage any single loser can cause will decline, and the odds of owning all the big winners will rise. The ideal choice for most investors is a total stock market index fund, a low-cost way to hold every stock worth owning.
近年多数共同基金近乎机械地模仿标普500，生怕持仓不同导致回报偏离指数。反向潮流中，一些基金公司推出持有25至50只股票的“集中”组合，称其为经理的“最佳想法”；这让人怀疑，同一经理的其他基金装的是否是最差想法。多数“最佳想法”基金并未明显跑赢平均，经理的想法是否值得拥有也成问题。对巴菲特这样确有能力的投资者，广泛分散会稀释少数优秀想法；对典型经理或个人，不分散却很愚蠢，因为很难用少数股票涵盖大多数赢家、排除大多数输家。持股越多，单个失败者的破坏越小，拥有所有大赢家的概率越高。多数投资者的理想选择是低成本全市场指数基金。
* Graham’s point about chemical and oil companies in the 1960s applies to nearly every industry in nearly every time period. Wall Street’s consensus view of the future for any given sector is usually either too optimistic or too pessimistic. Worse, the consensus is at its most cheery just when the stocks are most overpriced—and gloomiest just when they are cheapest. The most recent example, of course, is technology and telecommunications stocks, which hit record highs when their future seemed brightest in 1999 and early 2000, and then crashed all the way through 2002. History proves that Wall Street’s “expert” forecasters are equally inept at predicting the performance of 1) the market as a whole, 2) industry sectors, and 3) specific stocks. As Graham points out, the odds that individual investors can do any better are not good. The intelligent investor excels by making decisions that are not dependent on the accuracy of anybody’s forecasts, including his or her own. (See Chapter 8.)
格雷厄姆关于60年代化工和石油公司的观点，几乎适用于任何时期的任何行业。华尔街对行业未来的共识通常过度乐观或悲观；最乐观时股票往往最贵，最悲观时反而最便宜。最近例子是科技和电信股：1999年和2000年初前景看似最明亮时创纪录上涨，随后一路崩到2002年。历史证明，华尔街“专家”预测整体市场、行业和个股都同样不擅长；个人能做得更好的概率也不高。聪明投资者的优势，是决策不依赖任何人的预测准确，包括自己的预测。
* This figure, now known as the “dividend payout ratio,” has dropped considerably since Graham’s day as American tax law discouraged investors from seeking, and corporations from paying, dividends.
