故事真正的要点是，一些最初买家把债券转成股票，并一路持有到大跌。他们违背了华尔街老格言：“永远不要把可转换债券转股。”为什么？因为一旦转股，你就失去了“优先获得利息的债权人地位，加上取得可观利润机会”的战略组合。你很可能从投资者变成投机者，而且时机往往不利，因为股票通常已经大涨。既然“永不转股”是好原则，这些经验丰富的基金经理为何仍把Eversharp债券换成股票并遭受尴尬损失？无疑是被公司前景和股票“有利的市场走势”冲昏了头。华尔街并非没有几条谨慎原则，问题在于最需要它们时，人们总会忘掉。于是才有另一句老话：“照我说的做，别照我做的做。”

Our general attitude toward new convertible issues is thus a mistrustful one. We mean here, as in other similar observations, that the investor should look more than twice before he buys them. After such hostile scrutiny he may find some exceptional offerings that are too good to refuse. The ideal combination, of course, is a strongly secured convertible, exchangeable for a common stock which itself is attractive, and at a price only slightly higher than the current market. Every now and then a new offering appears that meets these requirements. By the nature of the securities markets, however, you are more likely to find such an opportunity in some older issue which has developed into a favorable position rather than in a new flotation. (If a new issue is a really strong one, it is not likely to have a good conversion privilege.)

look more than twice再三审视（化用 look twice “仔细看”）hostile scrutiny挑剔的审查too good to refuse好得无法拒绝strongly secured有充分保障的exchangeable for可换成Every now and then时不时地developed into a favorable position已经演变到有利的状态flotation发行（新证券的公开发行）

因此，我们总体上不信任新发行的可转换证券。和其他类似意见一样，这不是说绝对不能买，而是投资者下手前应反复审视。经过敌意般严格的检查，也许会发现少数好得无法拒绝的发行。理想组合当然是：担保坚实，可转换成一只本身就有吸引力的普通股，而且转换价仅略高于当前市价。偶尔会有新发行满足这些条件；但由证券市场的性质决定，这种机会更可能出现在后来发展到有利位置的老证券，而不是新发行。（新证券若本身真正很强，通常不会同时给出优厚转换权。）

The fine balance between what is given and what is withheld in a standard-type convertible issue is well illustrated by the extensive use of this type of security in the financing of American Telephone & Telegraph Company. Between 1913 and 1957 the company sold at least nine separate issues of convertible bonds, most of them through subscription rights to shareholders. The convertible bonds had the important advantage to the company of bringing in a much wider class of buyers than would have been available for a stock offering, since the bonds were popular with many financial institutions which possess huge resources but some of which were not permitted to buy stocks. The interest return on the bonds has generally been less than half the corresponding dividend yield on the stock—a factor that was calculated to offset the prior claim of the bondholders. Since the company maintained its $9 dividend rate for 40 years (from 1919 to the stock split in 1959) the result was the eventual conversion of virtually all the convertible issues into common stock. Thus the buyers of these convertibles have fared well through the years—but not quite so well as if they had bought the capital stock in the first place. This example establishes the soundness of American Telephone & Telegraph, but not the intrinsic attractiveness of convertible bonds. To prove them sound in practice we should need to have a number of instances in which the convertible worked out well even though the common stock proved disappointing. Such instances are not easy to find.*

美国电话电报公司广泛采用可转换证券融资，很好地展示了标准型可转换证券中“给予”和“保留”的微妙平衡。1913—1957年，公司至少发行九批可转换债券，多数通过向股东配售认购权。对公司而言，这种债券的重要优点是能吸引比发行股票更广的买家，许多资金雄厚却受限不能买股票的金融机构都愿意购买。债券利息收益通常不到对应股票股息率的一半，用以抵消债券持有人的优先受偿权。公司从1919年至1959年拆股，连续40年维持9美元股息，结果几乎所有可转换债券最终都转成普通股。买家多年下来表现不错，但仍不如一开始直接买股票。这个例子证明的是美国电话电报公司稳健，并不能证明可转换债券本身有吸引力。若要证明后者实践中稳健，需要找到多个普通股令人失望、可转换证券仍表现良好的案例，而这类案例并不好找。

Effect of Convertible Issues on the Status of the Common Stock

可转换证券对普通股地位的影响

In a large number of cases convertibles have been issued in connection with mergers or new acquisitions. Perhaps the most striking example of this financial operation was the issuance by the NVF Corp. of nearly $100,000,000 of its 5% convertible bonds (plus warrants) in exchange for most of the common stock of Sharon Steel Co. This extraordinary deal is discussed below pp. 429–433. Typically the transaction results in a pro forma increase in the reported earnings per share of common stock; the shares advance in response to their larger earnings, so-called, but also because the management has given evidence of its energy, enterprise, and ability to make more money for the shareholders.* But there are two offsetting factors, one of which is practically ignored and the other entirely so in optimistic markets. The first is the actual dilution of the current and future earnings on the common stock that flows arithmetically from the new conversion rights. This dilution can be quantified by taking the recent earnings, or assuming some other figures, and calculating the adjusted earnings per share if all the convertible shares or bonds were actually converted. In the majority of companies the resulting reduction in per-share figures is not significant. But there are numerous exceptions to this statement, and there is danger that they will grow at an uncomfortable rate. The fast-expanding “conglomerates” have been the chief practitioners of convertible legerdemain. In Table 16-3 we list seven companies with large amounts of stock issuable on conversions or against warrants.†

Indicated Switches from Common into Preferred Stocks

宜从普通股换入优先股的情形

For decades before, say, 1956, common stocks yielded more than the preferred stocks of the same companies; this was particularly true if the preferred stock had a conversion privilege close to the market. The reverse is generally true at present. As a result there are a considerable number of convertible preferred stocks which are clearly more attractive than the related common shares. Owners of the common have nothing to lose and important advantages to gain by switching from their junior shares into the senior issue.

大约1956年以前的数十年，同一公司的普通股收益率高于优先股；当优先股带有接近市价的转换权时尤其如此。如今通常相反。因此，有相当多可转换优先股明显比对应普通股更有吸引力。普通股持有人若把较次级的普通股换成更优先的证券，不会失去什么，却能获得重要好处。

EXAMPLE: A typical example was presented by Studebaker-Worthington Corp. at the close of 1970. The common sold at 57, while the $5 convertible preferred finished at 87½. Each preferred share is exchangeable for 1½ shares of common, then worth 85½. This would indicate a small money difference against the buyer of the preferred. But dividends are being paid on the common at the annual rate of $1.20 (or $1.80 for the 1½ shares), against the $5 obtainable on one share of preferred. Thus the original adverse difference in price would probably be made up in less than a year, after which the preferred would probably return an appreciably higher dividend yield than the common for some time to come. But most important, of course, would be the senior position that the common shareholder would gain from the switch. At the low prices of 1968 and again in 1970 the preferred sold 15 points higher than 1½ shares of common. Its conversion privilege guarantees that it could never sell lower than the common package.2

Stock-Option Warrants

股票认购权证

Let us mince no words at the outset. We consider the recent development of stock-option warrants as a near fraud, an existing menace, and a potential disaster. They have created huge aggregate dollar “values” out of thin air. They have no excuse for existence except to the extent that they mislead speculators and investors. They should be prohibited by law, or at least strictly limited to a minor part of the total capitalization of a company.*

mince no words直言不讳a near fraud近乎欺诈menace威胁out of thin air凭空total capitalization总资本（公司全部证券的总额）

开门见山地说，我们认为近年来认股权证的发展近乎欺诈，是现实威胁，也可能酿成灾难。它们凭空制造出巨额总“价值”，除了误导投机者和投资者，几乎没有存在理由。法律应禁止它，或至少严格限制在公司总资本的一小部分。

For an analogy in general history and in literature we refer the reader to the section of Faust (part 2), in which Goethe describes the invention of paper money. As an ominous precedent on Wall Street history, we may mention the warrants of American & Foreign Power Co., which in 1929 had a quoted market value of over a billion dollars, although they appeared only in a footnote to the company’s balance sheet. By 1932 this billion dollars had shrunk to $8 million, and in 1952 the warrants were wiped out in the company’s recapitalization—even though it had remained solvent.

Faust《浮士德》（歌德的诗剧）ominous precedent不祥的先例quoted market value按报价计算的市值wiped out被一笔勾销，归零recapitalization资本重组solvent有偿付能力的

要在历史和文学中找类比，可看歌德《浮士德》第二部描写纸币发明的段落。华尔街史上的不祥先例是American & Foreign Power Co.权证：1929年报价总市值超过10亿美元，却只在公司资产负债表脚注中出现；到1932年这10亿美元缩水至800万美元，1952年公司资本重组时权证被完全注销，尽管公司仍有偿付能力。

Originally, stock-option warrants were attached now and then to bond issues, and were usually equivalent to a partial conversion privilege. They were unimportant in amount, and hence did no harm. Their use expanded in the late 1920s, along with many other financial abuses, but they dropped from sight for long years thereafter. They were bound to turn up again, like the bad pennies they are, and since 1967 they have become familiar “instruments of finance.” In fact a standard procedure has developed for raising the capital for new real-estate ventures, affiliates of large banks, by selling units of an equal number of common shares and warrants to buy additional common shares at the same price. Example: In 1971 CleveTrust Realty Investors sold 2,500,000 of these combinations of common stock (or “shares of beneficial interest”) and warrants, for $20 per unit.

认股权证最初只是偶尔附在债券上，通常相当于部分转换权，金额不大，危害也小。20世纪20年代末，权证与其他金融滥用一起扩张，随后多年销声匿迹。像甩不掉的坏硬币一样，它们注定卷土重来；自1967年起已成为常见“金融工具”。为大型银行关联的新房地产项目筹资，甚至形成了标准做法：把等量普通股和可按同价买入额外普通股的权证捆成单位出售。例如1971年，CleveTrust Realty Investors以每单位20美元出售250万个这种“普通股（或受益权份额）加权证”的组合。

Let us consider for a moment what is really involved in this financial setup. Ordinarily, a common-stock issue has the first right to buy additional common shares when the company’s directors find it desirable to raise capital in this manner. This so-called “preemptive right” is one of the elements of value entering into the ownership of common stock—along with the right to receive dividends, to participate in the company’s growth, and to vote for directors. When separate warrants are issued for the right to subscribe additional capital, that action takes away part of the value inherent in an ordinary common share and transfers it to a separate certificate. An analogous thing could be done by issuing separate certificates for the right to receive dividends (for a limited or unlimited period), or the right to share in the proceeds of sale or liquidation of the enterprise, or the right to vote the shares. Why then are these subscription warrants created as part of the original capital structure? Simply because people are inexpert in financial matters. They don’t realize that the common stock is worth less with warrants outstanding than otherwise. Hence the package of stock and warrants usually commands a better price in the market than would the stock alone. Note that in the usual company reports the per-share earnings are (or have been) computed without proper allowance for the effect of outstanding warrants. The result is, of course, to overstate the true relationship between the earnings and the market value of the company’s capitalization.*

They don’t realize that the common stock is worth less with warrants outstanding than otherwise. Hence the package of stock and warrants usually commands a better price in the market than would the stock alone.

不妨想想这种安排真正意味着什么。通常，公司董事决定以增发普通股筹资时，现有普通股股东有优先认购权。这项权利同获得股息、分享公司成长、投票选举董事一样，是普通股价值的组成部分。若把增资认购权单独做成权证发行，就是从普通股固有价值中拿走一部分，转移到另一张凭证上。照此逻辑，也可把领取股息、分享出售或清算所得、股票投票权分别做成凭证。为什么最初资本结构中还要创造权证？只是因为人们不熟悉金融，不明白有权证流通时普通股本身会更不值钱。因此，股票加权证的组合通常比单卖股票取得更高市场价格。还要注意，公司报告计算每股盈利时，往往没有恰当计入流通权证影响，结果自然会夸大盈利相对于公司资本总市值的真实水平。

The simplest and probably the best method of allowing for the existence of warrants is to add the equivalent of their market value to the common-share capitalization, thus increasing the “true” market price per share. Where large amounts of warrants have been issued in connection with the sale of senior securities, it is customary to make the adjustment by assuming that the proceeds of the stock payment are used to retire the related bonds or preferred shares. This method does not allow adequately for the usual “premium value” of a warrant above exercisable value. In Table 16-4 we compare the effect of the two methods of calculation in the case of National General Corp. for the year 1970.

计入权证最简单、可能也是最好的方法，是把权证市值等价加到普通股总市值上，从而提高每股“真实”市场价格。若大量权证随优先证券出售，通常的调整是假定行权所得用于偿还相关债券或优先股。但这种方法没有充分计入权证高于可行权内在价值的常见“溢价价值”。表16-4以National General Corp. 1970年数据比较两种算法的效果。

Does the company itself derive an advantage from the creation of these warrants, in the sense that they assure it in some way of receiving additional capital when it needs some? Not at all. Ordinarily there is no way in which the company can require the warrant-holders to exercise their rights, and thus provide new capital to the company, prior to the expiration date of the warrants. In the meantime, if the company wants to raise additional common-stock funds it must offer the shares to its shareholders in the usual way—which means somewhat under the ruling market price. The warrants are no help in such an operation; they merely complicate the situation by frequently requiring a downward revision in their own subscription price. Once more we assert that large issues of stock-option warrants serve no purpose, except to fabricate imaginary market values.

derive an advantage from从……获得好处in the sense that在……的意义上exercise their rights行使权利expiration date到期日somewhat under略低于downward revision向下修正subscription price认购价格fabricate捏造，凭空制造

公司创造这些权证，是否能确保需要时获得额外资本？完全不能。通常，公司无法在权证到期前强迫持有人行权、为公司提供新资金。期间若公司要增发普通股筹资，仍须按通常方式向股东报价，也就是略低于市场价。权证对此毫无帮助，反而常因需要下调自身认购价而让局面更复杂。再次强调，大规模认股权证除了制造虚构市值，没有其他用途。

The paper money that Goethe was familiar with, when he wrote his Faust, were the notorious French assignats that had been greeted as a marvelous invention, and were destined ultimately to lose all of their value—as did the billion dollars worth of American & Foreign Power warrants.* Some of the poet’s remarks apply equally well to one invention or another—such as the following (in Bayard Taylor’s translation):

Practical Postscript

实务补记

The crime of the warrants is in “having been born.”* Once born they function as other security forms, and offer chances of profit as well as of loss. Nearly all the newer warrants run for a limited time—generally between five and ten years. The older warrants were often perpetual, and they were likely to have fascinating price histories over the years.

having been born已经出生（化用卡尔德隆名句“人最大的罪就是出生”）function as发挥……的作用run for a limited time有效期有限perpetual永久的

认股权证的罪，就在于“出生了”。一旦问世，它就像其他证券形式一样运作，既可能获利也可能亏损。几乎所有较新的权证都有期限，通常为五至十年；较老的权证往往永久有效，多年价格史可能极为引人入胜。

EXAMPLE: The record books will show that Tri-Continental Corp. warrants, which date from 1929, sold at a negligible 1/32 of a dollar each in the depth of the depression. From that lowly estate their price rose to a magnificent 75 3/4 in 1969, an astronomical advance of some 242,000%. (The warrants then sold considerably higher than the shares themselves; this is the kind of thing that occurs on Wall Street through technical developments, such as stock splits.) A recent example is supplied by Ling-Temco-Vought warrants, which in the first half of 1971 advanced from 2½ to 12½—and then fell back to 4.

date from始于negligible微不足道的in the depth of the depression在大萧条最严重的时候lowly estate卑微的境地technical developments技术性的变动（如拆股）fell back to回落到

例：记录显示，始于1929年的Tri-Continental Corp.权证在大萧条最深处每份只值微不足道的1/32美元；1969年却从如此低位升到辉煌的75又3/4美元，涨幅约242,000%。（当时权证价格甚至明显高于股票本身；拆股等技术变化会在华尔街造成这种现象。）较近案例是Ling-Temco-Vought权证，1971年上半年从2又1/2美元涨到12又1/2美元，随后又跌回4美元。

No doubt shrewd operations can be carried on in warrants from time to time, but this is too technical a matter for discussion here. We might say that warrants tend to sell relatively higher than the corresponding market components related to the conversion privilege of bonds or preferred stocks. To that extent there is a valid argument for selling bonds with warrants attached rather than creating an equivalent dilution factor by a convertible issue. If the warrant total is relatively small there is no point in taking its theoretical aspect too seriously; if the warrant issue is large relative to the outstanding stock, that would probably indicate that the company has a top-heavy senior capitalization. It should be selling additional common stock instead. Thus the main objective of our attack on warrants as a financial mechanism is not to condemn their use in connection with moderate-size bond issues, but to argue against the wanton creation of huge “paper-money” monstrosities of this genre.

shrewd operations精明的操作too technical a matter太过专业的问题（注意 too + 形容词 + a + 名词 的语序）market components市场价值的组成部分a valid argument for支持……的正当理由there is no point in没有必要top-heavy头重脚轻的senior capitalization优先证券资本（债券和优先股的总额）wanton肆意的，毫无节制的monstrosities怪物，畸形的产物genre类型（法语）

精明者无疑可偶尔在权证中开展有利操作，但技术性太强，不适合在此详谈。权证相对于债券或优先股所含转换权对应的市场价值，往往卖得更贵。因此，与其发行造成同等稀释的可转换证券，把权证附在债券上出售有一定道理。权证总量较小时，不必过分追究理论问题；若相对于流通普通股数量很大，则很可能说明公司优先资本结构头重脚轻，本应增发普通股。我们抨击权证这种融资机制，主要不是反对它附在适量债券发行中，而是反对肆意创造这种巨大的“纸币”怪物。

* Graham detested warrants, as he makes clear on pp. 413–416.

detested憎恶

格雷厄姆厌恶认股权证，第413—416页已经说得很清楚。

* Graham is pointing out that, despite the promotional rhetoric that investors usually hear, convertible bonds do not automatically offer “the best of both worlds.” Higher yield and lower risk do not always go hand in hand. What Wall Street gives with one hand, it usually takes away with the other. An investment may offer the best of one world, or the worst of another; but the best of both worlds seldom becomes available in a single package.

promotional rhetoric推销话术the best of both worlds两全其美go hand in hand相伴而行，同时出现in a single package在同一个组合里

格雷厄姆指出，尽管投资者常听到宣传，可转换债券并不会自动提供“两全其美”。高收益与低风险并不总能兼得；华尔街一只手给你的，通常会用另一只手拿走。投资可能给你一个世界中最好的一面，也可能给你另一个世界中最坏的一面，但两边最好的东西很少装在同一个组合里。

† According to Goldman Sachs and Ibbotson Associates, from 1998 through 2002, convertibles generated an average annual return of 4.8%. That was considerably better than the 0.6% annual loss on U.S. stocks, but substantially worse than the returns of medium-term corporate bonds (a 7.5% annual gain) and long-term corporate bonds (an 8.3% annual gain). In the mid-1990s, according to Merrill Lynch, roughly $15 billion in convertibles were issued annually; by 1999, issuance had more than doubled to $39 billion. In 2000, $58 billion in convertibles were issued, and in 2001, another $105 billion emerged. As Graham warns, convertible securities always come out of the woodwork near the end of a bull market—largely because even poor-quality companies then have stock returns high enough to make the conversion feature seem attractive.

据高盛与Ibbotson Associates统计，1998—2002年可转换证券年均回报4.8%，明显好于美国股票每年亏损0.6%，但显著低于中期公司债7.5%和长期公司债8.3%的年收益。美林称，20世纪90年代中期每年约发行150亿美元可转换证券；1999年翻倍至390亿美元，2000年580亿美元，2001年又达1,050亿美元。正如格雷厄姆警告，可转换证券总在牛市尾声纷纷出现，主要因为那时连低质公司的股票回报也足以让转换权看起来诱人。

* Recent structural changes in the convertible market have negated some of these criticisms. Convertible preferred stock, which made up roughly half the total convertible market in Graham’s day, now accounts for only an eighth of the market. Maturities are shorter, making convertible bonds less volatile, and many now carry “call protection,” or assurances against early redemption. And more than half of all convertibles are now investment grade, a significant improvement in credit quality from Graham’s time. Thus, in 2002, the Merrill Lynch All U.S. Convertible Index lost 8.6%—versus the 22.1% loss of the S & P 500-stock index and the 31.3% decline in the NASDAQ Composite stock index.

可转换证券市场近年的结构变化已削弱部分批评。格雷厄姆时代约占市场一半的可转换优先股，如今只占八分之一；期限缩短，降低可转换债券波动；许多证券还带有防止过早赎回的“赎回保护”。目前超过一半可转换证券达到投资级，信用质量较当年显著提高。因此2002年美林全美可转换证券指数下跌8.6%，而标准普尔500指数下跌22.1%，纳斯达克综合指数下跌31.3%。

* A bond is “called” when the issuing corporation forcibly pays it off ahead of the stated maturity date, or final due date for interest payments. For a brief summary of how convertible bonds work, see Note 1 in the commentary on this chapter (p. 418).

* Warrants were an extremely widespread technique of corporate finance in the nineteenth century and were fairly common even in Graham’s day. They have since diminished in importance and popularity—one of the few recent developments that would give Graham unreserved pleasure. As of year-end 2002, there were only seven remaining warrant issues on the New York Stock Exchange—only the ghostly vestige of a market. Because warrants are no longer commonly used by major companies, today’s investors should read the rest of Graham’s chapter only to see how his logic works.

认股权证在19世纪是极普遍的公司融资技术，在格雷厄姆时代也相当常见。此后它的重要性与流行度下降——这是少数会让格雷厄姆毫无保留高兴的现代发展之一。截至2002年末，纽约证券交易所仅剩七批权证，市场只余幽灵般痕迹。由于大公司已很少使用权证，今天的投资者阅读本章余下内容，主要应观察格雷厄姆如何推理。

* Today, the last remnant of activity in warrants is in the cesspool of the NASDAQ “bulletin board,” or over-the-counter market for tiny companies, where common stock is often bundled with warrants into a “unit” (the contemporary equivalent of what Graham calls a “package”). If a stockbroker ever offers to sell you “units” in any company, you can be 95% certain that warrants are involved, and at least 90% certain that the broker is either a thief or an idiot. Legitimate brokers and firms have no business in this area.

* The “notorious French assignats” were issued during the Revolution of 1789. They were originally debts of the Revolutionary government, purportedly secured by the value of the real estate that the radicals had seized from the Catholic church and the nobility. But the Revolutionaries were bad financial managers. In 1790, the interest rate on assignats was cut; soon they stopped paying interest entirely and were reclassified as paper money. But the government refused to redeem them for gold or silver and issued massive amounts of new assignats. They were officially declared worthless in 1797.

purportedly据称secured by以……作担保the radicals激进派the nobility贵族redeem兑换，赎回

“声名狼藉的法国指券”发行于1789年大革命时期。它最初是革命政府债务，声称由激进派从天主教会和贵族手中没收的房地产价值担保。但革命者不善理财：1790年指券利率被削减，随后完全停止付息并改作纸币；政府拒绝用金银兑付，又大量增发。1797年，指券被正式宣布作废。

Four Extremely Instructive Case Histories

Chapter 17Four Extremely Instructive Case Histories第17章 四个极具启发性的案例

本章导读本章标题里的 extremely 是个双关：这四个案例既“极其”有教益，又各自代表了华尔街近年来走到极端的某种现象。格雷厄姆用它们说明：分析师、基金经理、信托主管和放贷的银行家，都没有做好最基本的功课。第一个案例是宾州中央铁路——美国最大的铁路公司，1970 年破产。只要套用最简单的证券分析规则就能提前看穿它：利息保障倍数不到 2 倍（远低于铁路债券税前 5 倍的保守标准）、连续 11 年几乎不缴所得税、每股 6.80 美元的“利润”与每股 12 美元的“特别费用”分开披露。1968 年股价创新高时，称职的分析师就该把它的债券和股票清出账户。第二个是林-特姆科-沃特：靠借债疯狂并购，销售额十年间膨胀四百倍，负债高达 18.65 亿美元，随后巨亏，股价从 169½ 跌到 7⅛；格雷厄姆追问的是，商业银行为什么肯借出如此巨款。第三个是 NVF 收购沙伦钢铁：小公司用次级债券加认股权证吞下比自己大七倍的公司，有形权益从每股 23.71 美元缩水到约 3 美元，再用“递延债务费用”等会计花招把账做平并顺带避税。第四个是 AAA 企业：卖活动房屋的小生意靠“特许经营”概念包装上市，大券商承销，发行即翻倍，市盈率高达 115 倍；七个月后资本几乎亏光，两年内破产。结尾指出：投机大众无可救药，但承销商是否该为这类发行承担道义责任、SEC 是否应获得更多权力，是格雷厄姆留给华尔街和监管者的问题。

The word “extremely” in the title is a kind of pun, because the histories represent extremes of various sorts that were manifest on Wall Street in recent years. They hold instruction, and grave warnings, for everyone who has a serious connection with the world of stocks and bonds—not only for ordinary investors and speculators but for professionals, security analysts, fund managers, trust-account administrators, and even for bankers who lend money to corporations. The four companies to be reviewed, and the different extremes that they illustrate are:

pun双关语manifest显现的，明显可见的（此处是形容词）hold instruction含有教益grave warnings严重的警告trust-account administrators信托账户管理人

标题中的“极端”带有双关，因为这些公司历史代表了近年华尔街显现出的多种极端。凡与股票和债券市场有严肃关系的人都能从中得到教训与重大警告，不仅包括普通投资者和投机者，也包括专业人士、证券分析师、基金经理、信托账户管理人，甚至向公司放贷的银行家。下面审视四家公司及其所体现的不同极端：

Penn Central (Railroad) Co. An extreme example of the neglect of the most elementary warning signals of financial weakness, by all those who had bonds or shares of this system under their supervision. A crazily high market price for the stock of a tottering giant.

Penn Central宾州中央铁路公司（1968 年由宾夕法尼亚铁路与纽约中央铁路合并而成，1970 年破产）elementary最基本的under their supervision由他们监管tottering giant摇摇欲坠的巨人

Penn Central（铁路）公司：所有负责监督该体系债券或股票的人，都忽略了财务薄弱最基本的警告信号，是一个极端案例；这个摇摇欲坠的巨人，股票市价却高得疯狂。

Ling-Temco-Vought Inc. An extreme example of quick and unsound “empire building,” with ultimate collapse practically guaranteed; but helped by indiscriminate bank lending.

unsound不稳健的empire building帝国式扩张（靠不断并购把公司做大）indiscriminate不加区别的，滥的

Ling-Temco-Vought Inc.：快速而不稳健地“建立帝国”的极端案例，最终崩塌几乎注定；银行不加甄别的贷款又助长了扩张。

NVF Corp. An extreme example of one corporate acquisition, in which a small company absorbed another seven times its size, incurring a huge debt and employing some startling accounting devices.

incurring招致，背上（债务）startling令人吃惊的accounting devices会计手法

NVF Corp.：公司收购的极端案例，一家小公司吞下一家规模为自身七倍的公司，为此背负巨债，并采用一些惊人的会计手法。

AAA Enterprises. An extreme example of public stock-financing of a small company; its value based on the magic word “franchising,” and little else, sponsored by important stock-exchange houses. Bankruptcy followed within two years of the stock sale and the doubling of the initial inflated price in the heedless stock market.

franchising特许经营sponsored承销、背书（此处指券商为发行担保）stock-exchange houses交易所会员券商（house = 券商，本书常用）heedless漫不经心的，不加思考的

AAA Enterprises：小公司公开发行股票融资的极端案例。它的价值几乎只建立在“特许经营”这个魔法词上，却得到重要证券交易所会员公司的承销。股票出售后两年内，公司即告破产；在此之前，轻率的市场还曾让最初已虚高的价格翻倍。

The Penn Central Case

宾州中央铁路案例

This is the country’s largest railroad in assets and gross revenues. Its bankruptcy in 1970 shocked the financial world. It has defaulted on most of its bond issues, and has been in danger of abandoning its operations entirely. Its security issues fell drastically in price, the common stock collapsing from a high level of 86½ as recently as 1968 to a low of 5½ in 1970. (There seems little doubt that these shares will be wiped out in reorganization.)*

gross revenues总收入defaulted on对……违约bond issues债券（issue = 发行的证券）wiped out归零，血本无归reorganization重组（破产重整）

按资产和营业总收入计算，Penn Central是美国最大的铁路公司。1970年破产震惊金融界；它对多数债券违约，甚至面临完全停止运营的危险。旗下证券价格暴跌，普通股从1968年还高达86又1/2美元，跌至1970年的5又1/2美元。（这些股票在重组中几乎肯定会被全部注销。）

Our basic point is that the application of the simplest rules of security analysis and the simplest standards of sound investment would have revealed the fundamental weakness of the Penn Central system long before its bankruptcy—certainly in 1968, when the shares were selling at their post-1929 record, and when most of its bond issues could have been exchanged at even prices for well-secured public-utility obligations with the same coupon rates. The following comments are in order:

post-1929 record1929 年以来的最高价at even prices以相同的价格（不折价）well-secured有充分担保的public-utility obligations公用事业公司债券coupon rates票面利率are in order是恰当的，值得一提

我们的基本观点是，只要应用最简单的证券分析规则和稳健投资标准，早在破产前很久就能看出Penn Central体系的根本弱点——至少在1968年就应看出。当时股价创1929年以来新高，而其大多数债券都能按相同价格换成票息相同、保障良好的公用事业债券。以下几点值得评论：

1. In the S & P Bond Guide the interest charges of the system are shown to have been earned 1.91 times in 1967 and 1.98 times in 1968. The minimum coverage prescribed for railroad bonds in our textbook Security Analysis is 5 times before income taxes and 2.9 times after income taxes at regular rates. As far as we know the validity of these standards has never been questioned by any investment authority. On the basis of our requirements for earnings after taxes, the Penn Central fell short of the requirements for safety. But our after-tax requirement is based on a before-tax ratio of five times, with regular income tax deducted after the bond interest. In the case of Penn Central, it had been paying no income taxes to speak of for the past 11 years! Hence the coverage of its interest charges before taxes was less than two times—a totally inadequate figure against our conservative requirement of 5 times.

S & P Bond Guide标准普尔《债券指南》interest charges利息支出earned 1.91 times利润是利息的 1.91 倍（即利息保障倍数）coverage保障倍数（利润覆盖利息的倍数）investment authority投资界权威fell short of达不到to speak of值得一提的（no … to speak of：几乎没有）conservative保守的，稳健的

But our after-tax requirement is based on a before-tax ratio of five times, with regular income tax deducted after the bond interest. In the case of Penn Central, it had been paying no income taxes to speak of for the past 11 years!

但我们的税后标准，是以税前 5 倍的比率为基础的——先扣除债券利息，再按正常税率缴纳所得税。而宾州中央铁路过去 11 年几乎没缴过什么所得税！

with regular income tax deducted after the bond interest 是 with + 名词 + 过去分词的独立结构，说明“税后 2.9 倍”这一标准的前提：公司确实在付完利息之后按正常税率缴了税。既然宾州中央根本不缴税，它的利润就应直接与税前 5 倍的标准比较，而不到 2 倍显然远远不够。no … to speak of 意为“几乎没有”。

1. 《标准普尔债券指南》显示，该体系1967年和1968年的利息保障倍数分别为1.91和1.98。我们的《证券分析》规定，铁路债券最低保障倍数应为所得税前5倍，按正常税率扣税后2.9倍。据我们所知，从未有投资权威质疑这些标准。按税后盈利要求，Penn Central不符合安全标准。但这一税后要求本来假设税前保障5倍，并在支付债息后按正常税率扣税；Penn Central过去11年几乎没交所得税。因此它的税前利息保障倍数也不到2倍，对照我们保守的5倍标准，完全不足。

译者补充（非原文）：利息保障倍数＝息税前盈利÷利息费用。若只有1.98倍，盈利下降约一半就可能不足以付息；5倍标准则留下明显缓冲。Penn Central长期几乎不交税，使“税后1.98倍”看似尚可，实质税前也不到2倍。

2. The fact that the company paid no income taxes over so long a period should have raised serious questions about the validity of its reported earnings.

over so long a period在这么长的时期里（so + 形容词 + a + 名词的语序）reported earnings报告利润，账面利润

2. 公司长期不交所得税这一事实，本应让人严重质疑其报告盈利是否真实可靠。

3. The bonds of the Penn Central system could have been exchanged in 1968 and 1969, at no sacrifice of price or income, for far better secured issues. For example, in 1969, Pennsylvania RR 4½s, due 1994 (part of Penn Central) had a range of 61 to 74½, while Pennsylvania Electric Co. 4 3/8s, due 1994, had a range of 64¼ to 72¼. The public utility had earned its interest 4.20 times before taxes in 1968 against only 1.98 times for the Penn Central system; during 1969 the latter’s comparative showing grew steadily worse. An exchange of this sort was clearly called for, and it would have been a lifesaver for a Penn Central bondholder. (At the end of 1970 the railroad 4¼s were in default, and selling at only 18½, while the utility’s 4 3/8s closed at 66½.)

at no sacrifice of不牺牲……Pennsylvania RR 4½s宾夕法尼亚铁路公司票面利率 4.5% 的债券（RR = railroad；数字加 s 表示该利率的债券）due 19941994 年到期comparative showing相对表现called for理应采取，需要lifesaver救命稻草in default处于违约状态closed at收盘价为

3. 1968、1969年，Penn Central体系的债券本可在不牺牲价格或收入的情况下，换成安全得多的证券。例如1969年，Pennsylvania Railroad 1994年到期的4.5%债券（Penn Central的一部分）交易区间61—74又1/2；Pennsylvania Electric Co.同为1994年到期的4又3/8%债券区间64又1/4—72又1/4。后者1968年税前利息保障倍数4.20，Penn Central只有1.98，且1969年继续恶化。显然应当调换，这会挽救Penn Central债券持有人。（1970年末，铁路4又1/4%债券已违约，仅卖18又1/2；公用事业4又3/8%债券收于66又1/2。）

4. Penn Central reported earnings of $3.80 per share in 1968; its high price of 86½ in that year was 24 times such earnings. But any analyst worth his salt would have wondered how “real” were earnings of this sort reported without the necessity of paying any income taxes thereon.

worth his salt称职的thereon在其上（指对这些利润缴税）the necessity of……的必要

4. Penn Central报告1968年每股盈利3.80美元，当年最高价86又1/2美元，相当于24倍盈利。但凡合格分析师都会追问：无需为这种盈利缴纳任何所得税，它究竟有多“真实”？

5. For 1966 the newly merged company* had reported “earnings” of $6.80 a share—in reflection of which the common stock later rose to its peak of 86½. This was a valuation of over $2 billion for the equity. How many of these buyers knew at the time that the so lovely earnings were before a special charge of $275 million or $12 per share to be taken in 1971 for “costs and losses” incurred on the merger. O wondrous fairyland of Wall Street where a company can announce “profits” of $6.80 per share in one place and special “costs and losses” of $12 in another, and shareholders and speculators rub their hands with glee!†

in reflection of which反映这一点（指利润数字）the equity股东权益，全部股票（equity = 股权）special charge特别费用（一次性冲销）incurred on the merger因合并而发生的O wondrous fairyland啊，奇妙的仙境（反讽）rub their hands with glee高兴得直搓手

How many of these buyers knew at the time that the so lovely earnings were before a special charge of $275 million or $12 per share to be taken in 1971 for “costs and losses” incurred on the merger.

这些买家当中，有多少人当时知道：这么漂亮的利润数字，是尚未扣除一笔 2.75 亿美元（合每股 12 美元）特别费用的——这笔因合并而发生的“成本和损失”要到 1971 年才计提。

这是一个以句号结尾的反问句，意思是“几乎没人知道”。难点在 were before a special charge：before 表示“未扣除……之前的”，即所谓利润没有减去这笔费用；to be taken in 1971 是不定式作后置定语修饰 charge，指该费用将在 1971 年入账。

5. 1966年，新合并的公司报告每股“盈利”6.80美元，普通股随后升到86又1/2美元高点，对应股权估值超过20亿美元。当时有多少买家知道，如此漂亮的盈利并未扣除一项将在1971年确认的2.75亿美元特别费用，即每股12美元，用于合并产生的“成本与损失”？奇妙的华尔街仙境啊：公司可以在一处宣布每股“盈利”6.80美元，又在另一处列出每股12美元的特别“成本与损失”，股东和投机者竟还高兴得摩拳擦掌！

6. A railroad analyst would have long since known that the operating picture of the Penn Central was very bad in comparison with the more profitable roads. For example, its transportation ratio was 47.5% in 1968 against 35.2% for its neighbor, Norfolk & Western.*

long since早就operating picture经营状况roads铁路公司（railroads 的简称）transportation ratio运输比率（运输费用占营业收入的比例，越低越好）

7. Along the way there were some strange transactions with peculiar accounting results.1 Details are too complicated to go into here.

peculiar奇特的go into深入讨论

CONCLUSION: Whether better management could have saved the Penn Central bankruptcy may be arguable. But there is no doubt whatever that no bonds and no shares of the Penn Central system should have remained after 1968 at the latest in any securities account watched over by competent security analysts, fund managers, trust officers, or investment counsel. Moral: Security analysts should do their elementary jobs before they study stock-market movements, gaze into crystal balls, make elaborate mathematical calculations, or go on all-expense-paid field trips.†

arguable有争议的，可以商榷的no doubt whatever毫无疑问（whatever 加强否定）at the latest最迟investment counsel投资顾问gaze into crystal balls盯着水晶球看（指预测未来）all-expense-paid field trips费用全包的实地考察

But there is no doubt whatever that no bonds and no shares of the Penn Central system should have remained after 1968 at the latest in any securities account watched over by competent security analysts, fund managers, trust officers, or investment counsel.

但毫无疑问的是：最迟到 1968 年以后，任何由称职的证券分析师、基金经理、信托主管或投资顾问看管的证券账户里，都不应该再留有宾州中央铁路系统的任何债券和股票。

no doubt whatever 中的 whatever 加强否定，意为“毫无”；that 引导的同位语从句里又以 no bonds and no shares 作主语，形成多重否定。should have remained 是“本不该继续留着”，watched over by … 是过去分词短语修饰 account。

结论：更好的管理能否使Penn Central免于破产，尚可争论。但毫无疑问，最迟在1968年以后，任何由称职证券分析师、基金经理、信托主管或投资顾问监督的证券账户，都不应再持有Penn Central体系的任何债券或股票。教训是：证券分析师在研究股价走势、凝视水晶球、进行复杂数学计算或参加费用全包的实地考察前，应先把最基本的工作做好。

Ling-Temco-Vought Inc.

林-特姆科-沃特公司

This is a story of head-over-heels expansion and head-over-heels debt, ending up in terrific losses and a host of financial problems. As usually happens in such cases, a fair-haired boy, or “young genius,” was chiefly responsible for both the creation of the great empire and its ignominious downfall; but there is plenty of blame to be accorded others as well. †

head-over-heels栽跟头式的，不顾一切的terrific巨大的（此处不是“极好的”）fair-haired boy宠儿，红人ignominious downfall可耻的垮台

这是一个急速扩张、债务也急速膨胀的故事，最后留下巨额亏损和一大堆财务难题。此类案例常见的模式是：一位受宠的“年轻天才”既创造庞大帝国，也主要促成其不光彩的覆灭；不过其他人同样难辞其咎。

The rise and fall of Ling-Temco-Vought can be summarized by setting forth condensed income accounts and balance-sheet items for five years between 1958 and 1970. This is done in Table 17-1. The first column shows the company’s modest beginnings in 1958, when its sales were only $7 million. The next gives figures for 1960; the enterprise had grown twentyfold in only two years, but it was still comparatively small. Then came the heyday years to 1967 and 1968, in which sales again grew twentyfold to $2.8 billion with the debt figure expanding from $44 million to an awesome $1,653 million. In 1969 came new acquisitions, a further huge increase in debt (to a total of $1,865 million!), and the beginning of serious trouble. A large loss, after extraordinary items, was reported for the year; the stock price declined from its 1967 high of 169½ to a low of 24; the young genius was superseded as the head of the company. The 1970 results were even more dreadful. The enterprise reported a final net loss of close to $70 million; the stock fell away to a low price of 7 1/8, and its largest bond issue was quoted at one time at a pitiable 15 cents on the dollar. The company’s expansion policy was sharply reversed, various of its important interests were placed on the market, and some headway was made in reducing its mountainous obligations.

setting forth列出condensed income accounts简明损益表heyday全盛期awesome令人生畏的（此处不是“很棒的”）extraordinary items非经常性项目superseded被取代quoted报价15 cents on the dollar每 1 美元面值只值 15 美分interests权益，所持的业务（此处不是“兴趣”或“利息”）headway进展mountainous obligations堆积如山的债务

把1958—1970年间五个年份的简化利润表与资产负债表项目列出，就能概括Ling-Temco-Vought的兴衰，见表17-1。1958年公司起步尚小，销售额仅700万美元；1960年两年内扩大20倍，但仍相对不大。随后进入1967、1968年的鼎盛期，销售额再增20倍至28亿美元，债务则从4,400万美元膨胀到惊人的16.53亿美元。1969年又有新收购，债务进一步暴增到18.65亿美元，严重麻烦开始出现。公司报告扣除非常项目后巨亏；股价从1967年169又1/2美元高点跌至24美元；年轻天才也被撤换。1970年更糟：最终净亏损近7,000万美元，股价最低7又1/8美元，最大一笔债券一度只按面值15%报价。公司大幅逆转扩张政策，挂牌出售若干重要资产，并在削减如山债务方面取得一些进展。

The figures in our table speak so eloquently that few comments are called for. But here are some:

1. The company’s expansion period was not without an interruption. In 1961 it showed a small operating deficit, but—adopting a practice that was to be seen later in so many reports for 1970—evidently decided to throw all possible charges and reserves into the one bad year.* These amounted to a round $13 million, which was more than the combined net profits of the preceding three years. It was now ready to show “record earnings” in 1962, etc.

1961 年，公司出现了小额经营亏损，但它显然决定——采用了后来在 1970 年众多财报中都能见到的做法——把所有能计提的费用和准备金统统塞进这一个坏年头里。

2. At the end of 1966 the net tangible assets are given as $7.66 per share of common (adjusted for a 3-for-2 split). Thus the market price in 1967 reached 22 times (!) its reported asset value at the time. At the end of 1968 the balance sheet showed $286 million available for 3,800,000 shares of common and Class AA stock, or about $77 per share. But if we deduct the preferred stock at full value and exclude the good-will items and the huge bond-discount “asset,”† there would remain $13 million for the common—a mere $3 per share. This tangible equity was wiped out by the losses of the following years.

2. 1966年末，按三股拆为两股调整后，每股普通股对应有形净资产为7.66美元；1967年市价竟达到当时报表资产价值的22倍。1968年末资产负债表显示，2.86亿美元归属于380万股普通股与AA类股票，约每股77美元。但若按全额扣除优先股，并排除商誉及巨额债券折价“资产”，普通股只剩1,300万美元，即每股区区3美元。这点有形权益随后被数年亏损全部抹去。

3. Toward the end of 1967 two of our best-regarded banking firms offered 600,000 shares of Ling-Temco-Vought stock at $111 per share. It had been as high as 169½. In less than three years the price fell to 7 1/8.†

best-regarded最受敬重的banking firms投资银行（此处指承销商）offered公开发售

3. 1967年末，两家最受尊重的银行机构按每股111美元发行60万股Ling-Temco-Vought股票；此前最高曾达169又1/2美元。不到三年，股价跌到7又1/8美元。

4. At the end of 1967 the bank loans had reached $161 million, and a year later they stood at $414 million—which should have been a frightening figure. In addition, the long-term debt amounted to $1,237 million. By 1969 combined debt reached a total of $1,869 million. This may have been the largest combined debt figure of any industrial company anywhere and at any time, with the single exception of the impregnable Standard Oil of N.J.

stood at达到（某个数值）combined debt债务总额with the single exception of唯一的例外是impregnable坚不可摧的Standard Oil of N.J.新泽西标准石油公司（埃克森的前身）

4. 1967年末银行贷款已达1.61亿美元，一年后升到4.14亿美元，本应令人恐惧。此外长期债务为12.37亿美元；到1969年合计债务18.69亿美元。除坚不可摧的Standard Oil of New Jersey外，这可能是任何时代、任何地方工业公司最大的总负债。

5. The losses in 1969 and 1970 far exceeded the total profits since the formation of the company.

formation成立

5. 1969与1970年的亏损，远远超过公司成立以来的利润总和。

MORAL: The primary question raised in our mind by the Ling-Temco-Vought story is how the commercial bankers could have been persuaded to lend the company such huge amounts of money during its expansion period. In 1966 and earlier the company’s coverage of interest charges did not meet conservative standards, and the same was true of the ratio of current assets to current liabilities and of stock equity to total debt. But in the next two years the banks advanced the enterprise nearly $400 million additional for further “diversification.” This was not good business for them, and it was worse in its implications for the company’s shareholders. If the Ling-Temco-Vought case will serve to keep commercial banks from aiding and abetting unsound expansions of this type in the future, some good may come of it at last.*

MORAL教训current assets流动资产current liabilities流动负债advanced贷给，预付（此处是动词“提供贷款”，不是“上涨”）diversification多元化implications潜在影响aiding and abetting协助和教唆（法律用语，指做帮凶）some good may come of it或许能带来一些好处

教训：Ling-Temco-Vought故事最令我们不解的是，商业银行在其扩张期为何会同意借出如此巨款。1966年及以前，公司利息保障倍数已不符合保守标准，流动资产对流动负债、股东权益对总债务的比率也一样。但随后两年，银行竟又提供近4亿美元支持进一步“多元化”。这对银行不是好生意，对公司股东的影响更糟。若此案能让商业银行今后不再协助、纵容这种不稳健扩张，总算也会产生一点好处。

The NVF Takeover of Sharon Steel (A Collector’s Item)

NVF 收购沙伦钢铁（一件“收藏级”案例）

At the end of 1968 NVF Company was a company with $4.6 million of long-term debt, $17.4 million of stock capital, $31 million of sales, and $502,000 of net income (before a special credit of $374,000). Its business was described as “vulcanized fiber and plastics.” The management decided to take over the Sharon Steel Corp., which had $43 million of long-term debt, $101 million of stock capital, $219 million of sales, and $2,929,000 of net earnings. The company it wished to acquire was thus seven times the size of NVF. In early 1969 it made an offer for all the shares of Sharon. The terms per share were $70 face amount of NVF junior 5% bonds, due 1994, plus warrants to buy 1½ shares of NVF stock at $22 per share of NVF. The management of Sharon strenuously resisted this takeover attempt, but in vain. NVF acquired 88% of the Sharon stock under the offer, issuing therefore $102 million of its 5% bonds and warrants for 2,197,000 of its shares. Had the offer been 100% operative the consolidated enterprise would, for the year 1968, have had $163 million in debt, only $2.2 million in tangible stock capital, $250 million of sales. The net-earnings question would have been a bit complicated, but the company subsequently stated them as a net loss of 50 cents per share of NVF stocks, before an extraordinary credit, and net earnings of 3 cents per share after such credit.*

Had the offer been … 是省略 if 的虚拟语气倒装，等于 If the offer had been 100% operative；主句 would … have had 是对过去情况的虚拟。for the year 1968 插在 would 和 have had 之间，读时先跳过它抓主干。

1968年末，NVF Company长期债务460万美元，股本1,740万美元，销售额3,100万美元，净利润50.2万美元（未计37.4万美元特别收益），业务为“硫化纤维与塑料”。管理层决定收购Sharon Steel Corp.；后者长期债务4,300万美元，股本1.01亿美元，销售额2.19亿美元，净利润292.9万美元，规模为NVF七倍。1969年初，NVF向Sharon全部股份发出要约：每股Sharon可换取面值70美元、1994年到期的NVF次级5%债券，并附可按每股22美元购买1.5股NVF股票的权证。Sharon管理层强烈抵制，但失败。NVF最终取得88%股份，发行1.02亿美元5%债券及可认购219.7万股的权证。若要约100%生效，按1968年模拟合并，企业将有1.63亿美元债务、有形股本仅220万美元、销售额2.5亿美元。净利润较复杂，后来公司称：非常收益前每股NVF亏损0.50美元，计入后每股盈利0.03美元。

译者补充（非原文）：按100%收购的模拟数字，1.63亿美元债务只由220万美元有形股权缓冲，债务约为有形股权74倍；这就是“小公司吞大公司”造成的极端财务杠杆。

FIRST COMMENT: Among all the takeovers effected in the year 1969 this was no doubt the most extreme in its financial disproportions. The acquiring company had assumed responsibility for a new and top-heavy debt obligation, and it had changed its calculated 1968 earnings from a profit to a loss into the bargain. A measure of the impairment of the company’s financial position by this step is found in the fact that the new 5% bonds did not sell higher than 42 cents on the dollar during the year of issuance. This would have indicated grave doubt of the safety of the bonds and of the company’s future; however, the management actually exploited the bond price in a way to save the company annual income taxes of about $1,000,000 as will be shown.

effected完成，实施（动词，注意不是 affected）disproportions不成比例，失衡assumed responsibility for承担了……的责任top-heavy头重脚轻的（债务负担过重）into the bargain而且，此外impairment损害，减值year of issuance发行当年

第一点评论：1969年所有收购中，这无疑是财务比例最极端的一宗。收购方承担了新增且头重脚轻的债务，还顺带把模拟的1968年盈利变成亏损。新发行的5%债券当年最高只卖面值42%，足见此举严重削弱公司财务状况，也显示市场强烈怀疑债券安全性与公司前景。然而管理层后来竟利用低债券价格设计税务处理，每年为公司节省约100万美元所得税，后文将说明。

The 1968 report, published after the Sharon takeover, contained a condensed picture of its results, carried back to the year-end. This contained two most unusual items:

carried back to追溯至（把合并后的数字回算到）condensed picture简要概况

收购Sharon后发布的1968年报告，把交易结果模拟追溯至年末，其中有两个极不寻常的项目：

1. There is listed as an asset $58,600,000 of “deferred debt expense.” This sum is greater than the entire “stockholders’ equity,” placed at $40,200,000.

1. 资产项下列有5,860万美元“递延债务费用”，金额超过全部“股东权益”4,020万美元。

2. However, not included in the shareholders’ equity is an item of $20,700,000 designated as “excess of equity over cost of investment in Sharon.”

designated as被命名为excess of equity over cost权益超过投资成本的部分（即负商誉）

2. 但股东权益中又没有包含一项2,070万美元的“持有Sharon权益超过投资成本的部分”。

SECOND COMMENT: If we eliminate the debt expense as an asset, which it hardly seems to be, and include the other item in the shareholders’ equity (where it would normally belong), then we have a more realistic statement of tangible equity for NVF stock, viz., $2,200,000. Thus the first effect of the deal was to reduce NVF’s “real equity” from $17,400,000 to $2,200,000 or from $23.71 per share to about $3 per share, on 731,000 shares. In addition the NVF shareholders had given to others the right to buy 3½ times as many additional shares at six points below the market price at the close of 1968. The initial market value of the warrants was then about $12 each, or a total of some $30 million for those involved in the purchase offer. Actually, the market value of the warrants well exceeded the total market value of the outstanding NVF stock—another evidence of the tail-wagging-dog nature of the transaction.

hardly seems to be似乎根本不是viz.即（拉丁语 videlicet 的缩写）six points below低 6 个点（6 美元）at the close of 19681968 年年底some $30 million大约 3000 万美元（some = 大约）well exceeded大大超过outstanding流通在外的（股票）tail-wagging-dog尾巴摇狗的，本末倒置的

第二点评论：若剔除几乎不能算资产的债务费用，再把另一项目计入通常应归属的股东权益，NVF股票较真实的有形权益便只有220万美元。交易第一步就把NVF“真实权益”从1,740万美元降到220万美元；按73.1万股计算，每股从23.71美元降到约3美元。此外，NVF股东还把权利交给别人，让其能按比1968年末市价低6美元的价格，购买相当于现有股数3.5倍的新增股份。当时每份权证初始市值约12美元，本次收购要约所涉权证总值约3,000万美元，实际上远超NVF全部流通股票市值，再次显示这笔交易是“尾巴摇狗”。

译者补充（非原文）：权证让他人可买入约现有股数3.5倍的新股，意味着全部行使后原股东在总股数中的比例会被显著压缩；权证市值甚至高于现有股票总市值，也说明市场交易的重点已从企业本身转向附带权利。

The Accounting Gimmicks

会计花招

When we pass from this pro forma balance sheet to the next year’s report we find several strange-appearing entries. In addition to the basic interest expense (a hefty $7,500,000), there is deducted $1,795,000 for “amortization of deferred debt expense.” But this last is nearly offset on the next line by a very unusual income item indeed: “amortization of equity over cost of investment in subsidiary: Cr. $1,650,000.” In one of the footnotes we find an entry, not appearing in any other report that we know of: Part of the stock capital is there designated as “fair market value of warrants issued in connection with acquisition, etc., $22,129,000.”

pro forma备考的，假设合并已完成后重新编制的（拉丁语）hefty巨额的amortization摊销offset抵消Cr.贷方（credit 的缩写）fair market value公允市场价值

从模拟资产负债表转到下一年报告，又会看到几个怪异项目。除基本利息费用750万美元外，还扣除179.5万美元“递延债务费用摊销”；紧接下一行却有一项极不寻常的收入，几乎抵消前者：“持有子公司权益超过投资成本部分的摊销：贷记165万美元。”一则附注还列出我们从未在其他报告见过的项目，把部分股本称为“收购等事项所发行权证的公允市值，2,212.9万美元”。

What on earth do all these entries mean? None of them is even referred to in the descriptive text of the 1969 report. The trained security analyst has to figure out these mysteries by himself, almost in detective fashion. He finds that the underlying idea is to derive a tax advantage from the low initial price of the 5% debentures. For readers who may be interested in this ingenious arrangement we set forth our solution in Appendix 6.

What on earth到底（加强语气）in detective fashion像侦探一样derive a tax advantage from从……获得税收好处debentures无担保债券，信用债券ingenious巧妙的

这些项目究竟是什么意思？1969年报告正文完全没有提及。训练有素的证券分析师只得像侦探一样自行破解。最终会发现，核心思路是利用5%债券初始低价取得税收好处。对这项巧妙安排感兴趣的读者，可参见附录6中我们的推导。

Other Unusual Items

其他异常项目

1. Right after the close of 1969 the company bought in no less than 650,000 warrants at a price of $9.38 each. This was extraordinary when we consider that (a) NVF itself had only $700,000 in cash at the year-end, and had $4,400,000 of debt due in 1970 (evidently the $6 million paid for the warrants had to be borrowed); (b) it was buying in this warrant “paper money” at a time when its 5% bonds were selling at less than 40 cents on the dollar—ordinarily a warning that financial difficulties lay ahead.

bought in回购no less than多达due in 19701970 年到期paper money纸票子（讽刺权证像随手印出来的钱）lay ahead就在前面，即将到来

1. 1969年刚结束，公司便以每份9.38美元回购不少于65万份权证。这很反常，因为：（a）NVF年末现金只有70万美元，1970年又有440万美元债务到期，支付权证的约600万美元显然也得借；（b）公司回购这种权证“纸币”时，其5%债券市价还不到面值40%，通常已是在警告财务困难将至。

2. As a partial offset to this, the company had retired $5,100,000 of its bonds along with 253,000 warrants in exchange for a like amount of common stock. This was possible because, by the vagaries of the securities markets, people were selling the 5% bonds at less than 40 while the common sold at an average price of 13½, paying no dividend.

retired赎回注销（债券）a like amount等值数量vagaries变幻莫测，反复无常paying no dividend不派发股息

2. 部分抵消上述问题的是，公司用等量普通股交换，注销了510万美元债券及25.3万份权证。之所以能做到，是因为证券市场反复无常：人们按不到面值40%出售5%债券，毫无股息的普通股平均价格却有13又1/2美元。

3. The company had plans in operation not only for selling stock to its employees, but also for selling them a larger number of warrants to buy the stock. Like the stock purchases the warrants were to be paid for 5% down and the rest over many years in the future. This is the only such employee-purchase plan for warrants that we know of. Will someone soon invent and sell on installments a right to buy a right to buy a share, and so on?

4. In the year 1969 the newly controlled Sharon Steel Co. changed its method of arriving at its pension costs, and also adopted lower depreciation rates. These accounting changes added about $1 per share to the reported earnings of NVF before dilution.

5. At the end of 1970 Standard & Poor’s Stock Guide reported that NVF shares were selling at a price/earning ratio of only 2, the lowest figure for all the 4,500-odd issues in the booklet. As the old Wall Street saying went, this was “important if true.” The ratio was based on the year’s closing price of 8 3/4 and the computed “earnings” of $5.38 per share for the 12 months ended September 1970. (Using these figures the shares were selling at only 1.6 times earnings.) But this ratio did not allow for the large dilution factor,* nor for the adverse results actually realized in the last quarter of 1970. When the full year’s figures finally appeared, they showed only $2.03 per share earned for the stock, before allowing for dilution, and $1.80 per share on a diluted basis. Note also that the aggregate market price of the stock and warrants on that date was about $14 million against a bonded debt of $135 million—a skimpy equity position indeed.

AAA Enterprises

AAA 企业公司

History

历史

About 15 years ago a college student named Williams began selling mobile homes (then called “trailers”).† In 1965 he incorporated his business. In that year he sold $5,800,000 of mobile homes and earned $61,000 before corporate tax. By 1968 he had joined the “franchising” movement and was selling others the right to sell mobile homes under his business name. He also conceived the bright idea of going into the business of preparing income-tax returns, using his mobile homes as offices. He formed a subsidiary company called Mr. Tax of America, and of course started to sell franchises to others to use the idea and the name. He multiplied the number of corporate shares to 2,710,000 and was ready for a stock offering. He found that one of our largest stock-exchange houses, along with others, was willing to handle the deal. In March 1969 they offered the public 500,000 shares of AAA Enterprises at $13 per share. Of these, 300,000 were sold for Mr. Williams’s personal account and 200,000 were sold for the company account, adding $2,400,000 to its resources. The price of the stock promptly doubled to 28, or a value of $84 million for the equity, against a book value of, say, $4,200,000 and maximum reported earnings of $690,000. The stock was thus selling at a tidy 115 times its current (and largest) earnings per share. No doubt Mr. Williams had selected the name AAA Enterprise so that it might be among the first in the phone books and the yellow pages. A collateral result was that his company was destined to appear as the first name in Standard & Poor’s Stock Guide. Like Abu-Ben-Adhem’s, it led all the rest.* This gives a special reason to select it as a harrowing example of 1969 new financing and “hot issues.”

约15年前，一名叫Williams的大学生开始销售活动房屋，当时称“拖车”。1965年他把业务注册为公司，当年销售580万美元、公司所得税前盈利6.1万美元。到1968年，他加入“特许经营”潮流，向别人出售使用其商号销售活动房屋的权利；又想到用活动房屋作办公室，开展代办所得税申报业务，成立子公司Mr. Tax of America，自然也开始出售创意和名称的特许权。他把公司股数扩大到271万股，准备公开发行，并找到一家美国最大证券交易所会员公司与其他机构承销。1969年3月，他们按每股13美元向公众发行50万股AAA Enterprises，其中30万股由Williams个人出售，20万股为公司发行，使公司增加240万美元资金。股价迅速翻倍到28美元，股权总值8,400万美元，而账面价值约420万美元，最高报告盈利69万美元；即市价高达当前也是历史最高每股盈利的115倍。Williams选择AAA这个名称，大概是为了在电话簿和黄页排在前列，附带结果是公司也注定排在《标准普尔股票指南》第一位，像Abou Ben Adhem一样“名列群首”。因此它尤其适合作为1969年新融资与“热门发行”的惊心案例。

COMMENT: This was not a bad deal for Mr. Williams. The 300,000 shares he sold had a book value in December of 1968 of $180,000 and he netted therefor 20 times as much, or a cool $3,600,000. The underwriters and distributors split $500,000 between them, less expenses.

评论：这对Williams先生不是坏交易。他出售的30万股在1968年12月账面价值18万美元，却净得20倍之多，也就是整整360万美元。承销商和经销商扣除费用前分得50万美元。

There were ambitious plans for the future, of course—but the public was being asked to pay heavily in advance for the hoped-for realization of these plans.

Not an easy question to answer, but it deserves careful consideration by Wall Street and the government regulatory agencies.†

Subsequent History

后续发展

With its enlarged capital AAA Enterprises went into two additional businesses. In 1969 it opened a chain of retail carpet stores, and it acquired a plant that manufactured mobile homes. The results reported for the first nine months were not exactly brilliant, but they were a little better than the year before—22 cents a share against 14 cents. What happened in the next months was literally incredible. The company lost $4,365,000, or $1.49 per share. This consumed all its capital before the financing, plus the entire $2,400,000 received on the sale of stock plus two-thirds of the amount reported as earned in the first nine months of 1969. There was left a pathetic $242,000, or 8 cents per share, of capital for the public shareholders who had paid $13 for the new offering only seven months before. Nonetheless the shares closed the year 1969 at 8 1/8 bid, or a “valuation” of more than $25 million for the company.

went into进入（新业务）a chain of连锁的not exactly brilliant算不上出色（委婉说法）literally incredible简直难以置信pathetic可怜的8 1/8 bid买方出价 8.125 美元（bid = 买入报价）

获得扩大后的资本后，AAA Enterprises又进入两项业务：1969年开设地毯零售连锁店，并收购一家活动房屋制造厂。前九个月结果并不出色，不过略好于上年，每股盈利0.22美元，对0.14美元。接下来几个月发生的事简直难以置信：公司亏损436.5万美元，即每股1.49美元，耗尽融资前全部资本、发行股票所得240万美元，以及1969年前九个月报告盈利的三分之二。七个月前按13美元购买新股的公众股东，只剩可怜的24.2万美元资本，即每股0.08美元。尽管如此，股票1969年末买价仍为8又1/8美元，相当于给公司超过2,500万美元“估值”。

FURTHER COMMENT: 1. It is too much to believe that the company had actually earned $686,000 from January to September 1969 and then lost $4,365,000 in the next three months. There was something sadly, badly, and accusingly wrong about the September 30 report.

The year’s closing price of 8 1/8 bid was even more of a demonstration of the complete heedlessness of stock-market prices than were the original offering price of 13 or the subsequent “hot-issue” advance to a high bid of 28. These latter quotations at least were based on enthusiasm and hope—out of all proportion to reality and common sense, but at least comprehensible. The year-end valuation of $25 million was given to a company that had lost all but a minuscule remnant of its capital, for which a completely insolvent condition was imminent, and for which the words “enthusiasm” or “hope” would be only bitter sarcasms. (It is true the year-end figures had not been published by December 31, but it is the business of Wall Street houses associated with a company to have monthly operating statements and a fairly exact idea of how things are going.)

Final Chapter

最后一幕

For the first half of 1970 the company reported a further loss of $1 million. It now had a good-sized capital deficit. It was kept out of bankruptcy by loans made by Mr. Williams, up to a total of $2,500,000. No further statements seem to have been issued, until in January 1971 AAA Enterprises finally filed a petition in bankruptcy. The quotation for the stock at month-end was still 50 cents a share bid, or $1,500,000 for the entire issue, which evidently had no more than wallpaper value. End of our story.

good-sized相当大的capital deficit资本赤字（净资产为负）kept out of bankruptcy免于破产filed a petition in bankruptcy提交破产申请the entire issue全部已发行股票wallpaper value只配当壁纸的价值（指股票一文不值）

1970年上半年公司又报告亏损100万美元，已形成相当大的资本亏空。Williams先生贷款维持公司不破产，累计达250万美元。此后似乎未再发布报表，直到1971年1月AAA Enterprises终于申请破产。月底股票买价竟仍有每股0.50美元，即全部股票150万美元，而它显然只剩糊墙纸的价值。故事到此结束。

MORAL AND QUESTIONS: The speculative public is incorrigible. In financial terms it cannot count beyond 3. It will buy anything, at any price, if there seems to be some “action” in progress. It will fall for any company identified with “franchising,” computers, electronics, science, technology, or what have you, when the particular fashion is raging. Our readers, sensible investors all, are of course above such foolishness. But questions remain: Should not responsible investment houses be honor-bound to refrain from identifying themselves with such enterprises, nine out of ten of which may be foredoomed to ultimate failure? (This was actually the situation when the author entered Wall Street in 1914. By comparison it would seem that the ethical standards of the “Street” have fallen rather than advanced in the ensuing 57 years, despite all the reforms and all the controls.) Could and should the SEC be given other powers to protect the public, beyond the present ones which are limited to requiring the printing of all important relevant facts in the offering prospectus? Should some kind of box score for public offerings of various types be compiled and published in conspicuous fashion? Should every prospectus, and perhaps every confirmation of sale under an original offering, carry some kind of formal warranty that the offering price for the issue is not substantially out of line with the ruling prices for issues of the same general type already established in the market? As we write this edition a movement toward reform of Wall Street abuses is under way. It will be difficult to impose worthwhile changes in the field of new offerings, because the abuses are so largely the result of the public’s own heedlessness and greed. But the matter deserves long and careful consideration.*

Should every prospectus, and perhaps every confirmation of sale under an original offering, carry some kind of formal warranty that the offering price for the issue is not substantially out of line with the ruling prices for issues of the same general type already established in the market?

是否应该让每一份招股说明书——或许还有首次发行中的每一份成交确认书——都附带某种正式保证，保证该证券的发行价与市场上已有的同类证券的现行价格没有严重脱节？

Should … carry … 是一般疑问句，主语 every prospectus, and perhaps every confirmation of sale … 被插入语拉长；warranty that … 中的 that 引导同位语从句，说明保证的内容。out of line with 意为“与……不一致”，issues 在此指证券，ruling prices 指当时通行的市价。

教训与问题：投机大众积习难改，在金融上数不过3。只要看似“有行情”，他们什么都买、什么价格都付。某种风潮盛行时，只要公司贴上“特许经营”、计算机、电子、科学、技术或任何时髦标签，他们都会上钩。本书读者都是理性投资者，当然不会犯这种傻。但问题仍在：负责任的投资机构是否应出于职业道德，拒绝与此类企业发生关联——其中十家有九家可能注定失败？（作者1914年进入华尔街时，实际情况就是如此。相比之下，尽管57年间改革与监管众多，“华尔街”的道德标准似乎不升反降。）是否能、也是否应赋予美国证券交易委员会更多保护公众的权力，而不只要求招股书印出所有重要相关事实？是否应为不同类型公开发行编制并醒目发布某种成绩表？每份招股书，甚至每笔原始发行的成交确认书，是否都应正式保证发行价与市场上已交易的同类证券价格没有严重脱节？本版写作时，一场纠正华尔街弊端的改革正在推进。新股发行领域很难实行有价值的改变，因为弊端很大程度源于公众自己的轻率与贪婪。但此事值得长期、认真思考。

Notes · 注释（贾森·兹威格）

* How “shocked” was the financial world by the Penn Central’s bankruptcy, which was filed over the weekend of June 20–21, 1970? The closing trade in Penn Central’s stock on Friday, June 19, was $11.25 per share—hardly a going-out-of-business price. In more recent times, stocks like Enron and WorldCom have also sold at relatively high prices shortly before filing for bankruptcy protection.
Penn Central于1970年6月20—21日周末申请破产，金融界究竟有多“震惊”？6月19日星期五最后成交价仍是每股11.25美元，绝不像马上倒闭的价格。近年Enron、WorldCom等股票在申请破产保护前不久也仍以相对高价交易。
* Penn Central was the product of the merger, announced in 1966, of the Pennsylvania Railroad and the New York Central Railroad.
Penn Central由Pennsylvania Railroad与New York Central Railroad合并而成，合并于1966年宣布。
† This kind of accounting legerdemain, in which profits are reported as if “unusual” or “extraordinary” or “nonrecurring” charges do not matter, anticipates the reliance on “pro forma” financial statements that became popular in the late 1990s (see the commentary on Chapter 12).
这种会计戏法把“异常”“非常”或“非经常性”费用仿佛无关紧要一样剔除后报告利润，预演了20世纪90年代末流行的“模拟”财务报表，参见第12章评论。
* A railroad’s “transportation ratio” (now more commonly called its operating ratio) measures the expenses of running its trains divided by the railroad’s total revenues. The higher the ratio, the less efficient the railroad. Today even a ratio of 70% would be considered excellent.
铁路的“运输比率”（如今更常称经营比率）等于列车运营费用除以铁路总收入。比率越高，效率越低。今天即使70%也会被视为优秀。
† Today, Penn Central is a faded memory. In 1976, it was absorbed into Consolidated Rail Corp. (Conrail), a federally-funded holding company that bailed out several failed railroads. Conrail sold shares to the public in 1987 and, in 1997, was taken over jointly by CSX Corp. and Norfolk Southern Corp.
今天Penn Central已成为褪色记忆。1976年它被并入联邦资助、为多家失败铁路纾困的控股公司Consolidated Rail Corp.（Conrail）。Conrail于1987年公开上市，1997年由CSX Corp.与Norfolk Southern Corp.联合收购。
† Ling-Temco-Vought Inc. was founded in 1955 by James Joseph Ling, an electrical contractor who sold his first $1 million worth of shares to the public by becoming his own investment banker, hawking prospectuses from a booth set up at the Texas State Fair. His success at that led him to acquire dozens of different companies, almost always using LTV’s stock to pay for them. The more companies LTV acquired, the higher its stock went; the higher its stock went, the more companies it could afford to acquire. By 1969, LTV was the 14th biggest firm on the Fortune 500 list of major U.S. corporations. And then, as Graham shows, the whole house of cards came crashing down. (LTV Corp., now exclusively a steelmaker, ended up seeking bankruptcy protection in late 2000.) Companies that grow primarily through acquisitions are called “serial acquirers”—and the similarity to the term “serial killers” is no accident. As the case of LTV demonstrates, serial acquirers nearly always leave financial death and destruction in their wake. Investors who understood this lesson of Graham’s would have avoided such darlings of the 1990s as Conseco, Tyco, and WorldCom.
Ling-Temco-Vought Inc.由电气承包商James Joseph Ling于1955年创办。他充当自己的投资银行家，在得州州博览会搭摊派发招股书，向公众卖出首批价值100万美元股票。成功后，他开始收购数十家不同公司，几乎总用LTV股票支付。收购越多，股价越高；股价越高，又能收购更多。到1969年，LTV已是《财富》500强第14大公司，随后如格雷厄姆所示，整个纸牌屋坍塌。（后来仅从事钢铁的LTV Corp.最终于2000年末申请破产保护。）主要靠收购成长的公司称“连续收购者”，这个词与“连环杀手”相似并非偶然。LTV说明，连续收购者几乎总留下财务死亡与破坏。理解这一教训的投资者，本可避开90年代的宠儿Conseco、Tyco与WorldCom。
* The sordid tradition of hiding a company’s true earnings picture under the cloak of restructuring charges is still with us. Piling up every possible charge in one year is sometimes called “big bath” or “kitchen sink” accounting. This bookkeeping gimmick enables companies to make an easy show of apparent growth in the following year—but investors should not mistake that for real business health.
借重组费用掩盖真实盈利的丑陋传统至今仍在。把所有可能费用都堆进一年，有时称“大洗澡”或“厨房水槽”会计。这种手法让次年很容易显出表面增长，投资者不可误当成真正经营健康。
† The “bond-discount asset” appears to mean that LTV had purchased some bonds below their par value and was treating that discount as an asset, on the grounds that the bonds could eventually be sold at par. Graham scoffs at this, since there is rarely any way to know what a bond’s market price will be on a given date in the future. If the bonds could be sold only at values below par, this “asset” would in fact be a liability.
“债券折价资产”似乎是指LTV低于面值买入某些债券，并以将来可按面值出售为由，把折价部分当作资产。格雷厄姆嘲讽这种做法，因为几乎无法预知债券未来某日市价。若只能低于面值出售，这项“资产”实际上会成为负担。
† We can only imagine what Graham would have thought of the investment banking firms that brought InfoSpace, Inc. public in December 1998. The stock (adjusted for later splits) opened for trading at $31.25, peaked at $1305.32 per share in March 2000, and finished 2002 at a princely $8.45 per share.
我们只能想象格雷厄姆会怎样看待1998年12月把InfoSpace, Inc.推上市的投行。按后来拆股调整，股票开盘31.25美元，2000年3月最高1,305.32美元，2002年末则只剩“尊贵的”8.45美元。
* Graham would have been disappointed, though surely not surprised, to see that commercial banks have chronically kept supporting “unsound expansions.” Enron and WorldCom, two of the biggest collapses in corporate history, were aided and abetted by billions of dollars in bank loans.
格雷厄姆若看到商业银行长期继续支持“不稳健扩张”，一定失望，但不会惊讶。公司史上两次最大崩塌Enron与WorldCom，都得到数十亿美元银行贷款的协助与纵容。
* In June 1972 (just after Graham finished this chapter), a Federal judge found that NVF’s chairman, Victor Posner, had improperly diverted the pension assets of Sharon Steel “to assist affiliated companies in their takeovers of other corporations.” In 1977, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission secured a permanent injunction against Posner, NVF, and Sharon Steel to prevent them from future violations of Federal laws against securities fraud. The Commission alleged that Posner and his family had improperly obtained $1.7 million in personal perks from NVF and Sharon, overstated Sharon’s pretax earnings by $13.9 million, misrecorded inventory, and “shifted income and expenses from one year to another.” Sharon Steel, which Graham had singled out with his cold and skeptical eye, became known among Wall Street wags as “Share and Steal.” Posner was later a central force in the wave of leveraged buyouts and hostile takeovers that swept the United States in the 1980s, as he became a major customer for the junk bonds underwritten by Drexel Burnham Lambert.
1972年6月，格雷厄姆刚完成本章后，一名联邦法官认定NVF董事长Victor Posner不当挪用Sharon Steel养老金资产，“帮助关联公司收购其他企业”。1977年，美国证券交易委员会取得针对Posner、NVF与Sharon Steel的永久禁令，防止其继续违反联邦证券反欺诈法。委员会指控Posner家族从两家公司不当取得170万美元个人福利，高估Sharon税前盈利1,390万美元，错误记录存货，并“把收入和费用从一年挪到另一年”。被格雷厄姆冷静而怀疑地挑出的Sharon Steel，被华尔街笑称“Share and Steal”。后来Posner成为80年代杠杆收购与敌意收购浪潮的重要力量，也是Drexel Burnham Lambert承销垃圾债的大客户。
* The “large dilution factor” would be triggered when NVF employees exercised their warrants to buy common stock. The company would then have to issue more shares, and its net earnings would be divided across a much greater number of shares outstanding.
NVF员工行使权证购买普通股时会触发“大规模稀释”：公司须发行更多股份，净利润便要由大得多的流通股数共同分摊。
† Jackie G. Williams founded AAA Enterprises in 1958. On its first day of trading, the stock soared 56% to close at $20.25. Williams later announced that AAA would come up with a new franchising concept every month (if people would step into a mobile home to get their income taxes done by “Mr. Tax of America,” just imagine what else they might do inside a trailer!). But AAA ran out of time and money before Williams ran out of ideas. The history of AAA Enterprises is reminiscent of the saga of a later company with charismatic management and scanty assets: ZZZZ Best achieved a stock-market value of roughly $200 million in the late 1980s, even though its purported industrial vacuum-cleaning business was little more than a telephone and a rented office run by a teenager named Barry Minkow. ZZZZ Best went bust and Minkow went to jail. Even as you read this, another similar company is being formed, and a new generation of “investors” will be taken for a ride. No one who has read Graham, however, should climb on board.
Jackie G. Williams于1958年创办AAA Enterprises。上市首日股价猛涨56%，收于20.25美元。后来Williams宣称AAA每月都会推出一个新特许经营概念——如果人们愿意走进活动房屋，让“Mr. Tax of America”代办税务，想象一下他们还会在拖车里做什么！但在Williams耗尽创意前，AAA先耗尽时间与金钱。其历史让人想起后来一家同样管理层魅力十足、资产单薄的公司ZZZZ Best：80年代末市值约2亿美元，所谓工业吸尘业务却不过是一部电话、一个租来的办公室和一名叫Barry Minkow的少年。ZZZZ Best破产，Minkow入狱。就在你阅读时，另一家相似公司可能正在成立，新一代“投资者”又会被带去兜风；但读过格雷厄姆的人不该上车。
* In “Abou Ben Adhem,” by the British Romantic poet Leigh Hunt (1784–1859), a righteous Muslim sees an angel writing in a golden book “the names of those who love the Lord.” When the angel tells Abou that his name is not among them, Abou says, “I pray thee, then, write me as one that loves his fellow men.” The angel returns the next night to show Abou the book, in which now “Ben Adhem’s name led all the rest.”
英国浪漫主义诗人Leigh Hunt（1784—1859）的《Abou Ben Adhem》中，一名正直穆斯林看见天使在金册上写“爱上帝者的名字”。天使说其中没有Abou，他便答：“那么请把我写成爱同胞的人。”次夜天使回来展示金册，此时“Ben Adhem的名字名列群首”。
* By purchasing more common stock at a premium to its book value, the investing public increased the value of AAA’s equity per share. But investors were only pulling themselves up by their own bootstraps, since most of the rise in shareholders’ equity came from the public’s own willingness to over-pay for the stock.
公众以高于账面价值的价格购买更多普通股，提高了AAA每股权益。但投资者只是用自己的鞋带把自己提起来，因为股东权益增长大多来自公众自己愿意为股票多付的钱。
† Graham’s point is that investment banks are not entitled to take credit for the gains a hot stock may produce right after its initial public offering unless they are also willing to take the blame for the stock’s performance in the longer term. Many Internet IPOs rose 1,000% or more in 1999 and early 2000; most of them lost more than 95% in the subsequent three years. How could these early gains earned by a few investors justify the massive destruction of wealth suffered by the millions who came later? Many IPOs were, in fact, deliberately underpriced to “manufacture” immediate gains that would attract more attention for the next offering.
格雷厄姆的意思是：若投行不愿为热门股长期表现负责，就无权把首次公开发行后立刻上涨归为自己的功劳。许多互联网IPO在1999及2000年初上涨1,000%以上，随后三年多数下跌超过95%。少数早期投资者的盈利，怎能为后来数百万人遭受的巨额财富毁灭辩护？事实上，许多IPO被故意低价发行，以“制造”即时涨幅，为下一次发行吸引更多关注。
* The first four sentences of Graham’s paragraph could read as the official epitaph of the Internet and telecommunications bubble that burst in early 2000. Just as the Surgeon General’s warning on the side of a cigarette pack does not stop everyone from lighting up, no regulatory reform will ever prevent investors from overdosing on their own greed. (Not even Communism can outlaw market bubbles; the Chinese stock market shot up 101.7% in the first half of 1999, then crashed.) Nor can investment banks ever be entirely cleansed of their own compulsion to sell any stock at any price the market will bear. The circle can only be broken one investor, and one financial adviser, at a time. Mastering Graham’s principles (see especially Chapters 1, 8, and 20) is the best way to start.
格雷厄姆本段前四句可作为2000年初破裂的互联网与电信泡沫正式墓志铭。就像烟盒上的卫生警告无法阻止所有人点烟，监管改革也永远无法阻止投资者因自身贪婪而过量投机。（连共产主义也不能禁止市场泡沫：中国股市1999年上半年上涨101.7%，随后崩跌。）投行也不可能完全戒掉按市场能承受的任何价格销售任何股票的冲动。这个循环只能由每一名投资者、每一名财务顾问逐个打破。掌握格雷厄姆原则，尤其第1、8、20章，是最佳起点。

CHAPTER 18

八组公司的比较

A Comparison of Eight Pairs of Companies

成对比较能怎样揭示名气、增长与价格之间的错位？

独立精读增强版：保留英文原文、段落 ID、词汇提示、长难句、图片及注释结构；新增完整中文译文。扩展解释均标注“译者补充（非原文）”。

Chapter 18A Comparison of Eight Pairs of Companies第18章 八组公司的比较

本章导读本章是格雷厄姆的一次“新颖的写法”：他挑出八组在交易所名单上相邻、或者名字相近的公司，两两对照，用具体案例展示企业的性格、财务结构、经营策略、业绩起伏，以及市场对它们的投资与投机态度。每一组只评论“有特殊意义”的方面，之后大多附一段 SEQUEL（后续），交代 1970 年暴跌和 1971 年反弹中的表现。八组分别是：稳健的老牌信托 Real Estate Investment Trust 对暴走的 Realty Equities；同行业的 Air Products 对 Air Reduction（“质量”对“低市盈率”）；两家“商誉十亿美元”的健康行业公司 American Home Products 对 American Hospital Supply；市盈率超过 100 倍的 H & R Block 对只有 11 倍的 Blue Bell；小而极赚钱的 International Flavors & Fragrances 对庞大却微利的 International Harvester；McGraw Edison 对被出版热捧高的 McGraw-Hill；花样繁多的大集团 National General 对结构简单的 National Presto；以及中型企业 Whiting 对“小土豆”集团 Willcox & Gibbs。论证方式始终如一：把销售额、利润率、资本回报率、账面价值、股息和市盈率并排放进表格，让数字自己说话。成长快、盈利强的公司理所当然享有更高的市盈率，但“高多少才合理”无法用任何可证明的原则回答；而凡是基本面可疑却交易火爆的股票，几乎都明显高估，反过来也有被“过度冷落”或因盈利下滑而被过分悲观看待的便宜货。他还借 National General 讲了一个技术要点：认股权证的市值应该加到普通股上计算“真实市价”，一加之后市盈率翻到荒唐的 69 倍。结尾的“总体观察”给出他对证券分析工作的定位：不要去预测哪只股票未来表现最好，而应寻找少数能有把握判断“价格远低于价值”的例外情况，并把它们作为一组分散投资的一部分。

In this chapter we shall attempt a novel form of exposition. By selecting eight pairs of companies which appear next to each other, or nearly so, on the stock-exchange list we hope to bring home in a concrete and vivid manner some of the many varieties of character, financial structure, policies, performance, and vicissitudes of corporate enterprises, and of the investment and speculative attitudes found on the financial scene in recent years. In each comparison we shall comment only on those aspects that have a special meaning and import.

a novel form of exposition一种新颖的阐述方式（novel 此处是形容词“新颖的”）bring home使人深切体会到，让人明白vicissitudes兴衰变迁the financial scene金融界，金融舞台import重要意义（名词，此处不是“进口”）

本章将尝试一种新的论述方式。我们从证券交易所名单中选出八组成对的公司，它们在名单上的位置彼此相邻或相近，希望借此具体而生动地展示企业在性质、财务结构、经营政策、业绩和盛衰变化上的多种面貌，以及近年金融市场中各种投资与投机态度。每组比较只讨论具有特殊意义的重要方面。

Pair I: Real Estate Investment Trust (Stores, Offices, Factories, etc.) and Realty Equities Corp. of New York (Real Estate Investment; General Construction)

第一组：房地产投资信托（商店、写字楼、工厂等）与纽约房地产权益公司（房地产投资；一般建筑）

In this first comparison we depart from the alphabetical order used for the other pairs. It has a special significance for us, since it seems to encapsulate, on the one hand, all that has been reasonable, stable, and generally good in the traditional methods of handling other people’s money, in contrast—in the other company—with the reckless expansion, the financial legerdemain, and the roller-coaster changes so often found in present-day corporate operations. The two enterprises have similar names, and for many years they appeared side by side on the American Stock Exchange list. Their stock-ticker symbols—REI and REC—could easily have been confused. But one of them is a staid New England trust, administered by three trustees, with operations dating back nearly a century, and with dividends paid continuously since 1889. It has kept throughout to the same type of prudent investments, limiting its expansion to a moderate rate and its debt to an easily manageable figure.*

depart from偏离，不按照encapsulate浓缩地体现，概括handling other people’s money管理别人的钱（受托理财）financial legerdemain财务上的戏法、障眼法（legerdemain 原指魔术手法，源自法语）roller-coaster过山车式的，大起大落的stock-ticker symbols股票代码staid古板稳重的trustees受托人prudent审慎的

It has a special significance for us, since it seems to encapsulate, on the one hand, all that has been reasonable, stable, and generally good in the traditional methods of handling other people’s money, in contrast—in the other company—with the reckless expansion, the financial legerdemain, and the roller-coaster changes so often found in present-day corporate operations.

这一组对我们有特殊意义，因为它似乎把两样东西浓缩在了一起：一方面，是传统的代人理财方式中一切合理、稳定、总体良好的东西；另一方面——在另一家公司身上——则是当今公司经营中常见的鲁莽扩张、财务戏法和过山车式的大起大落。

第一组比较没有沿用其他各组的字母顺序。它对我们有特殊意义，因为它把鲜明的两面浓缩在一起：一面是传统受托理财中合理、稳定而总体良好的一切；另一面则是现代公司经营里常见的鲁莽扩张、财务戏法和过山车式变化。两家公司名称相似，多年来在美国证券交易所名单上紧挨着，股票代码REI和REC也很容易混淆。但其中一家是作风稳健的新英格兰信托，由三名受托人管理，经营史近百年，自1889年起从未中断分红。它始终坚持同一类审慎投资，只以适中速度扩张，并把债务限制在易于管理的水平。

The other is a typical New York-based sudden-growth venture, which in eight years blew up its assets from $6.2 million to $154 million, and its debts in the same proportion; which moved out from ordinary real-estate operations to a miscellany of ventures, including two racetracks, 74 movie theaters, three literary agencies, a public-relations firm, hotels, supermarkets, and a 26% interest in a large cosmetics firm (which went bankrupt in 1970).† This conglomeration of business ventures was matched by a corresponding variety of corporate devices, including the following:

sudden-growth venture突然膨胀起来的企业blew up its assets把资产急剧吹大（blow up 此处是“吹胀”）a miscellany of ventures五花八门的各种生意conglomeration大杂烩，混杂的集合体corporate devices公司层面的（融资）花招、手段

另一家则是典型的纽约式突然成长企业：八年间资产从620万美元膨胀到1.54亿美元，债务也按相同比例增长；业务从普通房地产扩展到五花八门的项目，包括两座赛马场、74家电影院、三家文学代理机构、一家公关公司、酒店、超市，以及一家大型化妆品公司26%的权益——后者于1970年破产。这种业务上的大杂烩，也配套了同样五花八门的公司融资手段，包括：

Here we find the Trust shares selling in the market for nine times the aggregate value of Equities stock. In Table 18-1B we present the situation about eight years later. The Trust had “kept the noiseless tenor of its way,” increasing both its revenues and its per-share earnings by about three-quarters.* But Realty Equities had been metamorphosed into something monstrous and vulnerable.

kept the noiseless tenor of its way静静地走自己的路（引自格雷《墓园挽歌》）metamorphosed into蜕变成monstrous and vulnerable畸形而脆弱的

The Trust had “kept the noiseless tenor of its way,” increasing both its revenues and its per-share earnings by about three-quarters. But Realty Equities had been metamorphosed into something monstrous and vulnerable.

信托公司一直“静静地走着自己的路”，收入和每股收益都增长了大约四分之三。而 Realty Equities 却已经蜕变成一个畸形而脆弱的怪物。

引号里的话出自托马斯·格雷的《墓园挽歌》（they kept the noiseless tenor of their way），形容不声不响、按部就班地过日子；tenor 此处是“进程、路线”而非“男高音”。increasing … 是现在分词短语，补充说明“走自己的路”的结果。

表18-1B展示了约八年后的情形。信托公司一直“不声不响地走自己的路”，收入和每股盈利都增加了约四分之三；Realty Equities却变成了一个畸形而脆弱的庞然怪物。

How did Wall Street react to these diverse developments? By paying as little attention as possible to the Trust and a lot to Realty Equities. In 1968 the latter shot up from 10 to 37 3/4 and the listed warrants from 6 to 36½, on combined sales of 2,420,000 shares. While this was happening the Trust shares advanced sedately from 20 to 30¼ on modest volume. The March 1969 balance sheet of Equities was to show an asset value of only $3.41 per share, less than a tenth of its high price that year. The book value of the Trust shares was $20.85.

华尔街如何回应这两种截然不同的发展？它尽量不理会信托公司，却对Realty Equities大加关注。1968年，后者股价从10美元猛涨到37又3/4美元，上市认股权证从6美元涨到36又1/2美元，两者合计成交242万份；同期，信托公司的股票只是在温和成交量中从20美元稳步升到30又1/4美元。Realty Equities于1969年3月的资产负债表显示，每股资产价值仅3.41美元，还不到当年最高股价的十分之一；信托公司的每股账面价值则为20.85美元。

The next year it became clear that all was not well in the Equities picture, and the price fell to 9½. When the report for March 1970 appeared the shareholders must have felt shell-shocked as they read that the enterprise had sustained a net loss of $13,200,000, or $5.17 per share—virtually wiping out their former slim equity. (This disastrous figure included a reserve of $8,800,000 for future losses on investments.) Nonetheless the directors had bravely (?) declared an extra dividend of 5 cents right after the close of the fiscal year. But more trouble was in sight. The company’s auditors refused to certify the financial statements for 1969–70, and the shares were suspended from trading on the American Stock Exchange. In the over-the-counter market the bid price dropped below $2 per share.*

Real Estate Investment Trust shares had typical price fluctuations after 1969. The low in 1970 was 16½, with a recovery to 26 5/6 in early 1971. The latest reported earnings were $1.50 per share, and the stock was selling moderately above its 1970 book value of $21.60. The issue may have been somewhat overpriced at its record high in 1968, but the shareholders have been honestly and well served by their trustees. The Real Estate Equities story is a different and a sorry one.
