Real Estate Investment Trust的股价在1969年后出现了通常的波动：1970年最低16又1/2美元，1971年初回升到26又5/6美元。最近报告的每股盈利为1.50美元，股价略高于1970年每股21.60美元的账面价值。它在1968年创纪录高位时或许略显昂贵，但受托人一直诚实而妥善地为股东服务。Realty Equities的故事则完全不同，而且令人遗憾。

Pair 2: Air Products and Chemicals (Industrial and Medical Gases, etc.) and Air Reduction Co. (Industrial Gases and Equipment; Chemicals)

第二组：空气产品与化学品公司（工业和医用气体等）与空气还原公司（工业气体与设备；化学品）

Even more than our first pair, these two resemble each other in both name and line of business. The comparison they invite is thus of the conventional type in security analysis, while most of our other pairs are more heteroclite in nature.† “Products” is a newer company than “Reduction,” and in 1969 had less than half the other’s volume.* Nonetheless its equity issues sold for 25% more in the aggregate than Air Reduction’s stock. As Table 18-2 shows, the reason can be found both in Air Products’s greater profitability and in its stronger growth record. We find here the typical consequences of a better showing of “quality.” Air Products sold at 16½ times its latest earnings against only 9.1 times for Air Reduction. Also Air Products sold well above its asset backing, while Air Reduction could be bought at only 75% of its book value.† Air Reduction paid a more liberal dividend; but this may be deemed to reflect the greater desirability for Air Products to retain its earnings. Also, Air Reduction had a more comfortable working-capital position. (On this point we may remark that a profitable company can always put its current position in shape by some form of permanent financing. But by our standards Air Products was somewhat overbonded.)

这两家公司不仅名称相似，业务也比第一组更接近，因此适合采用证券分析中常规的同业比较；本章其他多数配对反而较为异类。Air Products成立较晚，1969年的营业额还不到Air Reduction的一半，但其全部股票的市值却比后者高25%。表18-2说明，原因既在于Air Products盈利能力较强，也在于增长记录更好，这正是市场给“质量”更高估值的典型结果。Air Products按最近盈利的16.5倍交易，Air Reduction只有9.1倍；前者股价远高于资产支撑，后者只需账面价值的75%便可买到。Air Reduction分红更慷慨，但这也可理解为Air Products更值得把利润留在公司。Air Reduction的营运资本状况也更宽裕。（盈利企业总可通过某种长期融资改善流动状况，不过按我们的标准，Air Products的债券负担稍重。）

If the analyst were called on to choose between the two companies he would have no difficulty in concluding that the prospects of Air Products looked more promising than those of Air Reduction. But did this make Air Products more attractive at its considerably higher relative price? We doubt whether this question can be answered in a definitive fashion. In general Wall Street sets “quality” above “quantity” in its thinking, and probably the majority of security analysts would opt for the “better” but dearer Air Products as against the “poorer” but cheaper Air Reduction. Whether this preference is to prove right or wrong is more likely to depend on the unpredictable future than on any demonstrable investment principle. In this instance, Air Reduction appears to belong to the group of important companies in the low-multiplier class. If, as the studies referred to above†† would seem to indicate, that group as a whole is likely to give a better account of itself than the high-multiplier stocks, then Air Reduction should logically be given the preference—but only as part of a diversified operation. (Also, a thorough-going study of the individual companies could lead the analyst to the opposite conclusion; but that would have to be for reasons beyond those already reflected in the past showing.)

若要求分析师只比较企业前景，他不难认定Air Products比Air Reduction更有希望。但这是否足以让相对价格高得多的Air Products成为更有吸引力的股票？我们怀疑这个问题能否得到确定答案。华尔街通常重“质量”胜于“数量”，多数证券分析师大概会选择较好但较贵的Air Products，而不是较差但较便宜的Air Reduction。这种偏好最终对错，更可能取决于不可预测的未来，而不是某条可证明的投资原则。本例中，Air Reduction属于重要公司的低市盈率组。若前述研究确实表明这一组整体上可能胜过高市盈率股票，那么逻辑上应优先选择Air Reduction——但只能把它作为分散投资组合的一部分。（对个别公司的深入研究也可能得出相反结论，不过理由必须超出已经反映在历史业绩中的信息。）

译者补充（非原文）：“好公司”和“好价格”是两个问题。比如甲公司盈利增速更快，但市盈率40倍；乙公司增长较慢，市盈率10倍。若甲公司的优势未能持续足够久，较高买价就可能吞掉经营优势。格雷厄姆因此要求把低估值判断放进分散组合，而不是押注单一公司。

SEQUEL: Air Products stood up better than Air Reduction in the 1970 break, with a decline of 16% against 24%. However, Reduction made a better comeback in early 1971, rising to 50% above its 1969 close, against 30% for Products. In this case the low-multiplier issue scored the advantage—for the time being, at least.*

Pair 3: American Home Products Co. (drugs, cosmetics, household products, candy) and American Hospital Supply Co. (distributor and manufacturer of hospital supplies and equipment)

American Home Products Co.美国家庭用品公司American Hospital Supply Co.美国医院用品公司distributor分销商

第3组：American Home Products Co.（药品、化妆品、家居用品、糖果）与American Hospital Supply Co.（医院用品和设备的经销商及制造商）

These were two “billion-dollar good-will” companies at the end of 1969, representing different segments of the rapidly growing and immensely profitable “health industry.” We shall refer to them as Home and Hospital, respectively. Selected data on both are presented in Table 18-3. They had the following favorable points in common: excellent growth, with no setbacks since 1958 (i.e., 100% earnings stability); and strong financial condition. The growth rate of Hospital up to the end of 1969 was considerably higher than Home’s. On the other hand, Home enjoyed substantially better profitability on both sales and capital.† (In fact, the relatively low rate of Hospital’s earnings on its capital in 1969—only 9.7%—raises the intriguing question whether the business then was in fact a highly profitable one, despite its remarkable past growth rate in sales and earnings.)

1969年末，这两家都是拥有“十亿美元商誉”的公司，分别代表迅速成长且利润极高的“医疗健康产业”不同板块，下文简称Home和Hospital。表18-3列出两者的精选数据。它们共同的优点是：增长出色，1958年以来盈利从未倒退，也就是盈利稳定率100%；财务状况也很强。到1969年末，Hospital的增长率明显高于Home；另一方面，Home无论按销售额还是按资本计算，盈利能力都显著更高。（事实上，Hospital在1969年的资本回报率只有9.7%，这让人产生一个有趣的问题：尽管它过去的销售和盈利增长惊人，当时的业务是否真算得上高利润。）

When comparative price is taken into account, Home offered much more for the money in terms of current (or past) earnings and dividends. The very low book value of Home illustrates a basic ambiguity or contradiction in common-stock analysis. On the one hand, it means that the company is earning a high return on its capital—which in general is a sign of strength and prosperity. On the other, it means that the investor at the current price would be especially vulnerable to any important adverse change in the company’s earnings situation. Since Hospital was selling at over four times its book value in 1969, this cautionary remark must be applied to both companies.

CONCLUSIONS: Our clear-cut view would be that both companies were too “rich” at their current prices to be considered by the investor who decides to follow our ideas of conservative selection. This does not mean that the companies were lacking in promise. The trouble is, rather, that their price contained too much “promise” and not enough actual performance. For the two enterprises combined, the 1969 price reflected almost $5 billion of good-will valuation. How many years of excellent future earnings would it take to “realize” that good-will factor in the form of dividends or tangible assets?

clear-cut明确的rich价格过高的（市场用语：估值“贵”）conservative selection保守型选股lacking in promise缺乏前景good-will valuation商誉估值tangible assets有形资产

结论：我们的明确看法是，两家公司按当时价格都太“贵”，不适合遵循保守选股原则的投资者。这不是说公司缺乏前景，而是价格中包含的“前景”太多，现实业绩太少。两家公司合计的1969年市值中，约有50亿美元属于商誉估值。未来要连续多少年取得优异盈利，才能让这部分商誉以股息或有形资产的形式真正兑现？

SHORT-TERM SEQUEL: At the end of 1969 the market evidently thought more highly of the earnings prospects of Hospital than of Home, since it gave the former almost twice the multiplier of the latter. As it happened the favored issue showed a microscopic decline in earnings in 1970, while Home turned in a respectable 8% gain. The market price of Hospital reacted significantly to this one-year disappointment. It sold at 32 in February 1971—a loss of about 30% from its 1969 close—while Home was quoted slightly above its corresponding level.*

短期后续：1969年末，市场显然更看好Hospital的盈利前景，因为给它的市盈率几乎是Home的两倍。结果，受偏爱的Hospital在1970年盈利出现极轻微下降，Home却实现了可观的8%增长。市场对Hospital这一年的失望反应很大：1971年2月股价为32美元，比1969年末下跌约30%；Home的报价则略高于当时水平。

第四组：H & R 布洛克公司（所得税申报服务）与蓝铃公司（工装、制服等制造商）

These companies rub shoulders as relative newcomers to the New York Stock Exchange, where they represent two very different genres of success stories. Blue Bell came up the hard way in a highly competitive industry, in which eventually it became the largest factor. Its earnings have fluctuated somewhat with industry conditions, but their growth since 1965 has been impressive. The company’s operations go back to 1916 and its continuous dividend record to 1923. At the end of 1969 the stock market showed no enthusiasm for the issue, giving it a price/earnings ratio of only 11, against about 17 for the S & P composite index.

这两家公司都是纽约证券交易所相对较新的成员，名单上彼此相邻，却代表两种完全不同的成功故事。Blue Bell在竞争激烈的行业里艰苦成长，最终成为行业龙头。其盈利会随行业状况有所波动，但1965年以来增长令人印象深刻。公司经营始于1916年，自1923年起连续派息。1969年末市场对它毫无热情，只给出11倍市盈率，而标准普尔综合指数约为17倍。

By contrast, the rise of H & R Block has been meteoric. Its first published figures date only to 1961, in which year it earned $83,000 on revenues of $610,000. But eight years later, on our comparison date, its revenues had soared to $53.6 million and its net to $6.3 million. At that time the stock market’s attitude toward this fine performer appeared nothing less than ecstatic. The price of 55 at the close of 1969 was more than 100 times the last reported 12-months’ earnings—which of course were the largest to date. The aggregate market value of $300 million for the stock issue was nearly 30 times the tangible assets behind the shares.* This was almost unheard of in the annals of serious stock-market valuations. (At that time IBM was selling at about 9 times and Xerox at 11 times book value.)

相比之下，H&R Block的崛起如流星般迅猛。它最早公布的数据始于1961年，当年收入61万美元、盈利8.3万美元；八年后，在我们的比较时点，收入已飙升到5,360万美元，净利润达到630万美元。当时市场对这个优秀企业的态度近乎狂热：1969年末55美元的股价，是最近十二个月盈利的100多倍，而那已是公司历史最高盈利。全部股票市值3亿美元，接近股票背后有形资产的30倍。这在严肃的股市估值史上几乎闻所未闻。（当时IBM约为账面价值9倍，施乐约为11倍。）

Our Table 18-4 sets forth in dollar figures and in ratios the extraordinary discrepancy in the comparative valuations of Block and Blue Bell. True, Block showed twice the profitability of Blue Bell per dollar of capital, and its percentage growth in earnings over the past five years (from practically nothing) was much higher. But as a stock enterprise Blue Bell was selling for less than one-third the total value of Block, although Blue Bell was doing four times as much business, earning 2½ times as much for its stock, had 5½ times as much in tangible investment, and gave nine times the dividend yield on the price.

表18-4用金额与比率展示了Block和Blue Bell估值上的惊人差距。诚然，按每1美元资本计算，Block的盈利能力是Blue Bell的两倍，过去五年的盈利增速（从几乎为零起步）也高得多。但作为一项股票投资，Blue Bell的总市值还不到Block的三分之一，尽管它的营业额是Block的四倍、归属于股票的盈利是2.5倍、有形投入资本是5.5倍，按股价计算的股息率更是九倍。

INDICATED CONCLUSIONS: An experienced analyst would have conceded great momentum to Block, implying excellent prospects for future growth. He might have had some qualms about the dangers of serious competition in the income-tax-service field, lured by the handsome return on capital realized by Block.1 But mindful of the continued success of such outstanding companies as Avon Products in highly competitive areas, he would have hesitated to predict a speedy flattening out of the Block growth curve. His chief concern would be simply whether the $300 million valuation for the company had not already fully valued and perhaps overvalued all that one could reasonably expect from this excellent business. By contrast the analyst should have had little difficulty in recommending Blue Bell as a fine company, quite conservatively priced.

推断结论：有经验的分析师会承认Block势头很强，意味着未来增长前景优异。他或许担心所得税服务行业会因Block可观的资本回报而吸引激烈竞争；但想到雅芳等优秀企业在高度竞争领域仍能持续成功，他也不会轻率断言Block的增长曲线很快会走平。他真正应担心的是，3亿美元估值是否已经把这项优秀业务可合理期待的一切全部计价，甚至计价过度。相比之下，分析师应不难推荐Blue Bell：一家优秀而定价相当保守的公司。

SEQUEL TO MARCH 1971. The 1970 near-panic lopped one-quarter off the price of Blue Bell and about one-third from that of Block. Both then joined in the extraordinary recovery of the general market. The price of Block rose to 75 in February 1971, but Blue Bell advanced considerably more—to the equivalent of 109 (after a three-for-two split). Clearly Blue Bell proved a better buy than Block as of the end of 1969. But the fact that Block was able to advance some 35% from that apparently inflated value indicates how wary analysts and investors must be to sell good companies short—either by word or deed—no matter how high the quotation may seem.*

But the fact that Block was able to advance some 35% from that apparently inflated value indicates how wary analysts and investors must be to sell good companies short—either by word or deed—no matter how high the quotation may seem.

但 Block 竟能从那个看似虚高的价位再上涨约 35%，这一事实表明：无论报价看起来多高，分析师和投资者在“看空”好公司时——不管是嘴上说还是实际做——都必须多么谨慎。

主语是 the fact that … value（that 引导同位语从句），谓语是 indicates；how wary … must be to sell … short 意为“做……时必须多么谨慎”。sell short 一语双关：既是“卖空”这种操作，也是“低估、贬低”的习语，所以作者补上 by word or deed（言或行）。

截至1971年3月的后续：1970年近乎恐慌的行情令Blue Bell下跌四分之一，Block下跌约三分之一；随后两者又参与了大盘的异常反弹。1971年2月Block涨至75美元，Blue Bell涨幅更大，按三股拆为两股调整后相当于109美元。显然，以1969年末为起点，Blue Bell是更好的买入对象。但Block竟还能从看似虚高的价格再涨约35%，说明分析师和投资者无论口头还是实际操作，都必须极其谨慎，不要仅因报价看似很高就做空好公司。

Pair 5: International Flavors & Fragrances (Flavors, etc., for Other Businesses) and International Harvester Co. (Truck Manufacturer, Farm Machinery, Construction Machinery)

第五组：国际香精香料公司（为其他企业供应香精等）与国际收割机公司（卡车、农业机械、工程机械制造商）

This comparison should carry more than one surprise. Everyone knows of International Harvester, one of the 30 giants in the Dow Jones Industrial Average.† How many of our readers have even heard of International Flavors & Fragrances, next-door neighbor to Harvester on the New York Stock Exchange list? Yet, mirabile dictu, IFF was actually selling at the end of 1969 for a higher aggregate market value than Harvester—$747 million versus $710 million. This is the more amazing when one reflects that Harvester had 17 times the stock capital of Flavors and 27 times the annual sales. Infact, only three years before, the net earnings of Harvester had been larger than the 1969 sales of Flavors! How did these extraordinary disparities develop? The answer lies in the two magic words: profitability and growth. Flavors made a remarkable showing in both categories, while Harvester left everything to be desired.

Yet, mirabile dictu, IFF was actually selling at the end of 1969 for a higher aggregate market value than Harvester—$747 million versus $710 million. This is the more amazing when one reflects that Harvester had 17 times the stock capital of Flavors and 27 times the annual sales.

然而，说来奇怪，1969 年底 IFF 的总市值竟然高于 Harvester——7.47 亿美元对 7.10 亿美元。再想到 Harvester 的股本是 Flavors 的 17 倍、年销售额是它的 27 倍，这就更加令人惊讶了。

mirabile dictu 是拉丁语插入语，“说来奇妙”。第二句 the more amazing 中的 the 是副词，与后面的 when 从句呼应，意为“考虑到……就更加……”，不是定冠词。

这组比较会带来不止一个意外。人人都知道International Harvester，它是道琼斯工业平均指数30家巨头之一；但有多少读者听说过International Flavors & Fragrances——它在纽约证券交易所名单上恰好紧邻Harvester？然而令人惊叹的是，1969年末IFF的总市值竟更高：7.47亿美元，对7.10亿美元。更惊人的是，Harvester的股本是Flavors的17倍，年销售额是27倍；事实上仅三年前，Harvester的净利润还高于Flavors在1969年的全年销售额。这种巨大反差怎样形成？答案就在两个有魔力的词：盈利能力与增长。Flavors在两方面都表现非凡，Harvester则处处令人失望。

表18-5　第5组

The story is told in Table 18-5. Here we find Flavors with a sensational profit of 14.3% of sales (before income tax the figure was 23%), compared with a mere 2.6% for Harvester. Similarly, Flavors had earned 19.7% on its stock capital against an inadequate 5.5% earned by Harvester. In five years the net earnings of Flavors had nearly doubled, while those of Harvester practically stood still. Between 1969 and 1959 the comparison makes similar reading. These differences in performance produced a typical stock-market divergence in valuation. Flavors sold in 1969 at 55 times its last reported earnings, and Harvester at only 10.7 times. Correspondingly, Flavors was valued at 10.4 times its book value, while Harvester was selling at a 41% discount from its net worth.

sensational惊人的a mere仅仅inadequate不足的practically stood still几乎原地踏步makes similar reading读起来情况类似divergence in valuation估值上的分化Correspondingly相应地net worth净资产

表18-5讲清了这个故事。Flavors税前利润占销售额23%，税后仍达到惊人的14.3%，Harvester却只有2.6%；Flavors的股本回报率为19.7%，Harvester只有不足的5.5%。五年间Flavors净利润几乎翻倍，Harvester则基本停滞；把1969年与1959年相比，结论也相似。业绩差异带来了典型的股市估值分化：1969年Flavors按最近盈利55倍交易，Harvester只有10.7倍；Flavors为账面价值10.4倍，Harvester却比净资产折价41%。

COMMENT AND CONCLUSIONS: The first thing to remark is that the market success of Flavors was based entirely on the development of its central business, and involved none of the corporate wheeling and dealing, acquisition programs, top-heavy capitalization structures, and other familiar Wall Street practices of recent years. The company has stuck to its extremely profitable knitting, and that is virtually its whole story. The record of Harvester raises an entirely different set of questions, but these too have nothing to do with “high finance.” Why have so many great companies become relatively unprofitable even during many years of general prosperity? What is the advantage of doing more than $2½ billion of business if the enterprise cannot earn enough to justify the shareholders’ investment? It is not for us to prescribe the solution of this problem. But we insist that not only management but the rank and file of shareholders should be conscious that the problem exists and that it calls for the best brains and the best efforts possible to deal with it.* From the standpoint of common-stock selection, neither issue would have met our standards of sound, reasonably attractive, and moderately priced investment. Flavors was a typical brilliantly successful but lavishly valued company; Harvester’s showing was too mediocre to make it really attractive even at its discount price. (Undoubtedly there were better values available in the reasonably priced class.)

the first thing to remark首先要指出的wheeling and dealing钻营投机，纵横捭阖的交易top-heavy capitalization structures头重脚轻的资本结构（债务和优先证券过多）stuck to its extremely profitable knitting专注于本行（stick to one’s knitting 习语：只管自己的事）high finance高端金融运作（含贬义）prescribe the solution开出解决方案the rank and file of shareholders普通股东大众（rank and file 原指普通士兵）From the standpoint of从……的角度看lavishly valued估值过于慷慨的mediocre平庸的discount price折价

评论与结论：首先要指出，Flavors在市场上的成功完全来自核心业务的发展，没有借助公司间腾挪、收购计划、头重脚轻的资本结构或近年华尔街常见的其他手法。公司始终专注于自己利润极高的本行，这几乎就是全部故事。Harvester的记录提出的是完全不同的问题，但同样与“高级金融”无关：为什么许多大公司即使在整体繁荣的多年里仍变得相对缺乏利润？如果一家企业做着超过25亿美元的生意，却赚不到足以证明股东投入合理的利润，规模又有什么好处？我们不负责开出解决方案，但坚持认为，不仅管理层，普通股东也应意识到问题存在，并投入最优秀的人才与最大的努力加以解决。从普通股选择看，两只股票都不符合我们对稳健、相当有吸引力且价格适中的投资标准。Flavors是典型的经营极成功、估值却奢侈的公司；Harvester的表现又过于平庸，即使折价也不够吸引。（在合理定价一类中，无疑还有更好的选择。）

SEQUEL TO 1971: The low price of Harvester at the end of 1969 protected it from a large further decline in the bad break of 1970. It lost only 10% more. Flavors proved more vulnerable and declined to 45, a loss of 30%. In the subsequent recovery both advanced, well above their 1969 close, but Harvester soon fell back to the 25 level.

截至1971年的后续：Harvester在1969年末的低价使它在1970年大跌中免受更严重损失，之后只再跌10%。Flavors更脆弱，跌到45美元，损失30%。随后反弹中，两者都升到远高于1969年末的位置，但Harvester很快又回落到25美元附近。

Pair 6: McGraw Edison (Public Utility and Equipment; Housewares) McGraw-Hill, Inc. (Books, Films, Instruction Systems; Magazine and Newspaper Publishers; Information Services)

第六组：麦格劳·爱迪生公司（公用事业与设备；家用器具）与麦格劳-希尔公司（图书、影片、教学系统；杂志与报纸出版；信息服务）

This pair with so similar names—which at times we shall call Edison and Hill—are two large and successful enterprises in vastly different fields. We have chosen December 31, 1968, as the date of our comparison, developed in Table 18-6. The issues were selling at about the same price, but because of Hill’s larger capitalization it was valued at about twice the total figure of the other. This difference should appear somewhat surprising, since Edison had about 50% higher sales and one-quarter larger net earnings. As a result, we find that the key ratio—the multiplier of earnings—was more than twice as great for Hill as for Edison. This phenomenon seems explicable chiefly by the persistence of a strong enthusiasm and partiality exhibited by the market toward shares of book-publishing companies, several of which had been introduced to public trading in the later 1960s.*

vastly different fields截然不同的领域capitalization股本规模（发行在外的股份总额）one-quarter larger大四分之一the key ratio关键比率multiplier of earnings市盈率explicable可以解释的persistence持续存在partiality偏爱introduced to public trading上市（开始公开交易）

这两家名称如此相似的公司——下文有时简称Edison与Hill——实际上是在迥异领域经营的大型成功企业。我们选取1968年12月31日进行表18-6所示比较。两只股票价格约相同，但Hill股本较大，因此总市值约为Edison两倍。这看起来颇令人意外，因为Edison的销售额高约50%，净利润也高四分之一。结果是，关键比率即市盈率，Hill超过Edison两倍。主要解释似乎是市场长期热衷并偏爱图书出版公司；其中数家在20世纪60年代后期才上市交易。

Actually, by the end of 1968 it was evident that this enthusiasm had been overdone. The Hill shares had sold at 56 in 1967, more than 40 times the just-reported record earnings for 1966. But a small decline had appeared in 1967 and a further decline in 1968. Thus the current high multiplier of 35 was being applied to a company that had already shown two years of receding profits. Nonetheless the stock was still valued at more than eight times its tangible asset backing, indicating a good-will component of not far from a billion dollars! Thus the price seemed to illustrate—in Dr. Johnson’s famous phrase—“The triumph of hope over experience.”

overdone过头了just-reported刚刚公布的receding profits逐渐下降的利润tangible asset backing有形资产支撑good-will component商誉部分Dr. Johnson’s famous phrase约翰逊博士的名言（塞缪尔·约翰逊，18 世纪英国文人）The triumph of hope over experience希望战胜了经验（约翰逊评论丧偶者再婚的话）

事实上，到1968年末已经明显看出这种热情过头。Hill在1967年曾卖到56美元，是刚公布的1966年创纪录盈利的40多倍，但其利润1967年已有小幅下降，1968年又进一步下滑。也就是说，当时35倍的高市盈率被用在一家利润已连续两年倒退的公司上。即便如此，股价仍超过有形资产支撑的八倍，意味着商誉部分接近10亿美元！这个价格似乎正体现了约翰逊博士的名言：“希望战胜经验。”

SEQUEL TO EARLY 1971: The decline of McGraw-Hill’s earnings continued through 1969 and 1970, dropping to $1.02 and then to $.82 per share. In the May 1970 debacle its price suffered a devastating break to 10—less than a fifth of the figure two years before. It had a good recovery thereafter, but the high of 24 in May 1971 was still only 60% of the 1968 closing price. McGraw Edison gave a better account of itself—declining to 22 in 1970 and recovering fully to 41½ in May 1971.*

McGraw-Hill continues to be a strong and prosperous company. But its price history exemplifies—as do so many other cases—the speculative hazards in such stocks created by Wall Street through its undisciplined waves of optimism and pessimism.

McGraw-Hill依然是一家实力强、经营兴旺的公司。但它的股价史和许多其他案例一样，说明华尔街缺乏节制的一波波乐观与悲观，会在这类股票上制造巨大的投机风险。

Pair 7: National General Corp. (A Large Conglomerate) and National Presto Industries (Diverse Electric Appliances, Ordnance)

第七组：国民通用公司（大型企业集团）与国民普雷斯托工业公司（各类电器、军械）

These two companies invite comparison chiefly because they are so different. Let us call them “General” and “Presto.” We have selected the end of 1968 for our study, because the write-offs taken by General in 1969 made the figures for that year too ambiguous. The full flavor of General’s far-flung activities could not be savored the year before, but it was already conglomerate enough for anyone’s taste. The condensed description in the Stock Guide read “Nation-wide theatre chain; motion picture and TV production, savings and loan assn., book publishing.” To which could be added, then or later, “insurance, investment banking, records, music publishing, computerized services, real estate—and 35% of Performance Systems Inc. (name recently changed from Minnie Pearl’s Chicken System Inc.).” Presto had also followed a diversification program, but in comparison with General it was modest indeed. Starting as the leading maker of pressure cookers, it had branched out into various other household and electric appliances. Quite differently, also, it took on a number of ordnance contracts for the U.S. government.

这两家公司最值得比较之处，恰恰是差异巨大。下文简称General和Presto。我们选择1968年末研究，是因为General在1969年的减记让当年数据过于含混。此前一年还无法尽览General业务跨度的全部滋味，但已足够称得上多元化集团。《股票指南》的简述是：“全国连锁影院；电影及电视制作；储蓄贷款协会；图书出版。”当时或后来还可加上保险、投资银行、唱片、音乐出版、电脑服务、房地产，以及Performance Systems Inc.的35%权益——该公司刚由Minnie Pearl’s Chicken System Inc.改名。Presto也实行多元化，但相比General克制得多。它从压力锅龙头起家，扩展到其他家用和电器产品；另一个很不同的方向是承接若干美国政府军需合同。

Our Table 18-7 summarizes the showing of the companies at the end of 1968. The capital structure of Presto was as simple as it could be—nothing but 1,478,000 shares of common stock, selling in the market for $58 million. Contrastingly, General had more than twice as many shares of common, plus an issue of convertible preferred, plus three issues of stock warrants calling for a huge amount of common, plus a towering convertible bond issue (just given in exchange for stock of an insurance company), plus a goodly sum of nonconvertible bonds. All this added up to a market capitalization of $534 million, not counting an impending issue of convertible bonds, and $750 million, including such issue. Despite National General’s enormously greater capitalization, it had actually done considerably less gross business than Presto in their fiscal years, and it had shown only 75% of Presto’s net income.

表18-7概括了两家公司1968年末的状况。Presto的资本结构简单得不能再简单：只有1,478,000股普通股，总市值5,800万美元。General则有两倍以上的普通股，还发行可转换优先股、三批可认购大量普通股的认股权证、一大笔可转换债券（刚用来交换一家保险公司股票），以及不少不可转换债券。所有这些合计市值5.34亿美元，若计入即将发行的可转换债券则达7.5亿美元。尽管National General资本规模大得惊人，两家公司各自财年中，它的营业总额却明显低于Presto，净利润也只有Presto的75%。

The determination of the true market value of General’s common-stock capitalization presents an interesting problem for security analysts and has important implications for anyone interested in the stock on any basis more serious than outright gambling. The relatively small $4½ convertible preferred can be readily taken care of by assuming its conversion into common, when the latter sells at a suitable market level. This we have done in Table 18-7. But the warrants require different treatment. In calculating the “full dilution” basis the company assumes exercise of all the warrants, and the application of the proceeds to the retirement of debt, plus use of the balance to buy in common at the market. These assumptions actually produced virtually no effect on the earnings per share in calendar 1968—which were reported as $1.51 both before and after allowance for dilution. We consider this treatment illogical and unrealistic. As we see it, the warrants represent a part of the “common-stock package” and their market value is part of the “effective market value” of the common-stock part of the capital. (See our discussion of this point on p. 415 above.) This simple technique of adding the market price of the warrants to that of the common has a radical effect on the showing of National General at the end of 1968, as appears from the calculation in Table 18-7. In fact the “true market price” of the common stock turns out to be more than twice the quoted figure. Hence the true multiplier of the 1968 earnings is more than doubled—to the inherently absurd figure of 69 times. The total market value of the “common-stock equivalents” then becomes $413 million, which is over three times the tangible assets shown therefor.

如何确定General普通股资本的真实市值，是证券分析师很有意思的问题；对任何以严肃投资而非纯赌博为目的的人也很重要。规模较小、股息4.5美元的可转换优先股容易处理：普通股涨到合适水平时，假定其转换为普通股即可，表18-7就是这样做的。但认股权证应另行处理。公司计算“完全稀释”时，假定全部权证行使，所得资金用于偿债，余款再按市价回购普通股。这些假定对1968年每股盈利几乎没有影响，稀释前后都报告1.51美元。我们认为这种处理不合逻辑也不现实。权证是“普通股整体权益”的一部分，其市值也属于普通股资本的“实际市场价值”。因此，把权证市值直接加到普通股市值上，会彻底改变National General在1968年末的面貌：普通股的“真实市价”超过报价两倍，1968年盈利的真实倍数也翻倍到本质上荒谬的69倍；“普通股等价物”总市值达到4.13亿美元，是对应有形资产的三倍多。

译者补充（非原文）：假设普通股市值200万元、认股权证市值100万元，只看普通股会低估市场为整套普通股权益支付的价格。把两者合计为300万元，再与盈利比较，才更接近潜在稀释和权证价值共同造成的真实估值负担。

表18-7　第7组

These figures appear the more anomalous when comparison is made with those of Presto. One is moved to ask how could Presto possibly be valued at only 6.9 times its current earnings when the multiplier for General was nearly 10 times as great. All the ratios of Presto are quite satisfactory—the growth figure suspiciously so, in fact. By that we mean that the company was undoubtedly benefiting considerably from its war work, and the shareholders should be prepared for some falling off in profits under peacetime conditions. But, on balance, Presto met all the requirements of a sound and reasonably priced investment, while General had all the earmarks of a typical “conglomerate” of the late 1960s vintage, full of corporate gadgets and grandiose gestures, but lacking in substantial values behind the market quotations.

One is moved to ask how could Presto possibly be valued at only 6.9 times its current earnings when the multiplier for General was nearly 10 times as great.

人们不禁要问：General 的市盈率几乎是 Presto 的 10 倍，Presto 怎么可能只按当期收益的 6.9 倍估值？

One is moved to ask 意为“人不由得要问”（one 泛指任何人）。后面的间接疑问句保留了直接问句的倒装语序 how could Presto…，这是口语化写法；possibly 与 how could 连用加强“怎么可能”的语气。

与Presto对比，这些数字更显反常。人们不禁要问：General的市盈率接近Presto的十倍，Presto为何竟只值当期盈利的6.9倍？Presto各项比率都很令人满意，增长数据甚至好得可疑。我们是说，公司无疑从战时军需业务中获益不少，股东应准备好和平时期利润有所回落。但总体而言，Presto符合稳健且价格合理的投资全部条件；General则带着20世纪60年代末典型多元化集团的一切特征：公司工具花样繁多，姿态宏大，市价背后却缺乏扎实价值。

SEQUEL: General continued its diversification policy in 1969, with some increase in its debt. But it took a whopping write-off of millions, chiefly in the value of its investment in the Minnie Pearl Chicken deal. The final figures showed a loss of $72 million before tax credit and $46.4 million after tax credit. The price of the shares fell to 16½ in 1969 and as low as 9 in 1970 (only 15% of its 1968 high of 60). Earnings for 1970 were reported as $2.33 per share diluted, and the price recovered to 28½ in 1971. National Presto increased its per-share earnings somewhat in both 1969 and 1970, marking 10 years of uninterrupted growth of profits. Nonetheless its price declined to 21½ in the 1970 debacle. This was an interesting figure, since it was less than four times the last reported earnings, and less than the net current assets available for the stock at the time. Late in 1971 we find the price of National Presto 60% higher, at 34, but the ratios are still startling. The enlarged working capital is still about equal to the current price, which in turn is only 5½ times the last reported earnings. If the investor could now find ten such issues, for diversification, he could be confident of satisfactory results.*

后续：General在1969年继续多元化，债务也有所增加；但公司做了数千万美元的巨额减记，主要涉及Minnie Pearl炸鸡交易的投资价值。最终数据为税收抵免前亏损7,200万美元、抵免后亏损4,640万美元。股价1969年跌至16又1/2美元，1970年最低9美元，仅为1968年60美元高点的15%；1970年稀释后每股盈利报告为2.33美元，1971年股价回升到28又1/2美元。National Presto在1969和1970年每股盈利均略增，实现连续十年利润增长，但1970年崩盘中股价仍跌到21又1/2美元。这个价格很有意思：不到最近盈利的四倍，也低于当时归属于股票的净流动资产。1971年末National Presto升到34美元，涨60%，比率仍令人吃惊：扩大的营运资本仍约等于当前股价，股价又只有最近盈利的5.5倍。若投资者能找到十只这样的股票组成分散组合，就可有把握取得满意结果。

Pair 8: Whiting Corp. (Materials-Handling equipment) and Willcox & Gibbs (Small Conglomerate)

第八组：怀廷公司（物料搬运设备）与威尔科克斯-吉布斯公司（小型企业集团）

This pair are close but not touching neighbors on the American Stock Exchange list. The comparison—set forth in Table 18-8A—makes one wonder if Wall Street is a rational institution. The company with smaller sales and earnings, and with half the tangible assets for the common, sold at about four times the aggregate value of the other. The higher-valued company was about to report a large loss after special charges; it had not paid a dividend in thirteen years. The other had a long record of satisfactory earnings, had paid continuous dividends since 1936, and was currently returning one of the highest dividend yields in the entire common-stock list. To indicate more vividly the disparity in the performance of the two companies we append, in Table 18-8B, the earnings and price record for 1961–1970.

这两家公司在美国证券交易所名单上位置很近却并不紧挨。表18-8A的比较让人怀疑华尔街是否理性：销售和盈利较少、普通股对应有形资产只有另一家一半的公司，总市值却约为对方四倍。估值较高的公司即将报告扣除特别费用后的巨额亏损，并且十三年未派股息；另一家长期盈利令人满意，自1936年起持续派息，当时股息率还是整个普通股名单中最高的一批。为更生动展示两家公司表现差距，表18-8B附列了1961—1970年的盈利与股价记录。

The history of the two companies throws an interesting light on the development of medium-sized businesses in this country, in contrast with much larger-sized companies that have mainly appeared in these pages. Whiting was incorporated in 1896, and thus goes back at least 75 years. It seems to have kept pretty faithfully to its materials-handling business and has done quite well with it over the decades. Willcox & Gibbs goes back even farther—to 1866—and was long known in its industry as a prominent maker of industrial sewing machines. During the past decade it adopted a policy of diversification in what seems a rather outlandish form. For on the one hand it has an extraordinarily large number of subsidiary companies (at least 24), making an astonishing variety of products, but on the other hand the entire conglomeration adds up to mighty small potatoes by usual Wall Street standards.

throws an interesting light on有助于说明，揭示medium-sized中等规模的incorporated注册成立kept pretty faithfully to相当忠实地坚守industrial sewing machines工业缝纫机outlandish古怪的，离奇的For on the one hand因为一方面（For＝because，引出解释）subsidiary companies子公司mighty small potatoes微不足道的小东西（small potatoes 习语；mighty 口语＝very）

For on the one hand it has an extraordinarily large number of subsidiary companies (at least 24), making an astonishing variety of products, but on the other hand the entire conglomeration adds up to mighty small potatoes by usual Wall Street standards.

因为一方面，它拥有数量多得出奇的子公司（至少 24 家），生产的产品种类令人咋舌；另一方面，按华尔街通常的标准，整个大杂烩加起来却小得可怜。

句首的 For 是连词，相当于 because，解释上一句所说的“古怪”。small potatoes 是美式习语，指“无足轻重的小东西”；mighty 在此是口语副词，等于 very。

两家公司的历史很好地说明了美国中型企业的发展，与本书前面主要出现的大公司形成对照。Whiting创立于1896年，至少已有75年历史；它似乎相当忠实地坚守物料搬运业务，几十年来经营颇佳。Willcox & Gibbs历史更久，可追溯到1866年，长期是行业内著名的工业缝纫机制造商。过去十年它采取了一种颇古怪的多元化政策：一方面拥有异常多的子公司，至少24家，产品种类多得惊人；另一方面，按华尔街通常标准，整个集团加起来却仍小得可怜。

The earnings developments in Whiting are rather characteristic of our business concerns. The figures show steady and rather spectacular growth from 41 cents a share in 1960 to $3.63 in 1968. But they carried no assurance that such growth must continue indefinitely. The subsequent decline to only $1.77 for the 12 months ended January 1971 may have reflected nothing more than the slowing down of the general economy. But the stock price reacted in severe fashion, falling about 60% from its 1968 high (43½) to the close of 1969. Our analysis would indicate that the shares represented a sound and attractive secondary-issue investment—suitable for the enterprising investor as part of a group of such commitments.

characteristic of……的典型特征business concerns企业（concern＝公司）carried no assurance并不能保证indefinitely无限期地in severe fashion剧烈地secondary-issue二线股（非龙头公司的股票）commitments投入的头寸（本书常用）

Whiting的盈利变化很有美国企业的典型性：从1960年每股0.41美元稳步而显著地增长到1968年的3.63美元，但这并不保证增长会永远持续。到1971年1月止十二个月，每股盈利降到1.77美元，或许只是整体经济放缓的反映；股价反应却很剧烈，从1968年43又1/2美元高点到1969年末下跌约60%。我们的分析认为，这只股票属于稳健而有吸引力的二线股投资，适合进取型投资者把它作为一组同类持仓中的一项。

SEQUEL: Willcox & Gibbs showed a small operating loss for 1970. Its price declined drastically to a low of 4½, recovering in typical fashion to 9½ in February 1971. It would be hard to justify that price statistically. Whiting had a relatively small decline, to 16 3/4 in 1970. (At that price it was selling at just about the current assets alone available for the shares). Its earnings held at $1.85 per share to July 1971. In early 1971 the price advanced to 24½, which seemed reasonable enough but no longer a “bargain” by our standards.*

后续：Willcox & Gibbs在1970年出现小额经营亏损，股价剧跌至4又1/2美元，1971年2月又以典型方式回升到9又1/2美元。从统计数据很难为这一价格辩护。Whiting跌幅相对较小，1970年降至16又3/4美元；在这个价位，仅归属于股票的流动资产就大致等于股价。到1971年7月，每股盈利维持在1.85美元。1971年初股价涨到24又1/2美元，尚算合理，但按我们的标准已不再是“便宜货”。

General Observations

总体观察

The issues used in these comparisons were selected with some malice aforethought, and thus they cannot be said to present a random cross-section of the common-stock list. Also they are limited to the industrial section, and the important areas of public utilities, transportation companies, and financial enterprises do not appear. But they vary sufficiently in size, lines of business, and qualitative and quantitative aspects to convey a fair idea of the choices confronting an investor in common stocks.

with some malice aforethought带着几分“预谋”（malice aforethought 是法律术语“预谋恶意”，此处幽默自嘲）random cross-section随机的横截面样本qualitative and quantitative aspects定性与定量方面convey a fair idea让人大致了解confronting摆在……面前的

这些对比案例是我们有意挑选的，因此不能说是普通股名单的随机截面；它们也只限于工业企业，没有涵盖重要的公用事业、运输公司和金融企业。不过，这些公司在规模、业务类型及定性和定量特征上差异足够大，仍能相当真实地反映普通股投资者面对的选择。

The relationship between price and indicated value has also differed greatly from one case to another. For the most part the companies with better growth records and higher profitability have sold at higher multipliers of current earnings—which is logical enough in general. Whether the specific differentials in price/earnings ratios are “justified” by the facts—or will be vindicated by future developments—cannot be answered with confidence. On the other hand we do have quite a few instances here in which a worthwhile judgment can be reached. These include virtually all the cases where there has been great market activity in companies of questionable underlying soundness. Such stocks not only were speculative—which means inherently risky—but a good deal of the time they were and are obviously overvalued. Other issues appeared to be worth more than their price, being affected by the opposite sort of market attitude—which we might call “underspeculation”—or by undue pessimism because of a shrinkage in earnings.

indicated value推算出的价值For the most part大体上differentials差异，差距vindicated被证明正确questionable underlying soundness基本面可疑的稳健性inherently risky本质上有风险的a good deal of the time很多时候underspeculation投机不足（作者自创词，与“过度投机”相对）undue pessimism过度悲观

各案例中价格与指示价值的关系也差别很大。通常，增长记录较好、盈利能力较强的公司会以更高的当前市盈率交易，这在总体上合乎逻辑。但具体市盈率差距是否得到事实“证明”，或将由未来发展证明合理，无法有把握回答。另一方面，本章确有不少案例可以作出有价值的判断，尤其是那些基本面可靠性可疑、市场活动却极其活跃的公司。这些股票不仅具有投机性，也就是内在风险高，而且经常明显估值过高。另一些股票则似乎价值高于价格，却受市场相反态度——可称为“投机不足”——影响，或因盈利萎缩而遭过度悲观看待。

译者补充（非原文）：“投机不足”不是说股票毫无风险，而是市场关注过少或悲观过度，使价格可能低于保守估算的价值。能否成为投资机会，仍要检查财务实力、盈利稳定性和分散程度。

In studying the stock list for the material in this chapter, we were impressed once again by the wide difference between the usual objectives of security analysis and those we deem dependable and rewarding. Most security analysts try to select the issues that will give the best account of themselves in the future, in terms chiefly of market action but considering also the development of earnings. We are frankly skeptical as to whether this can be done with satisfactory results. Our preference for the analyst’s work would be rather that he should seek the exceptional or minority cases in which he can form a reasonably confident judgment that the price is well below value. He should be able to do this work with sufficient expertness to produce satisfactory average results over the years.

were impressed once again by再次深切感受到deem认为dependable and rewarding可靠且有回报的give the best account of themselves表现最好market action市场表现（股价走势）frankly skeptical坦率地说持怀疑态度well below value远低于价值expertness专业能力

为本章研究股票名单时，我们再次深切感受到：证券分析通常追求的目标，与我们认为可靠且有回报的目标差异很大。多数分析师试图挑出未来表现最好的股票，主要看市场走势，也考虑盈利发展。我们坦率怀疑这种做法能否取得满意结果。我们更希望分析师寻找少数特殊案例，在其中能够相当有把握地判断价格远低于价值；并且应以足够专业的方式完成这项工作，使多年平均结果令人满意。

Talk about “almost unheard of in the annals of serious stock-market valuations”! H & R Block remains a publicly-traded company, while Blue Bell was taken private in 1984 at $47.50 per share.
“接近30倍”对应表18-4“比率”部分“价格/账面价值”的2920%。若看到1999年末和2000年初许多高科技公司按资产价值数百倍交易，格雷厄姆恐怕会惊讶地摇头——真称得上“严肃股市估值史上几乎闻所未闻”。H&R Block仍是上市公司；Blue Bell于1984年以每股47.50美元私有化。
* Graham is alerting readers to a form of the “gambler’s fallacy,” in which investors believe that an overvalued stock must drop in price purely because it is overvalued. Just as a coin does not become more likely to turn up heads after landing on tails for nine times in a row, so an overvalued stock (or stock market!) can stay overvalued for a surprisingly long time. That makes short-selling, or betting that stocks will drop, too risky for mere mortals.
格雷厄姆是在提醒读者提防一种“赌徒谬误”：投资者以为股票只因估值过高就必然下跌。就像硬币连续九次出现反面，并不会让下一次出现正面的概率更高，估值过高的股票乃至整个市场也可能长期维持高估。这使做空——押注股价下跌——对普通人风险过大。
† International Harvester was the heir to McCormick Harvesting Machine Co., the manufacturer of the McCormick reaper that helped make the midwestern states the “breadbasket of the world.” But International Harvester fell on hard times in the 1970s and, in 1985, sold its farm-equipment business to Tenneco. After changing its name to Navistar, the remaining company was booted from the Dow in 1991 (although it remains a member of the S & P 500 index). International Flavors & Fragrances, also a constituent of the S & P 500, had a total stock-market value of $3 billion in early 2003, versus $1.6 billion for Navistar.
International Harvester承继自McCormick Harvesting Machine Co.；后者制造的麦考密克收割机帮助美国中西部成为“世界粮仓”。International Harvester在20世纪70年代陷入困境，1985年将农机业务出售给Tenneco；余下公司更名Navistar，1991年被剔除出道琼斯指数，但仍留在标准普尔500指数。International Flavors & Fragrances也属于标普500；2003年初总市值约30亿美元，Navistar约16亿美元。
* For more of Graham’s thoughts on shareholder activism, see the commentary on Chapter 19. In criticizing Harvester for its refusal to maximize shareholder value, Graham uncannily anticipated the behavior of the company’s future management. In 2001, a majority of shareholders voted to remove Navistar’s restrictions against outside takeover bids—but the board of directors simply refused to implement the shareholders’ wishes. It’s remarkable that an antidemocratic tendency in the culture of some companies can endure for decades.
关于格雷厄姆对股东行动主义的更多看法，参见第19章评论。他批评Harvester拒绝最大化股东价值，竟预示了未来管理层的行为。2001年，多数股东投票要求取消Navistar对外部收购要约的限制，董事会却直接拒绝执行股东意愿。某些公司的反民主文化能延续数十年，令人惊讶。
* McGraw-Hill remains a publicly-traded company that owns, among other operations, BusinessWeek magazine and Standard & Poor’s Corp. McGraw–Edison is now a division of Cooper Industries.
McGraw-Hill仍是上市公司，旗下业务包括《商业周刊》和Standard & Poor’s Corp.。McGraw-Edison现为Cooper Industries的一个部门。
* In “the May 1970 debacle” that Graham refers to, the U.S. stock market lost 5.5%. From the end of March to the end of June 1970, the S & P 500 index lost 19% of its value, one of the worst three-month returns on record.
格雷厄姆所说的“1970年5月崩盘”期间，美国股市下跌5.5%。从1970年3月底到6月底，标准普尔500指数损失19%，是有记录以来最差的三个月回报之一。
* National Presto remains a publicly-traded company. National General was acquired in 1974 by another controversial conglomerate, American Financial Group, which at various times has had interests in cable television, banking, real estate, mutual funds, insurance, and bananas. AFG is also the final resting place of some of the assets of Penn Central Corp. (see Chapter 17).
National Presto仍是上市公司。National General于1974年被另一家颇具争议的多元化集团American Financial Group收购；后者不同时期涉足有线电视、银行、房地产、共同基金、保险乃至香蕉。Penn Central Corp.的部分资产最终也归入AFG，参见第17章。
* Whiting Corp. ended up a subsidiary of Wheelabrator-Frye, but was taken private in 1983. Willcox & Gibbs is now owned by Group Rexel, an electrical-equipment manufacturer that is a division of Pinault-Printemps-Redoute Group of France. Rexel’s shares trade on the Paris Stock Exchange.
Whiting Corp.最终成为Wheelabrator-Frye的子公司，并于1983年私有化。Willcox & Gibbs现归Group Rexel所有；Rexel是法国Pinault-Printemps-Redoute Group旗下的电气设备制造商，其股票在巴黎证券交易所交易。

Endnotes · 尾注（本杰明·格雷厄姆）

1. The reader will recall from p. 434 above that AAA Enterprises tried to enter this business, but quickly failed. Here Graham is making a profound and paradoxical observation: The more money a company makes, the more likely it is to face new competition, since its high returns signal so clearly that easy money is to be had. The new competition, in turn, will lead to lower prices and smaller profits. This crucial point was overlooked by overenthusiastic Internet stock buyers, who believed that early winners would sustain their advantage indefinitely.
读者会记得，前文第434页提到AAA Enterprises曾试图进入这项业务，却迅速失败。格雷厄姆在此提出一个深刻而矛盾的观察：一家公司越赚钱，就越可能招来新竞争者，因为高回报清楚表明有容易赚的钱；新竞争又会带来更低价格和更少利润。过度热衷互联网股票的买家忽略了这一关键点，他们以为早期赢家能永久保持优势。

CHAPTER 19

股东与管理层：股息政策

Shareholders and Managements: Dividend Policy

管理层的资本配置与股息政策，怎样影响股东的实际权益？

独立精读增强版：保留英文原文、段落 ID、词汇提示、长难句、图片及注释结构；新增完整中文译文。扩展解释均标注“译者补充（非原文）”。

Chapter 19Shareholders and Managements: Dividend Policy第19章 股东与管理层：股息政策

本章导读格雷厄姆在这一章处理两个相关的问题：股东应当怎样对待管理层，以及公司应当怎样分配利润。第一部分他先承认失败：自 1934 年起他就呼吁股东对管理层采取更聪明、更有力的态度——可 36 年来股东群体几乎什么都没做成。真正“救场”的是一个外来因素：收购（take-over bids）。管理差导致股价低，低股价吸引想要多元化的公司或进取的个人前来收购，董事会因此被“敲打”得更在意自己挑选优秀高管的基本职责。他的结论很冷峻：差劲的管理层几乎从来不是被公众股东改变的，而是被某个个人或紧密团体夺取控制权之后才更换的；他只保留一个请求：认真阅读其他股东寄来的代理投票材料。第二部分谈股息。过去股东要求多分红、管理层想留存利润；如今投资者的态度在变，成长型公司少分红甚至不分红也能享有高股价，而 AT&T 与 IBM 的对比说明市场对此仍未形成定论。格雷厄姆的立场是：股东有权要求管理层要么正常派息（大约三分之二的盈利），要么明确证明留存利润确实提高了每股盈利；平庸公司以“扩张”为名压低股息，表面上就不合逻辑。最后一节区分股票分割和真正意义上的股票股息（后者是对近期再投资利润的凭证，纽交所以 25% 为分界线），并主张公用事业公司用定期的股票股息取代“先派现金股息、再向股东配股”的做法，因为后者让股东为实际上没拿到手的钱多缴了一道所得税。

Ever since 1934 we have argued in our writings for a more intelligent and energetic attitude by shareholders toward their managements. We have asked them to take a generous attitude toward those who are demonstrably doing a good job. We have asked them also to demand clear and satisfying explanations when the results appear to be worse than they should be, and to support movements to improve or remove clearly unproductive managements. Shareholders are justified in raising questions as to the competence of the management when the results (1) are unsatisfactory in themselves, (2) are poorer than those obtained by other companies that appear similarly situated, and (3) have resulted in an unsatisfactory market price of long duration.

managements管理层（本书中常用复数，指各公司的管理层）demonstrably明显地，可以证明地remove撤换（管理层）unproductive不出成果的，无能的are justified in有充分理由……competence能力，胜任程度similarly situated处境相似的of long duration持续很长时间的

自1934年以来，我们一直主张股东以更明智、积极的态度对待管理层：对确实做得好的人应宽厚；结果明显不如应有水平时，应要求清楚而令人满意的解释；对明显无能的管理层，应支持改进或撤换。若结果本身不理想、差于处境相似的公司，且长期造成不满意市价，股东有理由质疑管理能力。

In the last 36 years practically nothing has actually been accomplished through intelligent action by the great body of shareholders. A sensible crusader—if there are any such—would take this as a sign that he has been wasting his time, and that he had better give up the fight. As it happens our cause has not been lost; it has been rescued by an extraneous development—known as takeovers, or take-over bids.* We said in Chapter 8 that poor managements produce poor market prices. The low market prices, in turn, attract the attention of companies interested in diversifying their operations—and these are now legion. Innumerable such acquisitions have been accomplished by agreement with the existing managements, or else by accumulation of shares in the market and by offers made over the head of those in control. The price bid has usually been within the range of the value of the enterprise under reasonably competent management. Hence, in many cases, the inert public shareholder has been bailed out by the actions of “outsiders”—who at times may be enterprising individuals or groups acting on their own.

the great body of……的绝大多数，……的主体crusader为理想而奋斗的斗士（原指十字军战士）As it happens碰巧，事实上extraneous外来的，与本题无关的take-over bids收购要约diversifying their operations使业务多元化legion为数众多（these are now legion：这类公司如今多如牛毛）accumulation of shares（在市场上）逐步吸纳股份over the head of越过……（直接向股东发出要约，绕开管理层）The price bid出价（bid 是过去分词作后置定语，修饰 price）inert惰性的，不作为的bailed out被解救，被救出困境

过去36年，广大股东的明智行动几乎一事无成。理性的改革者也许应认定自己浪费时间、放弃斗争。可我们的事业被一个外来发展救了：收购或收购要约。第8章说，差管理造成低市价；低价又吸引无数寻求多元化的公司。大量收购或与原管理层协商完成，或在市场累积股份并越过控制人直接出价。报价通常接近企业在合理胜任管理下的价值。于是许多消极公众股东被“外来者”解救，有时是自行行动的积极个人或团体。

It can be stated as a rule with very few exceptions that poor managements are not changed by action of the “public stockholders,” but only by the assertion of control by an individual or compact group. This is happening often enough these days to put the management, including the board of directors, of a typical publicly controlled company on notice that if its operating results and the resulting market price are highly unsatisfactory, it may become the target of a successful take-over move. As a consequence, boards of directors have probably become more alive than previously to their fundamental duty to see that their company has a satisfactory top management. Many more changes of presidents have been seen in recent years than formerly.

This is happening often enough these days to put the management, including the board of directors, of a typical publicly controlled company on notice that if its operating results and the resulting market price are highly unsatisfactory, it may become the target of a successful take-over move.

如今这种事发生得已经够频繁，足以让一家典型的公众控股公司的管理层（包括董事会）明白：如果它的经营业绩以及由此形成的市场价格非常令人不满，它就可能成为一次成功收购行动的目标。

骨架是 often enough … to put X on notice that …（频繁到足以警告 X……）。X 是 the management … of a typical publicly controlled company，中间被插入语 including the board of directors 隔开；that 引导的从句才是“警告”的具体内容。

几乎没有例外的规则是：差管理层不会被公众股东行动替换，只会被个人或紧密团体取得控制权替换。这种事已足够常见，让公众持股公司管理层和董事会明白：经营结果及市价严重不佳，就可能成为成功收购目标。因此董事会大概比过去更警觉于基本职责，即确保公司有满意的最高管理层；近年更换总裁明显增多。

Not all companies in the unsatisfactory class have benefited from such developments. Also, the change has often occurred after a long period of bad results without remedial action, and has depended on enough disappointed shareholders selling out at low prices to permit the energetic outsiders to acquire a controlling position in the shares. But the idea that public shareholders could really help themselves by supporting moves for improving management and management policies has proved too quixotic to warrant further space in this book. Those individual shareholders who have enough gumption to make their presence felt at annual meetings—generally a completely futile performance—will not need our counsel on what points to raise with the managements. For others the advice would probably be wasted. Nevertheless, let us close this section with the plea that shareholders consider with an open mind and with careful attention any proxy material sent them by fellow-shareholders who want to remedy an obviously unsatisfactory management situation in the company.

remedial action补救措施controlling position控股地位quixotic堂吉诃德式的，不切实际的warrant further space值得再花篇幅gumption魄力，胆识make their presence felt让人感到自己的存在，发出自己的声音annual meetings股东年会futile徒劳的counsel建议，忠告（名词）plea恳请proxy material代理投票材料（公司或股东寄给全体股东、征集投票委托的文件）

But the idea that public shareholders could really help themselves by supporting moves for improving management and management policies has proved too quixotic to warrant further space in this book.

但是，“公众股东可以通过支持改进管理层和管理政策的行动来真正帮助自己”这一想法，已被证明过于堂吉诃德式的不切实际，不值得在本书中再花篇幅讨论。

主语是 the idea 加上一个很长的同位语从句 that public shareholders … policies，谓语是 has proved；too … to … 表示“太……以致不能……”。quixotic 来自《堂吉诃德》，指理想化而不切实际。

并非所有不满意公司都受益，变革也常在多年糟糕且无人补救后才发生，还要等足够多失望股东低价卖出，让外来者取得控制权。公众股东靠支持改进管理与政策来自救，已被证明太像堂吉诃德，不值得本书再占篇幅。敢在年会发声的人通常也不需要我们指导，其他人听了多半无用。不过仍请股东以开放心态认真阅读同为股东者寄来的代理材料，尤其对方想纠正明显不良管理时。

Shareholders and Dividend Policy

股东与股息政策

In the past the dividend policy was a fairly frequent subject of argument between public, or “minority,” shareholders and managements. In general these shareholders wanted more liberal dividends, while the managements preferred to keep the earnings in the business “to strengthen the company.” They asked the shareholders to sacrifice their present interests for the good of the enterprise and for their own future long-term benefit. But in recent years the attitude of investors toward dividends has been undergoing a gradual but significant change. The basic argument now for paying small rather than liberal dividends is not that the company “needs” the money, but rather that it can use it to the shareholders’ direct and immediate advantage by retaining the funds for profitable expansion. Years ago it was typically the weak company that was more or less forced to hold on to its profits, instead of paying out the usual 60% to 75% of them in dividends. The effect was almost always adverse to the market price of the shares. Nowadays it is quite likely to be a strong and growing enterprise that deliberately keeps down its dividend payments, with the approval of investors and speculators alike.*

minority少数股东的（指不掌握控制权的公众股东）liberal dividends慷慨的股息（liberal 此处不是“自由的”）for the good of为了……的利益direct and immediate advantage直接而立即的好处retaining the funds留存资金more or less或多或少，多少有点hold on to留住，不放手paying out派发（股息）adverse to不利于deliberately故意地，有意地keeps down压低alike（investors and speculators alike）投资者和投机者都一样

The basic argument now for paying small rather than liberal dividends is not that the company “needs” the money, but rather that it can use it to the shareholders’ direct and immediate advantage by retaining the funds for profitable expansion.

如今主张少派而不是多派股息的基本理由，已不是公司“需要”这笔钱，而是公司把资金留下来用于有利可图的扩张，能让股东直接、立即受益。

not that … but rather that … 是“不是因为……而是因为……”的并列表语从句结构；argument for doing 指“支持做某事的理由”；to someone’s advantage 意为“对某人有利”。

过去，公众或少数股东常与管理层争论股息政策。股东想多分红，管理层想留存盈利“增强公司”，要求股东为企业和自己的长期利益牺牲眼前利益。近年态度逐渐而显著改变。少分红的基本理由不再是公司“需要”钱，而是留存资金可用于有利扩张，直接、立即造福股东。早年通常是弱公司被迫留住利润，不能按惯例派60%至75%，股价几乎总受损；如今反而常是强劲成长企业主动压低股息，投资者与投机者都赞同。

There was always a strong theoretical case for reinvesting profits in the business where such retention could be counted on to produce a goodly increase in earnings. But there were several strong counter-arguments, such as: The profits “belong” to the shareholders, and they are entitled to have them paid out within the limits of prudent management; many of the shareholders need their dividend income to live on; the earnings they receive in dividends are “real money,” while those retained in the company may or may not show up later as tangible values for the shareholders. These counter-arguments were so compelling, in fact, that the stock market showed a persistent bias in favor of the liberal dividend payers as against the companies that paid no dividends or relatively small ones.1

theoretical case理论上的理由（case 此处指论据）goodly相当大的are entitled to有权prudent审慎的tangible values有形的、实实在在的价值compelling有说服力的persistent bias in favor of持续偏爱as against相对于，与……相比

若留存利润可可靠地显著提高盈利，理论上再投资一直有力；反面理由也很强：利润“属于”股东，谨慎经营范围内应付给他们；许多股东靠股息生活；收到的股息是“真金白银”，留在公司的利润以后未必变成股东可见价值。这些理由强到使市场长期偏爱慷慨派息者，冷落不派或少派者。

In the last 20 years the “profitable reinvestment” theory has been gaining ground. The better the past record of growth, the readier investors and speculators have become to accept a low-pay-out policy. So much is this true that in many cases of growth favorites the dividend rate—or even the absence of any dividend—has seemed to have virtually no effect on the market price.*

gaining ground逐渐得势，越来越被接受the readier越乐意（the + 比较级……the + 比较级 结构）low-pay-out policy低派息政策growth favorites受追捧的成长股

So much is this true that in many cases of growth favorites the dividend rate—or even the absence of any dividend—has seemed to have virtually no effect on the market price.

这一点如此明显，以至于在许多受追捧的成长股身上，股息率——甚至完全不派股息——似乎对市价几乎毫无影响。

So much is this true that … 是把 this is so much true that … 中的 so much 提前造成的倒装，强调“程度之深”；破折号里的 or even the absence of any dividend 是对主语 the dividend rate 的补充。

过去二十年，“有利可图的再投资”理论日益占上风。历史增长越好，投资者越愿接受低派息；很多热门成长股的股息率甚至完全不派息，似乎也几乎不影响市价。

A striking example of this development is found in the history of Texas Instruments, Incorporated. The price of its common stock rose from 5 in 1953 to 256 in 1960, while earnings were advancing from 43 cents to $3.91 per share and while no dividend of any kind was paid. (In 1962 cash dividends were initiated, but by that year the earnings had fallen to $2.14 and the price had shown a spectacular drop to a low of 49.)

striking引人注目的Texas Instruments德州仪器（美国半导体公司）advancing上涨（本书常用）initiated开始（首次派发）spectacular drop惊人的下跌

德州仪器是突出例子。普通股从1953年5美元涨到1960年256美元，每股盈利从43美分升到3.91美元，期间完全不派股息。（1962年开始现金派息，但盈利已降至2.14美元，股价也惊人地跌到49美元低点。）

Another extreme illustration is provided by Superior Oil. In 1948 the company reported earnings of $35.26 per share, paid $3 in dividends, and sold as high as 235. In 1953 the dividend was reduced to $1, but the high price was 660. In 1957 it paid no dividend at all, and sold at 2,000! This unusual issue later declined to 795 in 1962, when it earned $49.50 and paid $7.50.*

illustration例证sold as high as最高卖到（股价最高达到）issue股票（本书中 issue 常作此义）declined下跌

更极端的是苏必利尔石油。1948年每股盈利35.26美元，派3美元，最高235；1953年股息减至1美元，最高却660；1957年不派股息，竟涨到2000！后来1962年跌到795，当年盈利49.50美元、股息7.50美元。

Investment sentiment is far from crystallized in this matter of dividend policy of growth companies. The conflicting views are well illustrated by the cases of two of our very largest corporations—American Telephone & Telegraph and International Business Machines. American Tel. & Tel. came to be regarded as an issue with good growth possibilities, as shown by the fact that in 1961 it sold at 25 times that year’s earnings. Nevertheless, the company’s cash dividend policy has remained an investment and speculative consideration of first importance, its quotation making an active response to even rumors of an impending increase in the dividend rate. On the other hand, comparatively little attention appears to have been paid to the cash dividend on IBM, which in 1960 yielded only 0.5% at the high price of the year and 1.5% at the close of 1970. (But in both cases stock splits have operated as a potent stock-market influence.)

The market’s appraisal of cash-dividend policy appears to be developing in the following direction: Where prime emphasis is not placed on growth the stock is rated as an “income issue,” and the dividend rate retains its long-held importance as the prime determinant of market price. At the other extreme, stocks clearly recognized to be in the rapid-growth category are valued primarily in terms of the expected growth rate over, say, the next decade, and the cash-dividend rate is more or less left out of the reckoning.

While the above statement may properly describe present tendencies, it is by no means a clear-cut guide to the situation in all common stocks, and perhaps not in the majority of them. For one thing, many companies occupy an intermediate position between growth and nongrowth enterprises. It is hard to say how much importance should be ascribed to the growth factor in such cases, and the market’s view thereof may change radically from year to year. Secondly, there seems to be something paradoxical about requiring the companies showing slower growth to be more liberal with their cash dividends. For these are generally the less prosperous concerns, and in the past the more prosperous the company the greater was the expectation of both liberal and increasing payments.

A niggardly policy has often been imposed on a company because its financial position is relatively weak, and it has needed all or most of its earnings (plus depreciation charges) to pay debts and bolster its working-capital position. When this is so there is not much the shareholders can say about it—except perhaps to criticize the management for permitting the company to fall into such an unsatisfactory financial position. However, dividends are sometimes held down by relatively unprosperous companies for the declared purpose of expanding the business. We feel that such a policy is illogical on its face, and should require both a complete explanation and a convincing defense before the shareholders should accept it. In terms of the past record there is no reason a priori to believe that the owners will benefit from expansion moves undertaken with their money by a business showing mediocre results and continuing its old management.

Stock Dividends and Stock Splits

股票股息与股票分割

It is important that investors understand the essential difference between a stock dividend (properly so-called) and a stock split. The latter represents a restatement of the common-stock structure—in a typical case by issuing two or three shares for one. The new shares are not related to specific earnings reinvested in a specific past period. Its purpose is to establish a lower market price for the single shares, presumably because such lower price range would be more acceptable to old and new shareholders. A stock split may be carried out by what technically may be called a stock dividend, which involves a transfer of sums from earned surplus to capital account; or else by a change in par value, which does not affect the surplus account.*

stock dividend股票股息（以股票形式派发的股息）properly so-called名副其实的，严格意义上的stock split股票分割，拆股restatement重新表述，重新安排presumably大概，据推测earned surplus留存盈余（未分配利润的旧称）capital account股本账户par value面值

投资者必须理解真正股票股利与拆股的根本差别。拆股只是重述普通股结构，典型是一股变两三股；新股不对应过去某段时期特定留存盈利，目的是把单股市价降到新老股东更易接受的区间。技术上可用股票股利完成，把盈余转入资本账户；也可改变面值，不影响盈余账户。

What we should call a proper stock dividend is one that is paid to shareholders to give them a tangible evidence or representation of specific earnings which have been reinvested in the business for their account over some relatively short period in the recent past—say, not more than the two preceding years. It is now approved practice to value such a stock dividend at the approximate value at the time of declaration, and to transfer an amount equal to such value from earned surplus to capital accounts. Thus the amount of a typical stock dividend is relatively small—in most cases not more than 5%. In essence a stock dividend of this sort has the same overall effect as the payment of an equivalent amount of cash out of earnings when accompanied by the sale of additional shares of like total value to the shareholders. However, a straight stock dividend has an important tax advantage over the otherwise equivalent combination of cash dividends with stock subscription rights, which is the almost standard practice for public-utility companies.

真正的股票股利，应给股东一项有形凭证，代表近期较短时期（比如不超过两年）替他们留在公司再投资的特定盈利。认可做法是按宣告时近似价值计量，把等额数从留存盈余转入资本账户。因此典型股票股利较小，多数不超过5%。本质上，它与公司先从盈利付等额现金、再向股东出售同等总值新股的总体效果相同，但相比现金股息加认股权，纯股票股利有重要税收优势；后者是公用事业常见做法。

The New York Stock Exchange has set the figure of 25% as a practical dividing line between stock splits and stock dividends. Those of 25% or more need not be accompanied by the transfer of their market value from earned surplus to capital, and so forth.† Some companies, especially banks, still follow the old practice of declaring any kind of stock dividend they please—e.g., one of 10%, not related to recent earnings—and these instances maintain an undesirable confusion in the financial world.

We have long been a strong advocate of a systematic and clearly enunciated policy with respect to the payment of cash and stock dividends. Under such a policy, stock dividends are paid periodically to capitalize all or a stated portion of the earnings reinvested in the business. Such a policy—covering 100% of the reinvested earnings—has been followed by Purex, Government Employees Insurance, and perhaps a few others.*

Stock dividends of all types seem to be disapproved of by most academic writers on the subject. They insist that they are nothing but pieces of paper, that they give the shareholders nothing they did not have before, and that they entail needless expense and inconvenience.† On our side we consider this a completely doctrinaire view, which fails to take into account the practical and psychological realities of investment. True, a periodic stock dividend—say of 5%—changes only the “form” of the owners’ investment. He has 105 shares in place of 100; but without the stock dividend the original 100 shares would have represented the same ownership interest now embodied in his 105 shares. Nonetheless, the change of form is actually one of real importance and value to him. If he wishes to cash in his share of the reinvested profits he can do so by selling the new certificate sent him, instead of having to break up his original certificate. He can count on receiving the same cash-dividend rate on 105 shares as formerly on his 100 shares; a 5% rise in the cash-dividend rate without the stock dividend would not be nearly as probable.*

多数研究该问题的学者似乎反对一切股票股利，认为只是纸片，没给股东原先没有的东西，还带来不必要成本和麻烦。我们认为这是脱离实际的教条，忽视投资的现实与心理。定期5%股票股利确实只改变投资“形式”：100股变105股，所有权未变；但形式变化对股东有真实价值。若想兑现留存利润份额，可卖新证书，不必拆开原证书；还可期待105股继续按原每股现金股息派发，而100股现金股息直接提高5%的可能性没那么高。

The advantages of a periodic stock-dividend policy are most evident when it is compared with the usual practice of the public-utility companies of paying liberal cash dividends and then taking back a good part of this money from the shareholders by selling them additional stock (through subscription rights).† As we mentioned above, the shareholders would find themselves in exactly the same position if they received stock dividends in lieu of the popular combination of cash dividends followed by stock subscriptions—except that they would save the income tax otherwise paid on the cash dividends. Those who need or wish the maximum annual cash income, with no additional stock, can get this result by selling their stock dividends, in the same way as they sell their subscription rights under present practice.

Notes · 注释（贾森·兹威格）

* Ironically, takeovers began drying up shortly after Graham’s last revised edition appeared, and the 1970s and early 1980s marked the absolute low point of modern American industrial efficiency. Cars were “lemons,” televisions and radios were constantly “on the fritz,” and the managers of many publicly-traded companies ignored both the present interests of their outside shareholders and the future prospects of their own businesses. All of this began to change in 1984, when independent oilman T. Boone Pickens launched a hostile takeover bid for Gulf Oil. Soon, fueled by junk-bond financing provided by Drexel Burnham Lambert, “corporate raiders” stalked the landscape of corporate America, scaring long-sclerotic companies into a new regimen of efficiency. While many of the companies involved in buy-outs and takeovers were ravaged, the rest of American business emerged both leaner (which was good) and meaner (which sometimes was not).
讽刺的是，本版出版后收购很快减少，70年代和80年代初成为现代美国工业效率最低谷。1984年独立石油商T·布恩·皮肯斯敌意收购海湾石油后局面改变；德崇证券垃圾债融资推动“公司袭击者”出动，迫使僵化企业提高效率。许多被收购公司遭破坏，其余美国企业变得更精干（好事），也更冷酷（未必好）。
* The irony that Graham describes here grew even stronger in the 1990s, when it almost seemed that the stronger the company was, the less likely it was to pay a dividend—or for its shareholders to want one. The “payout ratio” (or the percentage of their net income that companies paid out as dividends) dropped from “60% to 75%” in Graham’s day to 35% to 40% by the end of the 1990s.
90年代这种讽刺更强：公司越强，越可能不派息，股东也越不想要。派息率从格雷厄姆时代60%—75%降到90年代末35%—40%。
* In the late 1990s, technology companies were particularly strong advocates of the view that all of their earnings should be “plowed back into the business,” where they could earn higher returns than any outside shareholder possibly could by reinvesting the same cash if it were paid out to him or her in dividends. Incredibly, investors never questioned the truth of this patronizing Daddy-Knows-Best principle—or even realized that a company’s cash belongs to the shareholders, not its managers. See the commentary on this chapter.
90年代末科技公司尤其主张全部盈利“投入业务”，声称回报高于股东拿到股息自行再投资。令人难信的是，投资者既不质疑这种家长式原则，也没意识到公司现金属于股东而非经理。
* Superior Oil’s stock price peaked at $2165 per share in 1959, when it paid a $4 dividend. For many years, Superior was the highest-priced stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange. Superior, controlled by the Keck family of Houston, was acquired by Mobil Corp. in 1984.
苏必利尔石油1959年股价最高2165美元，股息4美元；多年是纽交所最高价股票。休斯敦凯克家族控制，1984年被美孚收购。
* Today, virtually all stock splits are carried out by a change in value. In a two-for-one split, one share becomes two, each trading at half the former price of the original single share; in a three-for-one split, one share becomes three, each trading at a third of the former price; and so on. Only in very rare cases is a sum transferred “from earned surplus to capital account,” as in Graham’s day.
今天几乎所有拆股都通过份额变化完成：一拆二后每股约原价一半，一拆三后约三分之一。像格雷厄姆时代那样从留存盈余转资本账户极少。
† Rule 703 of the New York Stock Exchange governs stock splits and stock dividends. The NYSE now designates stock dividends of greater than 25% and less than 100% as “partial stock splits.” Unlike in Graham’s day, these stock dividends may now trigger the NYSE’s accounting requirement that the amount of the dividend be capitalized from retained earnings.
纽交所规则703管理拆股和股票股利；如今大于25%小于100%的股票股利称“部分拆股”，并可能触发从留存收益资本化股利金额的会计要求。
* This policy, already unusual in Graham’s day, is extremely rare today. In 1936 and again in 1950, roughly half of all stocks on the NYSE paid a so-called special dividend. By 1970, however, that percentage had declined to less than 10% and, by the 1990s, was well under 5%. See Harry DeAngelo, Linda DeAngelo, and Douglas J. Skinner, “Special Dividends and the Evolution of Dividend Signaling,” Journal of Financial Economics, vol. 57, no. 3, September, 2000, pp. 309–354. The most plausible explanation for this decline is that corporate managers became uncomfortable with the idea that shareholders might interpret special dividends as a signal that future profits might be low.
这项政策当年已少见，如今极罕见。1936和1950年纽交所约半数股票付“特别股息”，1970年不足10%，90年代低于5%。合理解释是管理者担心股东把特别股息解读为未来利润偏低信号。
† The academic criticism of dividends was led by Merton Miller and Franco Modigliani, whose influential article “Dividend Policy, Growth, and the Valuation of Shares” (1961) helped win them Nobel Prizes in Economics. Miller and Modigliani argued, in essence, that dividends were irrelevant, since an investor should not care whether his return comes through dividends and a rising stock price, or through a rising stock price alone, so long as the total return is the same in either case.
学界批评由默顿·米勒和弗兰科·莫迪利亚尼领衔；其1961年论文认为，只要总回报相同，投资者不应在意来自股息加涨价，还是仅来自涨价，股息政策因此无关。
* Graham’s argument is no longer valid, and today’s investors can safely skip over this passage. Shareholders no longer need to worry about “having to break up” a stock certificate, since virtually all shares now exist in electronic rather than paper form. And when Graham says that a 5% increase in a cash dividend on 100 shares is less “probable” than a constant dividend on 105 shares, it’s unclear how he could even calculate that probability.
格雷厄姆这一论证已不成立，今天可跳过。股票几乎全为电子形式，不必“拆开”证书；他所谓100股股息提高5%比105股维持股息更不“可能”，也不清楚如何计算。
† Subscription rights, often simply known as “rights,” are used less frequently than in Graham’s day. They confer upon an existing shareholder the right to buy new shares, sometimes at a discount to market price. A shareholder who does not participate will end up owning proportionately less of the company. Thus, as is the case with so many other things that go by the name of “rights,” some coercion is often involved. Rights are most common today among closed-end funds and insurance or other holding companies.
认股权今天比当年少见，它给现有股东有时折价买新股的权利；不参与者持股比例下降，因此所谓“权利”也带强迫性。今天多见于封闭式基金及保险等控股公司。
* The administration of President George W. Bush made progress in early 2003 toward reducing the problem of double-taxation of corporate dividends, although it is too soon to know how helpful any final laws in this area will turn out to be. A cleaner approach would be to make dividend payments tax-deductible to the corporation, but that is not part of the proposed legislation.
小布什政府2003年初推动减少公司股息双重征税，但最终帮助多大尚未知。更干净办法是让公司股息税前扣除，不过不在提案中。

Endnotes · 尾注（本杰明·格雷厄姆）

1. Analytical studies have shown that in the typical case a dollar paid out in dividends had as much as four times the positive effect on market price as had a dollar of undistributed earnings. This point was well illustrated by the public-utility group for a number of years before 1950. The low-payout issues sold at low multipliers of earnings, and proved to be especially attractive buys because their dividends were later advanced. Since 1950 payout rates have been much more uniform for the industry.
研究显示，典型情况下每1美元股息对市价的正面作用，可达每1美元留存盈利的四倍。1950年前公用事业很好说明：低派息公司市盈率低，后来提高股息后成为格外吸引的买点。1950年后行业派息率更统一。

CHAPTER 20

作为投资核心概念的“安全边际”

Margin of Safety

如何让买入价格承担错误，而不是让预测必须完美？

Chapter 20“Margin of Safety” as the Central Concept of Investment第20章 作为投资核心概念的“安全边际”

本章导读这是格雷厄姆自己认定的全书核心，也是巴菲特最推崇的一章。他把稳健投资的秘诀压缩成三个词：安全边际（MARGIN OF SAFETY），并用一条连贯的论证把前面各章串起来。先从债券和优先股说起：过去若干年的盈利必须远超固定利息（铁路公司要达到五倍以上），或者企业价值必须远高于债务，这段“余量”的作用是让投资者不必准确预测未来。接着移到普通股：正常情况下，股票的盈利收益率（盈利÷价格）高出债券利率的部分就是安全边际——按旧版的例子，9% 对 4%，十年累计约为买价的 50%；但在 1972 年的价位上，这一差距已经太小，即使分散持有优质股也有真实风险。他进一步指出，投资者最大的亏损并非来自为好公司出价过高，而是在景气年份买进低质量证券（“晴天投资、晴天价格”）；成长股的问题是价格常常高到把边际吞掉，而廉价股的价格与评估价值之间的差额本身就是边际。随后是三个引申：分散投资与安全边际互为表里（轮盘赌的算术说明，只有赔率对你有利时分散才有意义）；能否用数字、推理和经验证明安全边际的存在，正是区分投资与投机的试金石；只要价格足够低，平庸的证券甚至认股权证也可以成为真正的投资。结尾把投资归结为“像做生意一样”，提出四条商业原则：懂你的生意、别轻易让别人替你经营、靠算术而不靠乐观、有了知识和判断就要有行动的勇气——“你的对错不取决于大众是否同意你”。最后一句值得记住：取得满意的结果比多数人想的容易，取得卓越的结果比看上去难。

In the old legend the wise men finally boiled down the history of mortal affairs into the single phrase, “This too will pass.”* Confronted with a like challenge to distill the secret of sound investment into three words, we venture the motto, MARGIN OF SAFETY. This is the thread that runs through all the preceding discussion of investment policy—often explicitly, sometimes in a less direct fashion. Let us try now, briefly, to trace that idea in a connected argument.

古老传说中，智者们最终把人世间的兴衰变迁浓缩成一句话：“这一切也终将过去。”面对一个类似的挑战——用三个词提炼稳健投资的秘诀——我们斗胆提出这句箴言：安全边际（MARGIN OF SAFETY）。它是贯穿前面所有投资策略讨论的一条主线：有时说得很明确，有时表达得较为间接。现在，让我们尝试用一套连贯的论证，简要追溯这一思想。

译者补充（非原文） · 理解要点

“安全边际”不是预测市场何时上涨，而是事先留出容错空间。就像桥梁按远高于日常车流的承重标准建造：你不必准确预知明天会有多少辆车，也能承受一定的判断误差和意外。

boiled down归结为，浓缩为mortal affairs人间世事（mortal：凡人的、终有一死的）a like challenge类似的挑战（like 此处是形容词“相似的”）distill提炼venture the motto斗胆提出这句箴言（venture：冒昧地说出）the thread that runs through贯穿……的主线

All experienced investors recognize that the margin-of-safety concept is essential to the choice of sound bonds and preferred stocks. For example, a railroad should have earned its total fixed charges better than five times (before income tax), taking a period of years, for its bonds to qualify as investment-grade issues. This past ability to earn in excess of interest requirements constitutes the margin of safety that is counted on to protect the investor against loss or discomfiture in the event of some future decline in net income. (The margin above charges may be stated in other ways— for example, in the percentage by which revenues or profits may decline before the balance after interest disappears—but the underlying idea remains the same.)

所有经验丰富的投资者都知道，挑选稳健的债券和优先股时，安全边际至关重要。例如，一家铁路公司若想让其债券达到投资级标准，就应当在若干年的考察期内，税前盈利对全部固定费用的覆盖倍数超过五倍。过去盈利超过利息要求的这部分余量，就构成安全边际；如果未来净利润下降，投资者要依靠它来避免损失或陷入困境。（固定费用之上的余量也可以换一种说法来表示，例如：收入或利润最多可以下降多少百分比，才会使付息后的盈余降为零；但其根本思想相同。）

译者补充（非原文） · 数字例子

公司多年平均税前利润为 1 亿元，每年利息等固定费用为 2,000 万元，覆盖倍数就是 5 倍。利润即使下降 80% 到 2,000 万元，仍刚好能够付息；这 80% 的可下降空间，就是一种安全边际。

preferred stocks优先股fixed charges固定费用（主要指必须支付的利息等固定支出）better than five times五倍以上（better than 此处 = more than，即利息保障倍数超过 5）taking a period of years以若干年为考察期investment-grade issues投资级证券（issue = 证券，本书常用义）counted on被指望，被依赖discomfiture挫败，狼狈的处境the balance after interest付息之后的盈余

The bond investor does not expect future average earnings to work out the same as in the past; if he were sure of that, the margin demanded might be small. Nor does he rely to any controlling extent on his judgment as to whether future earnings will be materially better or poorer than in the past, if he did that, he would have to measure his margin in terms of a carefully projected income account, instead of emphasizing the margin shown in the past record. Here the function of the margin of safety is, in essence, that of rendering unnecessary an accurate estimate of the future. If the margin is a large one, then it is enough to assume that future earnings will not fall far below those of the past in order for an investor to feel sufficiently protected against the vicissitudes of time.

债券投资者并不期待未来的平均盈利会与过去完全相同；如果他能确定两者相同，所要求的安全边际本可很小。他也不会主要依赖自己对未来盈利将显著好于还是差于过去的判断。否则，他就必须根据一份精心预测的未来损益表来衡量安全边际，而不是重视历史记录已经显示出的余量。安全边际的作用，本质上就是让投资者不必精确估计未来。如果边际足够大，那么只需假定未来盈利不会远低于过去，投资者便可以相信自己能得到足够保护，抵御岁月中的种种变故。

译者补充（非原文） · 理解要点

格雷厄姆不是说未来预测毫无用处，而是说投资不能建立在“预测必须非常准”之上。若一项投资只有在收入连续十年每年增长 20% 时才划算，它的容错空间就很小；若收入零增长甚至小幅下降仍能还本付息，安全边际就更大。

Nor does he rely to any controlling extent on his judgment as to whether future earnings will be materially better or poorer than in the past, if he did that, he would have to measure his margin in terms of a carefully projected income account, instead of emphasizing the margin shown in the past record.

他也不会在任何决定性的程度上依赖自己对未来盈利会比过去明显更好还是更差的判断；如果他那样做，就必须根据一份精心预测的损益表来衡量安全边际，而不是看重过往记录所显示的边际。

The margin of safety for bonds may be calculated, alternatively, by comparing the total value of the enterprise with the amount of debt. (A similar calculation may be made for a preferred-stock issue.) If the business owes $10 million and is fairly worth $30 million, there is room for a shrinkage of two-thirds in value—at least theoretically—before the bondholders will suffer loss. The amount of this extra value, or “cushion,” above the debt may be approximated by using the average market price of the junior stock issues over a period of years. Since average stock prices are generally related to average earning power, the margin of “enterprise value” over debt and the margin of earnings over charges will in most cases yield similar results.

债券的安全边际还可以用另一种方式计算：比较企业总价值与债务金额。（优先股也可以作类似计算。）如果一家企业负债 1,000 万美元，而合理价值为 3,000 万美元，那么至少在理论上，企业价值可以缩水三分之二，债券持有人才会开始遭受损失。高于债务的这部分额外价值，也就是“缓冲垫”，可以用次级证券（如普通股）多年平均市值来作近似估计。由于平均股价通常与平均盈利能力相关，企业价值超过债务的幅度，与盈利超过固定费用的幅度，在大多数情况下会得出相近的结论。

企业价值 3,000 万美元、债务 1,000 万美元，价值缓冲为 2,000 万美元。企业价值要先损失约 66.7%，才会降到只够覆盖债务；这并不保证债券绝不违约，但说明债权前面有较厚的资产保护层。

So much for the margin-of-safety concept as applied to “fixed-value investments.” Can it be carried over into the field of common stocks? Yes, but with some necessary modifications.

以上讨论的是安全边际如何用于“固定价值投资”。那么，这一概念能否延伸到普通股领域？可以，但必须作一些必要的调整。

So much for……就说到这里fixed-value investments固定价值投资（指债券、优先股等本息固定的投资）carried over into移用到，延伸到

There are instances where a common stock may be considered sound because it enjoys a margin of safety as large as that of a good bond. This will occur, for example, when a company has outstanding only common stock that under depression conditions is selling for less than the amount of bonds that could safely be issued against its property and earning power.* That was the position of a host of strongly financed industrial companies at the low price levels of 1932–33. In such instances the investor can obtain the margin of safety associated with a bond, plus all the chances of larger income and principal appreciation inherent in a common stock. (The only thing he lacks is the legal power to insist on dividend payments “or else”—but this is a small drawback as compared with his advantages.) Common stocks bought under such circumstances will supply an ideal, though infrequent, combination of safety and profit opportunity. As a quite recent example of this condition, let us mention once more National Presto Industries stock, which sold for a total enterprise value of $43 million in 1972. With its $16 millions of recent earnings before taxes the company could easily have supported this amount of bonds.

在某些情况下，普通股也可以像优质债券一样，因为拥有同样大的安全边际而被视为稳健投资。例如，一家公司只发行了普通股，而在经济萧条时期，它的全部股票市值甚至低于按照其资产和盈利能力本可安全发行的债券金额，就会出现这种情况。1932—1933 年股价处于低位时，许多财务实力雄厚的工业公司正是如此。在这种情况下，投资者既能获得债券式的安全边际，又能保留普通股所具有的收入增加和本金升值机会。（他唯一缺少的是依法强制公司支付股息的权力，否则可以采取追索行动；但与所获优势相比，这只是一个很小的缺点。）在这种条件下买入普通股，可以得到一种理想但不常见的安全性与盈利机会的组合。举一个当时较新的例子：National Presto Industries 的全部企业价值在 1972 年为 4,300 万美元，而公司近期税前利润为 1,600 万美元；这样的盈利足以轻松支持同等金额的债券。

译者补充（非原文） · 理解要点

这里不是说“股价跌得多就安全”，而是说股权总价低到连一笔由资产和盈利充分保障的债务额度都不到。仍需核实资产是否真实可变现、盈利是否可持续，以及公司是否存在未计入的负债。

This will occur, for example, when a company has outstanding only common stock that under depression conditions is selling for less than the amount of bonds that could safely be issued against its property and earning power.

例如，当一家公司在外发行的证券只有普通股，而在萧条时期这些普通股的售价，还低于以该公司的资产和盈利能力为担保本可以安全发行的债券金额时，就会出现这种情形。
