In the ordinary common stock, bought for investment under normal conditions, the margin of safety lies in an expected earning power considerably above the going rate for bonds. In former editions we elucidated this point with the following figures:

对于在正常条件下作为投资而买入的一般普通股，安全边际存在于：预期盈利收益率明显高于当时的债券利率。我们在本书以前的版本中用下面这组数字说明过这一点：

lies in在于the going rate现行利率，当前市场利率elucidated阐明

Assume in a typical case that the earning power is 9% on the price and that the bond rate is 4%; then the stockbuyer will have an average annual margin of 5% accruing in his favor. Some of the excess is paid to him in the dividend rate; even though spent by him, it enters into his overall investment result. The undistributed balance is reinvested in the business for his account. In many cases such reinvested earnings fail to add commensurately to the earning power and value of his stock. (That is why the market has a stubborn habit of valuing earnings disbursed in dividends more generously than the portion retained in the business.)* But, if the picture is viewed as a whole, there is a reasonably close connection between the growth of corporate surpluses through reinvested earnings and the growth of corporate values.

假设一个典型案例中，按买入价格计算的盈利能力为 9%，债券利率为 4%；那么股票买方每年平均可获得 5% 的有利余量。超出的部分有一些以股息形式支付给他；即使他把股息花掉，这仍然计入他的总体投资结果。没有分配的余额则代表他被继续投入企业的资金。很多时候，这些再投资的利润并不能按相称幅度提高公司的盈利能力和股票价值。（这就是市场往往更愿意给已作为股息发放的利润较高估值，而较低评价留在企业内的利润的原因。）不过，从整体来看，由再投资利润推动的公司盈余增长，与企业价值增长之间仍有相当密切的联系。

译者补充（非原文） · 数字例子

以 100 元买入一股，正常化每股收益为 9 元，盈利收益率即 9%；若债券收益率为 4%，两者相差 5 个百分点。假设 3 元作为股息发放、6 元留在公司，这 9 元都属于股东的经济收益，但留存的 6 元只有在管理层能有效再投资时才真正增值。

accruing in his favor累积到他名下，对他有利地积累the excess超出的部分（指盈利率高出债券利率的部分）enters into计入，构成……的一部分undistributed balance未分配的余额for his account记在他的账上，归他所有commensurately相应地，成比例地disbursed支付出去的，发放的corporate surpluses公司盈余（留存的累积利润）

Over a ten-year period the typical excess of stock earning power over bond interest may aggregate 50% of the price paid. This figure is sufficient to provide a very real margin of safety—which, under favorable conditions, will prevent or minimize a loss. If such a margin is present in each of a diversified list of twenty or more stocks, the probability of a favorable result under “fairly normal conditions” becomes very large. That is why the policy of investing in representative common stocks does not require high qualities of insight and foresight to work out successfully. If the purchases are made at the average level of the market over a span of years, the prices paid should carry with them assurance of an adequate margin of safety. The danger to investors lies in concentrating their purchases in the upper levels of the market, or in buying nonrepresentative common stocks that carry more than average risk of diminished earning power.

在十年期间，股票盈利能力通常高于债券利息的部分，累计可能达到买入价格的 50%。这个幅度足以形成非常实在的安全边际；在有利条件下，它能够避免或减少损失。如果一个由二十只或更多股票组成的分散组合中，每只股票都具有这样的边际，那么在“相当正常的条件”下，组合获得有利结果的概率就会很高。因此，投资于有代表性的普通股这一策略，并不要求投资者具有非凡的洞察力和预见力也能成功。如果在若干年里按市场平均水平分批买入，所付价格应当自带足够安全边际的保障。投资者面临的危险，在于把买入集中在市场的高位，或者买进缺乏代表性、盈利能力下降风险高于平均水平的普通股。

译者补充（非原文） · 理解要点

分散化只能让多个“本来就略占优势”的投资结果更稳定，不能把昂贵资产变便宜。若 20 只股票都没有安全边际，只是同时买入，并不会自动降低估值风险。

As we see it, the whole problem of common-stock investment under 1972 conditions lies in the fact that “in a typical case” the earning power is now much less than 9% on the price paid.* Let us assume that by concentrating somewhat on the low-multiplier issues among the large companies a defensive investor may now acquire equities at 12 times recent earnings—i.e., with an earnings return of 8.33% on cost. He may obtain a dividend yield of about 4%, and he will have 4.33% of his cost reinvested in the business for his account. On this basis, the excess of stock earning power over bond interest over a ten-year basis would still be too small to constitute an adequate margin of safety. For that reason we feel that there are real risks now even in a diversified list of sound common stocks. The risks may be fully offset by the profit possibilities of the list; and indeed the investor may have no choice but to incur them—for otherwise he may run an even greater risk of holding only fixed claims payable in steadily depreciating dollars. Nonetheless the investor would do well to recognize, and to accept as philosophically as he can, that the old package of good profit possibilities combined with small ultimate risk is no longer available to him.*

在我们看来，1972 年条件下普通股投资的全部难题在于：一个“典型案例”的盈利能力，按买入价格计算已经远低于 9%。假设防御型投资者稍微侧重于大型公司中市盈率较低的股票，可以按近期盈利的 12 倍买入，也就是成本对应的盈利收益率为 8.33%。他可能获得约 4% 的股息收益率，另有相当于成本 4.33% 的利润替他留在企业里再投资。按这个基础计算，十年内股票盈利能力高于债券利息的幅度，仍然太小，无法构成充分的安全边际。因此，我们认为，即使分散持有一组稳健的普通股，当时也存在真实风险。这些风险可能被组合的盈利潜力完全抵消；事实上，投资者也可能不得不承担这种风险，否则他若只持有以持续贬值的美元偿付的固定债权，风险反而更大。尽管如此，投资者仍应当认识到并尽可能坦然接受：过去那种“良好盈利潜力与很小最终风险”兼得的组合，已经不再可得。

译者补充（非原文） · 口径提醒

这里的 8.33%、4% 和十年比较是 1972 年的历史情境，不是今天可以照抄的买入阈值。实际应用时，应以当前无风险利率、公司正常化盈利、通胀、税率和盈利稳定性重新计算。

However, the risk of paying too high a price for good-quality stocks—while a real one—is not the chief hazard confronting the average buyer of securities. Observation over many years has taught us that the chief losses to investors come from the purchase of low-quality securities at times of favorable business conditions. The purchasers view the current good earnings as equivalent to “earning power” and assume that prosperity is synonymous with safety. It is in those years that bonds and preferred stocks of inferior grade can be sold to the public at a price around par, because they carry a little higher income return or a deceptively attractive conversion privilege. It is then, also, that common stocks of obscure companies can be floated at prices far above the tangible investment, on the strength of two or three years of excellent growth.

不过，为优质股票支付过高价格的风险虽然真实存在，却不是普通证券买方面临的首要危险。多年的观察告诉我们，投资者最主要的损失来自：在经营环境有利时买进低质量证券。买方把眼前的好利润等同于长期“盈利能力”，并以为繁荣就等于安全。正是在这种年份，低等级债券和优先股可以按接近面值的价格卖给公众，因为它们提供稍高一点的收益率，或附带看似诱人的转换权；也正是在这种时候，一些默默无闻的公司仅凭两三年的高速增长，就能以远高于有形投入价值的价格发行普通股。

译者补充（非原文） · 通俗例子

一家周期性公司在行业高景气时利润从 1 亿元升到 5 亿元，市场把 5 亿元当成永久水平并给高估值；一旦产品价格回落，利润可能又回到 1 亿元甚至亏损。问题不是“利润曾经很好”，而是买价没有为正常化利润和周期下行留余地。

These securities do not offer an adequate margin of safety in any admissible sense of the term. Coverage of interest charges and preferred dividends must be tested over a number of years, including preferably a period of subnormal business such as in 1970–71. The same is ordinarily true of common-stock earnings if they are to qualify as indicators of earning power. Thus it follows that most of the fair-weather investments, acquired at fair-weather prices, are destined to suffer disturbing price declines when the horizon clouds over—and often sooner than that. Nor can the investor count with confidence on an eventual recovery—although this does come about in some proportion of the cases—for he has never had a real safety margin to tide him through adversity.

这些证券无论按安全边际的哪一种合理含义衡量，都没有提供充分保护。对利息和优先股股息的覆盖能力，必须用若干年数据检验，而且最好包括像 1970—1971 年那样的低迷经营期。如果普通股利润要被视为盈利能力的指标，通常也应作同样检验。因此，大多数在晴朗天气里、按晴天价格买入的投资，一旦天色转阴，就注定出现令人不安的价格下跌，甚至常常在那之前就已下跌。投资者也不能确信它们最终一定复苏——虽然其中确有一部分会恢复——因为他从一开始就没有真正的安全边际来帮助自己渡过逆境。

Nor can the investor count with confidence on an eventual recovery—although this does come about in some proportion of the cases—for he has never had a real safety margin to tide him through adversity.

又一个 Nor 引导的倒装句，承接上一句的否定意味；count on 被 with confidence 隔开；两个破折号之间是让步插入语，does come about 里的 does 表示强调；最后的 for 是连词“因为”。

The philosophy of investment in growth stocks parallels in part and in part contravenes the margin-of-safety principle. The growth-stock buyer relies on an expected earning power that is greater than the average shown in the past. Thus he may be said to substitute these expected earnings for the past record in calculating his margin of safety. In investment theory there is no reason why carefully estimated future earnings should be a less reliable guide than the bare record of the past; in fact, security analysis is coming more and more to prefer a competently executed evaluation of the future. Thus the growth-stock approach may supply as dependable a margin of safety as is found in the ordinary investment—provided the calculation of the future is conservatively made, and provided it shows a satisfactory margin in relation to the price paid.

成长股投资哲学有一部分与安全边际原则一致，另一部分却与之相冲突。成长股买方依赖的是高于历史平均水平的预期盈利能力。因此可以说，他在计算安全边际时，用预期盈利替代了历史记录。在投资理论上，没有理由认为经过谨慎估算的未来盈利一定不如单纯的历史记录可靠；事实上，证券分析越来越倾向于采用专业完成的未来评估。因此，成长股方法也可能提供与一般投资同样可靠的安全边际——前提是对未来的估计足够保守，而且相对于买入价格确实显示出令人满意的余量。

译者补充（非原文） · 理解要点

成长不是安全边际，只有“保守估计的未来价值明显高于买价”才是。如果估值必须依赖最乐观的增长率、利润率和终值假设同时实现，实际上没有留下多少边际。

The danger in a growth-stock program lies precisely here. For such favored issues the market has a tendency to set prices that will not be adequately protected by a conservative projection of future earnings. (It is a basic rule of prudent investment that all estimates, when they differ from past performance, must err at least slightly on the side of understatement.) The margin of safety is always dependent on the price paid. It will be large at one price, small at some higher price, nonexistent at some still higher price. If, as we suggest, the average market level of most growth stocks is too high to provide an adequate margin of safety for the buyer, then a simple technique of diversified buying in this field may not work out satisfactorily. A special degree of foresight and judgment will be needed, in order that wise individual selections may overcome the hazards inherent in the customary market level of such issues as a whole.

成长股策略的危险恰恰在这里。对于这类备受追捧的股票，市场往往给出一种价格，使得即便采用保守的未来盈利预测，也无法得到充分保护。（审慎投资有一条基本规则：凡估计值与过去业绩不同，至少应略微偏向保守低估。）安全边际永远取决于买入价格：在某个价格上很大，在更高价格上变小，在更高的价格上则完全消失。如果像我们所认为的那样，大多数成长股的平均市场价格过高，不能为买方提供充分的安全边际，那么在这个领域简单地分散买入，可能也得不到令人满意的结果。投资者需要格外出色的预见和判断，才能通过明智地挑选个股，克服这类股票整体上惯常高估值所带来的危险。

同一家公司的保守价值若为每股 100 元：以 60 元买入，价值比价格高约 67%；以 90 元买入，只剩约 11%；以 120 元买入则没有安全边际。公司没有变化，变化的是你支付的价格。

The margin-of-safety idea becomes much more evident when we apply it to the field of undervalued or bargain securities. We have here, by definition, a favorable difference between price on the one hand and indicated or appraised value on the other. That difference is the safety margin. It is available for absorbing the effect of miscalculations or worse than average luck. The buyer of bargain issues places particular emphasis on the ability of the investment to withstand adverse developments. For in most such cases he has no real enthusiasm about the company’s prospects. True, if the prospects are definitely bad the investor will prefer to avoid the security no matter how low the price. But the field of undervalued issues is drawn from the many concerns—perhaps a majority of the total—for which the future appears neither distinctly promising nor distinctly unpromising. If these are bought on a bargain basis, even a moderate decline in the earning power need not prevent the investment from showing satisfactory results. The margin of safety will then have served its proper purpose.

把安全边际思想用于低估证券或廉价证券时，它会显得更加清楚。按照定义，这类证券的价格与其显示出的或评估得出的价值之间存在有利差额，这个差额就是安全边际。它可以吸收估算错误或运气差于平均水平造成的影响。廉价证券的买方尤其看重投资抵御不利变化的能力，因为多数情况下，他并不真正看好公司的前景。当然，如果前景明确糟糕，那么无论价格多低，投资者都宁愿避开。但低估证券的范围来自许多企业——也许占全部企业的大多数——其未来既不明显乐观，也不明显悲观。如果以便宜价格买进，即使盈利能力温和下降，也不一定妨碍投资取得满意结果。此时，安全边际就发挥了它应有的作用。

你估算一项资产值 100 元，却只用 60 元买入。后来发现自己高估了 20%，真实价值只有 80 元，价格与价值之间仍有 20 元余量。若一开始用 95 元买入，同样的估算错误就会使投资立刻失去保护。

Theory of Diversification

分散投资的理论

There is a close logical connection between the concept of a safety margin and the principle of diversification. One is correlative with the other. Even with a margin in the investor’s favor, an individual security may work out badly. For the margin guarantees only that he has a better chance for profit than for loss—not that loss is impossible. But as the number of such commitments is increased the more certain does it become that the aggregate of the profits will exceed the aggregate of the losses. That is the simple basis of the insurance-underwriting business.

安全边际概念与分散投资原则之间有紧密的逻辑联系，两者互为表里。即使某项证券对投资者有利，它仍可能出现糟糕结果。安全边际只保证获利机会大于亏损机会，并不保证绝不亏损。但随着这类投资项目数量增加，利润总额超过亏损总额的确定性也会提高。这正是保险承保业务的简单基础。

译者补充（非原文） · 理解要点

保险公司知道单个保单可能巨亏，但只要每份保单的保费总体高于预期赔付与成本，并且风险不过度集中，大量承保后结果就更可预测。投资组合也是如此：先要有正的期望优势，再用分散降低单一判断失误的影响。

But as the number of such commitments is increased the more certain does it become that the aggregate of the profits will exceed the aggregate of the losses.

但随着这类投资的数目增加，利润总和超过亏损总和这件事就变得越来越确定。

这是 the more… 结构的变体：前半句 as the number… is increased 相当于 the more…，后半句 the more certain does it become 用了倒装（正常语序是 it becomes the more certain）；it 是形式主语，真正的主语是 that 从句。commitments 在本书中指投入的资金或头寸。

Diversification is an established tenet of conservative investment. By accepting it so universally, investors are really demonstrating their acceptance of the margin-of-safety principle, to which diversification is the companion. This point may be made more colorful by a reference to the arithmetic of roulette. If a man bets $1 on a single number, he is paid $35 profit when he wins—but the chances are 37 to 1 that he will lose. He has a “negative margin of safety.” In his case diversification is foolish. The more numbers he bets on, the smaller his chance of ending with a profit. If he regularly bets $1 on every number (including 0 and 00), he is certain to lose $2 on each turn of the wheel. But suppose the winner received $39 profit instead of $35. Then he would have a small but important margin of safety. Therefore, the more numbers he wagers on, the better his chance of gain. And he could be certain of winning $2 on every spin by simply betting $1 each on all the numbers. (Incidentally, the two examples given actually describe the respective positions of the player and proprietor of a wheel with 0 and 00.)*

分散投资是保守投资的一条公认信条。投资者如此普遍地接受它，其实也说明他们接受了安全边际原则；分散化正是安全边际的配套方法。用轮盘赌的算术可以把这一点说得更生动：如果一个人用 1 美元押一个号码，押中可获 35 美元利润，但输的概率是 37 比 1。他拥有的是“负安全边际”。对他而言，分散下注是愚蠢的：押的号码越多，最终盈利的机会越小。如果他每次在包括 0 和 00 在内的所有号码上各押 1 美元，那么每转一次轮盘，他必定亏 2 美元。可是，假设押中不是赚 35 美元，而是赚 39 美元，那么玩家就会拥有一个虽小却重要的安全边际。他押的号码越多，获利概率就越高；若在所有号码上各押 1 美元，每转一次甚至可以确定赚 2 美元。（顺便说一句，这两个例子正好分别描述了带 0 和 00 的轮盘中玩家和赌场经营者的位置。）

译者补充（非原文） · 数字复算

美式轮盘有 38 格。真实规则下全押共花 38 美元，中奖一格收回本金 1 美元并赚 35 美元，共拿回 36 美元，净亏 2 美元。若利润改为 39 美元，则共拿回 40 美元，净赚 2 美元。分散化放大的是既有的数学优势或劣势。

A Criterion of Investment versus Speculation

区分投资与投机的一个标准

Since there is no single definition of investment in general acceptance, authorities have the right to define it pretty much as they please. Many of them deny that there is any useful or dependable difference between the concepts of investment and of speculation. We think this skepticism is unnecessary and harmful. It is injurious because it lends encouragement to the innate leaning of many people toward the excitement and hazards of stock-market speculation. We suggest that the margin-of-safety concept may be used to advantage as the touchstone to distinguish an investment operation from a speculative one.

由于投资并没有一个得到普遍接受的单一定义，各种权威几乎可以按自己的意愿来界定它。许多人否认投资与投机之间存在任何有用或可靠的区别。我们认为这种怀疑没有必要，而且有害。它会助长许多人天生就有的倾向，使他们追逐股市投机的刺激与危险。我们建议，可以把安全边际概念作为一块试金石，用来区分投资操作与投机操作。

译者补充（非原文） · 判断问题

不要只问“它会不会涨”，而要问：即使我对增长、利润率或时间判断错了一部分，现有价格是否仍有可由数字说明的保护？若答案只能依赖市场情绪或下一位买家出更高价，就更接近投机。

pretty much as they please几乎随心所欲地injurious有害的lends encouragement to助长innate leaning天生的倾向to advantage有效地，很好地touchstone试金石

Probably most speculators believe they have the odds in their favor when they take their chances, and therefore they may lay claim to a safety margin in their proceedings. Each one has the feeling that the time is propitious for his purchase, or that his skill is superior to the crowd’s, or that his adviser or system is trustworthy. But such claims are unconvincing. They rest on subjective judgment, unsupported by any body of favorable evidence or any conclusive line of reasoning. We greatly doubt whether the man who stakes money on his view that the market is heading up or down can ever be said to be protected by a margin of safety in any useful sense of the phrase.

大多数投机者在冒险时，或许都相信胜算在自己这一边，因此也可能声称自己的操作有安全边际。每个人都会觉得买入时机正好，或者自己的能力胜过大众，或者所依赖的顾问或系统值得信任。但这些说法并没有说服力，因为它们建立在主观判断上，背后既没有一整套有利证据，也没有决定性的推理链条。一个人仅仅拿钱押注市场将上涨或下跌，我们非常怀疑这能否在“安全边际”的任何有用含义下称得上受到保护。

By contrast, the investor’s concept of the margin of safety—as developed earlier in this chapter—rests upon simple and definite arithmetical reasoning from statistical data. We believe, also, that it is well supported by practical investment experience. There is no guarantee that this fundamental quantitative approach will continue to show favorable results under the unknown conditions of the future. But, equally, there is no valid reason for pessimism on this score.

与此相反，投资者的安全边际概念——也就是本章前面所阐述的概念——建立在统计数据与简单、明确的算术推理之上。我们还认为，它也得到了实际投资经验的充分支持。当然，没人能保证这种基本的定量方法在未知的未来条件下仍会产生有利结果；但同样，也没有充分理由因此悲观。

译者补充（非原文） · 证据边界

格雷厄姆说的是“有依据的概率优势”，不是保证。数字可能失真、行业结构可能变化、历史样本也可能失效；所以安全边际需要与财务核验、业务判断和分散化配合。

Thus, in sum, we say that to have a true investment there must be present a true margin of safety. And a true margin of safety is one that can be demonstrated by figures, by persuasive reasoning, and by reference to a body of actual experience.

总而言之，我们认为：要成为真正的投资，就必须存在真正的安全边际；而真正的安全边际，必须能够用数字、令人信服的推理，以及一整套实际经验来证明。

Extension of the Concept of Investment

投资概念的延伸

To complete our discussion of the margin-of-safety principle we must now make a further distinction between conventional and unconventional investments. Conventional investments are appropriate for the typical portfolio. Under this heading have always come United States government issues and high-grade, dividend-paying common stocks. We have added state and municipal bonds for those who will benefit sufficiently by their tax-exempt features. Also included are first-quality corporate bonds when, as now, they can be bought to yield sufficiently more than United States savings bonds.

为了完成对安全边际原则的讨论，现在还必须进一步区分常规投资与非常规投资。常规投资适合典型的投资组合。历来归入这一类别的有美国政府债券以及高质量、支付股息的普通股。对于能从免税待遇中充分受益的人，我们还加入州政府和市政债券。此外，当一流公司债券——例如当时的情况——能提供比美国储蓄债券高出足够多的收益率时，也应包括在内。

译者补充（非原文） · 时代背景

这里列举的是美国当时的证券和税制环境，不能原样套用到其他国家或今天。可迁移的原则是：先界定适合普通投资者、结构简单且信用质量高的核心资产，再比较税后收益、期限、流动性和信用风险。

Under this heading have always come一直归在这个类别之下的有……（倒装：主语是后面的 issues 和 stocks）government issues政府债券（issue = 证券）municipal bonds市政债券tax-exempt features免税特性as now如现在这样

Unconventional investments are those that are suitable only for the enterprising investor. They cover a wide range. The broadest category is that of undervalued common stocks of secondary companies, which we recommend for purchase when they can be bought at two-thirds or less of their indicated value. Besides these, there is often a wide choice of medium-grade corporate bonds and preferred stocks when they are selling at such depressed prices as to be obtainable also at a considerable discount from their apparent value. In these cases the average investor would be inclined to call the securities speculative, because in his mind their lack of a first-quality rating is synonymous with a lack of investment merit.

非常规投资只适合积极型投资者，范围很广。最大的一类，是二线公司的低估普通股；当其价格不高于估算价值的三分之二时，我们建议买入。除此之外，中等等级的公司债券和优先股如果价格被压得很低，相对于其表面价值也有相当折价，往往同样有很多选择。在这些情况下，普通投资者可能会把它们称为投机证券，因为在他的观念中，不具备一流评级就等于没有投资价值。

译者补充（非原文） · 数字例子

估算价值 90 元，按“三分之二或更低”的标准，买价上限约为 60 元。但这个折价只有在价值估算可信、资产和现金流可核实、风险得到分散时才有意义；低评级本身既不等于便宜，也不等于必然不值得买。

It is our argument that a sufficiently low price can turn a security of mediocre quality into a sound investment opportunity—provided that the buyer is informed and experienced and that he practices adequate diversification. For, if the price is low enough to create a substantial margin of safety, the security thereby meets our criterion of investment. Our favorite supporting illustration is taken from the field of real-estate bonds. In the 1920s, billions of dollars’ worth of these issues were sold at par and widely recommended as sound investments. A large proportion had so little margin of value over debt as to be in fact highly speculative in character. In the depression of the 1930s an enormous quantity of these bonds defaulted their interest, and their price collapsed—in some cases below 10 cents on the dollar. At that stage the same advisers who had recommended them at par as safe investments were rejecting them as paper of the most speculative and unattractive type. But as a matter of fact the price depreciation of about 90% made many of these securities exceedingly attractive and reasonably safe—for the true values behind them were four or five times the market quotation.*

我们的观点是：足够低的价格可以把质量平庸的证券变成稳健的投资机会——前提是买方了解情况、经验丰富，而且作了充分分散。因为，只要价格低到足以形成可观的安全边际，这项证券就符合我们的投资标准。我们最喜欢的佐证来自房地产债券。20 世纪 20 年代，价值数十亿美元的这类债券按面值发行，并被广泛推荐为稳健投资。其中很大一部分的资产价值仅略高于债务，实际上具有高度投机性。到了 20 世纪 30 年代大萧条，大量债券停止付息，价格崩跌，有些跌到每 1 美元面值不足 10 美分。曾在面值附近把它们推荐为安全投资的同一批顾问，此时却把它们斥为最具投机性、最无吸引力的证券。可事实上，约 90% 的价格下跌让其中许多债券变得极具吸引力，而且相当安全，因为它们背后的真实价值达到市场报价的四五倍。

证券的“质量”和“价格”要分开看：好资产价格过高也可能危险，差一些的资产若价格远低于可回收价值则可能有优势。但前提是债权顺位、抵押物价值、处置成本和回收时间都经过核实，而不是看到跌了 90% 就自动判定便宜。

The fact that the purchase of these bonds actually resulted in what is generally called “a large speculative profit” did not prevent them from having true investment qualities at their low prices. The “speculative” profit was the purchaser’s reward for having made an unusually shrewd investment. They could properly be called investment opportunities, since a careful analysis would have shown that the excess of value over price provided a large margin of safety. Thus the very class of “fair-weather investments” which we stated above is a chief source of serious loss to naïve security buyers is likely to afford many sound profit opportunities to the sophisticated operator who may buy them later at pretty much his own price.†

买入这些债券后来确实获得了通常所谓的“巨额投机利润”，但这并不妨碍它们在低价时具有真正的投资属性。所谓“投机性”利润，是买方作出一次异常精明投资所得到的回报。它们完全可以被称为投资机会，因为仔细分析本可显示：价值超过价格的幅度提供了很大的安全边际。因此，我们前面所说的那类“晴天投资”——它是天真证券买家遭受严重损失的主要来源——后来却很可能为成熟的操作者提供许多稳健的获利机会，因为后者几乎可以按自己愿意的价格买入。

同一张证券在 100 元时可能是投机，在 10 元时可能成为投资，因为预期回收额没有按同样比例下降。分类取决于“价格相对价值和风险”的关系，而不是证券名称，也不是事后利润大小。

Thus the very class of “fair-weather investments” which we stated above is a chief source of serious loss to naïve security buyers is likely to afford many sound profit opportunities to the sophisticated operator who may buy them later at pretty much his own price.

因此，正是我们前面说过的、给天真的证券买家造成严重亏损的那一类“晴天投资”，很可能给老练的操作者提供许多稳妥的获利机会——后者可以在日后几乎按自己开的价把它们买下来。

The whole field of “special situations” would come under our definition of investment operations, because the purchase is always predicated on a thoroughgoing analysis that promises a larger realization than the price paid. Again there are risk factors in each individual case, but these are allowed for in the calculations and absorbed in the overall results of a diversified operation.

整个“特殊情况”领域也符合我们对投资操作的定义，因为买入总是建立在彻底分析之上，分析显示最终可实现的价值将高于买入价格。每一个个案仍有风险因素，但这些风险已经计入计算，并由分散操作的整体结果吸收。

译者补充（非原文） · 通俗例子

假设一项已公告并购的现金对价为 60 元，股票现价 55 元；如果成交可赚 5 元，若失败可能跌到 40 元。不能只看 5 元价差，还要估计成交概率、失败损失、等待时间和资金成本，并用多笔相互独立的交易分散单案失败风险。

To carry this discussion to a logical extreme, we might suggest that a defensible investment operation could be set up by buying such intangible values as are represented by a group of “common-stock option warrants” selling at historically low prices. (This example is intended as somewhat of a shocker.)* The entire value of these warrants rests on the possibility that the related stocks may some day advance above the option price. At the moment they have no exercisable value. Yet, since all investment rests on reasonable future expectations, it is proper to view these warrants in terms of the mathematical chances that some future bull market will create a large increase in their indicated value and in their price. Such a study might well yield the conclusion that there is much more to be gained in such an operation than to be lost and that the chances of an ultimate profit are much better than those of an ultimate loss. If that is so, there is a safety margin present even in this unprepossessing security form. A sufficiently enterprising investor could then include an option-warrant operation in his miscellany of unconventional investments.1

把这一讨论推到逻辑上的极端，我们甚至可以提出：买入一组处于历史低价的“普通股认股权证”所代表的无形价值，也可能构成一种站得住脚的投资操作。（这个例子有意要让人吃一惊。）这些权证的全部价值都取决于相关股票有朝一日能涨过行权价格；它们眼下没有任何可行权价值。不过，既然所有投资都建立在合理的未来预期上，那么就可以根据数学概率来评估这些权证：未来某轮牛市是否可能使其显示价值和市场价格大幅上升。这样的研究很可能得出结论：该操作潜在收益远大于潜在损失，而且最终获利的概率显著高于最终亏损的概率。如果确实如此，即使这种其貌不扬的证券形式也存在安全边际。足够积极、进取的投资者便可把权证操作纳入自己的非常规投资组合。

译者补充（非原文） · 风险提醒

这里是用来说明“任何证券都要看价格与赔率”，不是对权证的普遍推荐。现代期权和权证还受期限、波动率、稀释、流动性与发行人条款影响；大量价外权证到期归零，只有经过概率和组合层面的计算，才可能谈安全边际。

To Sum Up

总结

Investment is most intelligent when it is most businesslike. It is amazing to see how many capable businessmen try to operate in Wall Street with complete disregard of all the sound principles through which they have gained success in their own undertakings. Yet every corporate security may best be viewed, in the first instance, as an ownership interest in, or a claim against, a specific business enterprise. And if a person sets out to make profits from security purchases and sales, he is embarking on a business venture of his own, which must be run in accordance with accepted business principles if it is to have a chance of success.

投资越像做生意，就越显得聪明。令人惊讶的是，许多能干的商人在华尔街操作时，竟完全无视那些让他们在自己事业中取得成功的稳健原则。然而，任何公司证券首先都应被看成：对某一家具体企业的所有权权益，或者对该企业的一项债权。如果一个人打算从买卖证券中获利，他就是在经营自己的一门生意；若想有成功机会，就必须按照公认的商业原则来经营。

译者补充（非原文） · 理解要点

买股票不是在屏幕上交易代码，而是在某个价格上购买企业的一部分；买债券则是在某些条款下向企业出借资金。先问这门生意如何赚钱、资产和债务是什么、最坏情况会怎样，再问市场明天怎么报价。

businesslike像做生意一样的，讲求实际的with complete disregard of完全不顾undertakings事业，经营的生意in the first instance首先，首要地ownership interest in对……的所有权权益a claim against对……的债权embarking on开始从事

The first and most obvious of these principles is, “Know what you are doing—know your business.” For the investor this means: Do not try to make “business profits” out of securities—that is, returns in excess of normal interest and dividend income—unless you know as much about security values as you would need to know about the value of merchandise that you proposed to manufacture or deal in.

第一条也是最明显的原则是：“知道自己在做什么——了解自己的生意。”对投资者而言，这意味着：除非你对证券价值的了解，已经达到你在生产或经销某种商品前理应掌握其价值的程度，否则不要试图从证券中赚取“经营利润”——也就是超过正常利息和股息收入的回报。

译者补充（非原文） · 自测

如果你无法用几句话说明公司向谁收费、客户为什么持续购买、主要成本是什么、现金最终流向哪里，以及什么情况会证明判断错误，那么你可能还没有达到“了解这门生意”的程度。

in excess of超出merchandise商品，货物proposed to打算deal in经营，买卖（某种商品）

A second business principle: “Do not let anyone else run your business, unless (1) you can supervise his performance with adequate care and comprehension or (2) you have unusually strong reasons for placing implicit confidence in his integrity and ability.” For the investor this rule should determine the conditions under which he will permit someone else to decide what is done with his money.

第二条商业原则是：“不要让任何其他人替你经营生意，除非：（1）你能够以足够的谨慎和理解监督他的表现；或者（2）你有异常充分的理由，对他的诚信与能力给予完全信任。”对投资者来说，这条规则应当决定：在什么条件下，他才允许别人替自己决定资金如何运用。

译者补充（非原文） · 通俗例子

把钱交给基金经理并不等于卸下责任。你至少应能看懂其策略、费用、最大可能亏损、持仓透明度和退出条件；若完全无法监督，就必须对受托人的诚信、能力和利益一致性有非常强的证据。

supervise监督comprehension理解placing implicit confidence in对……给予无条件的信任（implicit 此处 = 绝对的、不加怀疑的）integrity诚信，正直

A third business principle: “Do not enter upon an operation—that is, manufacturing or trading in an item—unless a reliable calculation shows that it has a fair chance to yield a reasonable profit. In particular, keep away from ventures in which you have little to gain and much to lose.” For the enterprising investor this means that his operations for profit should be based not on optimism but on arithmetic. For every investor it means that when he limits his return to a small figure—as formerly, at least, in a conventional bond or preferred stock—he must demand convincing evidence that he is not risking a substantial part of his principal.

第三条商业原则是：“不要着手一项经营——无论是生产还是买卖某种商品——除非可靠的计算表明，它有相当大的机会取得合理利润。尤其要远离那些所得很少、可能损失很多的冒险。”对积极型投资者来说，这意味着他的获利操作必须建立在算术而不是乐观情绪之上。对每一位投资者来说，这还意味着：当他把收益限制在很小的幅度时——至少过去传统债券或优先股就是如此——他必须要求有令人信服的证据，证明自己并没有让大部分本金承担风险。

译者补充（非原文） · 理解要点

若一项投资最多赚 5%，最坏却可能亏 50%，仅凭“应该不会出事”并不够。收益有限的资产尤其要严格检查信用、抵押、期限和流动性，因为一次大亏可能吞掉多年的小收益。

enter upon着手，开始进行a fair chance相当大的机会ventures冒险的事业，投机项目not on optimism but on arithmetic不靠乐观情绪而靠算术as formerly像以前那样principal本金

A fourth business rule is more positive: “Have the courage of your knowledge and experience. If you have formed a conclusion from the facts and if you know your judgment is sound, act on it—even though others may hesitate or differ.” (You are neither right nor wrong because the crowd disagrees with you. You are right because your data and reasoning are right.) Similarly, in the world of securities, courage becomes the supreme virtue after adequate knowledge and a tested judgment are at hand.

第四条商业原则更为积极：“要有依据自己的知识和经验行事的勇气。如果你已经根据事实形成结论，并且知道自己的判断稳妥可靠，就照此行动——即使其他人犹豫不决或意见不同。”（大众反对你，既不会使你正确，也不会使你错误。你之所以正确，是因为你的数据和推理是正确的。）证券世界也是如此：只有在充分知识和经受检验的判断已经具备之后，勇气才会成为最高的美德。

译者补充（非原文） · 理解要点

这不是鼓励固执或逆向而行本身。顺序很重要：先有事实、数据和可检验的推理，再有行动的勇气；如果新证据推翻原判断，承认错误同样是理性的一部分。

Have the courage of your knowledge敢于坚持你的认知（仿自习语 have the courage of one’s convictions）sound正确的，稳妥的act on it照此行动supreme virtue最高的美德at hand已经具备，就在手边

(You are neither right nor wrong because the crowd disagrees with you. You are right because your data and reasoning are right.)

（你的对错并不取决于大众是否反对你。你之所以对，是因为你的数据和推理是对的。）

第一句的 because 从句否定的是“因果关系”而不是“对错”本身：不是“你既不对也不错，因为大众反对你”，而是“大众反对你这件事，既不能使你对，也不能使你错”。这是 not/neither … because 结构常见的歧义，要靠第二句的对照来确定。巴菲特多次引用这两句话。

Fortunately for the typical investor, it is by no means necessary for his success that he bring these qualities to bear upon his program—provided he limits his ambition to his capacity and confines his activities within the safe and narrow path of standard, defensive investment. To achieve satisfactory investment results is easier than most people realize; to achieve superior results is harder than it looks.

对典型投资者来说，幸运的是，他要取得成功，完全不必把上述所有素质都充分运用到自己的计划中——只要他把野心限制在能力范围内，并把活动限制在标准、防御型投资这条安全而狭窄的道路上。取得令人满意的投资结果，比多数人想象的容易；取得卓越的结果，则比看上去困难。

译者补充（非原文） · 落地理解

普通投资者不必靠频繁选股证明自己。低成本、广泛分散、不过度借贷、按计划再平衡并长期坚持，可能足以争取“满意”；若追求持续超越市场，就必须承认它需要更强的能力、纪律、时间和竞争优势。

对典型的投资者来说，幸运的是，他要取得成功，完全不必把这些素质都用到自己的投资计划上——只要他把野心限制在自己能力的范围内，把活动限制在标准的、防御型投资这条安全而狭窄的道路上。

Notes · 注释（贾森·兹威格）

* “It is said an Eastern monarch once charged his wise men to invent him a sentence, to be ever in view, and which should be true and appropriate in all times and situations. They presented him the words: ‘ And this, too, shall pass away.’ How much it expresses! How chastening in the hour of pride!—how consoling in the depths of affliction! ‘And this, too, shall pass away.’ And yet let us hope it is not quite true.”—Abraham Lincoln, Address to the Wisconsin State Agricultural Society, Milwaukee, September 30, 1859, in Abraham Lincoln: Speeches and Writings, 1859–1865 (Library of America,1985), vol. II, p. 101.
“据说，一位东方君主曾命令智者们替他想出一句话，让它永远摆在眼前，并且在任何时代、任何处境下都真实而恰当。他们献上的话是：‘这一切也终将过去。’它包含了多么丰富的含义！在骄傲时刻，它让人何等警醒；在苦难深处，它又给人何等安慰！‘这一切也终将过去。’不过，让我们希望它并非完全正确。”——亚伯拉罕·林肯，1859 年 9 月 30 日在密尔沃基威斯康星州农业协会的演讲，载于 Abraham Lincoln: Speeches and Writings, 1859–1865（Library of America，1985），第 II 卷，第 101 页。
* “Earning power” is Graham’s term for a company’s potential profits or, as he puts it, the amount that a firm “might be expected to earn year after year if the business conditions prevailing during the period were to continue unchanged” (Security Analysis, 1934 ed., p. 354). Some of his lectures make it clear that Graham intended the term to cover periods of five years or more. You can crudely but conveniently approximate a company’s earning power per share by taking the inverse of its price/earnings ratio; a stock with a P/E ratio of 11 can be said to have earning power of 9% (or 1 divided by 11). Today “earning power” is often called “earnings yield.”
“盈利能力”（earning power）是格雷厄姆用来表示公司潜在利润的术语；按他的说法，就是“如果某一时期的经营条件持续不变，一家公司年复一年可以被期待赚到的金额”（Security Analysis，1934 年版，第 354 页）。他的一些讲义清楚表明，这个术语所覆盖的是五年或更长时期。一个粗略而方便的每股盈利能力近似值，是市盈率的倒数：市盈率为 11 倍的股票，可以说盈利收益率约为 9%（即 1÷11）。今天，“盈利能力”通常称为“盈利收益率”（earnings yield）。
* This problem is discussed extensively in the commentary on Chapter 19.
第 19 章的评论部分对这个问题作了详细讨论。
* Graham elegantly summarized the discussion that follows in a lecture he gave in 1972: “The margin of safety is the difference between the percentage rate of the earnings on the stock at the price you pay for it and the rate of interest on bonds, and that margin of safety is the difference which would absorb unsatisfactory developments. At the time the 1965 edition of The Intelligent Investor was written the typical stock was selling at 11 times earnings, giving about 9% return as against 4% on bonds. In that case you had a margin of safety of over 100 per cent. Now [in 1972] there is no difference between the earnings rate on stocks and the interest rate on stocks, and I say there is no margin of safety…you have a negative margin of safety on stocks…” See “Benjamin Graham: Thoughts on Security Analysis” [transcript of lecture at the Northeast Missouri State University business school, March, 1972], Financial History, no. 42, March, 1991, p. 9.
格雷厄姆在 1972 年的一次演讲中优雅地概括了下文：“安全边际，是你按买入价格计算的股票盈利百分比与债券利率之间的差额；这一差额能够吸收不令人满意的发展。1965 年版《聪明的投资者》写作时，典型股票的售价为盈利的 11 倍，盈利收益率约 9%，而债券收益率为 4%。在这种情况下，安全边际超过 100%。现在［1972 年］，股票盈利率与利率之间已没有差额；所以我说股票没有安全边际……股票的安全边际为负……”见“Benjamin Graham: Thoughts on Security Analysis”（1972 年 3 月在 Northeast Missouri State University 商学院演讲的文字稿），Financial History，第 42 期，1991 年 3 月，第 9 页。
* This paragraph—which Graham wrote in early 1972—is an uncannily precise description of market conditions in early 2003. (For more detail, see the commentary on Chapter 3.)
这段话由格雷厄姆写于 1972 年初，却极其准确地描述了 2003 年初的市场状况。（更多细节见第 3 章评论。）
* In “American” roulette, most wheels include 0 and 00 along with numbers 1 through 36, for a total of 38 slots. The casino offers a maximum payout of 35 to 1. What if you bet $1 on every number? Since only one slot can be the one into which the ball drops, you would win $35 on that slot, but lose $1 on each of your other 37 slots, for a net loss of $2. That $2 difference (or a 5.26% spread on your total $38 bet) is the casino’s “house advantage,” ensuring that, on average, roulette players will always lose more than they win. Just as it is in the roulette player’s interest to bet as seldom as possible, it is in the casino’s interest to keep the roulette wheel spinning. Likewise, the intelligent investor should seek to maximize the number of holdings that offer “a better chance for profit than for loss.” For most investors, diversification is the simplest and cheapest way to widen your margin of safety.
“美式”轮盘通常在 1 至 36 之外还有 0 和 00，共 38 格。赌场给出的最高赔率是 35 赔 1。如果你在每个号码上各押 1 美元，会怎样？小球只会落入一个格子，你在该号码上赚 35 美元，却在其余 37 个号码上各输 1 美元，净亏 2 美元。这 2 美元的差额（占全部 38 美元投注的 5.26%）就是赌场的“庄家优势”，保证从平均结果看，轮盘玩家输的钱永远多于赢的钱。正如玩家越少下注越有利，赌场则希望轮盘不停转动。同样，聪明的投资者应尽量增加那些“获利机会大于亏损机会”的持仓数量。对多数投资者而言，分散投资是扩大安全边际最简单、成本最低的方法。
* Graham is saying that there is no such thing as a good or bad stock; there are only cheap stocks and expensive stocks. Even the best company becomes a “sell” when its stock price goes too high, while the worst company is worth buying if its stock goes low enough.
格雷厄姆的意思是：不存在脱离价格而单独成立的“好股票”或“坏股票”，只有便宜的股票和昂贵的股票。即使最优秀的公司，股价高到一定程度也会变成“卖出”；即使最差的公司，股价低到一定程度也可能值得买入。
† The very people who considered technology and telecommunications stocks a “sure thing” in late 1999 and early 2000, when they were hellishly overpriced, shunned them as “too risky” in 2002—even though, in Graham’s exact words from an earlier period, “the price depreciation of about 90% made many of these securities exceedingly attractive and reasonably safe.” Similarly, Wall Street’s analysts have always tended to call a stock a “strong buy” when its price is high, and to label it a “sell” after its price has fallen—the exact opposite of what Graham (and simple common sense) would dictate. As he does throughout the book, Graham is distinguishing speculation—or buying on the hope that a stock’s price will keep going up—from investing, or buying on the basis of what the underlying business is worth.
1999 年末至 2000 年初，科技股和电信股贵得离谱时，许多人仍把它们视为“稳赚不赔”；到了 2002 年，同一批人却躲开它们，认为“风险太大”——尽管用格雷厄姆在更早时期的原话说，“约 90% 的价格下跌使许多这类证券变得极具吸引力，而且相当安全”。同样，华尔街分析师总倾向于在股价高时给出“强力买入”，股价下跌后却标为“卖出”，这与格雷厄姆（以及简单常识）所主张的做法正好相反。正如全书反复强调的那样，格雷厄姆在区分投机——因为希望股价继续上涨而买入——与投资——根据底层企业的价值而买入。
* Graham uses “common-stock option warrant” as a synonym for “warrant,” a security issued directly by a corporation giving the holder a right to purchase the company’s stock at a predetermined price. Warrants have been almost entirely superseded by stock options. Graham quips that he intends the example as a “shocker” because, even in his day, warrants were regarded as one of the market’s seediest backwaters. (See the commentary on Chapter 16.)
格雷厄姆把“普通股选择权证”（common-stock option warrant）作为“认股权证”（warrant）的同义词。这是一种由公司直接发行、赋予持有人按预定价格购买公司股票权利的证券。认股权证后来几乎完全被股票期权取代。格雷厄姆打趣说，这个例子意在“吓人一跳”，因为即使在他那个年代，权证也被视为市场中最不入流的角落之一。（见第 16 章评论。）
